title: Fact check: This is not the grieving mother of a Sri Lankan man lynched in Pakistan
content:
This image is from a 2020 protest where an effigy of Pakistan PM Imran Khan was burnt in Lahore while Priyantha Kumara Diyawadana was a Sri Lankan man who was lynched by a mob in Pakistan's Sialkot for alleged blasphemy on December 3, 2021.
Priyantha Kumara Diyawadana, a 48-year-old Sri Lankan man was lynched and burned to death by a mob in Pakistan's Sialkot for alleged blasphemy on December 3, 2021. A video of a mob dragging the man's bruised body on the street went viral on social media. Now a photograph is being circulated with the claim that it shows the mother of the man crying in front of his charred body.
One such post can be seen below.
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the claim and the image is misleading. This is an old photo from a protest where an effigy of Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan was burned.
The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here .
We did a reverse search of the image and found that the original version (without filters) has been carried by multiple social media handles over the last several months.
The photo was also carried in a report by City 42 , a media outlet in Pakistan on July 9, 2020. In this version, it can be clearly seen that the woman is sitting in front of an effigy and not a body. According to the report, the woman seen in the image is Afshan Latif, a former superintendent of a government-run welfare center for destitute women, and she has been constantly making accusations on social media against top government officials, including Imran Khan. Taking a cue from this, we searched and found multiple reports by Pakistan's mainstream media outlets about Afshan Latif. According to these reports , Afshan Latif had alleged in 2019 that the welfare centre where she had been a superintendent was being used to supply underage orphan girls to powerful ministers. Over the years, she has been holding multiple protests and online campaigns against the ministers and government departments. We further found a Twitter handle under Afshan Latif's name which had multiple pictures and videos of protests by the same woman seen in the viral image. On July 8, 2020, the handle had also uploaded a video of Latif in the same attire as seen in the viral image. The burning effigy can also be seen in this video. The caption of the video in Urdu translates to: "Tying a rope around Imran Khan's neck, Afshan Latif is burning his effigy outside the Governor House after stomping on it and dragging it from the Lahore Assembly to Mall Road." A comparison between the viral image and a screenshot from the Twitter video can be seen here. #_____ pic.twitter.com/u3w47nK1x1 — Afshan Latif (@AfshanLatif3) July 8, 2020 advertisement A comparison between the viral image and a screenshot from the Twitter video can be seen here. Sri Lankan man mob lynched in Sialkot Priyantha Kumara, a Sri Lankan, was working as a manager at a local factory in Pakistan's Sialkot when on December 3, 2021, a mob tortured and burnt him to death for allegedly desecrating posters with the name of Prophet Muhammad, according to reports . Several people were arrested in the aftermath of the incident. The image of Priyantha Kumara's mother crying near his coffin after it was returned to Sri Lanka was carried by the Associated Press . i A similar claim was earlier fact-checked by AFP. It is hence clear that the viral photo in question is not related to the lynching of Priyantha Kumara but is from a protest where an effigy of Pak PM Imran Khan was set on fire. Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Jan 1, 2022 19:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Evolution of CRPF tactical gear over the decade? Not really
content:
The claim is misleading as the image shared as that of the CRPF jawan from 2011 was clicked in 2017, while the second image is of an elite commando of the paramilitary force.
It is the first day of the New Year and misleading posts have already flooded social media. Several viral tweets from January 1, 2022, claim that India's largest Central Armed Police Force - the CRPF - has undergone a gear upgrade in the last decade.
"CRPF jawan 2011 Vs CRPF Jawan 2022. Choose wisely India. Jai Hind," says the claim along with two images of what is said to be of CRPF personnel.
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. The image of a jawan has been shared as from 2011, while it was originally photographed in 2017. The second picture is of a member of CRPF's elite commando wing. AFWA probe
The first photo, claimed to be taken in 2011, shows a jawan donning khaki pants, an army-green vest and armed with an INSAS rifle.
A reverse search showed the photo was clicked by photographer Arbaz Mughal for Alamy News Live in Srinagar in 2017.
Hence, the first photo is not a decade old as the post wrongly claimed.
The second image shows another personnel in far-advanced military gear, including a night-vision-attached military helmet and a communication device. The word 'Commando' can be seen stitched on both sides of his grey uniform. A closer look showed the insignia on one of his sleeves that read "Valley QAT". Using this clue, we ran a keyword search to learn that the CRPF's elite anti-terrorism commando unit in Jammu & Kashmir is called the Valley Quick Action Team or ' Valley QAT '. They are highly trained and equipped to work in close quarters with the Indian Army and Jammu & Kashmir Police during counter-insurgency operations. A reverse image search of the commando's image - with 'Valley QAT' as a keyword - cleared our doubts. The same photo, along with a handful of similar images, was found on the website of stock photo firm Getty Images. This answered the question of why the equipment owned by the officer in the second image is far advanced than that of the jawan in the first. But has the CRPF altered their uniform post-2017 to grey? We checked the latest parade of the CRPF from December 23, 2021, on the YouTube channel of Doordarshan National. This confirmed that the khaki uniforms are still in place for CRPF personnel. Thus, it can be concluded that the two photos of CRPF jawans in the viral claim were not taken a decade apart or represent the upgrades the force has undergone over the years. Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Jan 2, 2022 00:01 IST

title: Fact Check: This is not Aryan Khan urinating in public at an airport
content:
This is a 2012 video that shows Twilight-fame actor Bronson Pelletier and not Aryan Khan. Pelletier was later arrested and sentenced for the act.
A video of a young man peeing in public at an airport is circulating on social media with the claim that he is Shah Rukh Khan's son Aryan. The 24-year-old was arrested by the Narcotics Control Bureau on October 3 last year in a drug-on-cruise case in Mumbai and granted bail more than three weeks later.
The video in circulation shows the youth, apparently disoriented, starting to pee in full public glare even as another man in red uniform tries to stop him. Onlookers can be heard gasping in disbelief.
One Twitter user shared this video with the caption, "ARYAN KHAN (S/O SHARUKH KHAN) FOUND 'HIGH' AT TORONTO AIRPORT".
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the man in the viral video is not Aryan Khan but Twilight-fame Canadian actor Bronson Pelletier. The video is from 2012 and Pelletier was then arrested for the act.
Reverse-searching key frames of the viral video, we found it was carried in a "Daily Mail" report dated February 23, 2013.
As per the report, the incident took place in December 2012 at the Los Angeles International Airport. Pelletier was reportedly found in a highly intoxicated state and was removed from a flight. He was given time to sober up in the terminal, and sometime later, was found urinating in public. He was later found guilty and sentenced to two years in probation.
Several other media outlets had also reported the incident .
We did not find any report of Aryan Khan peeing publicly at an airport. Clearly, an old and unrelated video is being circulated to target him. Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Jan 3, 2022 22:06 IST

title: Fact Check: 2018 image from Rajasthan shared as Brahmin protest against BJP in UP
content:
This image was taken in Rajasthan in 2018. Supporters of a local politician named Hansraj Patel were burning BJP flags after the party denied him a ticket for the state assembly elections at the time.
Ahead of the high-voltage elections in Uttar Pradesh, an image is circulating on social media with the claim that it shows Brahmins in UP's Deoria burning BJP flags and declaring not to vote for the party.
The archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim along with the image to be untrue. This is a 2018 image from Rajasthan which shows supporters of rebel BJP leader Hansraj Patel burning the party flag after he was denied a ticket in the state assembly elections.
Using keyword search, we found a similar claim posted on Twitter by Congress leader Acharya Pramod in July 2020. However, in response to the tweet, a user had posted a screenshot of an article from November 2018 by "Dainik Bhaskar" that carried the same image. 2018 , " " , 2 .... #_ pic.twitter.com/MJlszSBBcX — Jenish Patel (@sir_Jenishpatel) July 15, 2020
2018 , " " , 2 .... #_ pic.twitter.com/MJlszSBBcX — Jenish Patel (@sir_Jenishpatel) July 15, 2020
According to the "Dainik Bhaskar" report, the image is from Kotputli in Rajasthan and it shows supporters of local politician Hansraj Patel burning flags and an effigy of BJP after he was denied a seat in the state assembly elections.
BJP had declared Mukesh Goyal its candidate for Kotputli seat near Jaipur. Hansraj had also filed his nomination as an Independent candidate in protest.
The incident was also tweeted by "Zee Rajasthan". #RajasthanElectionOnZee : , , , @Ra_THORe , , @BJP4Rajasthan pic.twitter.com/XDjYL1jgVi — ZEE Rajasthan (@zeerajasthan_) November 19, 2018
#RajasthanElectionOnZee : , , , @Ra_THORe , , @BJP4Rajasthan pic.twitter.com/XDjYL1jgVi — ZEE Rajasthan (@zeerajasthan_) November 19, 2018
We also found videos of the protest carried by multiple local YouTube channels in November 2018.
A comparison between the image in question and a video from the 2018 protest in Kotputli can be seen below.
India Today's Kotputli correspondent Vikrant Sharma also confirmed to us that the protest was over party ticket, and the image in question was clicked in front of Hansraj's office on the Delhi-Jaipur NH48.
We also reached out to India Today's Deoria bureau in UP. Our correspondent confirmed that no such incident of Brahmins burning the BJP flag was reported in the district recently.
In 2019, the same image was circulated as from Bihar, and subsequently fact-checked .
Hence, it is clear that the image in question shows supporters of a rebel BJP leader in Rajasthan protesting in 2018 after the party denied him a ticket in the state assembly elections at the time. Published By: Namrata Agarwal Published On: Jan 5, 2022 21:43 IST

title: Fact Check: Crowd at Yogi's UP rally passed off as turnout at PM Modi's Punjab event
content:
This image is from a public meeting held by Yogi Adityanath in Deoband, Uttar Pradesh, on January 4.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public rally at Ferozepur in poll-bound Punjab on January 5 was cancelled after his convoy was halted on a flyover for around 20 minutes, as the road was blocked by protesters in the district's Hussainiwala area.
The incident has led to a blame game between the BJP and Congress, which is in power in Punjab. While the BJP blames the Punjab government for the security breach, the Congress claims low attendance at Modi's rally venue forced the PM to cancel the event.
In this context, an image showing packed crowds is circulating on social media with the claim that it shows the turnout at PM Modi's rally venue.
The archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim along with the image to be misleading. This image is from a rally held by Yogi Adityanath in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district recently.
Using reverse search, we found the image in question, along with a few others, posted by Adityanath on his official Twitter handle on January 4, 2021. According to the tweet, the image is from a rally held at Deoband in UP's Saharanpur district. ... ! ! pic.twitter.com/fND9FDEGF7 — Yogi Adityanath (@myogiadityanath) January 4, 2022
... ! ! pic.twitter.com/fND9FDEGF7 — Yogi Adityanath (@myogiadityanath) January 4, 2022
We also found multiple articles on the Deoband rally. According to news reports , on January 4, Adityanath laid the foundation stone of an Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) commando training centre and launched a number of development projects worth Rs 200 crore in Deoband. He'd also addressed a public meeting during the day. However, PM Modi was not part of the event.
A video from the event can be seen below.
On the other hand, on January 5, PM Modi's first public meeting in Punjab this election season had to be cancelled after his cavalcade got stuck due to protesters on a flyover, less than 10 km from the rally venue in Ferozepur.
After assessing safety issues, the PM's security agencies decided to return without visiting Ferozepur. Reports also said only a small number of people made it to the venue in the rainy weather.
Punjab BJP president Ashwani Sharma also alleged that several buses ferrying party supporters from different districts for the event were stopped by Punjab Police at various places.
However, it is clear that the image in circulation is from a public meeting held by Yogi Adityanath in UP's Deoband and not related to PM Modi's Ferozepur rally. Published By: Iram Ara Ibrahim Published On: Jan 6, 2022 22:36 IST

title: Fact Check: This pro-Khalistan rally is not linked to PM Modi's Punjab visit
content:
The video is old and not related to PM Modi's recent visit to Punjab.
The Union Home Ministry has formed a committee to enquire into the lapses in security arrangements during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to poll-bound Punjab on January 5.
The PM's Ferozepur rally was called off after he got stuck on a flyover for around 20 minutes because the road ahead was blocked by protesters.
In the backdrop of these events, a video of some Sikh bikers raising "Khalistan Zindabad" slogans has gone viral, with users hinting that this happened on the same day and around the same place where PM Modi's convoy was stopped.
A Twitter user shared the video with the caption, "Why Did The Congress Government Not Arrest Those Who Raised Slogans Of Khalistan Zindabad Yesterday? #PresidentRuleInPunjab".
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the viral video is not related to PM Modi's visit to Punjab. The video has been circulating on the Internet at least since December 27, 2021. AFWA probe
Commenting on the viral claim, one user said the video is from December 26, 2021, when a motorcycle rally was taken out in remembrance of "Chhote Sahibzade" (sons of Guru Gobind Singh) in Sirhind, Punjab.
Using this clue, we searched the Internet with Punjabi keywords and came across several Facebook posts from December 2021. As per the description given in these posts, the video is related to the " Kesari March " organised on the occasion of Shaheedi Jor Mela in Fatehgarh Sahib.
The Shaheedi Jor Mela is held every year from December 25-27 in memory of Guru Gobind Singh's sons Baba Zorawar Singh and Baba Fateh Singh who were bricked alive for refusing to accept Islam by then governor of Sirhind Nawab Wazir Khan.
Some YouTubers had also shared the video had also shared the video with the same description in December 2021.
The oldest post with the video that we could find is dated December 27, 2021.
We could not independently verify the video's location or date. However, it is certain that the video in circulation is not related to PM Modi's recent Punjab visit. Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Jan 7, 2022 00:05 IST

title: Fact Check: No, ministers didn't discuss removal of Sikhs from army, this is how doctored video was made
content:
This video is doctored. The actual video shows the Cabinet Committee on Security meeting that was held on December 8, 2021, after CDS General Bipin Rawat's death in a chopper crash. The audio was taken from a discussion that happened on Clubhouse social audio app.
A shocking video is doing the rounds on social media with the claim that the Indian government is planning to remove all Sikh soldiers currently serving in the Indian army.
In this blurry and shaky video of what looks like a meeting, some faces that are recognizable are of Home Minister Amit Shah, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval.
In the video, somebody can be heard saying, " Punjabi ko nikal do, so that I never have to fear kitne log army me jate hain. Nobody in the rest of India talks as much shit about how much they contribute to India as much as Punjabis. For the last two years, it has become sickening. Jaise Maratha regiment nahi hai, jaise South Indian soldiers nahin hain, and ek baar ye Punjabis nikal jayein na, to it will come to light to how effective it they actually were. And I will tell you, koi difference nahi hoga. Ek-ek ko nikal do. Sare general, sare soldiers, you know, top level se bottom tak, har ek Punjabi ko nikal do pure army defence infrastructure se. "
It is interesting to note that multiple Twitter handles with the names of girls have posted this video with similar captions .
For instance, one such handle wrote, "During Cabinet Committee Security Meeting Minister @ianuragthakur @DrSJaishankar Calls For Removal of #Sikhs From @adgpi #IndianArmy #IndiaStandsWithChanni v/s #BharatStandsWithModiJi"
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the visuals seen in the viral video are from a Cabinet Committee on Security meeting that was held on December 08, 2021, after the death of Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Bipin Rawat in a chopper crash in Tamil Nadu.
On the other hand, the audio heard in the video is from a discussion that happened on the social audio app Clubhouse.
It is noteworthy that this video has emerged after an alleged security breach happened during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent Punjab visit. Origin of the video
We found that this video shows the Cabinet Committee on Security meeting that was held after CDS General Bipin Rawat, his wife, and 11 others lost their lives in a chopper crash. This meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Home Minister Amit Shah, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, and NSA Ajit Doval were among the ones who attended the meeting. How we traced it
We found a comment by a Twitter user in which he specified that the video is related to a meeting that was held after the death of General Rawat.
Getting a clue from here, we found the actual video that was posted on the official YouTube channel of ANI on December 8, 2021. The same video was shared by other media outlets like The Tribune and The Times of India .
We compared the visuals of the viral video with this video and found many similarities between them. The colour and design of the clothes worn by the people in the video as well as the kind of interior are an exact match.
It is noteworthy that there is no audio in the original video, but just light background music. Clearly, the music in this video was removed and an unrelated audio was added to create confusion. Origin of the audio
The audio heard in the viral video has been taken from a discussion that happened on the Clubhouse app.
A screen recording of this discussion had gone viral on social media recently. The audio in this recording is much clearer than the one in the viral video. Even some cuss words that can be heard in the original video have been removed.
We also found that several people are claiming that OpIndia Editor-in-chief Nupur Sharma was also a part of this discussion.
Replying to such queries, Nupur said in one of her tweets that this viral clip is indeed from an old Clubhouse discussion. She also added that the suggestion to remove all Sikhs from defence was made by an anonymous handle.
PIB has also refuted the claim being made in this video. A tweet referring to a viral video claim that in a #Cabinet Committee meeting on Security, there was a call for the removal of Sikhs from the Indian Army. #PIBFactCheck The claim is #Fake No such discussion/meeting has taken place pic.twitter.com/ESec0ALjr3 — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) January 7, 2022
A tweet referring to a viral video claim that in a #Cabinet Committee meeting on Security, there was a call for the removal of Sikhs from the Indian Army. #PIBFactCheck The claim is #Fake No such discussion/meeting has taken place pic.twitter.com/ESec0ALjr3 — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) January 7, 2022
Evidently, a manipulated video is being shared to establish that the government is planning to remove Sikhs from the army. Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Jan 8, 2022 00:30 IST

title: Fact Check: These girls didn't thrash an eve-teaser inspired by Congress's 'Ladki hoon, lad sakti hoon' campaign
content:
This is a 2018 incident from Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh. It shows three students and a teacher beating a man with sticks after he harassed them in their college. The video has no connection with the Congress campaign in poll-bound UP.
Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra in November last year launched the 'Ladki hoon, lad sakti hoon' (I'm a girl, I can fight) campaign, focusing on women and women empowerment in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh.
Now, a video showing a group of girls beating a young man with sticks is being circulated on social media with the claim that it shows girls inspired by Priyanka Gandhi's 'Ladki hoon, lad sakti hoon' campaign. In the clip, the girls, who have their heads covered, are apparently thrashing a man who misbehaved with them.
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim along with the video to be misleading. While the video is indeed from Uttar Pradesh, it is over three years old. AFWA probe
With the help of keyword search, we found the same video carried by a Times of India report on December 10, 2018. The title of the video reads, "Watch: Girl students thrash eve-teaser inside school premises in UP's Baghpat."
On further search, we also found multiple media reports on the incident. According to these reports, the video is from Dharm Singh Saraswati Balika Inter College in Uttar Pradesh's Baghpat. As per the TOI report , three girls along with their teacher thrashed a man with sticks inside the campus after no action was taken by the school authorities against the man in spite of repeated complaints. The man who fled the spot was later arrested.
The same video in question was also carried by India Today and The Quint in their reports on this 2018 incident.
Congress had launched the party's 100-day action plan for the "Adhi Abadi", an outreach program for women voters in Uttar Pradesh in November 2021. As a part of this, a marathon event under 'Ladki hoon, lad sakti hoon' was also held in Lucknow on December 28.
However, it is evidently clear that the video in question is years old and cannot be connected to the recent Congress campaign. Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Jan 9, 2022 00:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Dulquer Salmaan's 'Salute' won't be screened at IFFR 2022
content:
'Salute' is not among the 10 Indian films to be screened at IFFR 2022.
Dulquer Salmaan's 'Salute' is one of the most awaited releases of the year for Malayalam movie lovers. The superstar's fans were further elated when some on social media claimed that the Rosshan Andrrews directorial will feature at the 51 st edition of the International Film Festival Rotterdam (IFFR 2022). "Salute receives Green Mat entry to the famous Rotterdam Film Festival," reads a Malayalam post on Facebook.
Many news websites also reported that 'Salute' is among the Indian movies to be screened at the prestigious film festival.
However, India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. While four Malayalam movies have found place in the 10-strong Indian list for the fest, 'Salute' is not among them. Also, there is no category called "Green Mat" at the IFFR. AFWA probe
Noted director Don Palathara, whose "Everything is Cinema" had premiered at the fest earlier, questioned reports of Salute's screening in IFFR through Facebook on January 7.
"Several local and national media have reported that Salute is selected for IFFR. They have copy-pasted a press release written by someone even without running a simple Google search," Don's post read.
"In an email exchange, IFFR had told the 'Salute' crew that they can consider the movie if sent. But in no manner did they confirm its inclusion in the fest. This email was used as the source of a press release based on which these reports were made. Media houses that have realised the truth have published clarifications," Palathara further said.
"I had spoken to Stefan Borsos, an IFFR official. He confirmed that 'Salute' has not made the cut. The list is now available on their website," he added.
Following this clue, we checked the IFFR website for the list of Indian movies to be screened. We found that 'Salute' was not among the 10 movies listed on the website under the filter "Produced in India".
Four Malayalam films Chavittu, The Harbour, Hawk's Muffin and Malik are named in the list, along with 'The Cloud Messenger', 'Urf', 'Duvidha', 'Crescent Night', 'Murmurs of the Jungle' and 'Madhu'. The details of these movies, along with the category they'll feature in, can be read on the IFFR website here .
Despite repeated efforts, Salute's director Rosshan Andrrews and PRO Manju Gopinath were unavailable for comment. This article will be updated once their response comes in.
But some news websites and social media posts have claimed that the movie is a "Green Mat entry" to the event.
To confirm if this could be a reason for the omission of 'Salute' from the list published, we reached out to Stefan Borsos, a programmer with IFFR. "There is no such category as Green Mat entry at the IFFR. I've never heard of it and don't understand what it's supposed to mean," he said.
Borsos also confirmed that 'Salute' has not made it to the final list of entries. "Salute" did not make it into the final selection of the 2022 edition of the festival, and hence, will not be screened," he added.
Prominent news websites such as "The Indian Express", "News 18 Malayalam", " The Cue " and " Cinestaan " have clarified that 'Salute' will not feature at the Rotterdam film festival.
Therefore, it can be concluded that the viral claim of Dulquer Salmaan's 'Salute' being selected for the International Film Festival Rotterdam 2022 is misleading. (Inputs from Bechu S in Thiruvananthapuram) Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Jan 11, 2022 01:00 IST

title: Fact Check: Netizens go down the wrong track over this 19th century steam locomotive
content:
The 19th century locomotive's name is "Texas". It was kept in Atlanta's Civil War Museum for years. In 2015, it was relocated to the Atlanta History Center where the above pictures were taken. It is not an archaeological finding.
A set of two images of an archaic steam engine locomotive has created a lot of buzz on the Internet for the past few days.
If some on social media are to be believed, there has been an "amazing" archaeological finding in Atlanta, United States, in recent times. Posting pictures of the classic locomotive, netizens claim, "They've uncovered the remains of a Civil War-era steam locomotive in pristine condition on the grounds of the Atlanta Cyclorama."
This post has already been shared over 39,000 times since it was posted in a Facebook group. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here .
However, India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. Though the steam engine does belong to the Civil War era, but it's not an archaeological finding.
Using reverse image search, we came across an article that carried one of the images in the set.
The report, published in December 2015, led us to a completely different story. It said that the Civil War-era locomotive's name is "Texas" and it was kept in Atlanta's Civil War Museum "Cyclorama Building" for years till it was relocated to Atlanta History Center in 2015.
For more information, we did some keyword search and came across a CNN article dated December 21, 2015. This report said that "Texas", the legendary Civil War-era locomotive, will be pulled by a truck and taken for restoration purposes.
A further keyword search led us to another report from which we came to know that in 2014, the mayor of Atlanta, Kasim Reed, announced that collections of the Civil War Museum will be relocated to Atlanta History Center in Buckhead.
We also found images of "Texas" after its renovation in another report published in April 2019. The locomotive is now kept in Atlanta History Center's exhibition area.
Therefore, we can conclude that the viral images are not of any archaeological finding, but were taken during the relocation of a Civil War-era locomotive in the United States.
(Inputs from Riddhish Dutta in Kolkata) Published By: Nayanika Sengupta Published On: Jan 11, 2022 22:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Thermocol recycling video shared as production of artificial sugar
content:
Conclusion - Experts have clarified that the video shows recycling of thermocol into synthetic resins for reuse. The plastic granules are then used for production of different plastic products such as chairs, tables, toys, decorative items, etc.
We have come across several news items and social media posts about eggs, rice and even milk being allegedly made from plastic. Many of these reports were later proven wrong.
And now, a video is circulating on the Internet with the claim that it shows artificial sugar being made from thermocol.
The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here , here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim along with the video to be misleading. The video actually shows recycling of thermocol.
With the help of keyword search, we found a similar video in a documentary uploaded on " Entrepreneur India TV ", the official YouTube channel of Institute for Industrial Development. IID is an incubator with the Government of India, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), and the department of start-ups, an initiative of the Uttar Pradesh government.
Similar to the viral video, in this documentary uploaded by IID in October 2020, we can see thermocol being converted into plastic granules. However, as per the documentary, the video shows recycling of thermocol waste that is hazardous to the environment. The video also explains the process and business of recycling thermocol into plastic granules.
We then shared the video in question with IID. Rubbishing the viral claim, a representative of the institution confirmed to AFWA that the video shows recycling of thermocol into plastic granules for reuse.
Plastic granules are used for manufacturing chairs, tables, toys, decorative items and other plastic products.
We also reached out to an expert from the field of polystyrene waste recycling, Dr Chandra Shekhar Sharma, Associate Professor at the Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Hyderabad.
Commenting on the viral video, Dr Sharma said, "This is thermocol being recycled into resins. Thermocol is first melted as slime and then subjected to wet spinning, followed by crushing to make resins."
We also found multiple other videos where thermocol can be seen recycled into resins.
Moreover, we could not find any credible report published recently about artificial sugar made from thermocol being caught anywhere in India.
Even in 2017, similar videos of plastic recycling were circulating on social media as of artificial sugar production.
According to a report by " The Hindu Business Line ", in 2017, the then minister of state for consumer affairs had told the Lok Sabha in a written reply that the government was aware of reports of rice and sugar being made of plastic. He, however, had said that no specific case of the presence of plastic rice and sugar had been detected in the country.
Hence, we can conclude that though food adulteration is not uncommon, the viral video actually shows recycling of thermocol and not production of artificial sugar. Published By: Abhro Banerjee Published On: Jan 12, 2022 21:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Woman gunned down by Taliban along with child for driving a car? This is not what happened
content:
The woman, her husband and their two daughters were shot dead by unidentified bikers in Sheikhupura district of Pakistan's Punjab province. The husband was driving the car when the incident took place in November 2021.
A disturbing video of a man, woman and two children lying dead inside a car is circulating on social media with the claim that they were shot dead by the Taliban just because the woman was driving the vehicle. Sharing the video, many even took a dig at Muslims for "feeling scared" in India.
The caption in Hindi along with the video translates to, "The Taliban shot dead a woman and her little child just because she was driving a car. And here in India, Muslims are feeling unsafe. Jihadis rioting and spreading terror in India should see that those who shot these innocents are your Muslim brothers only."
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the incident is not linked to the Taliban. Though the Islamist militia strongly opposes women rights, this particular incident took place in November 2021 when unidentified motorcyclists gunned down a couple and their two children in Sheikhupura district of Pakistan's Punjab province. AFWA probe
At the seventh second in the video, one can see the license plate of the car in which the bodies are lying. The number plate says "LEH 15 6840". The word "Punjab" can also be seen below the number plate.
Using keyword search, we found that similar number plates are being sold on Pakistani e-commerce websites . This gave us a clue that the incident might have taken place in Punjab, Pakistan. Next, we searched for the license number "LEH 15 6840" on Facebook. It is noteworthy that the Facebook optical character recognition (OCR) system can recognise characters and numbers written on an image.
Next, we searched for the license number "LEH 15 6840" on Facebook. It is noteworthy that the Facebook optical character recognition (OCR) system can recognise characters and numbers written on an image.
This led us to several Urdu posts , mostly from November 2021, with images identical to the viral video. The same car is also visible in these pictures. As per the description on these posts , a couple and their two daughters hailing from Lahore were shot dead at Maralpur village near Ferozwala in Sheikhupura district of Punjab, Pakistan.
Visuals from the viral footage were also used by Pakistani media outlets GNN and Dawn News .
The " Express Tribune " had published a detailed report on the incident. As per the report, Shahnawaz, a resident of Batapur in Lahore, his wife Zainab Awan, and their two daughters were attacked by armed men when they were traveling in a car on November 24, 2021. All four died on the spot and the attackers escaped.
According to the eyewitnesses, the man was found dead on the driving seat, with the woman in the passenger seat beside him. The two kids were in the back seat. This also contradicts the viral claim that the woman was driving the vehicle.
We also contacted Sheikhupura-based journalist Syed Ali Abbas Gilani who'd shared a Facebook post on the incident. He confirmed to us that the video is indeed from Sheikhupura and the claim that the woman was killed by the Taliban for driving a car is untrue. "Initial police investigation suggests that the victims might have been murdered over an enmity," Gilani said. Women under Taliban
The Taliban has imposed severe restrictions on women since it came to power in Afghanistan. In the latest curb, it has announced a ban on long-distance road trips for women travelling solo. According to the new rule, a male relative should accompany women for any distance beyond 45 miles.
The new rules also call on drivers not to allow women without veils to sit in their cars. Further, women and girls' presence in public life has become precarious across the country. Many are not being allowed to return to schools, and those who have resumed university classes are separated by a curtain from their male peers.
Restrictive rules such as stay-at-home orders continue. Most women still can't return to work, having been barred from an array of jobs, including in the government and entertainment sectors. Women have been barred from appearing in television dramas, soap operas and entertainment shows. Women news presenters must wear headscarves on screen.
The Taliban also abolished the ministry of women's affairs and rolled back a key law to protect women from abuses, according to reports.

title: Fact Check: Misleading claims on moon mission orbit around astronaut Rakesh Sharma on his birthday
content:
No astronaut from India has landed on the moon till now. Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian to travel to space. In 1984, Sharma, along with Russian cosmonauts, spent a week in space laboratory Salyut-7.
Social media was full of wishes for Rakesh Sharma, the first Indian to travel to space, as he turned 73 on January 13. Many even called him the first Indian astronaut to walk on the moon.
One such tweet in Hindi translates to, "Tribute to Rakesh Sharma, the first Indian astronaut to step on the moon, on his birthday."
However, the post is misleading as no astronaut from India has landed on the moon till now. Sharma though was the first Indian to travel to space. In 1984, he, along with two Russian cosmonauts, spent a week in space laboratory Salyut-7. India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) digs deeper. From the horse's mouth
AFWA spoke to the first Indian astronaut on his birthday over phone. "I have never been to the moon. But social media for years has been saying that I've been to the moon. I never visit social media, so I've never felt the need to correct these things," Sharma told us about the viral claim.
On April 3, 1984, Sharma flew on board Soyuz T-11 with two Soviet cosmonauts, Commander Yury Malyshev and flight engineer Gennady Strekalov, to the space station Salyut-7.
During the mission, he carried out several experiments in zero gravity. "I had orbited the Earth and our scientists had carried out several experiments using our equipment. In that sense, it was an opportunity well utilised," Sharma added.
The mission lasted eight days, and Sharma and his crewmates landed in Kazakhstan on April 11.
This historic mission was covered by the international media as it had a lot of geo-political significance and had taken Indo-Russia friendship even to space. Mission To Moon
Twenty-four American astronauts made the trip from Earth to the moon between 1968 and 1972. Russians have also made several unmanned missions and soft landings on the moon.
In comparison, India's mission to moon is still in an early stage. As per reports, Isro will launch the ambitious Chandrayaan-3 mission in the third quarter of 2022. The project has suffered delay due to the pandemic.
But India's manned mission to the moon is still a distant dream. "You got to first cut your teeth in making humans survive in the near-Earth orbit. We have not yet reached there. So we'll have to wait till we have enough expertise," says Rakesh Sharma.
"See, the moon has been done to death already. So now when you are going to the moon, you are not going for a visit, but to settle there. So that is a different ball game altogether," Sharma signed off. Published By: Abhro Banerjee Published On: Jan 13, 2022 22:45 IST

title: Fact Check: The Nuremberg Code does not say mandated use of masks is a war crime
content:
The excerpts used in the photo are not from the Nuremberg Code. There is no mention of masks in the entire document.
The Nuremberg Code is again part of social media discussions surrounding the coronavirus pandemic. According to a widely shared claim, imposing mandatory use of masks is considered a war crime under the Nuremberg Code.
"Elected officials/"leaders"/media/ educators/clergy...get the idea? When the public comes to understand the magnitude of vileness," says a claim with the viral photo .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. The word "mask" is not mentioned in the Nuremberg Code. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story AFWA probe Considered among the prominent documents in the history of medical ethics, the Nuremberg Code was formulated following the trial of Nazi doctors post World War II. The 10-point document talks about permissible medical experiments that can be conducted on human subjects.
Considered among the prominent documents in the history of medical ethics, the Nuremberg Code was formulated following the trial of Nazi doctors post World War II. The 10-point document talks about permissible medical experiments that can be conducted on human subjects.
The Nuremberg Code is available online on several websites. The document is divided into 10 points but there are no sections or articles as such. The word "mask" doesn't appear in it even once. Neither of the two paragraphs in the viral post is from the Code, we confirmed. It can be read here .
A Google search showed that the first paragraph seen in the post is taken from UNESCO's "Report of the International Committee of Bioethics Committee on Consent". The line is a part of Article 6 of the document that talks about consent. The UNESCO document can be read here . While there is no mention of ''mask'' or ''war crime'' in the UNESCO report, the succeeding paragraph in the post is not taken from it. "The Nuremberg Code has absolutely nothing to say about mask mandates. It does not apply to public health measures that the government may take to protect its citizens," AFP reported Professor Leslie E Wolf of the Georgia State College of Law as saying. This report can be read here . Pushpesh Pant, a retired teacher of International Relations said the Nuremberg Trials is often criticised as a trial by the victors over the vanquished. Many scholars hence argue it can't be considered as a universal law. "How do we know that the Nazis were the only ones carrying out experiments on human beings? How do we know the allies never did the same? So much water has down the rivers since the world wars and the Nuremberg Trials. One can't use napalm bombs agent, nerve gas etc and claim it is not a crime against humanity. Then it becomes a mockery," he added. This is not the first time the Nuremberg Code is being used to propagate fake news about Covid protocol and vaccination. News organisations have fact-checked claims involving the historic document in the past as well. Some of them can be read here and here . advertisement Hence, it is clear that the image in question is not an excerpt from the historic Nuremberg Code. title: Fact Check: British man finding ancient Roman treasure in his first try is old news
content:
The incident happened nearly 12 years ago and the viral post is copied from a news report dated September 9, 2009.
The story of a British man finding a rare haul of 10,000 Roman coins that are believed to have been underground for 1,700 years is viral on social media. Shared elaborately, the post says amateur Nick Davies made the discovery at a farmer's field near Shrewsbury in England's Shropshire.
"The haul could be put on display at Shrewsbury's new £10million heritage center, it was revealed today," claims the post .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. Nick Davies' discovery, which is now known as the famous Shrewsbury Hoard, was discovered over a decade ago in 2009. AFWA Probe
The image used along with the post shows a smiling man (Nick was then 30) alongside a broken pot and a large number of coins. A reverse search showed the image has been in circulation for several years. This proved that the photo is not from a recent development as claimed in the post.
Among the results were a DailyMail report published on September 9, 2009, that carried the same photo with the caption, "Strike it lucky: Nick Davies found this amazing haul of 10,000 Roman coins on his first-ever treasure hunt."
This is the first sentence of the viral post as well.
We also identified that the rest of the post has also been copied from the same news report.
Using a keyword search, we also found more reports about the incident which confirmed that Nick's wonder digging is from 2009 .
This proved that though the information mentioned is correct, the viral post is based on an incident that happened over 12 years ago.
According to a report published by BBC in October 2011, the Treasure Valuation Committee was to decide how the value of the hoard should be split between the owner of the land and Nick. This story can be read here .
A further search on Facebook showed that the story of Nick Davies's excavation is often shared as a recent story among groups and pages of history and archaeological enthusiasts.
However, it is clear beyond doubt that the incident in which the British man discovered a rare haul of 10,000 Roman coins originally happened over a decade ago in 2009. Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Jan 14, 2022 22:05 IST

title: Fact Check: Old, unrelated photos shared as from recent Naxal attack in Chhattisgarh
content:
While it is true that three jawans were injured in an IED blast in Chhattisgarh on January 14, none of these images are from the incident. These images are from different Naxal attacks that took place in India between 2013 and 2021.
Several pictures are being circulated on social media with the claim that they are from the blast site of an IED attack triggered by Naxalites in Chhattisgarh on Friday that injured three Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) jawans.
The post, that surfaced a day after the attack, claims that the images are from the blast site near Kosronda camp.
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that none of the images shared along with the post are recent. These are images from different Naxal attacks that took place in the country over the years. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Viral Image 1 The first two images show security personnel carrying an injured jawan and a damaged vehicle. These photos are from an IED explosion that took place in Chhattisgarh's Bijapur in November 2018. According to a report by The Indian Express , this suspected Maoist attack took place amid Assembly elections in the state, and it had injured six - including four BSF personnel. Viral Image 3 and 4 These two images showing two jawans in a hospital and a wheelchair were carried by multiple media reports in January 2021. According to news agency ANI, the images are from a Naxal attack on Chhattisgarh Armed Force (CAF) jawans. The two injured jawans were reportedly stable. 2 Chhattisgarh Armed Force (CAF) jawans of 16 battalion injured in IED blast triggered by naxals, 4 km from the Orchha police station in Narayanpur district. Both jawans are stable & have been brought to Raipur for better treatment: Commandant 16th battalion, CAF, Sadanand Kumar pic.twitter.com/7HG06GgVAZ — ANI (@ANI) January 12, 2021 Viral image 5 This image showing security forces near a damaged vehicle is over a decade old. According to the Associated Press , the photo is from a Maoist attack that took place in Odisha's Koraput on August 27, 2013. At least five people died and two others were injured in the incident. Viral Image 6 We found this image, purportedly of a blast, carried by multiple websites as from a scene from the 1981 Star Wars film, The Return of the Jedi . We then checked for the movie on the OTT platform Disney+Hotstar. Around 13 minutes into this movie , we can see a shot that exactly resembles the viral image. The same shot from the movie was also uploaded by a user on YouTube. Viral Image 7 The seventh viral image is from an encounter operation by the CRPF's COBRA Battalion 208 in 2016. This image was carried by The Indian Express on March 7, 2016. As per this report, three CRPF jawans died and 13 were injured in the chase behind top Maoist leaders in Chhattisgarh. Viral Image 8 The second last image is from a Maoist guerilla ambush against a police party in Chhattisgarh's Dantewada in May 2018. As per reports, the incident killed seven jawans who were providing security cover to a road construction project. As per a report by the Business Standard , the incident took place ahead of then Union home minister Rajnath Singh's visit. advertisement The same image was tweeted by ANI on May 20, 2018. Chhattisgarh: 3 jawans of Chhattisgarh Armed Force & 2 jawans of District Force killed and 2 jawans injured in an IED blast on a police vehicle in Dantewada's Cholnar Village. Troops of CRPF rushed to the spot, More details awaited. pic.twitter.com/J6a0JMpknn — ANI (@ANI) May 20, 2018 Viral Image 9 The last image with a Times of India logo is also from a Maoist attack in Chhattisgarh's Kanker that took place ahead of the first phase of Assembly elections in the state in November 2018. A BSF jawan was killed by Maoists in the incident. January 14 IED blast in Chhattisgarh According to an ANI report , three Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel were injured in a blast triggered by Naxals near the Kosronda camp in Chhattisgarh on Friday, January 14. There was brief firing for around 10 minutes after the blast. The SSB jawans were out for railway line protection duty and were patrolling the forest area when the blast occurred. It is, however, clear that all images in the post are old and not related to the January 14 blast in Chhattisgarh. Published By: Namrata Agarwal Published On: Jan 16, 2022 12:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Do not gulp down this morphed image of Kejriwal and Bhagwant Mann in front of liquor shops
content:
The viral image is morphed. In the original picture, Kejriwal and Mann are seen sitting on a cot amid mustard fields. This was during their interaction with farmers in Punjab's Chamkaur Sahib a few days back.
Arvind Kejriwal has announced that the AAP's chief ministerial candidate for Punjab will be announced on Tuesday, January 18. Party MP Bhagwant Mann is considered one of the front-runners for the post, and according to reports , even Kejriwal wanted to declare him the party's face initially. However, the AAP later decided that people of Punjab should suggest names and they also launched a mobile number for the purpose.
Mann faced a lot of flak due to his notorious drinking habit, and several videos of the MP in an inebriated state had emerged earlier. While in Delhi, the BJP has been up in arms against the Kejriwal government's new liquor policy. And now, amid hectic campaigning for the Punjab assembly elections, a picture of Mann and Kejriwal sitting in front of liquor shops is circulating on social media.
Many, including BJP leaders Naveen Kumar Jindal and Impreet Singh Bakshi , have posted the picture from their official Twitter handles. The caption in Hindi translates to, "Both are sitting at exactly their favourite spots."
Other such posts can be seen here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the viral image is morphed. In the original picture, Kejriwal and Mann are seen sitting on a cot amid mustard fields. This was during their interaction with farmers in Punjab's Chamkaur Sahib a few days back.
Using simple reverse search, we found the original pictures used to create the morphed image.
The AAP Punjab unit had released a short video of Kejriwal and Mann on their social media platforms on January 14, showing the duo sitting on a cot amid mustard fields and interacting with farmers.
AAP Punjab's Twitter handle posted the video with a caption in Punjabi that translates to, "Meeting with farmers at Chamkaur Sahib @ArvindKejriwal and @BhagwantMann. CM stopped his vehicle on the way in Channi's (Punjab CM Charanjit Singh Channi) constituency and interacted with farmers."
In this video, we can see the exact moment captured in the viral image, with the background of mustard fields changed to liquor shops.
The original image of Kejriwal and Mann sitting in the mustard fields of Chamkaur Sahib was also published in " The Tribune " on January 14. The caption says, "A video grab of Bhagwant Mann and Arvind Kejriwal interacting with farmers in Punjab."
We also found the image of the liquor shops superimposed on the viral picture in an article published in " Navbharat Times " in November 2020.
Hence, it is proved that amid the hullabaloo of Punjab elections, a morphed image of Arvind Kejriwal and Bhagwant Mann has gone viral on social media with misleading claims. Published By: Nayanika Sengupta Published On: Jan 17, 2022 17:01 IST

title: Fact Check: 2010 image from Germany passed off as construction of LPG pipeline in Gorakhpur
content:
Though such a project is in the works, the image used was taken in Germany in April 2010. This pipeline was constructed for supplying natural gas from Russia to Western Europe.
As elections in Uttar Pradesh draw closer, the precarious Covid-19 situation has ensured that political parties and their supporters rely on digital campaigns more than ever.
And since the BJP announced Yogi Adityanath as its candidate from Gorakhpur (Urban), a section of social media users are sharing a postcard with an image of an under-construction project. In the viral image, a huge pipe can be seen being laid underground with the help of cranes.
The postcard reads, "World's longest LPG pipeline coming up in UP's Gorakhpur, to be commissioned by 2023. The Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline is being built at a cost of Rs 10,000 crore. The 2,757-km long pipeline will supply gas to 34 crore households. A game-changing project that will usher in LPG revolution in India!"
The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim along with the image to be misleading. Though such a project in UP is in the works, the picture used on the viral postcard was originally taken 12 years ago in Germany.
Using keyword search, we came across an article from March last year that had used the same image to report on the LPG pipeline work in UP.
We then ran a reverse search on this higher resolution image and found a report published by " The New York Times " on April 8, 2010. Here, the caption along with the picture says, "Cranes lower a section of pipe into the ground near Lubmin, Germany. Sean Gallup/Getty Images".
For further confirmation, we visited the official " Getty Images " website and found the original photograph which was taken by Sean Gallup in Germany.
The Getty Images caption said, "A worker shouts commands as cranes lower a section of pipe into the ground for the OPAL pipeline on April 8, 2010 near Lubmin, Germany. The OPAL and NEL pipelines will carry natural gas from Russia arriving through the Nord Stream pipeline from the Baltic Sea across Germany and to other countries in Europe. The Nord Stream project delivers Russian natural gas directly to western Europe and avoids countries in between, such as Poland and Ukraine."
A report by " The Times of India " dated February 22, 2019, gave details of the Rs 9,000-crore Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline project.
Then petroleum minister Dharmendra Pradhan had said the 1,987-km long pipeline will cater to cooking fuel needs of a fourth of India's population. The pipeline, traversing from the Gujarat coast to UP via Madhya Pradesh will "possibly be the longest in the world", the minister had said.
Therefore, we can conclude that the viral image is not of the Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline project but was taken in Germany in April 2010.
