title: Fact Check: No, this photo is not from 'inaugural' Air India flight after Tata takeover
content:
This is an old photo of Air India Captain Jehan Dastoor taken in 2017 onboard a flight. Officially there is no "first Air India flight" after Tata takeover. Ratan Tata was not onboard any Air India flight recently.
A photo of industrialist Ratan Tata, chairman emeritus of Tata Sons, has gone viral. In the photo, he is seen standing next to a man in uniform, onboard an aircraft.
Several Facebook and Twitter users shared this photo with the claim, "This is the pilot flying the first Tata Air India flight. His name is Jehan Dastur. 29th January 2022."
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. This is an old photo, taken in 2017.
Archived versions of the posts can be seen here and here .
Who's the man standing with Ratan Tata?
While investigating the photograph three questions arose. First, who is the person in this photo standing with Ratan Tata? Second, when was this photo taken? And third, was Ratan Tata present onboard the first AI flight that took off after Tata Group took over Air India?
We first reverse-searched this image. But it did not yield any useful results. Following that, we visited the website of Federation of Indian Pilots a registered body of Indian pilots.
We searched the Members' List on the website, first with the keyword "Dastur", and then with "Dastoor". While conducting the search with the keyword "Dastoor" we found listed Capt. Jehan Dastoor. The website states that this captain works with NACIL - A or Air India. The photo of Captain Jehan Dastoor in this website appears similar to the man in the viral photo. It can be reasonably inferred that Captain Dastoor was indeed the person standing with Ratan Tata in the viral photograph. When was this photo taken? Now, the website states that Dastoor is a captain of Air India. But the uniform he is seen wearing in the viral photo is that of a co-pilot not of a pilot. As per aviation rules , a first officer wears epaulets on his shoulders that have three stripes; a captain, on the other hand, wears epaulets with four stripes. This indicates that the photo in question is an old one, likely from a time when Dastoor was a first officer or co-pilot. To set the record straight, we got in touch with the pilot himself and he confirmed that it is indeed an old photo. "I think, after the Tata takeover, the first AI flight had taken off from Mumbai for Newark on January 28. Although I was a part of the crew member in that flight, this viral photo is an old one. It was taken in 2017 when Mr. Tata was travelling onboard one of our flights. At that time, I was still a first officer or co-pilot," Dastoor told India Today. advertisement Despite several requests, however, Dastoor did not share the original photo with us. "With all due respect, I have locked my Facebook account after this photo has gone viral with misleading claims. It is for my personal collection. But the fact remains that it is an old photo and has nothing to do with the January 28 flight," Dastoor stated. Was Ratan Tata travelling on the first flight? On January 27, Air India was officially handed back to Tata Group. As per news reports , the Tata Group plans to enhance onboard services in a phased manner starting with Mumbai-Newark and Mumbai-Delhi flights, where special meals were reportedly served on Friday, January 28. Going by this statement, the Mumbai-Newark flight appears to be the first Air India flight after the Tata Group took over the airline, which took off in the wee hours of January 28. However, Ratan Tata was not present in that flight. Nor, he was at the Mumbai airport during take-off. A captain on board this flight confirmed to India Today, "The flight took off at 1.14 am on January 28 and there were three pilots Darryl Paris, Gagan Dutt and Jehan Dastoor on board, along with co-pilot Sonam Yadav. Rata Tata was not present at the airport or onboard." advertisement To further confirm the claim, we got in touch with Sameek Bhattacharya, an Air India spokesperson. "We have not officially demarcated any flight as the first flight that took off after Tata Group took over Air India. Second, Ratan Tata was not onboard any Air India flight in the recent past. So, in all probability, the claim of this viral photo might be fake," Bhattacharya told India Today. Hence, we can conclude that the claim with this viral photo is misleading. This is an old photo of an Air India pilot with Ratan Tata that was taken in 2017. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Arshi Aggarwal Published On: Feb 2, 2022 23:32 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi did not say demonetisation was beneficial; viral video edited
content:
Rahul Gandhi misspoke during his speech at a Congress rally in Jaipur on January 28, 2020. He, however, corrected himself immediately. The correction has been edited out in the viral videos.
Former Congress President Rahul Gandhi has remained critical of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's demonetisation drive since its announcement on November 8, 2016. Recently, however, a few netizens claimed that the opposition leader praised the move as well.
A video has gone viral on social media that claims that the Congress leader lauded demonetisation in a rally. In that video, Rahul can be seen saying in Hindi, "Jo vyekti note bandi jaisa kaam kar sakta hai Aap kisi bhi yuva se puch lo, note bandi se fayda hua ya nuksan. Aath saal ke bacche ko puch lo, beta note bandi se fayda hua ya nuksan, wo kahega fayda hua."
This roughly translates to, "A person who can do something like demonetisation You can ask any youth if the note ban was useful. Ask an eight-year-old if the note ban did good or not, and they will say that it was beneficial."
While sharing this clip , a Facebook user claimed that Rahul Gandhi now declared that the demonetisation drive was beneficial. Another user claimed , "Here is our star campaigner. See how he works faithfully for our party."
The archived version of similar claims can be found here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found these claims to be misleading. The viral video has been edited. At the rally in question, Rahul Gandhi experienced a slip of the tongue while speaking, following which, he immediately corrected himself. That part has been edited out.
The word "Yuva Akrosh" is visible on the stage where Rahul Gandhi was speaking. With the help of this keyword, we searched and came across a video from which the viral clip was snipped out.
The official YouTube channel of the Indian National Congress shared this video on January 28, 2020. This rally, per the video's title, took place in Jaipur, Rajasthan. At the 34:21 mark, that part appears from which the viral clip has been clipped.
Here, Gandhi can be heard saying exactly what was seen in the viral clip. However, when referring to the eight-year-old, he says, "Aath saal ke bacche ko puch lo, beta note bandi se fayda hua ya nuksan, wo kahega fayda hua. [Correcting himself] Nuksan hua. Fayda kaha hua; nuksan hua." This translates to, "It caused losses. Where was the gain? It led to losses."
This faux pas made the news as well. We found a Patrika report that states Gandhi made such mistakes twice during the Jaipur rally, and that he corrected himself within moments.
Therefore, it can be concluded that the viral video claiming that Rahul Gandhi praised demonetisation is misleading, and not true.
(With Inputs from Riddhish Dutta in Kolkata) Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Feb 3, 2022 16:53 IST

title: Fact Check: 15-year-old video of Mayawati on 'Fundamentalist' Muslims shared out of context ahead of UP polls
content:
This clip has been edited and presented out of context from a longer press statement given by Mayawati in November 2006. The BSP leader was talking about the 2006 municipal elections in Meerut.
Days ahead of the first phase of the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, a video featuring Mayawati has been making the rounds on social media. The video was shared with the claim that the Bahujan Samaj Party supremo has asked people to vote for the Bharatiya Janata Party, instead of "radical" Muslim groups. The video was circulated with hashtags including #UPElections2022.
In this 30-second video , Mayawati can be heard saying, "The Muslim community prefers fanatics. To stop the fundamentalist Muslim's wife from winning the elections, I asked them to transfer their votes to the BJP. In Meerut, scheduled caste people the Muslims didn't; their votes went to the fundamentalists but upon my insistence, the scheduled caste, the backward caste, and the upper caste voters associated with us, they transferred their votes to the BJP. So that the fundamentalists don't win the elections."
The archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the video in question is more than a decade old. Mayawati was speaking in the context of the 2006 Meerut municipal corporation elections.
With the help of a keyword search, we found the longer version of the same video in an ABP news report. According to this television news report shared by an unrelated YouTube account, the video was ten years old when it became viral again. The video's title claims the comments were made by Mayawati on November 10, 2006.
In this longer version of the video, Mayawati can be heard saying, "You know that previously, the mayor of Meerut was for our party. So, why didn't we win this time? That's because that seat turned into a Hindu-Muslim tussle. And you know that people of the Muslim community prefer fanatics. The candidate of our party was also Muslim. But the one who left our party, the sitting MLA, made his wife contest the elections. You are well aware of his radical statements that led to Muslims joining him. His wife could have won the election. The candidate of our party was not a fundamentalist. To stop the fundamentalist Muslim's wife from winning the elections, I asked them [voters] to transfer their votes to the BJP."
A few months ahead of the 2007 assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, local body elections were held in the state between October and November 2006. While all major parties participated in the elections, the BSP stayed away. Reportedly, however, despite staying away from the municipal elections, the presence of the BSP was felt everywhere. A December 2006 Economic & Political Weekly report noted that the polls were "BSP-centric since BSP controlled the agenda."
Instead of participating in the civic polls, the BSP had asked its vote-bank to vote for the party best placed to defeat the Samajwadi Party in the election, be it the Congress or the BJP.
We also found that in November 2006, multiple media outlets reported on the aforementioned press meeting held by Mayawati.
According to a November 2006 report in the Hindustan Times , on November 10, 2006, Mayawati had held a press meet where she talked about the BSP's tactical support to the BJP and the Congress in the local body elections that had recently concluded. During this meeting, she spoke about how the BSP foiled the plans of "fundamentalist'" Haji Yaqoob Qureshi in Meerut.
She said, in Meerut, the contest was between the BJP candidate Madhu and UDF candidate Sanjida, wife of then-Minister of State for Minority Welfare Haji Yaqub Qureshi, who was previously a part of the BSP. Mayawati claimed that "Haji had deserted the BSP and was following a fundamentalist agenda."
Following these remarks made to the press, supporters of Qureshi burnt Mayawati's effigies and staged protests across Uttar Pradesh. Responding to the backlash, Mayawati addressed the press again and claimed reports had failed to understand her words. "Some channels have shown that I have called the Muslims fundamentalists. Such a twist to my statement is wrong," she had said at the time.
Per the Hindustan Times, Mayawati said at the time: "Along with Islam, all religions have highlighted the spirit of brotherhood and harmony. No religion permits people to sow the seed of discord in society. Everyone knows that Haji Yaqub Qureshi had always tried to cash in on hate. Even Muslim scholars have opposed the misdemeanour of the Haji. It was to ensure the defeat of the fundamentalist ideology that I got the vote of my party transferred to the party that was in a position to defeat Haji's wife."
She added, "Muslims are part of the Bahujan Samaj and I have never called Muslims fundamentalists."
It is thus clear that the video in question has been edited from a longer video of a press meet held by Mayawati almost 15 years ago in the context of the 2006 municipal elections in Uttar Pradesh.
(With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi) Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Feb 3, 2022 17:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Predecessor al-Baghdadi's photo shared as dead IS chief Abu Ibrahim al-Qurayshi
content:
The man in the picture is Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi -- the former chief of the Islamic State who was neutralised in 2019. It was after Baghdadi's fall that al-Qurayshi became the numero uno of the Islamic State.
On January 20, militants of the Islamic State attacked Ghwaryan prison, which reportedly housed more than 3,000 of their comrades. The attack triggered a retaliation. The international coalition-supported Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) took 11 days to complete their counter-operation and regain control. The operation reportedly claimed the lives of 121 SDF personnel and four civilians along with that of 374 IS fighters.
Abu Ibrahim al-Hashimi al-Qurayshi was killed during a raid by US forces on a house in northern Syria on Wednesday, February 2. Reportedly, al-Qurayshi, who was named the leader of ISIL shortly after his predecessor Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi's death in 2019, blew himself up during the raid, killing members of his own family.
Following the announcement of his death, Twitter was abuzz with information on the Islamic State leader. Several people shared images of the raided building along with alleged images of al-Qurayshi. Among these is a close-up photo of a bearded middle-aged man donning a jacket and headscarf.
"Islamic State leader Abu Ibrahim al-Qurayshi killed in Syria -- US", one such tweet read .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the image to be misleading. The man in the picture is in fact al-Baghdadi -- al-Qurayshi's predecessor.
Also called Abdullah Qardash and Amir Mohammed Said Abdul Rahman al-Mawla, al-Qurayshi was with his family on the second floor of a three-storey residential building in Atmeh, Syria when the US forces struck. As per reports, US officials said the military chose to conduct a raid with troops instead of bombing the compound to minimise harm to the family that lived on the first floor. However, the Islamic State leader blew himself up, along with his family as the US troops zeroed in on his location.
The US had offered a $10 million reward for any information about 46-year-old al-Qurayshi, reports state . We noticed that the image on the bounty poster looked different from that of the image shared by many after his death. Many reliable media outlets also used the same image of a bald, clean-shaved man while reporting the elimination of the militant chief.
Following this clue, we ran a reverse search on the image in question. The results were all related to the Islamist outfit but most dated back to 2019. Among the top results was a CNBC report published on October 27, 2019, about the then-US President Donald Trump confirming the death of the Islamic State chief Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi. We found the photo of Baghdadi inside the story that looked similar to the image shared now as al-Qurayshi.
Further searches revealed the same photo was used by multiple media organisations for al-Baghdadi. Days after his death, al-Qurayshi was declared the new premiere of the "Caliphate".
Most of these articles credited agencies like AFP and Getty Images as sources. We searched al-Baghdadi's name on these websites and found the same photo. "In this undated handout image provided by the Department of Defence, ISIS leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi is seen in an unspecified location," a part of the photo's caption on Getty Images reads. The photo was dated 'Unspecified".
AFP was more informative. "The elusive chief of the IS group al-Baghdadi has appeared for the first time in five years in a propaganda video released on April 29 by the jihadist organisation. It is unclear when the footage was filmed, but Baghdadi referred in the past tense to the months-long fight for Baghouz, IS's final bastion in eastern Syria, which ended last month," the caption read.
Interestingly, Baghdadi, 48 at the time of his demise, also killed himself by means of an explosive vest like his successor to avoid capture by US Special Forces .
Hence, it is clear that the image used by many people as that of killed Islamic State leader Abu Ibrahim al-Hashimi al-Qurayshi is that of his predecessor, Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi. Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Feb 4, 2022 19:00 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of UP election candidate saying he wants to 'earn money by becoming MLA' is from 2017
content:
This video is from the 2017 UP Legislative Assembly election. The man seen in the video is Gopal Chaudhary, an independent candidate who contested from UP's Agra South constituency in 2017.
Election is a time when politicians try to present their best selves in front of the electorate. But a video recently making the rounds on social media flies in the face of such conventional wisdom.
The video in question sees a man openly confessing that he is contesting elections for money and personal gain. According to the social media posts, he is a candidate contesting for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. "I'm not contesting elections on any issue. I'm fighting for a personal agenda, which is to earn money by becoming an MLA," the man can be heard saying in the video.
The archived versions of a similar post can be seen here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the claim along with the video is misleading. This video is from the 2017 assembly election in UP.
The video in question has the logo of the news website, The Quint. In the video, the man has been identified as an independent candidate Gopal Chaudhary and for a fraction of a second, 'Agra' can be seen written on the top-right corner of the video.
We did a keyword search and found the same video report published by The Quint on January 28, 2017. This confirms that the video is old and is not related to the upcoming UP elections which will be held in seven phases from February 10 to March 10.
The description of the video reads as follows, "The election season is upon us and from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Congress Vice President Rahul Gandhi, everyone is busy making election promises to the voters. However, Gopal Chaudhary, one of the independent candidates from the Agra constituency, has a different approach. Chaudhary sent ripples across social media when he made an 'honest claim' that he is contesting elections to make money and he has no intention to work for public welfare."
Several media outlets also reported this unusual confession made by a candidate.
According to a 2017 report in The Indian Express, Chaudhary contested the 2017 assembly elections in UP from the Agra South constituency. Chaudhary received 464 (0.21 per cent) votes in the election.
The election to the 17th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly was held from February 11 to March 8, 2017
The viral video was also tweeted by ANI on January 27, 2017. #WATCH : Independent candidate Agra South Gopal Chaudhary says 'my only reason for coming into politics is money, I'll fool people" pic.twitter.com/sYfPIdhiYC — ANI UP/Uttarakhand (@ANINewsUP) January 27, 2017
#WATCH : Independent candidate Agra South Gopal Chaudhary says 'my only reason for coming into politics is money, I'll fool people" pic.twitter.com/sYfPIdhiYC — ANI UP/Uttarakhand (@ANINewsUP) January 27, 2017
It is hence clear that the video in question is over five years old and not is related to the upcoming elections. Published By: Arshi Aggarwal Published On: Feb 4, 2022 23:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video from Darjeeling passed off as BJP leader being heckled in UP
content:
While a campaigning BJP MLA was recently chased away by villagers in Muzaffarnagar, UP, this particular video is from West Bengal. In 2017, Dilip Ghosh, the former state president of the BJP, and others were heckled and chased in Darjeeling by locals.
Amid the high-octane election campaign in Uttar Pradesh, a video showing BJP leaders getting heckled by people has gone viral with the claim that this happened in Uttar Pradesh recently. Multiple Facebook and Twitter users shared the video with the caption in Hindi that translates to, "The condition of BJP is pathetic. Another BJP leader was welcomed in Uttar Pradesh with kicks and punches." India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the viral video is from West Bengal. In 2017 Dilip Ghosh, the former state president of BJP and others were heckled and chased in Darjeeling by locals. These viral posts have been archived here and here . AFWA probe With the help of the InVid tool and reverse image search we have found the truth behind the viral video. A similar video of the attack on the BJP leaders was uploaded on the YouTube channel of ABP News with the title "Attack on BJP President Dilip Ghosh in Darjeeling ". A similar video of the incident was also uploaded on another YouTube channel called NMF News. Both these videos were uploaded on October 6, 2017. According to these news clips, the now-BJP national vice president along with a few others were heckled by locals in Darjeeling. The incident was reported by The Indian Express on October 6, 2017. As per this report, after the withdrawal of the indefinite strike called by the Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (GJM) on the issue of Gorkhaland, a Bengal BJP delegation led by Dilip Ghosh, the former state president of the party, visited Darjeeling. As per the news report, Ghosh was chased and heckled, allegedly by supporters of Binay Tamang in Darjeeling. As per news reports , a couple of weeks ago during the Uttar Pradesh election campaign, BJP MLA Vikram Singh Saini was chased away by people in his constituency in Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh. But the viral video in question is a five-year-old one from Darjeeling, West Bengal, and has no link to the UP election. Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: Feb 5, 2022 00:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Ajit Anjum did not tweet he will leave journalism if BJP comes back to power in UP
content:
This screenshot of the tweet purportedly by Ajit Anjum is fake and digitally created. The journalist confirmed that he has not made such an announcement on the microblogging site.
The voters of Uttar Pradesh head to the polling booths for the first phase of Assembly elections in a few days. Social media is abuzz with heated campaigns by political parties. A lot of misinformation is also passed over these platforms as the voting day draw closer.
In the latest, a tweet, purportedly by senior journalist Ajit Anjum is circulated on social media where he claims to leave journalism if BJP comes back to power in UP.
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the tweet circulated as Ajit Anjum's is fake. The journalist himself told us that he has not made any such announcement on Twitter. AFWA probe
According to the screenshot in circulation, Ajit Anjum made the tweet on January 31, 2022.
We checked Ajit Anjum's tweets from his official handle ( @ajitanjum ) n this date but couldn't find it. We also checked the archived version of the tweet in question on the web archiving tool " Wayback Machine ". However, none of the Tweets made by Ajit Anjum on January 31 or the adjacent days was available in the archives.
Also, as per the screenshot, Ajit Anjum made the tweet from a verified Twitter handle. However, the official handle of Ajit Anjum -- which has over 1.2 million followers is not verified. Ajit's Twitter followers include several political leaders and journalists. For further clarity, we further reached out to Ajit Anjum. Speaking to AFWA, the journalist said, "A few days back some social media handles were claiming that I have announced to leave journalism if Yogi Adityanath comes back to power in UP. Now, a fake screenshot of a tweet is in circulation claiming that I will leave my profession if BJP comes back to power in UP. All these are absurd. I have never made any such remarks. Also, my Twitter handle @ajitanjum is not verified. However, the fake screenshot in circulation has a verification tick mark." On February 5, 2022, Ajit Anjum himself shared the screenshot of the alleged tweet and confirmed he never posted such a remark on the microblogging platform. . . . . . pic.twitter.com/jolZFCznCD — Ajit Anjum (@ajitanjum) February 5, 2022 On the same day, Ajit also tweeted a video of him speaking about the fake social media posts circulating in his name and the frequent trolls he receives from the IT cells. advertisement The video is shared with a caption in Hindi that translates as, "Various types of false rumours are being spread about me in a planned manner. Photoshop creations are also circulated. It shows how much the IT cell dislikes me touring the country and voicing my opinion." .. . IT . . Link https://t.co/GMsxF5ffXV pic.twitter.com/2TPNELWrRy — Ajit Anjum (@ajitanjum) February 5, 2022 It is hence clear that the screenshot circulated in the name of Ajit Anjum is fake. The journalist never tweeted saying he will leave journalism if BJP comes back to power in UP. (With inputs from Kamala Kuniyal in New Delhi) Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Feb 5, 2022 21:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video does not show Kanhaiya Kumar getting beaten up by Congress workers
content:
A youth named Devansh Bajpai allegedly threw "ink" at Kanhaiya Kumar on February 1 in the Congress party office in Lucknow. The viral video is that of Bajpai being heckled.
Just days away from the first phase of the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, social media saw claims that Kanhaiya Kumar, Congress's new star recruit, was heckled and attacked by his own party member in Lucknow. Sharing a video of the alleged incident , some Facebook users claimed that Kanhaiya was beaten by his own party workers.
The claim, originally in Hindi, roughly translates to, "Rahul Gandhi's darling Kanhaiya Kumar has been beaten by Congress workers." A flag of the Congress party is visible in the low-quality video.
Archived versions of some similar posts can be seen here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room found this claim to be not true. Kumar was not being attacked in the video making the claim.
With the help of some keywords from the viral post, we came across a report published in " The Times of India " on February 2. It stated that "ink" was allegedly thrown at Kumar by a youth named Devansh Bajpai in the Lucknow Party office.
But Kanhaiya Kumar was not seen in the viral video. It was still not clear who was the person being heckled in that viral video. So, with the help of the Invid tool, we took some screenshots of the viral video and ran a reverse image search.
This led us to multiple media reports of that day about this incident in the Congress office. We came across a video uploaded by News24 on its YouTube channel on February 1 alongside a caption in Hindi which translates to, "Ink thrown on Kanhaiya Kumar outside the Congress party office." When we compared both frames, it became clear that both the videos are the same and this video is from the Lucknow party office of Congress.
We found another video report published by Zee Uttar Pradesh-Uttarakhand where it was mentioned that Devansh Bajpai, who allegedly threw "chemicals" at Kanhaiya, was beaten by the party workers. But the suspect's face was not visible enough.
Further search took us to a YouTube video uploaded by Times Now on February 1. In this video, the man Bajpai can easily be seen at the 11-12 second mark. His face reappears clearly towards the end of the video.
So we conclude that the viral video claiming Kanhaiya Kumar has been beaten by his own party workers is not true. It was Devansh Bajpai who got heckled by Congress workers.

title: Fact Check: Old video shared as Baloch fighters shooting down Pak military chopper
content:
This video has been in circulation since 2020. News reports claimed it was footage of a Russian chopper being mistakenly shot down by Azerbaijan on November 9, 2020.
Pakistani troops clashed with the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) following two attacks by the insurgent group. While the BLA claimed hundreds of Pakistani defence personnel were killed in the attacks on army posts in Naushki and Panjgur districts, the Pakistani government claimed that the final death toll stands at 20 militants and nine soldiers.
A video was shared on social media claiming that it captured the terrorist organisation shooting down a Pakistani military helicopter in Panjgur. "#Balochistan Exclusive footage of Pak Army helicopter shot down by Balochistan libration Armyfreedom fighters in #Panjgur," one such tweet claimed.
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim to be misleading. The video used in the tweet was shared online at least as early as 2020.
The video was of poor quality and was too pixelated to run a keyframe search. But we found a better version of the same video posted as a reply to the tweet by a user who alleged the claim to be wrong.
Posted on November 9, 2020, the tweet read, "Nagorno-Karabakh: Russian helicopter shot down over Armenia. Azerbaijan has admitted to shooting the aircraft down by accident."
We ran a reverse search of the video's keyframes on Yandex and found several posts dating back to November 2020. Most of these were posted by Russian users that claimed what the video showed was a Russian chopper shot down by Azerbaijan.
The video was uploaded on November 10, 2020, on Instagram by " chp.kbr " — a local news page that appears to be from Russia's Nalchik region. "The Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry said that the country's army accidentally shot down a Russian helicopter and apologizes to the Russian side," the English translation of the Russian caption read.
A similar claim was found on another Russian Instagram page called " armiya_rf " that uploaded the video on November 9, 2020. "These frames appeared on the network, eyewitnesses claim that they captured the moment the missile hit the Russian Mi-24," the post on the page with more than 200,000 followers said.
The video was also found published on an independent news website called " bulgarianmilitary.com " with the same claim on November 10, 2020.
We ran a Google keyword search to find out more about the circumstances that led to the incident. Long-standing rivals Armenia and Azerbaijan fought over the control of the Nagorno-Karabakh region for over a month starting in late September 2020. The conflict ended in a decisive Azerbaijani victory on November 10, 2020, who took control of the Armenian-dominated Nagorno-Karabakh.
On November 9, 2020, a Russian Mi-24 military helicopter was mistakenly shot down by Azerbaijan while flying over Armenia. The ill-fated chopper was accompanying a column of Russian troops in Armenia while it was hit by the Azeri missile. Two of the crew died while another sustained injury, reports said. Azerbaijan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs released an apology and offered compensation following the incident.
The date of the incident matches the time when most of the Russian handles had published the video on social media. We found the same video on YouTube claiming to be of the shot down Mi-24.
Though not the same one in question, a similar video was found in a report by the Daily Star on November 9, 2020, which showed the burning wreckage of the helicopter.
It is thus clear that the video is not from the recent clashes in Balochistan. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Feb 6, 2022 22:17 IST

title: Fact Check: Youth from Bihar didn't hack into Google, nor was he offered Rs 3.66 cr job
content:
Chaudhary didn't hack Google, but he notified them about a bug in their systems. Google acknowledged his bug report and enlisted him as a bug-hunter.
Stories of white hat hackers getting job offers from tech giants after bringing said giants down to their knees through their mysterious hacking skills are fun to hear or read. They echo themes of David and Goliath that many enjoy. But a lot of times, the story is not what you hear. Such is the case of a young man from Bihar, whose exploits are being mythologised online.
Many on social media shared an image of a young man called Rituraj Chaudhary who did something extraordinary: he hacked the world's largest search engine website, Google, in a matter of seconds.
The viral post in Hindi roughly translates to, "This man, Rituraj Chaudhary, hacked Google for 51 seconds a few nights ago. Google officials in the USA went crazy. But Rituraj resumed Google's services and mailed them about a flaw on their website that can be used to hack the system."
This claim further adds, "Google held a meeting for 12 hours in the US and finally decided to hire Rituraj and sent him an offer letter with a package of Rs 3.66 crores per annum. Rituraj didn't have a passport. So, Google talked to the Government of India, and the newly made passport reached his home within two hours. Rituraj will fly to the US in a private jet. He is studying B.Tech second-year in IIT Manipur and belongs to Mungergunj, a small village near Bihar's Begusarai."
Archived versions of similar claims can be found here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found these viral posts to be misleading. Rituraj didn't hack Google but found a security bug in their website. He is neither going to the USA nor is he joining Google. AFWA Probe
Using keywords, we searched the Internet for news reports on this and came across an article published by DNA on February 4.
In that report stated no extraordinary tale, just that Chaudhary informed Google about a flaw or bug in the website that could have easily helped hackers' to take advantage.
According to a report published in Dainik Bhaskar on February 3, Google admitted to the flaw at their end and sent Chaudhary an acknowledgement mail. The report further added that Google often rewards those who find flaws on their website. Currently, Chaudhary's findings were in the Phase-2 level. He will be awarded by Google when they reach Phase-0.
Many researchers work on " bug hunt " for Google, which starts at Phase-5 and goes up to Phase-0.
An AajTak report confirmed that Chaudhary's name was included in the researchers' list of Google. We dug further on this and found the list of bug hunters by Google where Chaudhary's name was featured.
While speaking to The Lallantop , Chaudhary dismissed rumours about getting a job in Google worth Rs 3.66 crores and flying to the USA. Chaudhary also added that he was not an IIT-Manipur student — there is no IIT in Manipur. He is, in fact, a student at the Indian Institute of Information Technology Manipur (IIIT-Manipur).
When AFWA reached out to Chaudhary, he texted back saying, "All the rumours about getting a job in Google and flying to the states are fake. It is impossible to make a passport within hours." When asked about receiving a reward from Google, he said, "Google gives rewards after they fix that bug and that takes around two to three months."
Therefore, we conclude that the stories about Chaudhary joining Google and receiving a huge salary are not true.
(with inputs from Riddhish Dutta) Published By: Amrtansh Arora Published On: Feb 6, 2022 22:34 IST

title: Fact Check: Year-old Defence Ministry report shared with dynasty spin ahead of UP polls
content:
Although Rajnath's elder son and Noida's sitting MLA Pankaj Singh has gotten a ticket from the party, his younger son Neeraj Singh hasn't been offered any. The newspaper report is also more than a year old.
Unemployment is one of the foremost issues in the upcoming Assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Manipur, and Goa. Parties contesting for the polls have therefore made jobs-creation an important plank. On social media, however, an image has gone viral that shows a newspaper report about the Defence Ministry abolishing 9,300 posts. A viral screenshot of the newspaper report also carried an image of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The headline of the report in Hindi reads, "9,300 Military Engineer Services posts abolished by the Defence Ministry." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Sharing the cut-out of this report, several Facebook users called Singh out. For example, one user shared this screenshot alongside a caption quoting, "Both his sons got tickets for the 2022 assembly elections. That's why the job ticket for our children has been cancelled." Archived versions of similar claims can be seen here and here . India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found this claim to be misleading as only one of Rajnath Singh's sons has been given a ticket for the upcoming polls. At the same time, the news report in the photo is also an old one. AFWA Probe With the help of some keywords, we found Rajnath Singh's family details in a Jagran Josh report. It mentioned that the former Home Minister has two sons and a daughter named Pankaj Singh, Neeraj Singh, and Anamika Singh respectively. After searching for keywords of Pankaj Singh, it led us to an Economic Times report which noted that he is already the sitting MLA from Noida, and has now been awarded a ticket for the second time from the same constituency by the Bharatiya Janata Party. But when we searched for the keywords of Neeraj Singh, no such result appeared, which could suggest that he had been given a ticket too. A National Herald report stated that Neeraj has been denied a ticket by the party. It also mentioned that this time, the BJP decided to not give tickets to family members of elected representatives, barring those who are already elected members. Further, a Fact-Check story by the " Viswas News " made it clear that Rajnath's younger son Neeraj Singh, hasn't got a ticket from the party. While looking closely into the viral newspaper cutting, we noticed that "Jagran Bureau" was written below the headline. After searching for keywords related to this, it took us to a Jagran report published on May 7, 2020. Media outlets like the Hindustan Times and The Indian Express also published similar reports on May 7 and 8, 2020. The abolition of the posts, reportedly, is one of the outcomes of recommendations made by the Lt Gen DB Shekatkar committee report on enhancing the army's combat potential and trimming its expenditure. Therefore, we conclude that the claim made in the viral post is misleading as one, this is an old news report, and two, not both of Rajnath Singh's sons have gotten a ticket for the upcoming polls. title: Fact Check: Old hoax claiming Lata Mangeshkar sang 'Yeh Jeevan Hai' for Kishore Kumar resurfaces
content:
The cover of Kishore Kumar's "Yeh Jeevan Hai" by Lata Mangeshkar is not a private recording, done specifically for Kishore Kumar. It was part of Mangeskar's album "Shraddhanjali: My Tribute To The Immortals".
As India mourned the death of Lata Mangeshkar, tributes for the legendary singer poured in from all quarters on social media. Amid this, several netizens shared an emotional story involving Mangeshkar and another legendary singer, Kishore Kumar. The viral story claims that Lata Mangeshkar sang Kishore Kumar's popular number 'Yeh Jeevan Hai' and gifted it to him on a special tape on her birthday. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Multiple Facebook users have posted this story with the song of Lata Mangeshkar. The viral story read "Once Kishore Kumar asked Lata Mangeshkar, which of his song she liked the best. Lata smiled and asked him,'Dada, bol doon ya gaa kar sunao'... To which Kishore Da said, 'Gaa kar hi sunaiye'. Lata laughed and said OK, but not today."
As India mourned the death of Lata Mangeshkar, tributes for the legendary singer poured in from all quarters on social media. Amid this, several netizens shared an emotional story involving Mangeshkar and another legendary singer, Kishore Kumar.
The viral story claims that Lata Mangeshkar sang Kishore Kumar's popular number 'Yeh Jeevan Hai' and gifted it to him on a special tape on her birthday.
Multiple Facebook users have posted this story with the song of Lata Mangeshkar.
The viral story read "Once Kishore Kumar asked Lata Mangeshkar, which of his song she liked the best. Lata smiled and asked him,'Dada, bol doon ya gaa kar sunao'... To which Kishore Da said, 'Gaa kar hi sunaiye'. Lata laughed and said OK, but not today."
The story further read, "Few months later it was Lataji's birthday and Kishore Kumar received a gift box from Lataji. Kishore Da used to always wish Lataji on her birthday with gifts. It had a note on it from Lataji, it said, 'Dada, aapne itni baar mere janamdin par tohfe bheje hain, ese return gift samaj lena, aur zaroor bataana aap ko agar aacha laga'. He opened the box and there was a tape inside."
The story also claimed, "It was the song Lataji loved most from all of Kishore Da's song... sung by Lata herself. She had contacted HMV recording studio and gone there recorded it only for Kishore Kumar. It seems Kishore Da listened to this song many times when he sat alone in his room. Nobody had heard this Kishore song sung by Lata exclusively for Kishore Kumar. Just listen to it, released by his wife Leena for the first time ever. Never heard before, enjoy." India Today Anti-Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the rendition of Kumar's "Yeh Jeevan Hai" by Mangeshkar was not a private recording, especially for Kumar. It was part of Mangeshkar's album "Shraddhanjali: My Tribute To The Immortals" where she paid a tribute to her colleagues from the singing world. Kumar's "Yeh Jeevan Hai" from the film "Piya Ka Ghar" was one among them. The archived versions of the viral posts are saved here and here . AFWA probe With the help of keywords search we found that this internet story has gone viral previously as well. We have found an article written by film critic Subhash K Jha and published last February last year on the portal IWMBUZZ.com . As per the report, the viral story is a hoax. The portal quoted Lata Mangeshkar, who denied the viral claim to the author. advertisement "I don't recall any such incident. Kishore Da and I were very close to one another. He would make me laugh so much during our recordings for me. I cannot single out any one of his songs as my favourite. There were so many: Koi Lauta De Mere Beete Huey Din (from the film 'Do Dooni Chaar'), Woh Sham Kuch Ajeeb Tthi ('Khamoshi'), and Mera Jeevan Kora Kagaz ('Kora Kagaz'). Kishoreda was filled with masti but when he sang, he projected so much emotion in his voice," Mangeshkar had said at the time. Since the story went viral again after the passing of Lata Mangeshkar on Sunday, AFWA contacted the founder editor of the website IWMBUZZ.com , Siddhartha Laik to confirm the year-old story. "We stand by our story" , said Laik. To further cross check the viral story involving Lata Mangeshkar and Kishore Kumar, we contacted Mahesh Rathore, the private secretary to Lata Mangeshkar. "I have been with Lataji for the last 26 years. I have never heard this story from her or anybody else. This is probably the first time I am hearing this", Rathore told AFWA over the phone. advertisement AFWA contacted writer, poet Yatindra Mishra, the author of the award-winning book, "Lata- Sur Gatha" — a biography in Hindi on Mangeshkar published in 2016. " I have never heard about any such incident from Lataji ever," Mishra told us. The song "Yeh Jeevan Hai" was composed by Laxmikant-Pyarelal for the film "Piya Ka Ghar." Mangeshkar's cover of the song can be found on a number of music-streaming platforms like Gaana and JioSaavn. Thus, we conclude that the viral story involving Lata Mangeshkar and Kishore Kumar and the song "Yeh Jeevan Hai" is a baseless rumour. title: Fact Check: No, Shah Rukh Khan did not spit while offering prayers for Lata Mangeshkar
content:
Shah Rukh Khan did not spit, rather he blew out air after offering prayers. Reciting holy verses and then blowing air into something is called Ruqyah in Islamic tradition. Although Muslims differ on whether Ruqyah can be performed for the dead.
A video clip of actor Shah Rukh Khan offering prayers for Lata Mangeshkar has gone viral for the wrong reasons. Many on social media shared this video, claiming that Khan spat after reciting prayers.
Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson Prashant Patel Umrao quote-tweeted another person who shared the viral video and wrote, "Shahrukh is Spitting!".
Another user posted the same video and wrote in the caption, " Spitting while Paying last respects??? What an ugly culture @iamsrk !!! disrespectful to #LataDidi".
India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found this misleading. Khan did not spit, rather he blew air after offering prayers. Reciting holy verses and then blowing air is called Ruqyah in Islamic tradition.
The archived versions of the viral posts are saved here and here .
After this claim was made by several people, many on social media shared the original video of the incident. While the viral video is only 13 seconds long, the longer version of the video shared online showed how the actor encircled the mortal remains of Lata Mangeshkar and made gestures to pay tribute to her. He was accompanied by his manager Pooja Dadlani. The most secular person .But this secularism always brings hate for him #ShahRukhKhan #LataDidi #LataMangeshkarPassesAway pic.twitter.com/St6gY3FdNa — Azharul Akash (@AzharulAkash3) February 6, 2022
The most secular person .But this secularism always brings hate for him #ShahRukhKhan #LataDidi #LataMangeshkarPassesAway pic.twitter.com/St6gY3FdNa — Azharul Akash (@AzharulAkash3) February 6, 2022
This was also reported by the mainstream media which can be seen here and here .
To defend the actor's gesture, some netizens even shared a clip from Khan's film "My Name is Khan", where he can be seen blowing air on his son in the movie.
AFWA showed the viral video to a few Muslim scholars who are experts in Islamic studies.
Professor Junaid Haris of the department of Islamic studies from Delhi's Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) university explained Khan's gestures.
"He is surely not spitting. This is a typical Muslim tradition of blowing air into something after reciting the holy verses. This is called Ruqyah or Ar-Ruqyah AshShar'iyyah in Arabic and Dum in Urdu," said Professor Junaid Haris of JMI. "But I failed to understand why the actor is doing this in front of the mortal remains of somebody. This is not done during the last rites at all," the professor added.
We have found the definition of "Ruqyah" on Islamic websites that have elaborated on how to perform Ruqyah on old and sick persons.
Muslims differ on whether Ruqyah can be performed for the dead.
As per Asad Khan Falahi, another expert on Islamic studies told AFWA, "We normally perform this ritual of reciting Ayat and then performing Dum or blowing air on persons who are unwell and need blessings of Allah to be cured."
"You blow on something after reciting the holy verse, not on air. So, it could be Shah Rukh's own belief that he has done during the last rites. But in Islam you do not do Ruqyiah in front of dead," explained Haris.
Islamic scholars might differ on the opinion of whether this Islamic ritual can be done on dead or not, but one thing is clear: Khan did not spit in front of Lata Mangeshkar's mortal remains; rather he blew air following a Muslim tradition after offering prayers. Published By: Arshi Aggarwal Published On: Feb 7, 2022 15:54 IST

title: Fact Check: Old image of BJP flags abandoned in waste container goes viral ahead of UP polls
content:
The claim is misleading as the image has been in circulation since at least 2018.
With only days away from the first phase of the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, social media has been abuzz with heated campaigning by political parties, and a whole lot of misinformation spread by people, either knowingly or unwittingly.
One such piece of misinformation was an image showing several Bharatiya Janata Party flags dumped in a public waste container, with the claim that this photo was from western Uttar Pradesh.
Retired IAS officer Surya Pratap Singh was among the many who tweeted the picture. "Here, someone from western Uttar Pradesh sent this to me. Now, it's up to you," the translation of the tweet from his verified handle read.
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim misleading. This photo has been in circulation for over three years at least.
A reverse search of the image produced several results. Among them was a tweet from December 4, 2018.
This confirmed that the image was definitely not a recent one and was at least three years old.
More posts with the same photo were found on Facebook when we searched with the Hindi lines used in the tweet.
We found that this image was used by supporters of different opposition parties to call out the BJP. Here is a tweet from 2021 using the same photo. We also found a photo story carried by lokmat.com on December 11, 2018, which contained the photo in question. The story was a compilation of top social media memes following the counting of assembly poll votes in five states on December 11. Telangana, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Mizoram and Madhya Pradesh were the five states that witnessed the counting of votes on the day. Though the actual origin of the image couldn't be located, it is clear that the virally shared photo is not a recent one from poll-bound Uttar Pradesh. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Feb 7, 2022 19:14 IST

title: Fact Check: 50% seats in NIT-Goa reserved for home students, is it an exception?
content:
It is true that 40 percent of the seats at NIT-Goa are reserved for students from Goa under the Home State Quota. However, it is not an exception. Every NIT in India has seats reserved under Home State Quota.
As assembly polls approach Goa, a claim, supporting the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, has gone viral on social media.
Highlighting the achievements of the BJP government in Goa, a few social media users have stated that, "BJP has delivered 40% Reservations for Goans in NIT-Goa. It's a special exception only for Goa."
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral claim was misleading. While it is true that 40 percent of seats in NIT Goa are reserved for "home students," it is, however, no exception.
All NITs across the country have seat reservations under Home State Quota as prescribed by the Union Ministry of Education (formerly the Ministry of Human Resource Development).
While investigating the claim, we first conducted a keyword search to check if any such reservation exists in NIT-Goa.
We found a news report published in May 2017. It stated that until 2016-17, NIT-Goa had a 50 percent reservation for Home State Quota, and that it was jointly shared by Goa along with Dadra Nagar Haveli, Diu and Daman and Lakshadweep.
However, following a demand raised by former chief minister Manohar Parikkar, the criteria was changed. Starting with the 2017-18 session, 40 percent of seats would be reserved exclusively for the students of Goa, and the remaining ten percent would be shared by students from Dadra Nagar Haveli, Diu and Daman, and Lakshadweep.
We then visited the website of Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JOSAA) to verify the current status of this allocation. Every year, the Ministry of Education sets up JOSAA to manage and regulate the joint seat allocation for admissions to 114 institutes for that academic year.
The business rule formulated by JOSAA for the 2021-22 academic year states that NIT-Goa has a reservation of 50 percent seats for the Home State Quota.
It stated that 40 percent of the Home State seats were reserved for students belonging to Goa. The remaining ten percent of the Home State seats are shared by students of Union Territories of Daman and Diu, Dadra Nagar Haveli, and Lakshadweep. However, any vacant Home State seats out of the ten percent mentioned above will be allocated to students from Goa.
The business rule formulated by JOSAA clearly speaks of Home State seat reservation for other NITs as well.
It states that apart from NIT-Goa and NIT-Srinagar, all NITs in India have 50 percent reservation for Home State Quota.
Like NIT-Goa, NIT-Srinagar also has reservation for more than one state or union territories. A special quota of five percent seats in NIT-Srinagar are reserved for students of Ladakh. Any unfilled seats out of the five percent mentioned above can be filled by the students of Jammu and Kashmir.
Students of states or union territories where there are no NITs, can apply for the Home State Quota at other NITs as specified by JOSAA. However, unlike Goa and Srinagar, there is no limit for such reservations.
To further confirm the rule, we got in touch with Dr. Kiran Teeparthi, the associate dean of NIT-Andhra Pradesh.
"Every NIT in India has a 50 percent reservation for home students. Even we have it for NIT-Andhra Pradesh," Teeparthi, who is an alumnus of NIT-Jamshedpur and NIT-Warangal, told India Today.
According to the JOSAA, eligible candidates who can apply for Home State quota are those candidates "whose Home State is the same as the state in which the Institute is located".
To understand the meaning of the criteria, we got in touch with Sumit Kumar Biswas, the Senior Superintendent of NIT-Durgapur.
He explained that Home State Quota does not actually mean the state where the student's permanent address is located. It is the registered address of the institution from where the student had appeared for their senior secondary exams.
"Say, if a student from Nagaland had studied plus two from an institution in Bengal, then he would apply at NIT-Durgapur and not at NIT-Nagaland for Home State Quota," Biswas explained.
Hence, we can conclude that the viral claim is misleading. Not just NIT-Goa, every NIT in India has seats reserved under Home State Quota. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Feb 7, 2022 21:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Old photos of Mumbai college Independence Day celebration crop up in Karnataka hijab row
content:
These photos were taken during pre-Covid Independence Day celebrations at Mumbai's Anjuman-I-Islam college in 2018 and 2019. It has no connection with the ongoing hijab protests in the southern state.
Karnataka is at the centre of a political storm as the row over hijabs in educational institutions refuses to die down. A month after six women were barred from entering classes for wearing the hijab at a Women's Government PU College in Udupi, protests and counter-protests have now spread across several college campuses. More than 100 male students went for classes wearing saffron shawls on February 2. On February 5, 200 boys in Bhandarkar's College, Kundapur, reportedly came to college wearing saffron shawls raising the slogan " Jai Shri Ram ". Meanwhile, the state government has asked institutions to follow existing uniform rules until the Karnataka High Court takes a call. On Twitter, debates on the issue have raged on as well, a lot of them under the hashtag #KarnatakaHijabRow. Among these debates and opinions, however, were also images of women donning tricolour headscarves. "If you have a dare to wear our Indian flag instead #HijabIsOurPride #HijabisOurRight #KarnatakaHijabRow," one such tweet read. Archived links of similar tweets can be seen here and here . India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim to be misleading. The photos in circulation with the claim that they are from Karnataka were actually taken at a Mumbai college during the Independence Day celebrations in 2018 and 2019. AFWA Probe The image in some of these tweets showed women marching, wearing tricolour hijab. A reverse search on Google took us to a report by the Financial Express published on August 15, 2018. The photo story was a collection of the best images of Independence Day celebrations from different parts of the country. The photo by the Press Trust of India (PTI) featured ninth in the story along with the caption, "Students of Anjuman Islam College march during the 72nd Independence Day parade, in Mumbai." Clearly, the image of college students in Mumbai was shared as a scene from Karnataka. We also checked the other image that is shared with similar claims. While the tweet claims the photo to be from Karnataka, a reverse search took us to an article by The Hindu published on December 30, 2019. It was a listicle of the most liked photos of the year on the daily's Instagram page. The image in question was listed ninth in it along with the title, "Students of the Anjuman-I-Islam college in Mumbai don tricolour headscarves before flag hoisting during Independence Day celebrations at the college." We also located the photo on The Hindu's Instagram page . Uploaded on August 15, 2019, with the same caption, the photo was taken by the late senior photojournalist Vivek Bendre who died in 2021. Following the clue that the origin of both the images is the same, we ran a keyword search on Google for the Independence Day celebrations at Anjuman-I-Islam College. This returned several similar photos from 2019. One such image was also available on the website of the British-American visual media company Getty Images . It was captioned, "Students of Anjuman I Islam College take selfie to celebrate 73rd Independence Day, on August 15, 2019 in Mumbai, India." A similar search on YouTube took us to a short video uploaded on August 15, 2020. We found students donning similar headscarves in this brief recap of the college's Independence Day celebration the previous year. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Hence, it is clear that the images of women in tricolour headscarves shared with the claim that they are from Karnataka, were actually taken during Independence Day celebrations at Mumbai's Anjuman-I-Islam college. They have no connection with the ongoing hijab protests in the southern state. (With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi) Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: Feb 7, 2022 23:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Bhagwant Mann call Kejriwal a robber? No, viral video is doctored
content:
The viral video is doctored. In the original video, Bhagwant Mann was said "daaku" or robbers. Not Kejriwal.
Weeks before the Punjab assembly elections and amid the on-going high-octane political campaigning, a video of Aam Aadmi Party's (AAP) chief ministerial candidate Bhagwant Singh Mann has gone viral where he can be heard saying that Kejriwal robbed everything from a family whose daughter was about to get married. title: Fact Check: No, Mayawati hasn't pledged support to BJP in UP assembly polls, viral video old
content:
This viral clip is from October 2020. At the time, Mayawati had said her party would vote for BJP or any other party's candidate in the then-upcoming UP MLC elections to defeat SP's second candidate. In the ongoing election campaign in UP, Mayawati has slammed both BJP and SP.
A video clip featuring Bahujan Samaj Party supremo Maywati has gone viral with the claim that she recently announced her party would support the Bharatiya Janata Party — or any other party — in pursuit of defeating the Samajwadi Party in the soon-to-begin assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh. Several people shared the viral clip featuring the BBC's logo on Facebook and Twitter , claiming this to be a recent announcement. In the viral clip, Mayawati read out a statement in Hindi: "The BSP will do everything to defeat the SP's second candidate. And to do this, if it is required for our party MLAs to sacrifice their votes to the BJP — or any other party — we will even do that." India Today Anti-Fake News War Room ( AFWA) found that this viral clip is from October 2020. At the time, Mayawati had said her party would vote for the BJP or any other party's candidate in the then-upcoming Uttar Pradesh MLC elections to defeat the SP's "second candidate." In the ongoing election campaign in Uttar Pradesh, Mayawati has criticised both the BJP and the SP. The viral posts are archived here and here . AFWA probe Since the viral clip contained the BBC logo, with the help of keywords searches, we found the original video embedded in an article on the BBC website , published on November 2, 2020. This clip is over three minutes long. The same viral clip was also tweeted by news agency ANI on October 29, 2020. The caption of the tweet read, "#WATCH BSP Chief Mayawati says that her party will vote for BJP or any party's candidate in future UP MLC elections, to defeat Samajwadi Party's second candidate. 'Any party candidate, who'll be dominant over SP's 2nd candidate, will get all BSP MLAs' vote for sure,' she said." #WATCH BSP Chief Mayawati says that her party will vote for BJP or any party's candidate in future UP MLC elections, to defeat Samajwadi Party's second candidate. "Any party candidate, who'll be dominant over SP's 2nd candidate, will get all BSP MLAs' vote for sure," she said. pic.twitter.com/ki4W6ZAwgE — ANI (@ANI) October 29, 2020 This was reported by other news outlets and YouTube channels as well, around the same time. As per these news reports, a few months before the polls to 12 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats , to be held on January 28, 2021, Mayawati announced in October 2020 that her party would vote for any other political outfit, including the BJP, in order to ensure the defeat of the SP in the then-upcoming elections to the Upper House of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, and the Rajya Sabha. But Mayawati may not have the same views now. The BSP leader has attacked both the BJP and the SP in her recent election campaigns. As per news reports , on February 5, during a BSP election rally in Saharanpur, she has slammed both parties for their "anti-Dalit politics" and urged voters to support the BSP in the upcoming assembly elections and reject the BJP, the SP, and even the Congress. Hence, we conclude that this clip of Mayawati supporting the BJP is misleading, in the context of the upcoming assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh. title: Fact Check: Old video of Bangladesh cleric hitting out at Yati Narsinghanand goes viral amid Karnataka Hijab row
content:
The viral video has been edited. The person in the video is Syed Irshad Ahmad Al Bukhari of Dinajpur, Bangladesh. He was responding to Yati Narsinghanand's comments on Islam.
Amid the Karnataka hijab row, a video of a man has gone viral with the claim that he threatened all Hindus with dire consequences if they did not convert to Islam. Several Twitter users shared the video that declared in Hindi text, "These people have decided your fate. They are just waiting for Modi to be out of the picture. Let's ensure that all our Hindu brothers are aware of this. Hindus, see this with clear eyes and hear this with your ears clear. Use WhatsApp to make sure every Hindu brother in your contacts list sees this." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Some Twitter users even shared the video with the trending hashtag #KarnatakaHijabRow. In the 29-second-long clip, a man can be heard speaking in Hindi. He says, "There is still time. Repent. Ask for forgiveness from God's messenger. Or your body won't even be burnt. Vultures, crows, and jackals will feed on your body." Then, after a jump cut, the man says, "I am inviting you, read the Kalma and become a Muslim. If you want deliverance, read the Kalma and become a Muslim." India Today Anti-Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral video was edited. The person in the video is Saeed Irshad Ahmed Al Bukhari of Dinajpur, Bangladesh. He was responding to Yati Narsinghanand's comments on Islam. AFWA probe With the help of InVid and reverse image search, we found that a longer version of the same video was tweeted in May 2021. In the caption, journalist Swati Goel Sharma wrote, "Friendly message from Bangladesh: Corona pandemic and the many deaths and cremations in India is because of 'blasphemy' by Narsinghanand. Hindus, do tauba, otherwise your dead bodies won't be cremated but eaten by cheel-kawwe. Ae pandit Narsinghanand, accept our Islam." Using this as a clue, with the help of keyword search, we found the original video on Facebook, belonging to one Dr Syed Irshad Ahmad Al Bukhari. The original video was over seven minutes long and it was posted on April 30, 2021. According to the Bengali caption of the Facebook post, the man delivering the speech, Bukhari. And he had arranged a human chain in the Dinajpur district of Bangladesh to protest the controversial comments made by Hindu religious leader Yati Narsinghanand against Islam. According to his Facebook profile , Bukhari is a lecturer at the Islamic Research Centre in Dinajpur, Bangladesh. Missing context Listening carefully to the entire speech delivered by Syed Irshad Ahmed Al Bukhari, we confirmed that the viral clip was an edited one and the relevant portions have been chopped out in the viral clip to give a different context to it. Bukhari began his speech with, "Today we've gathered here in Dinajpur, Bangladesh, after the Jumma's Namaz just to say one thing. That India's shameless and wicked Pandit Narsinghanand Saraswati, who has insulted and disrespected our Rasool Allah, we just want to say that we two crore Muslims of the world are ready to sacrifice our lives on our Rasool Allah's feet." advertisement So, the context of his speech can be established as a protest against Narsinghanand. But only a small part of his speech was forked out and used in the viral clip. The viral clip also has a jump cut in between two frames, which suggests the clip was edited deliberately to give it a different colour. In the last half of the original video, the man can be heard saying, "In a list of 100 religious teachers' names, Rasool Allah was at the first position. It was a Christian who kept Rasool Allah at the top of the list; that a Christian recognizes who Rasool Akhal Akhal is, but Narsinghanand Saraswati, you don't have enough knowledge to understand that." Then he kept on saying, addressing Narsinghanand: "I am inviting you to read the Kalma and become a Muslim. If you want deliverance, read the Kalma and become a Muslim." Thus, we confirm that the viral clip was edited deliberately to give it a different context. We also confirmed that the speech was not delivered in India but in Bangladesh. And finally, it has nothing to do with the Karnataka Hijab row. (With input from Yash Mittal) Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Feb 9, 2022 23:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Decade-old video of Yogi Adityanath distributing money shared with claims of bribery during assembly polls
content:
This is a 10-year-old video of Yogi Adityanath, who was an MP from Gorakhpur at the time. In this video, he was taped helping villagers who lost their crops to a fire. This has nothing to do with the ongoing elections.
With six more phases of the Uttar Pradesh assembly polls yet to take place, social media is full of supporters of various parties attempting to influence the electorate. Amid this, a video of UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath distributing money has been shared by several people. The viral video sees the CM sitting in a chair, surrounded by people. A few people were seen touching his feet after receiving money. Those sharing the video accused the CM of bribing voters during the ongoing assembly elections. "This is how he's contesting. For the first time in this country's history, we are witnessing a Chief Minister distributing money to win elections," claimed a Twitter user . The video has also gone viral on Facebook with the same claim. #UPElections2022 #BoycottBJP #aimim___ @asadowaisi @JamiatUlama_in @aimim_national pic.twitter.com/74ct66dUi1 — Aleem Shaikh (@AleemSh98477102) February 10, 2022 Archived version of the same claim can be found here and here . India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found this claim misleading. The viral video is about a decade old and has nothing to do with the ongoing assembly elections. AFWA Probe With the help of InVid, we sliced the video into key frames. Through reverse search of the images, we found several fact-check reports based on this video. Results led us to a fact-check report on the same video published by The Quint on March 23, 2019. The report noted that this video initially went viral just before the 2019 Lok Sabha Elections. India Today also fact-checked the same claim during the Lok Sabha elections. That report mentioned that this viral video was actually from 2012 and had nothing to do with the then-ongoing polls. The original video was uploaded by a person called Vinay Kumar Gautam in 2012. He spoke to AFWA and confirmed that it was shot in April 2012. At that time, Yogi Adityanath was a Lok Sabha MP from Gorakhpur. According to Gautam, several people in and around Gorakhpur faced a huge financial crisis at the time after they lost their crops to a fire. The then-MP reached out to these villagers and helped them financially using the MP fund. However, later Goutam deleted this video from YouTube. Thus, we conclude that the viral video of Yogi Adityanath distributing money is about a decade old and has nothing to do with the ongoing election. title: Fact Check: Video of BJP-TRS clash in Telangana shared as violence against BJP workers in Uttar Pradesh
content:
The video was shot at Telangana's Jangaon district on February 9, 2022. Workers of the ruling TRS party confronted BJP members who objected to the burning of PM Modi's effigy.
A video of a scuffle has gone viral on social media. Many have shared the clip, in which a handful of Bharatiya Janata Party workers can be seen attacked in broad daylight, claiming this took place in Uttar Pradesh amid the assembly polls. One such tweet can be seen here .
Similar claims have been archived here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim misleading. The video is from Telangana's Jangaon district. The video shows BJP workers clashing with members of the ruling Telangana Rashtra Samithi. The incident has no connection to the ongoing polls in UP. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story AFWA Probe When we searched, we found no recent reports of major political clashes in UP. Upon a closer look at the video, we noticed the writing on one of the traffic islands. It said "Jangaon Traffic Police."
When we searched, we found no recent reports of major political clashes in UP. Upon a closer look at the video, we noticed the writing on one of the traffic islands. It said "Jangaon Traffic Police."
Jangaon is a district in Telangana — located 85 kilometres away from Hyderabad. The people chasing the BJP workers donned pink shawls. Pink is the dominant colour of the TRS — the state's ruling party. We also confirmed that in the video, the language on the storefront signs (aside from English) was Telugu.
We spotted a huge billboard towards the end of the video with the photo and name of K Chandrasekhar Rao a.k.a. KCR — the chief minister of Telangana, and the TRS supremo.
This confirmed that the video is not from Uttar Pradesh as claimed by many; rather it was shot in Telangana.
We ran a Google keyword search to learn more about the clash. According to media reports, the incident took place on February 9, 2022, when workers of the two parties faced off.
On February 8, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had told the Rajya Sabha that the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014 was not a smooth affair. He said there was no consultation over the process and consequently, both Telangana and Andhra Pradesh suffered.
The Prime Minister's remarks weren't well-received by the TRS who decided to organise protests against him. On February 9, Jangaon MLA Muthireddy Yadagiri Reddy called upon TRS members to stage a protest against the PM. Party workers organised a motorcycle rally.
The TRS' decision to burn an effigy of Modi in the town was contended by flag-bearing BJP supporters who arrived at the spot, reports state . This led to a physical confrontation between the two groups during which the video in circulation was shot. A detailed report of the incident can be read here .
We also found the viral video on the YouTube channel of TV9 Telugu uploaded on February 9.
Another popular Telugu channel, NTV Telugu had more visuals of the incident.
Thus, it is clear that the video in circulation captures a tussle between BJP and TRS workers in the Jangaon district of Telangana. It has nothing to do with either Uttar Pradesh or the ongoing assembly polls there.
(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow) Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Feb 14, 2022 17:39 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Arvind Kejriwal did not say he is a BJP-RSS man; viral video doctored
content:
Viral clip was doctored. The first and the last part of the video where Kejriwal talks about a BJP supporter who spoke about voting for the AAP were clipped out.
Amid the ongoing assembly polls in five states, where Aam Aadmi Party is also a contender, a video clip has gone viral featuring Delhi Chief Minister and party supremo Arvind Kejriwal. This seven-second clip was shared by many with the claim that in it, Kejriwal admitted to his ties with the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. In that video, Kejriwal can be heard saying in Hindi, "We come from a Jan Sangh family. We have been life-long BJP supporters. My father, who belonged to Jan Sangh, was jailed during the emergency." "Kejriwal admits he is a BJP-RSS man," a Twitter user claimed sharing the video. The official handle of Dadra and Nagar Haveli Congress Sevadal has also shared this video alongside a caption that reads, "We have already been telling this. It's now wide and open. Kejriwal is BJP/RSS Pawn. Paidaieshi BJP wale hain ye ." We have aalready been telling this. It's now wide and open. Kejriwal is BJP/RSS Pawn. Paidaieshi BJP wale hain ye. #AAP_BJP_Exposed pic.twitter.com/o0CJ5DhTyy — Dadra and Nagar Haveli Congress Sevadal (@SevadalDNH) February 13, 2022 Archived versions of similar claims can be seen here , here , and here . advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found this claim to be misleading. The viral video has been doctored. Kejriwal in the original video was referring to another person; not himself. AFWA Probe The logo of NDTV 24X7 was clearly visible in this video. So, we searched for a source with relevant keywords. Search results led us to a video uploaded by the NDTV on YouTube on February 4, 2020. At the 4.11-minute-mark, Kejriwal can be heard criticising the top BJP leadership for seeking votes against the issue of anti-CAA protest in Shaheen Bagh. At that time, the 2020 Delhi Assembly Elections were around the corner. At the one-minute-39-seconds mark, Kejriwal said in Hindi, "I was watching a channel where a BJP-man was speaking. He said 'We come from a Jan Sangh family. We have been life-long BJP supporters. My father, who belonged to Jan Sangh, was jailed during the emergency. But this time I'll vote for Kejriwal.'" In the viral clip, the first and the last part of Kejriwal's words have been edited out. We also found an NDTV news report about this interview. Thus, it is clear that the viral video of Arvind Kejriwal where he said he was a BJP-RSS man was edited to give it a false context.
