title: Fact Check: Old video from Bihar circulated as BJP workers attacking man after victory in UP
content:
This is a 2019 video from Bihar's Kaimur district. The man being beaten up is a ward councillor's son who was accused in a murder case.
A video of a man being brutally thrashed by others in the presence of policemen has been circulating on social media. The video was shared with the claim that it showed Bharatiya Janata Party members attacking an innocent man after the party's record win in the recently concluded assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here , here , and here . The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the claim along with the video was misleading. This video is from Bihar and was shot in 2019. AFWA PROBE We found the official Twitter handle of UP police's fact check unit responding to a post saying the video in question was from a 2019 incident in Bihar's Kaimur district, and not related to UP. , , #UPPViralCheck #UPPolice https://t.co/ToOUzgvsfc pic.twitter.com/vtCFq6d2Ka — UPPOLICE FACT CHECK (@UPPViralCheck) March 11, 2022 Taking a cue from this, we ran a keyword search and found screenshots from the same video carried in an India Today report published on October 5, 2019. According to the report, the video showed a ward councillor's son, accused in a murder case, being attacked in the Shivaji Chowk area of Bhabua in Bihar's Kaimur district. He was accused of shooting a young man who later succumbed to his injuries in a city hospital. The man was later admitted to Kaimur Sadar Hospital for treatment. Kaimur's SP told the media at the time that the deceased was shot over a private dispute with the perpetrator. The Dainik Jagran , Live Hindustan , and News18 reported on the same story in October 2019. According to these reports, the man being thrashed in the video was Shahid Rain. The young man he allegedly shot was Madhav Singh, a resident of Sikhathi village. Reports also added that information about the death of the young man, however, made the public furious and there were attacks at hospitals where Shahid Rain was undergoing treatment. Several local shops were also attacked. It is thus clear that the video in question is old and from Bihar. It has nothing to do with the BJP's recent victory in UP assembly elections. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Mar 11, 2022 21:29 IST

title: Fact Check: Old photos shared as brothers from Prayagraj dying by suicide following Akhilesh Yadav's defeat in UP
content:
The viral photo has no connection with the ongoing Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. One photo is from Ramgarh when a Bokaro resident died by suicide in November 2020. Prayagraj's police also refuted the claim.
On Thursday, March 10, Yogi Adityanath scored a major win for the Bharatiya Janata Party in Uttar Pradesh. Amid this, a collage of three photos went viral on social media. Several Facebook users shared the collage, where three different persons could be seen hanging. The claim in Hindi alongside these photos translated to: "Three brothers died by suicide in Prayagraj after watching Akhilesh Yadav getting defeated in the UP polls." EMBED The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the images had nothing to do with the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. No such incidents of three brothers dying by suicide took place in Prayagraj, following the poll results. Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here . AFWA PROBE While investigating the claim, we first conducted a keyword search to find out whether any search incident took place in Prayagraj while the counting process was on. We found no media reports. We then reverse-searched the images and found the source of the first image. Two different news outlets — Sanjeevni Today and Sudama News carried the first photo in reports published in November 2020. According to the reports, the photo is from Ramgarh, where a Bokaro resident Randhir Kumar, 25, died by suicide. We also got in touch with Ajay Kumar, the SSP of Prayagraj. "No such incidents have been reported in Prayagraj," Kumar told India Today. Although we could not verify the source of the other two photographs used in this claim, we can still confidently conclude that these photos are in no way of three brothers dying by suicide following the results of the UP assembly election. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow) Published By: Namrata Agarwal Published On: Mar 11, 2022 22:53 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi didn't play badminton post Congress defeat in recent Assembly polls
content:
This video is from March 9, 2022, a day before the poll results were declared. Rahul went to Sullamussalam Arts and Science College in Kerala's Malappuram and enjoyed a game of Badminton in the new indoor stadium.
Indian National Congress has yet again tasted disappointment in the recent assembly elections in five states. The grand old party received a major setback even in Punjab -- a state where it was in power. Meanwhile, a video of the former party President Rahul Gandhi playing shuttle badminton has gone viral on social media along with the claim that he was seen playing amidst the party's heavy defeat.
In the video, Rahul can be seen playing badminton in an indoor court surrounded by a few party leaders, police, and security guards. Rahul's shots are applauded by the crowd in the video.
"After Congress faced humiliation in the five states, Rahul Gandhi was seen playing badminton", quoted a Hindi Facebook page named "Best Hindi News" while sharing this video.
The official Facebook page of 'Punjab Kesari Madhya Pradesh/Chattisgarh' also posted the same video alongside a caption in Hindi that reads, "Rahul Gandhi was seen in a bit relaxed mood after the result of the 5 state assembly elections was declared. The video has gone viral."
Archived versions of these claims can be seen here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found this claim to be not true. Rahul didn't play badminton after the results were announced. This video was shot in Kerala a day before the counting on March 10.
With the help of a few relevant keywords, we came across an article published by ABP News . The news report's cover image was a collage of two images of the Congress leader. While Rahul was photographed enjoying ice cream in one, he was holding a badminton racket in the other.
Although the report was published on 10 March 2022, the headline clearly mentioned that the said activities were done by Rahul in Kerala before the poll results were announced.
Further search led us to a YouTube video published by the official channel of Rahul Gandhi on March 9 -- a day before the poll results were declared .
The description of this video explained that he enjoyed a game of badminton at the new indoor stadium at Sullamussalam Arts and Science College Areekode, Ernad, Malappuram.
The official YouTube page of the Indian National Congress also uploaded the same video on March 9.
Thus, it is clear that the video of Rahul Gandhi playing badminton was shot a day before the election results were declared on March 10. Published By: tanishka Published On: Mar 12, 2022 19:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Old photo from UK shared claiming BJP's victory in Uttar Pradesh featured at NYSE
content:
The building in the image is Thomson Reuters building at London's Canary Wharf. This image is in circulation since the first Yogi govt came into power in 2017.
BJP's scintillating victory in four state assembly elections including Uttar Pradesh has thrilled party supporters. The waves of celebration by pro-BJP handles on social media are yet to die down. Among the posts that were shared by them include an image allegedly from the New York Stock Exchange with a digital scroll that showed the news of the BJP's win "in India's biggest state."
"Just ZOOM and see at New York Stock exchange what is displayed in digital display," the photo was captioned by a user on Facebook.
Similar posts have been archived here and here .
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found this claim to be not true. The building in the picture is not the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). The image was found online after the UP assembly elections in 2017.
We ran a keyword search on Google to find reports of assembly elections in India being displayed at the NYSE. But there were none.
"Modi wins landslide election victory in India's biggest state," the news scroll on the building read. When the line was Googled, a news report by Reuters was found. The photo story (https://reut.rs/3KKnvIl) was published on March 11, 2017. It was on this day Yogi Adityanath led BJP government retained power in Uttar Pradesh for the second time. A reverse image search of the viral photo was conducted. This led us to tweets by BJP IT wing in-charge Amit Malviya and Rajya Sabha MP Om Prakash Mathur . Both leaders had tweeted the viral photo from their verified handles on March 12, 2017. News of BJP's big win under Prime Minister Modi splashed in Canary Warf, prominent business district of London. Zoom it.. #IAmNewIndia pic.twitter.com/Z17OtsUatL — Amit Malviya (@amitmalviya) March 12, 2017 This confirmed that the viral image is old. We noticed that Amit Malviya had claimed the spot of the photograph in his tweet. He identified the place as "Canary Warf, prominent business district of London," and not the New York Stock Exchange. With the help of Google Maps, we verified the premises of both places in question. While the exterior images of the Thomson Reuters building in Canary Wharf looked very similar to the photo, the area around NYSE looked different. Neither could we find any photos of a news screen at the front side of the NYSE building. In the viral photo, the news was displayed in a single-line digital news scroll with orange text. The same was found on the Thomson Reuters building . This concluded that the photo was not taken in the United States as claimed in the post. Hence, it can be concluded that the image shared following the BJP's victory in the assembly polls to Uttar Pradesh is old. The image seen in the photograph is not the New York Stock Exchange as claimed. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow) Published By: Namrata Agarwal Published On: Mar 13, 2022 23:15 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Bengal government is not paying GST for Muslim traders
content:
West Bengal government has not taken such a decision. Ghulam Rabbani, Bengal's Minister of State for the minority affairs has confirmed this to AFWA. These claims have been making rounds on the internet since 2018.
A few days after West Bengal minister Chandrima Bhattacharya was handed over the key responsibility of the finance department, she presented her debut budget at the state assembly on Friday, March 11. Meanwhile, a screenshot has gone viral on social media claiming that the West Bengal government has waived off the GST for the Muslim traders of the state.
Social media users on Facebook and Twitter have shared a Hindi screenshot that read, "GST waived off for the Muslim traders. Mamata government will pay their GST."
The text further read, "Mamata Banerjee-led government of West Bengal has made a big decision. According to the Mamata government, the trade of Muslims was hurt by the introduction of the GST. That is why her government will pay all the due taxes of the Muslim businessmen. This means their taxes have been waived. The population of the Muslim community in Bengal has reached 35%. In such a situation, control of forming or dissolving any government is in their hands. This particular decision of the Mamata-led government proves that Bengal has indeed become an Islamic state." GST _ _ pic.twitter.com/Ugo6brVhoo — ... (@MilanProf) March 9, 2022
GST _ _ pic.twitter.com/Ugo6brVhoo — ... (@MilanProf) March 9, 2022
Archived versions of the posts can be seen here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the screenshot's content is not at all true. The West Bengal government has neither taken nor announced any such decision.
With the help of a few relevant keywords, we tried to find any reports regarding the same. But there were no media reports that supported the claim. It is unlikely that such a major decision by the state government would go unreported by news outlets.
Further search led us to some 4-year-old social media posts that made the same claim. A Twitter user had posted a cut-out of a Hindi newspaper on July 14, 2018. The headline of the story read, "The state government of West Bengal will now pay the taxes of Muslim traders." @India_Policy pic.twitter.com/p6fmClaZxn — Aditya (@arallan78) July 14, 2018
@India_Policy pic.twitter.com/p6fmClaZxn — Aditya (@arallan78) July 14, 2018
The report revealed that the then finance minister of the state, Amit Mitra, had announced some support to the traders to file GST. Thus, we ran some more keywords to know the exact quote made by Amit Mitra on the matter. But again, there was no story available regarding this.
Another striking factor in the story was a spelling mistake in its headline. The Hindi spelling of "businessmen" is wrong in the headline, which usually doesn't happen with mainstream newspapers.
We reached out to West Bengal's Minister of State for minority affairs, Ghulam Rabbani, who dismissed the claim. "These are rumours which have been spread by the opposition to defame our chief minister. Our party chief has always condemned the way GST was implemented. But claims like waving of GST from the Muslims doesn't make any sense," he said.
Thus, it becomes evident that the West Bengal government has not made any decision to waive off the GST of the Muslim traders. Although it is true that Mamata Banerjee (http://bitly.ws/show/pgUC) has often been accused by the opposition parties of doing Muslim appeasement politics in the state.
(With inputs from Yash Mittal, New Delhi) Published By: Namrata Agarwal Published On: Mar 14, 2022 00:54 IST

title: Fact Check: 2019 news clip from Haryana goes viral as proof of BJP capturing booths during UP assembly polls
content:
This news clip is from the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. It has no connection to the recent assembly election in Uttar Pradesh. In fact, it's not from UP at all. It's from Palwal in Haryana.
Allegations of booth-capturing and EVM-rigging continue to spread on social media following the sweeping electoral victory of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh.
A video of a news clip went viral along with the claim that voters were influenced by the BJP's polling agents in booths in UP. pic.twitter.com/6OyGyXhGKS — Santosh Diwate (@diwate_santosh) March 11, 2022 The clip featured a reporter talking to a group of women who complained that a polling agent named Giriraj forced them to press the button with the BJP's Lotus symbol. Sir, This is what u are talking about, #BOOTH capturing Dear PM Modi, This is how u win your election And the EC knows this & deliberately sitting silent & giving winning certificate to BJP @realumeshsingh @RoopeshSinghINC @RobbieK014 @ashharwarsi_inc @IYCLegalCell @MaryDenniz pic.twitter.com/WoRYNrASd1 — Darryl (@Trendsetting123) March 12, 2022 The captions of such viral posts said things like, "Now don't say that the secret of BJP's victory is the blessings of the people," or " Sir, This is what u are talking about, #BOOTH capturing. Dear PM Modi, This is how u win your election And the EC knows this & deliberately sitting silent & giving winning certificate to BJP." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The India Today Anti-Fake news War room ( AFWA) found that the viral news clip was from the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. In the original report, voters alleged booth-capturing in Faridabad, Haryana. The archived viral posts can be seen here and here . AFWA probe The location mentioned in the viral NDTV news clip was Faridabad, Haryana. This made it clear that the video was not related to the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls. We found the original news clip on the YouTube channel of NDTV India, uploaded on May 13, 2019. The video was titled, "The Election Commission took action after the Faridabad video of booth-capturing went viral." In the original video, a reporter spoke to a group of women who alleged that a person named Giriraj forced them to cast their votes in favour of the BJP. A minute into the YouTube video, the viral portion of the news clip was seen. We took this as a clue and looked for news reports regarding the allegations from that time. We found several news reports from 2019 . As per the reports, after a video of a person influencing voters at a booth in Palwal, Haryana went viral during the 2019 Lok Sabha polls, the Election Commission ordered re-polling. The person named Giriraj mentioned in the viral video was also arrested. Thus, it is clear that this video that went viral with allegations of booth-capturing in UP is not from the state at all. Nor is it from any of the recently-concluded assembly polls. It's from 2019. (With input from Yash Mittal) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Mar 14, 2022 20:06 IST

title: Fact Check: No, this video does not show LK Advani breaking down after watching 'The Kashmir Files'
content:
This video shows Advani at a screening of the 2020 film 'Shikara' directed by Vidhu Vinod Chopra — a film that also tackled the exodus of Kashmiri Hindus in the 90s.
Discussions on Vivek Agnihotri's new film 'The Kashmir Files', which tackles the exodus of Kashmiri Hindus in the 1990s and insurgency in the state, has dominated social media in the last few days.
Amid praise and criticism of the film, a video went viral with the claim that it showed veteran Bharatiya Janata Party leader LK Advani at a movie theatre, overcome with emotion after watching the film.
BJP leader Manish Grover, among others, shared the video with the aforementioned claim on his verified Facebook page.
The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here , here and here .
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the claim along with the video was misleading. This video is from the screening of the movie 'Shikara' in 2020. AFWA probe
We noticed that many social media users pointed out the video in circulation was old. With the help of a keyword search, we found the same video and screenshots from it carried by several news reports in 2020. As per the reports, the video of Advani breaking down is from the screening of the Vidhu Vinod Chopra-directed film 'Shikara'. This movie was based on the exodus of Kashmiri Hindus in the 90s as well.
The video was also tweeted by Chopra himself in February 2020. "Shri LK Advani at the special screening of #Shikara. We are so humbled and grateful for your blessings and your appreciation for the film Sir," the director wrote while sharing the video. Shri L K Advani at the special screening of #Shikara We are so humbled and grateful for your blessings and your appreciation for the film Sir. @foxstarhindi @rahulpandita pic.twitter.com/oUeymMayhc — Vidhu Vinod Chopra Films (@VVCFilms) February 7, 2020 In a February 2020 interview , Chopra also spoke about his relationship with Advani and how the BJP leader had helped him financially in the early years of his career. He said that this was the reason he sent Advani a special invitation for the special screening of 'Shikara'. Moreover, we couldn't find any credible report about Advani attending the screening of 'The Kashmir Files'. The official Twitter handle of Vivek Agnihotri has no mention of the veteran leader attending the film's screening. With the available information, it is clear that the video of Advani breaking down at the movie theatre is from the screening of 'Shikara', and not related to 'The Kashmir Files'. (With inputs from Anil Kumar in New Delhi) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Mar 14, 2022 20:39 IST

title: Fact Check: This Ugandan cop was NOT attacking reporters with a catapult for asking irrelevant questions
content:
In 2021, the Ugandan police seized a consignment of catapults that were supposedly meant to be used as weapons. During a press conference, Fred Enanga, a police spokesperson, demonstrated how they were used. He did not attack reporters.
An image of a man in a police uniform aiming a slingshot has gone viral with the claim that this was the Uganda police spokesperson hitting a reporter for asking "irrelevant questions."
Many on Facebook and Twitter shared this image with the caption, "Newly appointed Uganda police spokesperson hit a reporter with a catapult for asking irrelevant questions."
The India Today Anti-Fake News War room ( AFWA) found that this claim was false. In 2021, Ugandan policemen seized a shipment of catapults. During the ensuing press conference, Fred Enanga, a police spokesperson, demonstrated how they were used.
The viral posts are archived here and here .
With the help of a keyword search, we found the original video of the Uganda police press conference uploaded to the YouTube channel of UBC Television Uganda on April 13, 2021. As per the details given alongside, Uganda cops were investigating a criminal gang that was allegedly "trading terror activities using catapults to destabilize the country."
While addressing the media during a weekly brief, a police spokesperson, Fred Enanga, said suspects were apprehended in the matter and the police were trying to look for the rest of the gang members.
In the YouTube video, we can see the police officers demonstrating to the reporters present during the media briefing the capabilities of the slingshots.
This incident was reported by several news outlets in 2021. Enanga, during the briefing, said that the catapults or slingshots were "capable of firing metallic projectiles or bearings," which made them deadly, "once possessed and used by the wrong elements." Thus, we can conclude that the viral posts falsely claimed the policeman was attacking reporters for supposedly asking irrelevant questions. title: No, this video doesn't show US army troops paradropping into Ukraine during ongoing war
content:
The video was shot in 2016 from the Fort Bragg base in North Carolina in the US. It shows the Airborne Division perform static line jumps over the base's Sicily Drop Zone. It is unrelated to the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine.
Recently, US President Joe Biden moved 12,000 troops along the borders with Russia, such as Latvia, Estonia, Lithuania, and Romania, vowing to "defend every inch of NATO territory — every single inch."
Despite the White House's refusal to make a military intervention in Ukraine, a video has gone viral on social media featuring soldiers being paradropped from a Globemaster III aircraft. Several posts on social media claim this video shows US soldiers landing in Ukraine. One such post can be seen here .
The India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found the claim to be false. This video is from 2016 and shows the Airborne units of the US military making a static line jump. It is unrelated to the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. AFWA Probe
First, we checked if the US had announced a military intervention in Ukraine. Using advanced search on Google, we filtered out the latest developments on the subject. However, there were no such news reports.
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes gave several results. This included articles on a YouTube video released in 2016 about the mobile game Pokemon GO. The video was released by animator Nicholas King aka 'Nickels', who combined CGI with original footage of paratroopers to create a dark comedy about how common Pokemons were distributed. We identified that the frame in which the Pokemons are loaded on the aircraft looked similar to a scene in the viral video. The background of both these frames looked the same. The video was uploaded on Nickel's YouTube channel on August 8, 2016.
The video was uploaded on Nickel's YouTube channel on August 8, 2016.
We also found a webpage called 'Wordless Tech' that had a similar photo. The page was titled 'Paratroopers Static Line Jump'. Published on July 28, 2016, the image was a screenshot from the video in which soldiers boarded the plane.
"Watch those paratroopers performing static line jumps from C-17 Globemaster III aircraft. They are from the 82nd and 101st Airborne Division, jumping over Sicily Drop Zone at Fort Bragg, North Carolina," the webpage read.
Pursing this clue, we looked up Fort Bragg military installation on Google Maps. Using 3D satellite and Street View options, we discovered that the buildings and lamb poles of Fort Bragg's Pope Army Airfield looked similar to the ones in the video.
The Wordless Tech page also had a link to a YouTube page. This took us to a longer version of the video that went viral as the American intervention in the Russia-Ukraine war. The verified page of AiirSource Military , which has 39.7 lakh subscribers, uploaded the video on May 28, 2016.
The description of the video was the same as the one found on Wordless Tech.
Hence, we concluded that this video had nothing to do with the Russia-Ukraine war — it was almost six years old. Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Mar 15, 2022 20:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of exorcism passed off as forced conversion of Hindu girl in Pakistan
content:
While incidents of forced conversion have been reported in Pakistan, this video does not show that. It shows an act of exorcism. The man seen torturing the girl is Haji Muhammad Ullah, a self-proclaimed exorcist from the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region of Pakistan.
Atrocities on minorities in Pakistan, particularly forced conversions of Hindu minor girls, have been reported widely inside and outside Pakistan . Recently, a video of a girl being tortured by two men went viral with the claim that this was a Hindu girl being electrocuted to forcibly convert her to Islam. Several Twitter and Facebook users shared the viral video with claims like, "Viral Video from Pakistan: How Muslims torture Hindu girls by giving electric shocks to forcibly convert them to Islam. This video is from KPK, Pakistan". The India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found that this video does not show the forced conversion of a Hindu girl. It shows an exorcism ritual. The man seen torturing the girl is Haji Muhammad Ullah, a self-proclaimed exorcist from the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region of Pakistan. AFWA probe We found this video was also shared on Reddit , where several people claimed it did not capture forced conversion, rather it showed exorcism. One Reddit user referred to the conversation in the viral video, which is in mixed Pashto language, and commented that the people in the video were talking about demons. Another Reddit user claimed the man in the video was a known Pakistani exorcist called Haji Muhammad Ullah. Taking this as a clue, we looked up Haji Muhammad Ullah on social media. A self-proclaimed exorcist of Achini Meira area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Pakistan, this man has a YouTube channel with over 80,000 subscribers. He also has a Facebook page with over 11 lakh followers and an Instagram account . His YouTube and Facebook pages are full of similar videos that show him supposedly treating people with "mystical powers". He claimed to have special powers to cure people who were ill and possessed by "evil spirits". We could not find the exact viral video in any of his social media accounts. But comparing other similar videos of exorcism from his YouTube channel with the viral one, we are confirmed that it was the same room with the same carpet and wall paint. We tried to decipher the conversation in the viral video with the help of the Azure video analyzer for media , but the results didn't yield much. We then sought the help of Ahmad Sahel Arman , an Afghani journalist from Kabul who is versed in the Pashto language. As per Arman, the language in the video was mixed Pakistani-Pashto. The girl in the video claimed she was possessed by spirits. The man then tried to cure her allegedly using mystical powers. Subsequently, the girl chanted Allah's name. We tried to contact the Haji Muhammad Ullah over the phone in Pakistan, but he was unreachable. We will update the story accordingly if he responds. We can, however, conclude that the viral video has nothing to do with conversion. It is an exorcism ritual captured on video. title: Fact Check: No, Centre is NOT offering interest-free loans under KCC scheme from April 1
content:
The Centre has not made any such announcement. Farmers have to pay an interest of 7% p.a. (provided the government gives a subsidy of 2%) for loans up to Rs. 3 lakhs for 5 years. If farmers repay the first loan on time, the second loan comes at an interest rate of 4% p.a.
A screengrab from a newspaper has been going viral that states that from April 1, the Centre will offer loans at zero per cent under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme. The screengrab was shared along with captions that expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. One such post's caption said in Hindi: "Honourable Prime Minister, we are grateful to you." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim to be misleading. No such announcement has been made by the union government. Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here . AFWA PROBE
A screengrab from a newspaper has been going viral that states that from April 1, the Centre will offer loans at zero per cent under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme.
The screengrab was shared along with captions that expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. One such post's caption said in Hindi: "Honourable Prime Minister, we are grateful to you."
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim to be misleading. No such announcement has been made by the union government. Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here . AFWA PROBE
While investigating the claim, we first conducted a keyword search to find out whether the government had made any such announcements recently. We did not find a single news report or government press release that stated the government was offering an interest-free loan under the KCC scheme.
To understand the present interest structure of loans under the KCC scheme, we visited the website of the State Bank of India.
The SBI website stated that farmers could avail loans up to Rs 3 lakhs under the KCC scheme at an interest of seven per cent if the union government gave a subsidy of two per cent per annum on it. This meant that the actual interest rate was nine per cent per annum. The website was last updated on March 11, 2022, at the time of writing this.
According to news reports, under the KCC scheme, farmers could avail loans up to Rs. 3 lakhs in five years for an interest rate of only four per cent per annum. However, for this to apply, farmers needed to repay their existing loans on time. If the farmer repaid the initial loan on time, he could get a rebate of three per cent. In this case, the farmer would need to pay interest at the rate of four per cent per annum only. To further confirm the claim, we got in touch with an SBI spokesperson. "No, we have not received any such circular yet that states loans under KCC would be interest-free from April 1, 2022," the SBI spokesperson told India Today. Hence, we can conclude that the claim of this post is misleading. The union government has not made any announcement on providing interest-free loans under the KCC scheme. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in Lucknow) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Mar 16, 2022 21:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Here's why viral RTI reply says only 89 Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants in J&K
content:
The RTI reply provides the figure of deaths since 1990 — it does not include deaths from 1989. That's why the death toll of Kashmiri Pandits appears low. As per news reports, J&K police said that over 200 Kashmiri Pandits have been killed since 1989.
Vivek Agnihotri's new film, 'The Kashmir Files', has brought the killings and the exodus of Kashmiri Pandits in the late 80s and the early 90s into the mainstream and discussions around it have dominated social media since its release. Amid the discussion, an image of an RTI response has gone viral on social media with the claim that only 89 Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants in Jammu and Kashmir. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story While this figure has been quoted by many, some raised doubts on social media about its authenticity, asking if the figure accounted for Kashmiri Pandits killed in Srinagar alone or in the whole of Jammu and Kashmir. Several Facebook users shared the photo of the viral RTI response with captions like, "Kashmir Police replies in the RTI on Kashmiri Pandits' killing. Total Pandits killed = 89, Total other faiths killed = 1635." The India Today Anti-Fake News War Room ( AFWA) found that the RTI response provided the death toll since 1990 and did not include killings in 1989. The viral posts are archived here , here and here . What did the RTI reply say? Last year, RTI activist PP Kapoor from Haryana's Samalkha (Panipat), raised multiple queries in his RTI application regarding the rehabilitation and migration of Kashmiri Pandits and others in the valley. One of the queries asked for the "number of Kashmiri Pandits who were killed by terrorist attacks". The DSP of the district police headquarters in Srinagar informed in the RTI reply on November 27, 2021, that number of "Kashmiri Pandits who were killed by terrorist attacks since the inception of militancy 1990 = 89". It is to be noted that the RTI activist did not ask about the number of deaths of Kashmiri Pandits starting from a particular year. In the reply, the J&K police provided figures only from 1990 and excluded the year 1989. AFWA got in touch with Kapoor over the phone, who has confirmed that the figure quoted in the RTI reply projected the number of Kashmiri Pandits killed in the entire state and not of Srinagar alone unlike as perceived by several netizens. How many Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants? As per news reports which quoted the J&K police and the state government, over 200 Kashmiri Pandits have been killed due to militancy since 1989. As per a report published in The Indian Express in 2008 , "Jammu and Kashmir Police report says that 209 Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants since 1989." According to this report, "of the 209 Kashmiri Pandits killed, 109 died in 1990." That means that over 100 people were killed in 1989 alone — something that was not covered in the 2021 RTI response. A 2010 report from journalist Shujaat Bukhari in The Hindu quoted data provided by the Jammu and Kashmir government that said 219 Kashmiri Pandits had been killed by militants since 1989. Replying to a question from People's Democratic Party member Syed Basharat Bukhari, then Revenue Minister Raman Bhalla told the Assembly in Jammu that "219 Pandits were killed in Kashmir from 1989 to 2004." Shujaat Bukhari , who wrote the aforementioned report, was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in Srinagar in 2018. Thus, it is clear that the wide gap in the number of Kashmiri Pandits killed as per news reports and as per the RTI response is different because of the base years that have been taken into account in each. That's why the death toll appears low in the RTI reply that has gone viral. Published By: tanishka Published On: Mar 17, 2022 12:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Old incident of diplomat's arrest in Ukraine for smuggling revived amid ongoing war
content:
This incident of arrest and seizure by Ukrainian authorities took place in February 2021 near the Ukraine-Poland border. Recently, Ukraine's State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) donated $1 million seized from that incident to the armed forces.
A photo of a box full of currency notes has gone viral on social media with the claim that Ukrainian authorities arrested a diplomat who was trying to smuggle money and gold from the country. Several Twitter users shared the image with captions like: "The Ukrainian Investigative Bureau has arrested a Ukrainian diplomat while he was trying to smuggle $140,000, 68,000 euros, 12 kilograms of gold bars and 13.8 kilograms of gold jewellery." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The India Today Anti-Fake News War room ( AFWA) found that the claimed arrest and seizure by Ukrainian authorities actually took place in February 2021 near the Ukraine-Poland border. The viral posts are archived here and here . AFWA PROBE With the help of a keywords search, we came across a Ukrainian news report titled, "The DBR will transfer $1 million of the seized funds to the Armed Forces". As per the report, the State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) had confiscated about $1 million worth of gold and foreign currency, and valuables from a Ukrainian embassy employee in the EU last year. "At the Yahodyn checkpoint on February 28, 2021, during a search of a diplomatic minibus, DBR investigators found and seized almost 68,000, more than $140,000, more than 12 kg of gold bars, and gold jewellery weighing 13.8 kg," the report said. Taking this as a clue, we looked up the website and the social media accounts of Ukraine's State Bureau of Investigation (DBR). The DBR announced a donation of $1 million to the Ukrainian government for the army's needs on March 17. The Facebook page of the DBR also shared details about this donation. It confirmed that the DBR had seized gold and currency worth about $1 million from one of the employees of the Ukrainian Embassy in the EU who attempted to illegally take them abroad. Now "these funds are transferred to the state budget and can be used for the needs of the Armed Forces of Ukraine," a post on the DBR's Facebook page read. "At the checkpoint of Yagodin of the Volyn Customs Service on February 28, last year, investigators of the DBR conducted an inspection of a diplomatic minibus, in which almost 68 thousand euros, over 140 thousand US dollars, over 12 kilograms of gold bars and gold jewellery with a total weight of 13.8 kg, and a lot of cigarettes were seized," a rough translation of the post said. This seizure was a joint operation conducted by the Security Service of Ukraine (SSU) and the DBR. Both the SSU's and the DBR's Twitter accounts had posted about this operation on March 1, 2021. The verified YouTube channel of the SSU had shared a video of the seizure on March 1, 2021. The details given in the YouTube video were the same that shared by the DBR in their press note recently about the donation. The same incident was also reported by international news agencies last year. Thus, it is clear that an old incident of an arrest of a diplomat was falsely claimed to be recent. Published By: Abhishek Chakraborty Published On: Mar 18, 2022 13:12 IST

title: Fact Check: This is not Russia preparing mass graves for its soldiers killed in Ukraine war
content:
This is a 2021 video from Russia's Surgut city. According to its Mayor, the graves were dug ahead of the 2021 winter. He said the practice is common in northern cities of Russia where winters are harsh.
More than 150,000 troops are deployed by Russia as part of its war efforts in Ukraine. As per the American intelligence estimates, the invasion army has already lost over 7,000 personnel since the start of the war.
Amid this revelation by the media , a video of long rows of dug graves is circulated on social media with the claim that it was prepared by the Russian government for their soldiers brought dead from Ukraine.
One such post on Facebook that received over 270K views until the time of filing this story can be seen below.
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the claim along with the video is misleading. This video has been on the internet at least since 2021. According to Russian authorities, it showed a common practice in the northern cities of Russia where graves are dug ahead of the winter.
We did a reverse search of the keyframes of the viral video and found the same video shared by Russian social media handles at least since October 2021. This confirmed that the video is old and not related to the Russia-Ukraine war that started in February 2022.
Some netizens who posted the video in 2021 also claimed that the video is from Russia's Surgut. https://t.co/phYBnevUZb — @MagyarMaidan (@MagyarMaidan) October 9, 2021
https://t.co/phYBnevUZb — @MagyarMaidan (@MagyarMaidan) October 9, 2021
Using online tools Live Transcribe and Google Translator we translated the audio component of the video shared in 2021. According to the audio, the graves were prepared in a city cemetery in Surgut "ahead of the fourth wave of Covid-19."
However, we found some other responses to the video which stated that the winter in Surgut is harsh and hence the graves are dug in advance as a common practice.
We further checked the Instagram handle of Surgut Mayor Andrey Filatov and found the same video of mass graves in question posted by him on March 7, 2022.
In his clarification note, Filatov stated that the video was from 2021 and it showed graves being dug ahead of winter in Surgut. He added that such practices were common for at least a decade and a half in northern cities of Russia where winter is extreme.
The clarification was posted along with the clipping from an interview provided by him to a channel regarding the video. View this post on Instagram A post shared by (@filatov_surgut)
A post shared by (@filatov_surgut)
The explanation provided by the Mayor in the Russian language was loosely translated as, "For several days now, a fake video has been circulating on the Internet claiming that the Surgut cemetery is being prepared to receive the soldiers who died during the special operation. I declare unequivocally that this information is false. The video is indeed from our cemetery, but the footage is from last year. We already commented on them in September 2021. At that time, the graves were being prepared for winter. This is a standard procedure for earthworks in northern cities. Due to the fact that we have rather low temperatures in winter, all work of this specific nature is carried out in advance. This has been practised for at least 15 years."
Multiple Russian news portals have also published this clarification provided by the Mayor of Surgut. The reports also confirms that in winter the ground in this region freezes, making it difficult to dig graves.
It is hence clear that the video in question is old and not related to the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Mar 20, 2022 05:19 IST

title: Fact Check: These minors thrashed by UP police in Chandauli was not due to sloganeering for Pakistan
content:
The viral video is related to an incident that took place in Chandauli in 2021. Two cops of UP police were suspended for thrashing two minors over allegations of theft. The incident has no connection to any incidents of slogans raised in favour of Pakistan.
A disturbing video of police atrocities against two people has gone viral with the claim that UP policemen are thrashing them for shouting slogans in favour of Pakistan.
Multiple Twitter and Facebook users have posted this viral clip along with the Hindi caption that reads, "UP police is teaching them a lesson for shouting slogans in favour of Pakistan".
The 2021 incident has no connection to any pro-Pakistan sloganeering.
With the help of keywords search, India Today found a couple of news reports along with the same video or the screen grab of the viral video. The Hindi news portal " Amar Ujala ", used a screengrab of the same viral video and published a news report on May 2, 2021.
As per the news report, this incident took place in Balua Police station area of UP's Chandauli district. Following an allegation of a theft in a mobile store in that area, the local police chowki in-charge Shivanand Verma and constable Dilip Kumar reached the spot and brutally thrashed two suspects. The video of the police atrocities was caught on camera and went viral.
According to the Chandauli police, the two personnel were suspended after a departmental inquiry.
The Chandrauli Police refuted the claim that the incident was linked to pro-Pakistan sloganeering, as had been claimed by social media users. @UPPViralCheck https://t.co/7Tx0ncnOOg pic.twitter.com/CointCNYZY — Chandauli Police (@chandaulipolice) March 20, 2022
@UPPViralCheck https://t.co/7Tx0ncnOOg pic.twitter.com/CointCNYZY — Chandauli Police (@chandaulipolice) March 20, 2022
The Times of India had reported the same incident along with the viral video on May 6, 2021. The headline of the video story reads, " UP: Cops brutally beat up minors over mobile theft allegation, video goes viral"
Thus, it is confirmed that an old incident related to theft and police atrocities against minors has gone viral with a communal twist. Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Mar 20, 2022 19:18 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Bhagwant Mann isn't the youngest Chief Minister in Punjab's history
content:
SAD leader Parkash Singh Badal holds the record of being the youngest CM in the history of Punjab. When he entered office in 1970, Senior Badal was only 43 years old.
Social media is abuzz with posts of appreciation and wishes for the new AAP government in Punjab. The new chief minister, Bhagwant Mann, was sworn-in on March 16, Wednesday, at Bhagat Singh's ancestral village, Khatkar Kalan.
Among these were posts that congratulated the AAP leader on becoming the youngest Chief Minister of Punjab. "Bhagwant Singh Mann has been elected the 28th Chief Minister of Punjab. He's also been honoured as the youngest CM of Punjab, by becoming the CM at the age of 48," one such poster in Punjabi read.
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room has found that the claim is misleading. The record of being the youngest chief minister of Punjab is held by Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) patriarch Parkash Singh Badal. When sworn in as the chief minister in 1970, Senior Badal was 43 years old. AFWA Probe
While checking, we learned that Bhagwant Mann is actually 48 years old, as claimed in the post. He was born on October 17, 1973. However, there were no reports in the mainstream media that called him the youngest chief minister of Punjab. This was a major hint that the claim could be inaccurate, as it is unlikely for news organisations to skip such feats. No official handles of the AAP claimed to have given Punjab the youngest CM ever.
We looked up the list of chief ministers of Punjab, which showed that senior SAD leader Parkash Singh Badal had held the office at the age of 43.
Using Google keyword search, we retrieved more information on the topic. Following 94-year-old Parkash Badal's defeat from his bastion of Lambi in the 2022 Assembly polls, several national dailies pointed out his unique achievement of being chief minister at age 43. Given below are news reports that name the nonagenarian as the youngest CM in the state.
Born on December 8, 1927, Senior Badal became a legislator for the first time in 1957. The five-time CM's first tenure in office was from 1970 to 1971-- when he was 43 years old.
"From 1970-71, Badal became the youngest chief minister of an Indian state. He first became chief minister of Punjab in March 1970 and headed a coalition government of Akali Dal [Sant] and Jana Sangh," an India Today article published on the leader's 89th birthday said.
We further confirmed the information on the official website of SAD. "He has been the chief minister of the state from 1970 to 1971, from 1977 to 1980, from 1997 to 2002, and from 2007 to 2017 [two consecutive terms]... In 1970, he became the youngest chief minister of an Indian state," his profile on the party website read.
Hence, it can be concluded that AAP's Bhagwant Mann isn't the youngest chief minister in the history of Punjab. The unique record is held by Parkash Singh Badal.
(With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi) Published By: tanishka Published On: Mar 20, 2022 20:19 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Malaysia hasn't agreed to hand over Zakir Naik to India
content:
There are no recent reports of India engaging Malaysia over the extradition of Zakir Naik. The footage in circulation is from 2018. Two days after airing this story, ABP News, among other media outlets, confirmed the Malaysian government rejecting Naik's deportation to India.
Several social media users recently claimed that controversial Islamic televangelist and preacher Zakir Naik is being extradited to India from Malaysia. The claim, shared along with the footage of a news report by ABP Live, hailed the Narendra Modi-led government for this. "Zakir Naik being brought back to India another achievement by MODI govt.. burnol stocks for liberals needed," one such tweet said. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Similar claims have been archived here and here . The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim misleading. The news clip shared was from 2018. AFWA Probe Naik is wanted in India for hate speech, money laundering, and terror-related activities . We first looked for recent news reports on Naik. We set the Google custom time range to just the past month in our search. However, there were no reports by any mainstream news outlet. Since the video circulated along with the claim belonged to ABP Live, we checked the channel's Facebook page next. When we searched with his name, we found the news report in question was uploaded to the page on July 4, 2018.

Naik is wanted in India for hate speech, money laundering, and terror-related activities . We first looked for recent news reports on Naik. We set the Google custom time range to just the past month in our search. However, there were no reports by any mainstream news outlet.
Since the video circulated along with the claim belonged to ABP Live, we checked the channel's Facebook page next. When we searched with his name, we found the news report in question was uploaded to the page on July 4, 2018.
We ran a keyword search with a time range set to 2018. This led us to a report by Alt News from 2021 that debunked a similar claim about Zakir Naik's extradition. We found that the picture of Naik and the logo of a Facebook page on the video fact-checked by Alt News was the same as those on the videos shared now. The source of this video was a Facebook page called "Phir Ek Bar Modi Sarkar".
Hence, it became clear that the video was not new at all. We also found several news reports of then-Malaysian PM Mahathir Mohamad rejecting Naik's deportation to India. "As long as he is not creating any problem, we will not deport him because he has been given permanent residency status," the leader said at the time . These reports stated that India tried to get Naik from Malaysia via the extradition treaty between the two countries. On July 6, ABP Live also published a similar report that confirmed Malaysia's unwillingness to hand over Naik to India. This story can be read here. There was also a 2019 report in the Economic Times that said Mahathir denied PM Modi asking for Naik's extradition. He said that Modi made no extradition request when they met at Russia's Vladivostok during an economic forum. Thus, it can be safely concluded that India has not recently engaged Malaysia over the extradition of Zakir Naik. The news footage shared by several users is from 2018. title: Fact Check: Rahul Gandhi mocked on social media with clipped video from 2020
content:
The viral video is clipped. In the original speech, delivered in Jaipur Rajasthan on January 28, 2020, Gandhi made the faux pas but immediately corrected himself.
A video of Rahul Gandhi has been doing rounds on social media in which, he can be heard saying, "Not only in Hindustan, the Indian youth can bring change to the entire nation."
Several social media users shared the video, mocking Rahul Gandhi.
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral video was clipped. In the original video, the Congress leader corrected himself within moments of this faux pas.
Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here . AFWA PROBE
While investigating the claim, we first noticed that the podium in front of Gandhi mentioned the words "Yuva Aakrosh Rally" and the date "January 28".
Taking this as a cue, we conducted a keyword search and found the original video uploaded to YouTube on January 28, 2020. Caption with this video reads, "Shri Rahul Gandhi addresses Yuva Aakrosh Rally in Jaipur, Rajasthan."
At the 2:35 minutes mark in this video Rahul Gandhi could be seen making the statement given in the viral video.
In the original video, Gandhi first stated, "Not only in Hindustan, but the Indian youth can also bring change to the entire nation." However, he immediately corrected himself and said, "Not only in India, but the Indian youth can also bring changes to the whole world."
Hence, we can conclude that the claim with this video is misleading. The viral video is a clipped version of the original video. In the original video, Gandhi corrected his mistake immediately after saying it. Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Mar 21, 2022 21:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Simulated video of Ethiopian plane crash shared as final moments before Chinese Boeing 737 crash
content:
This is a simulation video of the deadly Ethiopian Airlines plane crash that took place on March 10, 2019. This simulation video was made using X-Plane 11, a computer program.
A passenger plane with over 130 people on board crashed on Monday afternoon, March 21, in a mountainous area of China. The Boeing 737 plane, operated by China Eastern Airlines, reportedly went down in Guangxi , an autonomous region in southern China.
Even as casualties remained unknown at the time of writing this, a ten-second-long video allegedly from the ill-fated flight went viral on social media.
The video , which appears to be taken from the window of a plane, captured the sound of crying passengers. The first few seconds of the video showed the plane tumbling towards the ground. It crashed right before the ten-second mark. A Boeing 737 just crashed in southern China. This was one of the last moment recorded on the plane. maybe the only moment. Viewers' discretion advised. pic.twitter.com/rzdRpNBEem — A Bass (@chanteur_sagi) March 21, 2022 "A Boeing 737 just crashed in southern China. This was one of the last moments recorded on the plane. maybe the only moment. Viewers' discretion advised," a Twitter user wrote sharing the video. Archived versions of similar claims can be seen here and here . The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found this claim to be false. The viral video was a computer-generated simulation of another plane crash that took place nearly three years ago. AFWA Probe As per news reports, the Chinese plane crashed into a mountain. But in the viral video, we could barely see any mountainous terrain. In the comments under the video, many stated that the video was that of a crashing Ethiopian Airlines plane. Others suggested it was a simulated clip. Taking this as a cue, we looked for images of Ethiopian Airlines. We compared the logo of Ethiopian Airlines with the logo that appeared on the plane's wing in the viral video and found them to be the same. So, does this video capture the final moments of an Ethiopian Airlines plane crash? No. We reverse-searched frames from the viral video, and it took us to a YouTube video uploaded to a channel called Bull Bosphorus on March 11, 2019. The video was a simulation of the Ethiopian Airlines crash that occurred on March 10, 2019. A Boeing 737 Max crashed and claimed the lives of 157 people. In the simulation, the viral clip appears at the 9:33 mark. It was clearly asserted in the description of the video: "This is not exactly what happened, this is only a simulated flight crash for Ethiopian Airlines flight ET302." Therefore, it can be concluded that the simulated video of the 2019 Ethiopian crash was falsely shared as the recent crash in Southern China. title: Fact Check: Video earlier claimed to be from Russia-Ukraine war now shared as crashing Chinese Boeing
content:
This video has been on the internet since March 13, 2022, at least. It was earlier shared as a Russian jet shot down by Ukraine forces in Kharkiv.
A China Eastern Airlines' Boeing 737-800 aircraft carrying 132 people crashed on March 21 in South China's Guangxi region. An official statement on the cause of the accident and the number of dead is still awaited. No survivors were found in the crash at the time of writing this.
Amid this, a video of an aeroplane crashing down vertically was circulated on social media with claims that it showed the ill-fated Chinese plane.
The archived version of the post can be seen here .
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim along with the video to be misleading. This is an old video that has also been circulated as from the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict.
We ran a reverse image search of the keyframes of the video in question and found the same video uploaded by several social media users at least since March 13, 2022. This confirmed that the video is old and not related to the March 21 plane crash in China. As per these posts , the video shows a Russian jet shot down by Ukraine forces in Kharkiv.
Berlin-based journalist Julian Röpcke tweeted the same video on March 13 as from the Ukraine-Russia war. He also tweeted a second video saying it showed the two pilots of the jet on their way down on parachutes. Zwei Piloten an Fallschirmen auf dem Weg nach unten. pic.twitter.com/pbsJJfuMvi — Julian Röpcke (@JulianRoepcke) March 13, 2022

The report also reiterated that the video showed a two-manned Russian jet being shot down by Ukraine's defence forces.
As per this report, on the same day, Kharkiv's regional governor Oleh Synyehubov through Telegram confirmed that a Russian jet had been shot down in the region. While we couldn't independently verify the source of the video in question, it is clear that the video is old and not related to the Boeing 737 crash in China.

title: Fact Check: No, Arvind Kejriwal did not pay tribute to Bhagat Singh with his shoes on
content:
The photo was taken on March 13, when Kejriwal and Mann together visited Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar. They both paid their tributes to Bhagat Singh in Khatkar Kalan on March 16. Kejriwal was seen not wearing shoes while doing so.
A photo of new Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann and Aam Aadmi Party supremo and Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal has been making the rounds of social media with a questionable claim.
Some shared the photo claiming that, unlike his party colleagues, Kejriwal wore shoes while paying tribute to Indian revolutionary Bhagat Singh. ... pic.twitter.com/8DoS8P3CcO — Dinesh Chauhan (@dinesh_chauhan) March 20, 2022
... pic.twitter.com/8DoS8P3CcO — Dinesh Chauhan (@dinesh_chauhan) March 20, 2022
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the photo was not related to the claim in any way. The photo was taken on March 13 at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar.
Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here .
While investigating the claim, we first reverse-searched the image and found the same image was published by the Dainik Jagaran on March 14.
The caption did not give us a clear indication of the exact location of the photo. However, it was clear that the photo was taken on March 13, the day Kejriwal and Mann paid visits to the Golden Temple, Jallianwala Bagh, and the Durgiana Temple in Amritsar.
To further confirm the exact location of the photo, we got in touch with Amit Sharma, the AajTak correspondent in Amritsar, who confirmed, "This photo was taken in Jallianwala Bagh."
Taking it as a cue, we conducted another keyword search and found a Facebook video that captured their visit.
At the 6:25 mark in this video, we can see the same red building in the background that's also visible in the viral image. Even the floor design, visible in the video, looked similar to the viral image. PAYING TRIBUTE TO BHAGAT SINGH
This brings us to the next question: Did Arvind Kejriwal recently pay tribute to Bhagat Singh?
We conducted a keyword search and found a few news reports that said Kejriwal was present in Khatkar Kalan, the native village of freedom fighter Bhagat Singh, on March 16. He was there to grace the swearing-in ceremony of Bhagwant Mann.
Prior to this event, Kejriwal and Mann paid homage at the memorial of Bhagat Singh in Khatkar Kalan.
We found a video uploaded to the official Facebook page of the Aam Aadmi Party on March 16 where Kejriwal and Mann could be seen paying tribute to Bhagat Singh.
In this video, both Kejriwal and Mann can be seen wearing different attires from that in the viral image. More importantly, Kejriwal was not wearing his shoes while paying tribute to Bhagat Singh.
Hence, we concluded that the claim along with the photo was false. The photo was taken on March 13, when Kejriwal and Mann visited the Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar. Both paid tribute to Bhagat Singh in Khatkar Kalan on March 16.

title: Fact Check: These saffron-clad bikers are not en route to Telangana from Maharashtra following Shivaji statue row
content:
This video has been available online since 2020 and is claimed to be of Shivaji Jayanti celebrations in Maharashtra's Nandgaon. There are no reports of inter-state movement by any group in the wake of violence in Bodhan.
Twelve people were arrested in four cases after two groups engaged each other physically in Telangana's Nizamabad district over the installation of a Shivaji statue. The issue boiled over to Nizamabad's Bodhan town on Sunday , March 20, where Section 144 was imposed by the police to avoid further untoward incidents.
Amid this, a video went viral on social media allegedly showing Hindu groups en route to Bodhan from Maharashtra. "Thousands of Hindu brothers are arriving in Bodhan from Maharashtra," one such post was captioned.
Similar claims have been archived here and here .
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the claim was misleading. This video has been in circulation online since at least 2020.
We started by checking for reports on the movement of pro-Shivaji groups from Maharashtra to Telangana or Andhra Pradesh. We did not find anything relevant. All stories we came across were about the state of affairs in Bodhan .
Then, we ran a reverse search of the video's keyframes. Among the results were a few YouTube uploads that claimed the video was shot in Maharashtra's Nandgaon during the Shivaji Jayanti celebrations in 2020.
"SHIV JAYANTHI UTSAW (NANDGAON)," the title of a video uploaded on February 27, 2020 read.
"Nandgaon bike rally for shiv jayanti," another video uploaded on March 14, 2020, was titled.
We searched with these keywords on YouTube and found a few more versions of the same video that didn't pop up on Google. Shivaji Jayanti falls on February 19. All the videos were uploaded on days after February 19, 2020, we confirmed.
We conducted another round of reverse search of the video's keyframes using combinations of keywords in Marathi and English to spot authentic reports on the video's origin. However, we couldn't find any.
This report will be updated once the source is confirmed.
However, it can be safely concluded that the video of saffron-clad bikers is not associated with the row over Shivaji's statue in Telangana's Bodhan.

title: Fact Check: Old image from Australia passed off as Ukrainian firefighters amid ongoing war
content:
This is a 2019 photo of three exhausted Australian firefighters battling bushfires in Tasmania.
As Ukraine continues to resist the Russian aggression, several firefighters from other European countries have reportedly come forward to help the firefighters of Ukraine . Amid this, an image of three exhausted-looking firefighters has gone viral with the claim that these are Ukrainian firefighters and rescuers.
Several Facebook users shared the photo with the same claim.
ALSO READ | Fact Check: This is not Russia preparing mass graves for its soldiers killed in Ukraine war
The India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found that the viral image does not show the firefighters from Ukraine. This is a 2019 photo of three Australian firefighters battling bushfires in Tasmania.
With the help of reverse image search, we found that this image was shared by an Australian music band called The Wolfe Brothers on their Facebook page on February 1, 2019. As per this Facebook post, this image is of three firefighters in Tasmania who were fighting a wild bushfire. The post also said that this photo was captured by another firefighter, John Lyons.
Taking this as a clue, with the help of a keywords search, we found a news report with the same viral image published on an Australian news portal called SBSNews on February 3, 2019.
According to this news report, this is photo showed worn-out Tasmanian firefighters who were struggling to control several bushfires in the state. The report also said, "The photo, taken by firefighter John Lyons and shared by The Wolfe Brothers, shows Jason Luck, John Kroczewski, Paul Catteral covered in ash."
ALSO READ | Fact Check: Video earlier claimed to be from Russia-Ukraine war now shared as crashing Chinese Boeing
The same image was also published in the Daily Mail on February 3, 2019, with the headline, "The unsung heroes of this great nation: Photo of three exhausted firefighters covered in soot goes viral as Tasmania is ravaged by out-of-control blazes."
The incident of bushfires in Tasmania was reported by The Guardian. Reportedly, about 520 crews worked on more than 50 fires. About 173,000 hectares were burnt across Tasmania, the report said.
As per the Fire Centre Research Hub of Australia, these fires were ignited by lightning storms in December 28, 2018, January 16, 2019, and January 29, 2019.
Thus, it is clear that an old image of Australian firefighters from Tasmania has been passed off as Ukrainian firefighters. title: Fact Check: Old video of Gaza bombing goes viral as Russian airstrike on Ukraine's Ministry of Defence building
content:
This video shows how Israeli airstrikes razed the Al-Shorouk Tower in Gaza in May 2021. No credible news report as of March 23 confirmed the Ministry of Defence building in Kyiv was hit by Russian missiles.
Amid the intense Russian-Ukraine war, a dramatic video of airstrikes levelling a multistoried building has gone viral with the claim that it showed Russian missiles razing the Ministry of Defence building in Ukraine.
Several Facebook users shared this video with captions like: "Three missiles, the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense building was instantly razed to the ground. Before the Russian troops launched the missile, they did two strange things: 1. Notify foreign reporters to shoot nearby. 2. Notify all people in the building to evacuate. The missile accurately blasted the ground floor and caused the building to collapse, and finally shot the middle. Not an indiscriminate shooting, it is purely to shock Ukraine!"
The India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found this video showed Israeli airstrikes razing the Al-Shorouk Tower in Gaza in May 2021. No credible news report at the time of writing this on March 23 confirmed if the Ministry of Defence building in Kyiv was hit by Russian missiles.
The viral posts are archived here and here .
With the help of the InVid tool and reverse image search, we found that the same video has been on the internet since May 2021. We found the video uploaded to Daily Motion in May 2021 as an Israeli bombing in Gaza.
The same video was posted by the verified Twitter handle of ABC News on May 14, 2021. The tweet said, "Video shows the moment an Israeli airstrike hit and levelled the 14-story Al-Shorouk Tower in Gaza amid an escalating conflict between Israel and Hamas." Video shows the moment an Israeli airstrike hit and leveled the 14-story Al-Shorouk Tower in Gaza amid an escalating conflict between Israel and Hamas. https://t.co/Zwdwp29nE2 pic.twitter.com/O3xPEoCR20 — ABC News (@ABC) May 13, 2021
Video shows the moment an Israeli airstrike hit and leveled the 14-story Al-Shorouk Tower in Gaza amid an escalating conflict between Israel and Hamas. https://t.co/Zwdwp29nE2 pic.twitter.com/O3xPEoCR20 — ABC News (@ABC) May 13, 2021
Several international media outlets reported this incident.
According to media reports , the Al-Shorouk Towe r, a major media hub in one of Gaza's busiest neighbourhoods collapsed after being hit by the missiles during airstrikes carried out by Israel Defence Force (IDF) in May 2021.
As per the news reports , it was the third Gaza building destroyed during the conflict, as Israel struck three tower blocks in the heart of Gaza City in 24 hours.
Hence, it is clear that the viral video shows an old Israeli airstrike in Gaza and it is not related to the ongoing Russia-Ukraine crisis.

title: Fact Check: Muslim men in this video were not attacked because of 'The Kashmir Files'
content:
The incident took place in Surat where a shopkeeper was attacked for refusing to pay a ransom. It has no connection with 'The Kashmir Files'. It was not a hate crime.

title: Fact Check: Old video of Odisha bus accident victims shared as charred bodies of women and children in Birbhum violence
content:
This video is from a February 2020 accident when a bus caught on fire after coming in contact with an overhead power transmission wire in Odisha's Ganjam district.
Six women and two children were burnt to death during the violence that took place at Rampurhat in West Bengal's Birbhum district on February 22, following the murder of a deputy panchayat chief of the Trinamool Congress. Houses were torched after the murder. A probe is on to identify the connection between the TMC leader's murder and the violence.
Amid this, a video showing a group of women and children lying on the ground with burn marks was circulated on social media with claims that it captured scenes from the Rampurhat incident. A screenshot from one such post can be seen below. We have not used the video in this story due to its graphic nature.
The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here .
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the video was from a fire incident that took place in Odisha in 2020, not from Birbhum.
We ran a reverse search of the keyframes of the viral video on Google and found the same video tweeted by a person in February 2020. As per the tweet, the video was from the 2020 North East Delhi riots. Though the information provided in the tweet did not look credible, we were able to confirm that the video was at least two years old.
In the viral video, we could see a private bus parked near the crowd. This gave the clue that the incident could have been a bus accident. Closely observing the bus, we found the name, 'WWW.DJGADDI.IN' written on it. The website of 'DJGaddi' states it is an online ticket booking platform functioning in Odisha. We then searched for news reports on bus accidents that took place in Odisha around February 2020 and found videos and images from the same location seen in the viral video carried by multiple news reports since February 9, 2020. As per these reports , the incident took place in the Golanthara area of Odisha's Ganjam district on February 9, 2020. At least nine people were electrocuted to death and several got injured when a bus with over 40 passengers caught fire after coming in contact with an overhead power transmission wire. The incident was also reported by ANI on Twitter. The bus seen in the viral video can be seen in this ANI post. Odisha: At least 6 persons dead and around 40 passengers injured after the bus they were travelling in caught fire after coming in contact with 11 KV live electric wire in Ganjam district, Brahmapur. Injured persons have been sent to MKCG Medical College and Hospital. pic.twitter.com/MFB6YsOIqN — ANI (@ANI) February 9, 2020 Multiple video reports about the incident are also available. According to an NDTV report , the Odisha government suspended four engineers following the Ganjam bus tragedy. It is thus clear that the video is old and not related to the Birbhum violence. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Mar 24, 2022 17:47 IST

title: Fact Check: No, victims of Birbhum violence were not Hindu tribals
content:
No Hindu men or women were killed at Bogtui village in Bengal's Birbhum. All the deceased were Muslims. The 8 deceased persons reportedly were Sheli Bibi (32), Tuli Khatun (7), Nurnehar Bibi (75), Rupali Bibi (44), Jahanara Bibi (38), Lili Khatun (18), Kazi Sajidur Rahman (22) and Mina Bibi (40).
West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Bannerjee reached out to the victims' families on Thursday, March 24, following the violence in the Bogtui village of the state's Birbhum district where eight people were burnt to death.
Amid this, several people on Twitter added a sectarian twist to the violence and claimed that the victims are all Hindus.
One such post said in Hindi, "Today, TMC's jihadi goons burnt alive 12 tribal Hindus, including ten Hindu women and two children in Bengal. But this barbaric terrorist act is missing from the discourse in the country. The Indian media is more concerned about the citizens of Ukraine."
The India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) found that no Hindu men or women were killed at Bogtui. All the deceased were Muslims.
The viral posts are archived here , here and here . AFWA probe Several mainstream news outlets have reported details about the victims of the Bogtui incident and their families. The Telegraph published a report on March 24 that carried the survivors' accounts. According to this report, all the eight people who were killed were family members of Mihilal Sheikh and his elder brother Banirul Sheikh. Both brothers reportedly survived the massacre as they managed to escape in time. Mihilal recounted the events he had witnessed on Monday night to The Telegraph .
Several mainstream news outlets have reported details about the victims of the Bogtui incident and their families. The Telegraph published a report on March 24 that carried the survivors' accounts.
According to this report, all the eight people who were killed were family members of Mihilal Sheikh and his elder brother Banirul Sheikh. Both brothers reportedly survived the massacre as they managed to escape in time. Mihilal recounted the events he had witnessed on Monday night to The Telegraph .
As per Mihilal, the eight deceased included Mihilal's wife Sheli Bibi, 32, his daughter Tuli Khatun, 7, his mother Nurnehar Bibi, who was a 75-year-old widow, his elder sister Rupali Bibi, 44, his sister-in-law Jahanara Bibi, 38, his niece Lili Khatun, 18, Lili's husband Kazi Sajidur Rahman, 22, and another sister-in-law Mina Bibi, 40.
The same names of the victims were reported by other news outlets as well. AFWA contacted Shyam Singh, a senior IPS officer of West Bengal police, who confirmed that "all the victims in Birbhum were from the minority community," and the viral message was "fake". As soon as the messages about the victims being Hindu went viral, the West Bengal Police's official Twitter account clarified that the claim was fake. The tweet said no Hindu women or children were killed at village Bogtui, Rampurhat, Birbhum. The Twitter account also said, "Legal action is being initiated against the persons who are trying to communalise this tragic incident through misleading posts to create social unrest in the state of West Bengal". pic.twitter.com/lCRVO04k7w — West Bengal Police (@WBPolice) March 23, 2022 The state government has formed a special investigation team to probe the case while the Centre has sought a report on the incident within 72 hours. In the meantime, it is clear that social media posts claiming the victims of the Birbhum violence were Hindu tribal men and women are misleading. All eight people killed in the incident are Muslims.
