title: Fact Check: Viral photo of 1500 private jets at WEF 2022 in Davos is actually from 2016
content:
This photo is not from WEF 2022. These were passenger jets parked at the Swiss Airforce base in Duebendorf, Switzerland, on January 21, 2016.
The World Economic Forum (WEF) in Davos, Switzerland 2022 has just concluded. Nearly 100 participants and dozens of political leaders from India attended the event and presented the country's position on the energy situation, food security, and health equity there. Amid this, a photo of parked jets has gone viral on social media with the claim that a record 1,500 private jets arrived at the World Economic Forum in Switzerland to discuss what they can do about our carbon footprint. The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that this photo was not from the WEF 2022. These were passenger jets parked at the Swiss Airforce base in Duebendorf, Switzerland on January 21, 2016. This airport is used for the arrivals and departures of participants of the WEF. The viral posts are archived here and here . AFWA Probe A reverse image search led us to a 2019 report in The Guardian . The report about the WEF titled, "Record private jet flights into Davos as leaders arrive for climate talks," used the same photo that was credited to Reuters. We found the original photo on the Reuters website . It dates back to 2016 and was shot by Arnd Wiegmann. The caption read, "Passenger jets are parked at the Swiss Airforce base in Duebendorf, Switzerland January 21, 2016. The airport Duebendorf in Duebendorf is used for arrivals and departures of participants of the annual meeting of the World Economic Forum (WEF) in Davos." The World Economic Forum does not deal with climate change exclusively. The Russian invasion of Ukraine, the economy, technology, health, and food and energy crises were talking points in this year's conference aside from climate change and the environment. The organisers of WEF this year had also encouraged people to reach Davos by train rather than planes to cut the carbon emissions. Thus, we concluded that the viral image showing multiple jets parked in the airport was not from this year's WEF at Davos. It was more than six years old. (With input from Adarsh Singh) Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: May 30, 2022 19:38 IST

title: Fact Check: Far from his last, this Sidhu Moose Wala interview with Sonam Bajwa is more than a year old
content:
This video of Sonam Bajwa interviewing Moose Wala is from March 2021. In the days leading up to his tragic demise on May 29, the Punjabi singer gave interviews to multiple media outlets.
The assassination of Punjabi singer and Congress leader Shubhdeep Singh Sidhu, better known as Sidhu Moose Wala, has shocked the nation. He was shot multiple times in the Jawaharke village of the Mansa district in Punjab on May 29. Amid fans expressing shock and grief on social media, a video of an interview featuring the Punjabi singer was shared widely with the claim that this was Moose Wala's final interview before his death. In the video , actor Sonam Bajwa spoke to Moose Wala about his struggles in the music industry. But was this his "last interview"? The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the video was more than a year old and was definitely not the last interview the 28-year-old musician gave. AFWA Probe A quick search led us to the original video of the interview from March 2021 on Zee5's website. The 42-minute long interview was from a talk show "Dil Diyan Gallan" hosted by Bajwa. In it, Bajwa and Moose Wala discussed his life, career, and music. He also addressed controversies surrounding him. The clip that is now going viral was taken from a promo video for this episode of the show that we found on the Zee Punjabi YouTube channel. This interview with Bajwa was widely reported by many news outlets . Reportedly, it was his first TV interview. Definitely not the last interview In the time since the now-viral interview, Moose Wala gave several others. In fact, we found two recent interviews that took place just days before his assassination. His interview with On Air was published on May 26. And the one with Lok Opinion was published on May 30, the day after his death. The video's YouTube title mentions that it was recorded a day before the tragedy, on May 28. Moose Wala lost to Aam Aadmi Party's Dr. Vijay Singla from the Mansa constituency in the recent assembly elections in Punjab. In the Lok Opinion interview, the singer said he wouldn't be contesting elections again. Thus, we conclude that the viral clip of Sonam Bajwa interviewing Sidhu Moose Wala was not his "last interview". He recorded interviews with news channels just days before his death. (With inputs from Yash Mittal) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: May 31, 2022 17:08 IST

title: Fact Check: The Pied Piper of Bangladesh! Man attracting bees using flute is not devout Hindu, he's a Muslim honey collector
content:
The man in this video is Mehtab Morol, a Muslim honey collector from Jessore, Bangladesh. He plays the flute to attract honey bees and his story has been reported by many Bangladeshi news outlets.
Just like the legendary Pied Piper of Hamelin from German folktales who was known for his ability to command rats (and children) through his tunes, a modern-day devout Hindu man allegedly has the power to sway honey bees through his flute. A video has been making the rounds of social media with this claim.
Many on social media shared the video of a man dressed in yellow trunks and a saffron headband, playing the flute. A swarm of bees surrounded him, with many even sitting all over his face and body as he played a melody. Those sharing the video on Facebook and Twitter claimed that this devout man's ability to mesmerise bees through his flute was an example of the greatness of Sanatan Dharma or Hinduism.
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the man in this video is Mehtab Morol, a Muslim honey collector from Jessore, Bangladesh.
The viral posts are archived here and here .
Eighteen seconds into the viral video, a framed photo of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman , widely known as Bangabandhu, the founding father and the first president of Bangladesh, could be seen behind the man. This hinted at the video possibly being from Bangladesh.
Subsequent searches with relevant keywords led us to many Bangladeshi news portals that reported this story. We also found more videos of the man on the YouTube channel of Gtv News and the Facebook page of Maasranga Television .
As per these reports, the man in the video was Mehtab Morol, a professional honey collector from the Jessore district of Bangladesh. The viral clip could also be seen in the Gtv News report from June 2021.
Morol, per these reports, has been collecting honey for the last twenty years. He uses several tricks associated with sound to coax bees out of their honeycombs to collect honey.
"Initially, I had made sounds using different utensils to attract the bees. I used to feed the honeybees so that they would become my pet. Then I started playing the flute, and they were attracted to the tune. They don't sting me," Morol told Gtv News. Not Sanatan Dharma
Tohid Moni , a journalist from Jessore who covered Morol's story for Sarabangla and Gtv News told India Today over the phone that Morol is Muslim. Rahul Ray, another journalist from Jessore who covered this story for Maasranga Television, told us, "Mehtab is certainly a Muslim by birth. There is no Hindu connection. Honey collection is his profession. Besides the honey collection, Mehtab also shows this trick to people curious about his stunt."
To get to the bottom of the matter, we went to the horse's mouth. When India Today got in touch with him, Morol confirmed that he is Muslim. He added, "I have been doing this experiment with honey bees since last year. This is not fake or any false trick. I have challenged people to disprove it. These bees come to me whenever I play the flute and then I feed them." Do honey bees like the flute?
Dr Monowar Hossain, a Zoology professor at the Jahangirnagar University of Dhaka, Bangladesh explained to Maasranga Television, that honey bees have a fascination for particular sound wave frequencies.
"The frequency of flutes attracts honey bees. Another reason is that since Mehtab feeds these bees whenever they come to him, their brains get conditioned to believe that if they move towards that particular sound, they will get food."
Thus, we confirmed that the man in the video seen attracting honey bees with his flute is a Muslim honey collector from Bangladesh called Mehtab Morol. His unique ability has been reported by several media outlets in Bangladesh. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Jun 1, 2022 16:17 IST

title: Fact Check: Yes, Bhagwant Mann took a photo with a Goldy Brar, but this wasn't Sidhu Moose Wala's alleged murderer
content:
The man in the photo with Bhagwant Mann is also called Goldy Brar. He is a farmer from Fazilka in Punjab. He has no connection with the Canada-based gangster allegedly involved with Moose Wala's murder.
The name Goldy Brar has been all over social media following the assassination of Punjabi singer Shubhdeep Singh Sidhu, known popularly as Sidhu Moose Wala. Brar, along with others, has allegedly claimed responsibility for the murder.
The Punjabi singer and Congress leader's death followed the Punjab Police withdrawing security for 424 people, including him. Following Moose Wala's death, the Punjab government faced harsh criticism. Amid the online hullabaloo, a photo of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and another man went viral with a string of questionable claims.
The photo was a screengrab of a Facebook post made by a man called Goldy Brar on March 10. Standing alongside him in a photo was the Punjab CM. The caption said, "Congratulations CM saab."
This screengrab was shared with a wild claim. It said, "Sidhu Moosewala's murder conspirator gangster Goldy Brar is in Canada. Canada is home to Khalistanis. Bhagwant Mann govt removed Sidhu's security yesterday. Sidhu is killed today. Connect the dots What is the connection between Canada based Goldy Brar who is taking credit for the assassination of Moose Wala and Punjab CM Mann? Below is the picture of the two."
Similar posts can be seen here , here , and here .
Did Mann really meet the man who allegedly murdered the Punjabi singer and political rival? And did the two pose for a photo after Mann was elected to the Chief Minister's office?
India Today Anti Fake News War Room's (AFWA) investigation found that the photo was real, and the man standing with Mann is indeed called Goldy Brar. However, he is not the gangster suspected to be involved in Moose Wala's murder.
READ MORE: Fact Check: Far from his last, this Sidhu Moose Wala interview with Sonam Bajwa is more than a year old The namesake
A reverse search of the photo led us to the Facebook profile of Goldy Brar. On March 10, the day the Aam Aadmi Party won 92 of Punjab's 117 assembly constituencies, Brar shared his photo with Mann.
On his Facebook profile, we found another video from May 29, the day Moose Wala was assassinated. It was captioned in Punjabi, "I am Goldy Brar, son of Rajinder Singh, resident of village Jandwala. My picture is being misused on social media after today's tragic incident, the murder of Sidhu Moose Wala. I will take legal action against those people."
In the video , he appealed to the Punjab government to take action against those spreading misinformation about his involvement with Moose Wala's assassination.
To further clarify the matter, India Today got in touch with Brar, a farmer from the Fazilka district in Punjab. He said that he had no connection with the man allegedly involved in Moose Wala's murder — except for his name.
Speaking about the photo, Brar said that he volunteered for the AAP during its 2022 Punjab assembly polls campaign. He said that he met Mann at Mohali in January and that's where the two posed for the photo. Following the AAP's historic victory in Punjab, he shared the photo on Facebook. The other Goldy
As per reports, Punjab Police said that aside from Brar, gangster Lawrence Bishnoi was involved in the killing. Lucky, a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, has taken responsibility from Canada. Goldy Brar, whose real name is Satwinderjit Singh, is known to be a close aide of Bishnoi. Based in Canada, Brar is wanted in the 2021 murder of Faridkot District Youth Congress president Gurlal Singh Pehlwan. Reportedly , a total of 16 criminal cases have been registered against Brar in Punjab — he has been acquitted in four cases. In connection to Moose Wala's murder, a Facebook post supposedly made by Brar said , "I, along with Sachin Bishnoi Dhattaranwali, Lawrence Bishnoi group, take responsibility for the killing of Sidhu Moose Wala. His name came up in connection with the murder of Vicky Middukhera and Gurlal Brar and despite this, the police did nothing."
Vicky Middukhera was a Youth Akali Dal leader who was shot dead in Mohali, in August 2021. Middukhera reportedly was close to Bishnoi. The name of Shagan Preet Singh, Moose Wala's manager, had cropped up in connection with the murder. Singh reportedly fled from India to Australia before the police could reach him. Gurlal Brar was Goldy Brar's cousin. The Students' Organisation of Panjab University leader was killed in 2020.
So, while a man named Goldy Brar has claimed responsibility for the murder of Sidhu Moose Wala, the man in the photo with Bhagwant Mann — also called Goldy Brar — has no connection with that.
(Written by Yash Mittal) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 1, 2022 20:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Freedom fighter's pic shared as fictitious Assamese revolutionary along with an unverifiable anecdote
content:
The viral image shows renowned Karnataka-born freedom fighter Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay. We found no records of Hazarika. We were also unable to ascertain the veracity of the story that has been online since at least 2017.
On social media, people have been sharing the photo of an elderly woman claiming she is Kamaladevi Hazarika, a revolutionary from Assam who gave a befitting reply to a pastor who tried to proselytise her and her family to Christianity. In a nutshell, the story people shared alongside the photo was as follows: A pastor named Cruz was sent to Assam to promote Christianity. There, he was employed by a prestigious family to teach English to a boy. Soon, the pastor realised that the boy's grandmother was the most influential person in the family, and if he was able to convert her to Christianity, the whole family would follow suit. The pastor then began telling the grandmother stories of how Jesus Christ cured leprosy, gave sight to the blind, etc. The grandmother, however, said that this was nothing compared to the miracles of Lord Rama and Lord Krishna. Despite this, the pastor did not lose hope. One day, he brought a cake from the church and offered it to the old lady. As soon as she consumed it, the pastor exclaimed that because she had eaten a church offering, she was now Christian. The grandmother boxed the pastor's ear and told him that, by his logic, him eating at her place every day, breathing the air and drinking the water in the land of Hinduism meant he was now Hindu. Many shared this story. Similar posts can be seen here , here , and here . The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the woman seen in the photo was Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, a well-known freedom fighter and social reformer from Mangalore, Karnataka. At the same time, there are no historical records of any revolutionary named Kamaladevi Hazarika hailing from Assam. AFWA Probe We could not find any evidence about a popular revolutionary from Assam called Kamaladevi Hazarika. Even searches in multiple languages did not yield any results. However, we did find that the same story has been circulating online since at least 2017. What's noteworthy is that according to CrowdTangle, a social media analysis tool, this story was posted more than 100 times on Facebook in the past week and garnered nearly 31,000 interactions at the time of writing this story. Who is the lady in the photo? A reverse search of the viral photo led us to the website of the Centre For Cultural Resources And Training , an autonomous Indian organisation under the aegis of the Ministry of Culture. The site stated that this was the photo of Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, a notable social reformer, freedom fighter, and art enthusiast. It also stated that CCRT was also pioneered by Chattopadhyay. Chattopadhyay received multiple awards in recognition of her public service, like the Padma Bhushan, the Padma Vibhushan, the Ramon Magsaysay Award, and the UNESCO Award. She died in Mumbai on October 29, 1988, at the age of 85. Chattopadhyay's biography, " Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay Portrait of a rebel ", written by Jamila Brijbhushan, is available on the Wayback Machine. Using keyword search, we tried finding if there was any mention of a pastor named Cruz in it. The search did not yield any results. Her biographer speaks We sent the viral claim to Sakuntala Narasimhan, the author of another Chattopadhyay biography called " Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay: The Romantic Rebel ". Narasimhan told India Today that Chattopadhyay did not have any such encounter in her lifetime. "I have met Kamaladevi, and spent a lot of time with her before writing my book on her. I have never heard of this story about the Christian pastor Cruz," she said. We also asked Narasimhan if Chattopadhyay had any Assamese link, to which she said, "As far as I know, she had no Assamese connection. I have also spoken to some of her former co-workers and freedom fighters but have never heard of any of her connections to Assam." To sum it up, freedom fighter Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay's photo was shared by many on social media with the claim that she was Kamaladevi Hazarika, a supposed Assamese revolutionary. We found no records of Hazarika. We were also unable to ascertain the veracity of the story that has been online since at least 2017. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Jun 1, 2022 21:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Kareena Kapoor did not ask people to not watch 'Laal Singh Chaddha', 2020 video shared with false spin
content:
The viral video is from an August 2020 news debate about nepotism in Bollywood. It has nothing to do with 'Laal Singh Chaddha'.
The buzz around Aamir Khan's highly-anticipated upcoming movie "Laal Singh Chaddha", a remake of Tom Hanks' Hollywood hit "Forrest Gump", has been loud on social media. However, amid the memes and discussions, a video that features Khan's co-star Kareena Kapoor Khan has gone viral with a startling claim.
Those sharing the video claimed that Kapoor appealed to people to boycott "Laal Singh Chaddha". It was also shared along with the hashtag #BoycottLaalSinghChaddha.
In the viral video , she could be heard saying, "The audience has made us, no one else has made us. The same people pointing fingers are the ones who have made these nepotistic stars right? Aap jaa re ho na film dekhne? Mat jao (You're going to theatres to watch the film? Don't go). Nobody has forced you. So I don't understand it. I find this whole discussion is completely weird."
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral clip was taken from a 2020 news debate and it has no connection with "Laal Singh Chaddha". Kapoor was responding to a question about nepotism in Bollywood.
The viral posts are saved here and here . AFWA Probe
A simple reverse search of frames from the viral video led us to an August 2020 report in Pinkvilla. It quoted the same response from Kapoor that had gone viral in an interview about nepotism in Bollywood.
Another report in India Times around the same time mentioned this interview was given to journalist Barkha Dutt for "We The Women".
We then found the longer version of the interview on the YouTube channel of Mojo Story, a news outlet led by Dutt. The title of the YouTube video was, "Kareena Kapoor has been called the Ultimate Insider. This is what she says on the Nepotism Debate".
Around the 3.35 mark in the video, Dutt asks Kapoor, "The way I see it, Kareena you will definitely get an easier start, you will definitely get more doors to open, but if the audience doesn't like you there's nothing you can do about it." Kapoor's response was the section seen in the viral clip.
So, it is clear that in this video from 2020, what Kareena Kapoor said was in the context of nepotism in Bollywood. It has nothing to do with "Laal Singh Chaddha". Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 1, 2022 23:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Huge crowd at jawan's funeral in Gujarat shared as Sidhu Moose Wala's last rites
content:
This video from October 2021 shows the funeral of Harish Parmar, a jawan from Gujarat who was killed during a clash with insurgents in Jammu and Kashmir.
The assassination of popular Punjabi singer and Congress politician Sidhu Moose Wala on May 29 was met with grief from fans across India. His funeral was attended by thousands and was covered by the national media. However, amid this, many on social media shared a video of a mass gathering , claiming it was from Moose Wala's funeral. One such post can be seen below. A sea of people could be seen in the video surrounding an open shed where the pyre was likely placed. This supposed scene from Moose Wala's funeral contained overlaid text that mentioned the 28-year-old singer's name. More such posts can be seen here and here . The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the video was not from Moose Wala's funeral at all. It was from the 2021 funeral of a jawan from Gujarat who was killed during a clash with insurgents in Jammu and Kashmir. READ MORE: Fact Check: Far from his last, this Sidhu Moose Wala interview with Sonam Bajwa is more than a year old AFWA Probe A reverse search of the keyframes of the video led us to multiple similar YouTube videos from October 2021. These videos claimed to capture the funeral of a soldier called Harish Parmar in Gujarat's Kheda district. Just like the viral video, people in these videos could be seen holding the Indian national flag. Other longer videos also showed the funeral procession. Per news reports , Harish Parmar, 25, died in an insurgent attack in the Poonch sector of Jammu and Kashmir in October 2021. He was cremated at the Vanzaria village in the Kapadvanj Taluk of the Kheda district in Gujarat. Around 50,000 people had gathered to pay their last respects to the young soldier. We reached out to the India Today bureau in Kheda, where our reporter Hetali Shah confirmed that the video was indeed from the funeral of Harish Parmar. With the help of locals in Vanzaria, we were also able to gather photographs and videos of the funeral ground seen in the viral video. Locals also confirmed to India Today that no other recent funeral had witnessed a gathering of thousands. We noticed multiple similarities between the images and videos from Vanzaria and the viral video. For instance, the terrain of the funeral ground, the open shed where funerals are held, as well as a bushy tree near the structure looked similar. It is noteworthy that this video has been in circulation on the internet since October 2021, shared as scenes from funerals of other soldiers. Thousands attended Moose Wala's funeral Thousands of people indeed attended the last rites of Moose Wala at Punjab's Mansa village. A video from his funeral tweeted by ANI can be seen below. #WATCH | A huge crowd joins the funeral procession of singer Sidhu Moose Wala in Punjab's Mansa. The last rites of the singer will be performed today. pic.twitter.com/LHkvjrUyVz — ANI (@ANI) May 31, 2022 Thus, we conclude that the video in question was from the funeral of a jawan in Gujarat and is not related to Sidhu Moose Wala in any way. (With inputs from Hetali Shah and Yash Mittal) READ MORE: Fact Check: Yes, Bhagwant Mann took a photo with a Goldy Brar, but this wasn't Sidhu Moose Wala's alleged murderer Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jun 2, 2022 21:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Kerala has many Messi fans but this old video does not show celebration of Argentina's La Finalissima 2022 win
content:
This video is from July 2021 when Messi fans in Kerala celebrated Argentina's Copa America win.
Lionel Messi stole the show in front of a packed crowd at the Wembley Stadium as Argentina's national football team celebrated a 3-0 victory over Italy to claim La Finalissima 2022. Following this, a video went viral on social media claiming it showed the legendary Indian fans in Kerala celebrating Argentina's victory.
The video showed a bike rally with men carrying Argentina's flag, hooting and cheering as they sped on a road. A Twitter user shared the video with the claim, "My town in India celebrating Argentina's win today. We love Messi".
The archived version of this post can be seen here .
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that though the video was from the Indian state of Kerala, it was almost a year old. Obviously, it has no connection with Argentina's victory in La Finalissima 2022.
In the viral video, several people could be seen wearing masks, indicating that it was likely shot in 2020 or 2021 when Covid-19 masking rules were stricter. When we reverse-searched frames from the video, we found that many people had shared it in 2021.
The bikes could be seen crossing a bridge located near a beach. An abundance of palm trees also suggested that it was shot in a coastal area. We were able to spot two bike number registration plates- 'KL11B' and 'KL10P'. While the RTO code 'KL11' is registered under Kozhikode, Kerala . 'KL10' is registered under Kerala's Malappuram . Both districts are located in the Northern part of Kerala , indicating that this video could have been shot somewhere in that region. What did a Keralite Messi fan say? We found a video of a similar bike rally by Messi fans in India that was shared by ESPN Argentina's Twitter account on July 11, 2021. ESPN credited the video to someone called KM Sudhi from Kerala. Sudhi is a member of the Kerala Youth Congress. India Today reached out to Sudhi, who told us that the viral video in question was indeed from Kerala. Sudhi confirmed to us that his friend had sent this video to him. "This video was shot in Kerala after Messi-led Argentina won the Copa America title in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on July 11, 2021," Sudhi said, adding he too was a massive fan of Messi. We also found multiple media reports stating how the soccer fans in Kerala celebrated Argentina's Copa America victory in July 2021 with bike rallies. Thus, we concluded that last year's video of Lionel Messi fans in Kerala celebrating Argentina's Copa America win was shared as fans' reaction to the team's La Finalissima 2022 victory. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jun 3, 2022 02:31 IST

title: Fact Check: Underwater tunnel from Europe shared as proposed Brahmaputra river project in Assam
content:
While India's first underwater road-rail tunnel across the Brahmaputra is in the works, this photo is unrelated to the project. It shows the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel — an under-construction underwater tunnel between Denmark and Germany.
A high-speed train emerges from a tunnel. Adjacent to it, heavy vehicles speed past on busy roads. What appears to be an ordinary sight is made special because of its physical location — underneath a mighty tempestuous river. This is what the proposed underwater tunnel being built under the Brahmaputra river in Assam is projected to look like, or at least that's what a viral photo on social media claims. "Underwater road and railway line, this is said to be a 14 km long tunnel built under the Brahmaputra river in Assam. This is the new India," a tweet that carried the photo boasts. The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. This was a graphical depiction of the Fehmarn Belt Fixed Link or the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel, an immersed tunnel system that will link the German island of Fehmarn with the Danish island of Lolland. The tunnel system is still under construction. A plan is in place India's first underwater road-rail tunnel is set to be built across the Brahmaputra. According to news reports, the Rs 7,000 crore project is the brainchild of the Railway Ministry, the Road Transport Ministry and the Border Road Organisation (BRO). A first of its kind in India, the tunnel will be 9.8 kilometres long and serve both civilian and strategic purposes, a May report in The Federal said. A Times of India report said the proposed project will contain three parallel tunnels — one for road, another for rail, and the third one for emergency use. It will be constructed using tunnel boring machines and may take in excess of two years to complete. So, the tunnel project is real. But is the photo that's being shared showing the same project? But does it look like this? A reverse search of the photo returned results in plenty. The website for World Highways magazine used the photo in a June 2017 report on the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel — an underwater tunnel between Denmark and Germany that's still under work. Built under the European Union's Trans European Network (TEN-T) programme, the 18 km-long immersed tunnel combined road and rail link connecting the Baltic Sea regions of Germany and Denmark, the report said. A website called TricksFast also used the same image in a July 2021 article about the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel. The photo was also used on the first page of a document by an organisation called Tunnel Engineering Consultants (TEC) that called Fehmarnbelt "the world's longest immersed tunnel." More details of the ambitious project can be seen in the video below. India Today has debunked similar claims before that wrongly attributed European tunnels to upcoming projects from other parts of the world. Thus, we concluded that while a tunnel system under the Brahmaputra river in Assam has been proposed, the photo shared has nothing to do with it — it is of a European tunnel that's still under construction. (With inputs from Adarsh Singh in New Delhi) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Jun 3, 2022 20:10 IST

title: Fact Check: A different Jama Masjid! This photo of a damaged dome is from a UP mosque, not Delhi
content:
This image shows the dome of the Jama Masjid at Uparkot in UP's Bulandshahr which was damaged in 2017.
Heavy rains and hailstorm in Delhi on May 30 were a respite to the sweltering heat, but they came at a cost. The historic Jama Masjid suffered damage that included the finial of the main dome getting dislodged.
The incident was widely reported and following it, a photo of a dislodged dome was circulated on social media with the claim that it showed the damaged Jama Masjid dome. One such post can be seen below.
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the photo in question is not from Delhi. It was taken in 2017 in Uttar Pradesh. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of the viral image led us to several media reports from October 2017 that carried the same photograph. According to a Patrika report from October 21, 2017, the photo showed an old Jama Masjid at Uparkot in UP's Bulandshahr. One of the three domes of the mosque had collapsed during the afternoon prayers, injuring three children and a dozen of adults. One of the children succumbed to injuries on the way to the hospital.
A video report about the incident was published by News18 on October 24, 2017. The photo that is now in circulation is a screenshot from this video report. Following the damage caused by Monday's storm in Delhi, the Shahi Imam of the Jama Masjid wrote to the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) requesting removal of the dangling part of the crown and repair of the ornamental structure.
Following the damage caused by Monday's storm in Delhi, the Shahi Imam of the Jama Masjid wrote to the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) requesting removal of the dangling part of the crown and repair of the ornamental structure.
In the letter to ASI's Director General V Vidtavathi, Jama Masjid Shahi Imam Syed Ahmed Bukhari mentioned that after being broken into multiple pieces in the storm, some parts fell on the terrace below the main dome, and one very heavy part is "still hanging precariously from the dome and it may fall any time".
It is thus clear that the viral image in question is from a 2017 incident in Uttar Pradesh and is not related to Delhi's Jama Masjid getting damaged in a storm. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jun 3, 2022 23:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Hardik Patel did not get slapped after joining BJP, viral video is from 2019
content:
This video is more than three-year-old. Hardik was slapped by a man named Tarun Gajjar during a poll speech in Gujarat's Surendranagar in April 2019, months after he joined Congress.
Days after quitting the Congress, Gujarat Patidar leader Hardik Patel joined the ranks of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Thursday. Meanwhile, a video of the new recruit in the saffron camp has gone viral on social media with the claim that he was 'welcomed' with a slap.
In the seven-second-long muted video , Patel is slapped by a man while speaking from a stage.
Users have shared this video alongside a caption in Hindi that translates to, "Warm welcome and greeting to Hardik Patel as soon as he joins BJP."
Archived versions of similar claims can be seen here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. This video shows Hardik Patel getting slapped more than three years ago when he was still with the Congress party. AFWA Probe
A keyword search on Google showed multiple news reports published in April 2019 -- suggesting that the incident is not recent.
An article in 'The Economic Times' from April 19, 2019, noted that Patel was delivering his speech at Gujarat's Surendranagar district for the Lok Sabha elections when he was slapped by an unidentified man. As the logo of 'Hindustan Times' was visible in the viral video, we searched for the original one and found it uploaded on April 19. We found the now viral part 12 seconds into this original version. According to a report published in India Today , the man who slapped Patel was later identified as Tarun Gajjar. It also noted that Gajjar had some personal grudge against the Patidar leader and hence slapped him. Hardik Patel, the young face of the Patidar caste of Gujarat, made his political debut with Congress in 2019. Now, his move to the BJP months before the state assembly polls has further dented the aspirations of the Congress party to seize power in the saffron fort. Thus, it is safe to conclude that the video of Hardik Patel getting slapped was not shot after he joined the BJP but from 2019 when he was a member of Congress. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 4, 2022 22:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Youth who got away injured after water park accident "killed" by netizens!
content:
The video was shot on May 28, 2022, at Mukundra park in Rajasthan's Jhalawar district. The victim didn't succumb to his injuries. The youth received three stitches for his head injury and was later discharged from the nearby hospital.
Amusement parks are supposed to give visitors a happy time. People buy tickets hoping to have fun and leave with memories to cherish. It is the last place one would expect tragedy to strike.
If a video circulating on social media is to be believed, that is exactly what happened to a youth who was fatally injured following an accident at Kanpur's Blue World Theme Park. The footage shows a young man dropping unconscious in a pool after colliding with a woman who came sliding into the water. Blood is seen gushing out from his head as his friends carry him off.
"A woman sliding in the Blue Word theme park collides with a young man. The youth died on the spot due to the collision. The video of the death went viral. Wherever it is from, this incident should not be seen from the point of view of news. The lesson that can be learnt from this incident is that we and our family should be very serious and careful while having fun in the water park. There should never be any carelessness in the swimming pool," a Facebook post alongside the video read.
Similar claims have been archived here and here.
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. The video shows an accident that happened at Mukundra water park in Rajasthan. The injured person didn't die but was let go after undergoing treatment for his head injury.
Despite multiple efforts, we couldn't retrieve any reports of accidental death at amusement parks in Kanpur or anywhere else in recent times. However, when we looked for accidents and head injuries caused at water parks, there were a few articles available. Among these was a report by Aajtak published on June 3, 2022.
The report said that a man was hurt at Mukundra park on Kota Road of Rajasthan's Jhalawar district. While the video has gone viral on social media, the injured youth is undergoing treatment at SRG Hospital, the story said. From the screengrabs attached alongside the report, it became clear that it was the same incident from the viral video.
Following this clue, we looked up the Mukundra water park in Jhalawar. Ran by the Mukundra Hotels & Resorts, Google Maps had several photos of the park. We found the pool and the twin spiral water slides similar to those in the video in these images.
Meanwhile, a similar search on Blue World Theme Park showed the structure and colour scheme of the water slides here are different to those seen in the video. For further clarity, we reached out to stringer Firoz Ahmed, who compiled the report for AajTak. He confirmed that the video is from Rajasthan and not Uttar Pradesh.
"It happened on May 28, 2022. The victim belongs to Kota's Ramganj Mandi. He was rushed to the Emergency OT at Jhalawar's SRG Hospital where he got 3 stitches for the wound. He was later discharged," Firoz said. No police report was filed and the woman involved in the accident belonged to the same group as the victim, he added.
Firoz shared more photos and videos from the accident spot that helped us confirm that it happened at Mukundra water park in Rajasthan.
Hence, it is clear that a man didn't collapse and die in Kanpur's Blue World Theme Park following a mishap as claimed in the post. The footage shows a minor accident that happened in Jhalawar, Rajasthan.
(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in New Delhi and Firoz Ahmed in Rajasthan) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 4, 2022 23:41 IST

title: Fact Check: This viral video does not show midnight police action against Kanpur "rioters"
content:
The viral video is neither recent nor from Kanpur. This 2020 video was from the Mumbra area of Thane in Maharashtra.
Kanpur witnessed incidents of stone-pelting and violence on June 3, Friday. As per reports , 36 people have been arrested and 1,000 others listed as unknown accused on charges of rioting and attempt to murder. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed the police to identify those responsible and take strict action. There are several videos of police action on the alleged rioters doing the rounds on social media. Among these is a video that shows policemen thrashing a few men on the street at night. Multiple verified Twitter handles and Facebook users have posted this viral video alongside a Hindi caption that translates to, "These strange sounds coming from the streets of Kanpur at midnight have been called auspicious in the scriptures. Babaji's police taking good care of Jihadi stone pelters." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the viral video is neither recent nor from Kanpur. This 2020 video was from the Mumbra area of Thane in Maharashtra. The viral posts are saved here , here and here . AFWA probe A reverse image search of the viral video's keyframes gave us clues that this video had circulated earlier on the internet, besides multiple claims. While some netizens had claimed the video was from Indore during the days of Covid lockdown, some others claimed that it was from Telangana . Several users raised doubts over these viral claims and said the video was from Mumbra, Thane. Taking this as a clue, we ran a keyword search accordingly in Hindi and found multiple news reports published on Hindi news portals which had reported the real story of the video. A YouTube news channel, "Hindustani Reporter," had uploaded a news clip along with the same viral video to report an incident on March 29, 2020. As per this report, the incident happened on March 27, 2020, in Kausa, Shree Lanka area of Mumbra, when supporters of two local politicians clashed. The police resorted to a lathi-charge to disperse the mob and regain control of the situation. Thus, it is clear that a two-year-old video from Maharashtra is being circulated with the misleading claim that it shows police action in Kanpur after the recent Friday violence. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Jun 5, 2022 02:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Sonia Gandhi's 7-year-old comment goes viral as response to fresh ED summons
content:
While the ED has summoned Sonia and Rahul Gandhi, this 2015 video shows what Sonia Gandhi said after a Delhi court asked them to appear in the National Herald case.
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned Congress president Sonia Gandhi and MP Rahul Gandhi to appear before it on June 8 in connection with the National Herald money laundering case.
Amid this development, a video clip has gone viral on social media as the Congress leader's reaction to the ED's move. "I am the daughter-in-law of Indira Gandhi. I am not scared of anyone", Sonia Gandhi is heard saying in Hindi in the video.
Multiple Facebook users have posted this video clip alongside a Hindi caption that translates to, "When the police come to catch a loafer who steals in the streets, he says that my uncle is an MLA or minister. Just like that, when the ED calls Sonia for interrogation on stealing from the government treasury, Sonia says, I am Indra's daughter-in-law".
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that while the ED has summoned Sonia and Rahul Gandhi, this viral video is from 2015. It shows what Sonia Gandhi had said after a Delhi court asked them to appear in the National Herald case.
The viral posts are saved here and here . AFWA probe
Relevant searches using keywords on Google led us to several articles and news clips published by the mainstream media in 2015. A news bulletin uploaded on the YouTube channel of India Today in December 2015 showed the exact reaction of Sonia Gandhi that has gone viral now.
The same video was uploaded on the news portal of " The Hindu " around the same time.
" NDTV " and " The Times Of India " had also published news reports on Sonia Gandhi's comments.
Per these reports, Sonia Gandhi had said this in 2015 after a trial court in Delhi asked her and Rahul Gandhi, along with five others to appear in the National Herald case. The petitioner Subramanian Swamy had accused the Congress leaders of cheating in court.
Hence, it is clear that Sonia Gandhi's comment about being Indira Gandhi's daughter-in-law was not made recently after being summoned by the ED. The viral clip is seven years old. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 5, 2022 22:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Now, shootout scene from web series shared as murder of Sidhu Moose Wala
content:
This video is neither related to Moose Wala's murder nor is it real. This is a scene from a Hindi web series called "Shukla The Tiger" that has been streaming online since 2021.
It was reported that 30 empty bullet shells were recovered from the crime scene where Punjabi singer and Congress leader Sidhu Moose Wala was shot dead by unidentified assailants on May 29. Several days after the murder at Jawaharke village in Mansa, the investigators are yet to zero in on the assailants.
Meanwhile, a video has gone viral on social media with the claim that it showed the ambush by the killers on Moose Wala. "Waheguru ji, see how the killers of Moose Wala attacked him," the translation of a Punjabi Facebook post that shared the video read.
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. The footage isn't real but clipped from an action series streaming online. AFWA Probe
When the keyframes of the video were reverse searched on Google, several YouTube videos were found.
The top result, uploaded on August 31, 2021, was titled "Gangster gun fire attitude WhatsApp status."
Another user, who had uploaded the video on May 27, 2021, had said it showed an attack on Neeraj Bawana. Neeraj is a notorious gangster who is serving his term in the Tihar jail and allegedly has networks across Delhi, Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan.
This confirmed that the video is not the footage of the fatal ambush on the murdered singer and politician as it is available online for over a year now.
While the visuals looked very dramatic to be original, the search showed no hints to locate its origin. We chose to check the comments below all YouTube links that featured the clip. In this way, it was found a person had mentioned the name of the web series "Shukla The Tiger" as a comment to the video on a channel called " WhatsApp Status ".
When checked, it was found that "Shukla The Tiger" is a Hindi action web series streaming on MX Player since 2021. As the artist from the trailer looked similar to the man in the viral video, we checked the web series.
Six minutes into the eighth episode of the series named " Ek Dhokha ", a shootout erupts between two rival groups. We noticed that the Bolero SUV and the dress of the men seen firing at the rivals are the same as that in the video. A comparison can be seen below.
This helped us confirm that the viral video being shared as the attack on slain singer-politician Sidhu Moose Wala is not real. It is a scene from a web series called "Shukla The Tiger".
(With inputs from Yash Mittal in New Delhi) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 5, 2022 23:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Did a Hindu family in US convert to Islam? 2015 photo of German family shared with false spin
content:
This viral photo is seven years old and from Egypt. This was a German family that embraced Islam.
A Hindu family of four in the US converted to Islam. Well, at least that is what a viral photo claims. Many on Facebook shared a photo of four people — an adult man and an adult woman, and a boy and a girl. The photo also contained text that said that these four supposedly Hindu people in the US embraced Islam. The India Today Anti Fake News War room (AWFA) found that the viral image is seven years old and from Egypt. It shows a German family that converted to Islam. The viral posts are archived here and here . AFWA Probe A reverse search of the photo led us to an old news report that had published the viral photo along with other photos of the same family. This article was published on the Egyptian news portal youm7.com on November 6, 2015. According to this article, a German family had converted to Islam at the Al-Tawhid mosque in Hurghada City, Egypt on November 6, 2015. As seen in the viral photo, the German man, Donel Klaus, his wife, and their children were welcomed by the Imam of the mosque. Each family member was gifted a copy of the Quran. The images were also posted on a Facebook page called "Muslim Players" on November 7, 2015, with the caption: "The German Donel Klaus and his family reverted to Islam today at Hurghada, Egypt. They entered Masjid At-Tawheed and asked for the Imam to declare shahada. Masha Allah!! Congratulations and welcome to your big family." Another youm7.com report on from November 7, 2015, gave details about how many foreigners converted to Islam on November 6, at the various mosques of the Egyptian city of Hurghada. It also mentioned the conversion of the Donel Klaus family. We could not find any credible news report confirming any religious conversion of a Hindu family to Islam in the US recently. Thus, we concluded that an old photo of a German family that converted to Islam in Egypt was shared with a false spin. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Jun 6, 2022 22:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Drone strike from Azeri-Armenian war viral as Ukrainian attack on Russian tanks
content:
This video is unrelated to the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Shot in 2020, the video shows Azerbaijan neutralising Armenian tanks during the Nagorno-Karabakh war.
As per the latest reports, Russia has intensified shelling in the Sievierodonetsk and Lysychansk regions as Ukrainian forces refuse to give in. As the conflict thus drags on with no visible sign of peace, a video has gone viral on social media with the claim that it shows a successful Ukrainian drone strike on Russian tanks. "Ukraine's armed forces show a video with a Bayraktar drone destroying Russian tanks," wrote a Facebook user while sharing it . The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. The footage is not from the Ukraine-Russian war. It was shot in 2020 when Armenia and Azerbaijan clashed for the control of the Nagorno-Karabakh region. AFWA Probe The claim names Bayraktar drones responsible for neutralising enemy ground units. Forbes calls Turkish-made Bayraktar TB2 "the most celebrated drone of the age." Known for its armour-breaching capacity, Ukraine's original fleet of drones was estimated to be 36 strong. There are reports of replacements still reaching Ukraine as many of these have been lost in the course of the war . Where is the video from? A reverse search of the video's keyframes on Yandex returned results in plenty — most dating back to 2020. Among the top results was an Instagram post from a verified account of noted Russian TV journalist Olga Skabeyeva. View this post on Instagram A post shared by #60 (@olgaskabeeva) On September 28, 2020, Skabeyeva shared the same video, writing, "Azerbaijani video with an Armenian tank. The hope that by morning they would change their minds did not come true." This confirmed that the video is not recently shot from Ukraine as claimed in the viral post. Yandex also led us to a handful of YouTube videos that were uploaded in September 2020. Like Skabeyeva's post, they claimed it showed Azerbaijan on the offence against Armenian troops. Some of these videos can be seen below. Azerbaijan and Armenia fought over the control of long-disputed Nagorno-Karabakh territory from September to November 2020. Supported by Turkey, Azerbaijan made major breakthroughs before a ceasefire came into force . We checked for more evidence to assert that the viral video was from the war in 2020. We found a photo story on the Karabakh conflict in a Turkish news portal. It explained how Turkish-made Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) helped Azerbaijan edge out its foe on the battlefield. The story contained many visuals of destroyed tanks that looked similar to the scenes from the viral video. Similarly, another website called " sonhaberler.com " in September 2020 used a screenshot from the viral video to report the total damage suffered by Armenia in the conflict. India Today has earlier debunked claims that linked unrelated visuals to the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict. Hence, we concluded that the video of a lethal drone strike shared as a Ukrainian offence against Russia was shot almost two years ago when Armenia fought Azerbaijan. Published By: Chanchal Chauhan Published On: Jun 7, 2022 02:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Definitely not Tamil Nadu! This video of people driving over the Indian flag is from Karachi
content:
This video is from Tariq road in Pakistan's Karachi. Also, it is at least two years old.
Among the more bizarre sights on the internet this week was a video of a bunch of cars driving over the Indian flag taped to the road, all the while cheered by people carrying Pakistan's flag. Bizarre as the sight was, the claim alongside it was questionable. Those sharing the video said this scene was from Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu. The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the video in question was not from Tamil Nadu, but from Karachi, Pakistan. Geolocating the video As mentioned earlier, one can see many people holding the Pakistani flag in this video. At three minutes 38 seconds of the video, we noticed a white van with "The Hunar Foundation " written on it. According to the website of The Hunar Foundation , the organisation is based out of Karachi and focuses on providing technical training in Pakistan. This indicated that the video was likely from Pakistan. There were other such clues. For example, the rickshaws seen in the video do not look similar to the ones seen on the Tamil Nadu roads. We also noticed in the video that most four-wheelers had yellow licence plates. Karachi-based journalist Tauseef Razi Mallick told India Today that in Pakistan, yellow licence plates were found in the Sindh province, whose capital is Karachi. At the start of the video, we noticed the signboard of a shop with "Sanam'' written on it. When we searched for shops named Sanam in Karachi, we came across a "Sanam Boutique" whose font and design looked similar to the one in the video . According to this site, the boutique is located in Tariq Road, Delhi Mercantile Society in Karachi. In a 2017 YouTube video of Tariq Road in Karachi, we came across the same Sanam Boutique as seen in the viral clip. The Google Maps Street View of Tariq Road can be seen below. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Is this video from a recent protest? We found that the same video or screenshots from it have been in circulation on the internet since at least March 2020. In the video, a number of people can be seen wearing masks. This indicates that the video is likely not from before the Covid-19 pandemic. So, while we weren't able to pinpoint the date of the video or why this event took place, we could say with certainty that this video was from Karachi, Pakistan — not Tamil Nadu. title: Fact Check: 2021 prayer service for Pak politician viral as mass gathering against Nupur Sharma's comments
content:
Although Muslim-majority countries have jointly protested against Sharma's comments, the video going viral is more than a year old and is from Lahore, Pakistan. This gathering took place during a memorial for a Pakistani politician.
Amid international backlash following Nupur Sharma's controversial remarks on Prophet Muhammad during a primetime television news debate, a video of a massive gathering went viral. Those sharing this clip claimed it was from a protest against the former BJP spokesperson. The video was shared with hashtags like #OurProphetOurHonour and captions in Hindi that read, "For the sake of Prophet Muhammad, people of Saudi Arabia, Iran, Qatar, Kuwait, Libia, Oman, Bahrain, and Afghanistan have come together." Archived versions of some similar claims can be seen here and here . The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found these posts to be misleading and have nothing to do with the ongoing row. The video is more than a year old and is from Lahore, Pakistan. AFWA Probe A reverse search of the screenshots from the viral clip led us to the same video uploaded to YouTube on January 4, 2021. A channel named "Labbaik News" from Pakistan shared it with the title: "Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi Chehlum | TLP Chehlum 2021." We also found a tweet from January 3, 2021, that contained the same video. The text in Urdu claimed this gathering was "spiritual scenes of Chehlum of Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Subsequent searches led us to a report on a Pakistani website published on January 3, 2021. It noted that thousands of people attended the Chehlum — a remembrance and prayer service on or about the fortieth day after death — for Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi. He was the founder of Tehreek-e-Labbaik, a far-right political party in Pakistan. On November 19, 2020, Rizvi died at the age of 54.
