title: Fact Check: Shocking CCTV footage of brutal public murder in Delhi's Azadpur shared with false Rohingya spin
content:
The video shows Rohit and Rahul Kali brutally attacking Narender in Delhi's Azadpur. The police confirmed to India Today that both parties involved are Hindu and there was no communal angle to this crime.
A shocking video has gone viral with the claim that it captured communal violence in broad daylight. In the CCTV footage, two men could be seen attacking a man even as a crowd was present. One onlooker attempted to stop the assault. However, one of the assailants hit the victim's head with rocks and stabs him several times. Following that, he also appeared to slit the victim's throat. Those sharing this graphic video claimed that the assailants were Rohingya Muslims and the victim was a Hindu man. Other similar claims can be seen here and here . The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral video is from Delhi's Azadpur and has no communal angle to it. Both the victim and the culprits are Hindu. AFWA Probe A reverse search of the keyframes of the video led us to several news reports related to the incident. An India Today report stated that the incident occurred in the afternoon of June 3 in New Delhi's Azadpur. According to the report, a quarrel broke out after Narender, the victim, repeatedly approached Rahul Kali to borrow money to buy drugs. Per the police, an annoyed Rahul called his brother Rohit Kali to Mandir Wali Gali in Azadpur. The duo then brutally attacked Narender. Following the attack, Narender was rushed to the BJRM hospital for treatment. Later, he was referred to a higher centre where he was declared brought dead. The Indian Express quoted the DCP of Northwest Delhi Usha Rangnani saying, "The accused brothers, Rahul and Rohit Kali, have been arrested. The victim, Narender alias Bunti, and Rahul were previously involved in cases of robbery and snatching." An FIR has reportedly been filed under IPC sections 302 (murder) and 34 (common intention). To verify if Rohit and Rahul Kali were Rohingya Muslims, India Today contacted the Adarsh Nagar Police Station, under which Azadpur falls. Inspector Rajendra there confirmed that the incident was not communal and everyone involved — Rohit Kali, Rahul Kali, and Narender — is Hindu. Thus, we conclude that the incident in the viral video was not communal. Rohit and Rahul Kali, the brothers who brutally killed Narender, are not Rohingya Muslims; they are Hindus. (Written by Yash Mittal) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Jun 7, 2022 21:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Doctored image shared to advertise BJP's 'blooming' foothold in Tamil Nadu
content:
This image is doctored. In the original image, the men are hoisting a BSP flag. The Telangana spokesperson of BSP tweeted the original photo on May 31.
The Tamil Nadu unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party staged a protest in Chennai against fuel price hikes on June 2. Reportedly, the event was attended by over 15,000 party cadres. Amid these developments, a post cheering for BJP workers in Tamil Nadu has gone viral on social media. "Lotus is blooming in Tamil Nadu," several users captioned a photo that showed four men hoisting the party flag, standing on each other's shoulders. The photo was tweeted by multiple verified handles including Himachal Pradesh BJP spokesperson Prajwal Busta and former North Delhi Mayor Ravinder Gupta . The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the viral image was doctored. In the viral photo, BJP's flag replaced the Bahujan Samaj Party flag. AFWA Probe A reverse search of the image showed a handful of results. The top result was a May 31 tweet from the account of Shirisha Swaero Akinapally, the spokesperson of the BSP's Telangana unit. However, in this photo, the men were seen hoisting a BSP flag. "Our brothers and sisters climbed the ladder and hoisted the blue flag at the heartbeat of the masses. Millions of such youths are following in the footsteps of @RSPraveenSwaerofor the establishment of a Bahujan Rajya Sabha in Telangana," Akinapally wrote in Telugu. It was retweeted by many, including BSP Telangana state coordinator RS Praveen Kumar. . . @RSPraveenSwaero . @Mayawati @AnandAkash_BSP @ramjigautambsp pic.twitter.com/gkLh8FnnBz — Shirisha Swaero Akinapally (@ShirishaSwaero) May 31, 2022 We also found the photo with the BSP flag uploaded on a Pinterest page called " Ambedkari Status ". We ran the two images on the image error analysis platforms Forensically and FotoForensics. When an image is examined under Error Level Analysis on these websites, altered or appended parts stand out in colour grade from the rest of the image. While there were no evident mismatches on the BSP image, the orange portion of the BJP flag stood out on the FotoForensics test . Similarly, the BJP flag appears glared out compared to the rest of the image's scale on Forensically as well. This can be seen below. Thus, we concluded that the photo used of the BJP flag was a doctored one. The original photo had a BSP flag. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Jun 8, 2022 01:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Cops recently lathicharged people in Kanpur, but this video is from Gorakhpur, and from 2019
content:
While cops lathicharged protestors in Kanpur on June 3, this video is from 2019 and shows police action during an anti-CAA protest in Gorakhpur.
Kanpur recently witnessed violence on June 3, following controversial remarks made by a former BJP spokesperson, Nupur Sharma on the Prophet Muhammad. Police resorted to lathicharge to control the crowd.
Now, a video of cops lathi-charging people has gone viral. Many on Facebook shared it claiming the police lathicharge was from the recent Kanpur incident.
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral video is neither recent nor from Kanpur. It is from a 2019 anti-CAA protest in Gorakhpur.
The viral posts are archived here and here .
A reverse search of some keyframes of the video led us to the same video shared by the Facebook page of MMIS - Majlis E Mohammadi Islamic Samiti Official on December 20, 2019. It said the incident was in Gorakhpur.
Subsequent searches led us to a video report by Live Hindustan from December 20, 2019. Per this news report, after Friday namaz, people gathered to protest against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) at Nakhash Chowk, Gorakhpur. There was stone-pelting during the protest and subsequently, the police dispersed the crowd by charging with batons and firing tear gas shells.
The exact portion of the viral video can be seen after the 1.10-minute mark in the YouTube video.
During the anti-CAA protests in 2019, several parts of Uttar Pradesh witnessed violence and police lathicharge. The viral video from Gorakhpur alongside other incidents from different parts of UP was also reported by The Lallantop, which can be seen here .
Per reports, at least a dozen people, including two police officials were injured in the violence that broke out in Kanpur on June 3. Eighteen people have reportedly been arrested in connection with the violence.
Thus, it is clear that although the UP police had resorted to lathicharge in Kanpur to control the crowd, the viral video in question has nothing to do with it. The video is from 2019 and was shot during an anti-CAA protest in Gorakhpur. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 8, 2022 17:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Salman Khurshid digs up Akhilesh era pics to bulldoze Yogi rule
content:
Three of the four photos tweeted by Congress leader Salman Khurshid are from 2016 when Akhilesh Yadav was the CM.
Bulldozers have become somewhat synonymous with strongman chief ministers following a trend of demolition drives against alleged criminals. Popularised by Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath, demolishing homes and shops of those accused of crimes has now become the modus operandi of other Bharatiya Janata Party CMs.
While this method has come under criticism from civil society and opposition leaders, veteran Congress party leader Salman Khurshid's attempt to call out the UP's CM for this was less than successful. Sharing a series of photos of demolished buildings, Khurshid tweeted , "Not Ukraine, these are photos of Unnao and Farrukhabad of Buldozerland".
Khurshid's tweet was retweeted by many, including Congress leader Alka Lamba. Others tweeted the photos as well, some criticising, and some praising the Yogi Adityanath government.
The archived versions of such posts can be seen here , and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that three out of the four images shared by Khurshid are from former CM Akhilesh Yadav's regime. Old pics recycled
A reverse search of the first three photos led us to similar images in an Amar Ujala report from May 2016. In 2016, Akhilesh Yadav was the Chief Minister of UP. Yogi Adityanath came to power in September 2017.
As per the Amar Ujala reports, these photos were from a demolition drive in Loha Mandi (iron market) and Bartan Bazar (utensils market), located between Ataullah Nala and Chhota Chauraha in Unnao. The district administration demolished around 85 supposedly illegal buildings in the area.
We were unable to find a source for the fourth photo tweeted by Khurshid. What did Khurshid say?
India Today contacted Khurshid and asked the veteran Congress leader about the photos. He said, "The images were shared with me by the locals of Farrukhabad where demolition is happening. At the time of tweeting the post, I was not aware the first three images were old."
Khurshid claimed that the fourth photo was from Farrukhabad. India Today has reached out to the local who shared the fourth photo with Khurshid. This story will be updated as and when we receive a response.
As per reports , for the last month and a half, a demolition drive has been on in Farrukhabad. Authorities have demolished more than a dozen allegedly illegal buildings worth crores of rupees.
However, it is clear that three of the four photos shared by Khurshid are indeed from 2016 and not related to the Yogi Adityanath government.
Update: After getting in touch with a local, India Today was able to ascertain that the fourth photo shared by Khurshid was current. The photo showed a demolished house on Narkasa road in Kadrigate, Farrukhabad. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 8, 2022 20:46 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Moeen Ali boycott IPL over Nupur Sharma row? Unofficial Twitter account spins lie
content:
This Twitter account does not belong to Moeen Ali. The English cricketer is not active on Twitter. There also aren't any reports that suggest he has commented on the ongoing row.
Have Nupur Sharma and Naveen Jindal's controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad created a stir in the cricketing world as well? Several social media users claim so.
A tweet supposedly from cricketer Moeen Ali has gone viral stating that the English all-rounder has demanded an apology from India following the aforementioned remarks.
The tweet from the account @Moeen_Ali18 states, "If India does not apologize for its blasphemous statement, I will never go to India to play match again, I will also boycott the IPL. And I will appeal to my fellow Muslim brothers to do the same. I Love Muhammad P.B.U.H ."
The Archived versions of the Twitter account and the tweet can be seen here and here respectively.
At the time of writing this, more than 13,000 people had retweeted the tweet. Others on Facebook and Twitter shared screenshots of the tweet. Archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here .
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the viral Tweet and the Twitter account do not belong to Moeen Ali. The English cricketer is neither active on Twitter, nor has he commented on the controversy. An impostor account
A quick look at the bio of the Twitter account in question reveals the words, "Not Official."
Further, we looked for Moeen Ali's official Twitter account but found nothing. On Ali's profile on the England Cricket Board's official website, all linked social media accounts were either inactive or unavailable.
The Twitter account mentioned there was @MoeenAli. It had less than a hundred followers and zero tweets. It was also an unverified account.
Following this, we looked for media reports on Ali's comments on the controversy and found nothing. The cricketer recently visited India to play for Chennai Super Kings in the 15th edition of the Indian Premier League.
The Bharatiya Janata Party, on June 5, suspended spokesperson Nupur Sharma and expelled Delhi media head Naveen Kumar Jindal after their controversial remarks on Prophet Mohammad that drew flak from several Muslim-majority countries.
Thus, we concluded that the viral tweet was not tweeted by English cricketer Moeen Ali. It was from an unofficial account.
(Written by Yash Mittal) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 8, 2022 21:59 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral 'Boycott Qatar 2022' banner at stadium has nothing to do with Nupur Sharma
content:
Fans of German football club Freiburg unfurled this banner before a Bundesliga match at Europa-Park Stadion on April 02, 2022, in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany. It has nothing to do with the ongoing controversy over Nupur Sharma's remarks.
While several countries — particularly Muslim-majority nations — have condemned the remarks made by Nupur Sharma on the Prophet Muhammad, social media trends indicate that Qatar in particular has earned the wrath of Indians. Trends like "Qatar Exposed" and "Boycott Qatar Airways" dominated Twitter.
With that in the background, one photo has been shared widely that deserves to be examined. The photo shows a "Boycott Qatar 2022" banner being raised at a stadium. People sharing the photo claimed this was in the aftermath of the diplomatic tensions between India and Qatar following the now-suspended Bharatiya Janata party spokesperson's comments. Many on Twitter shared the photo with hashtags like "Qatar Exposed".
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that this banner had no connection with the recent controversy. Fans of the German football club Freiburg raised this banner before a Bundesliga match at the Europa-Park Stadion on April 02, 2022, in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany.
The viral posts are archived here and here .
A reverse search of the photo led us to several news reports that published the photo in April this year.
The Guardian used this photo on April 7 in a report on the FIFA World Cup that's scheduled to be held in Qatar later this year. The Guardian credited the photo to Getty Images.
We found the original photograph on the website of Getty Images . The caption for the photograph was taken by Matthias Hangst said, "Fans of Freiburg display a banner about boycotting the FIFA World Cup 2022 in Qatar before the Bundesliga match between Sport-Club Freiburg and FC Bayern München at Europa-Park Stadion on April 02, 2022, in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany."
This image was also published on websites like the Middle East Monitor and Inside the Games in reports about alleged human rights violations in Qatar.
Amnesty International recently released a report that has alleged human rights violations, exploitation, and deaths of migrant labourers in Qatar while working for the World Cup.
The Guardian noted, "The latest Amnesty International report into private security firms who employ tens of thousands of migrant workers in Qatar is pretty damning. It says they are still subject to 'forced labour' and several other cases of abuse and it criticises Fifa for failing "to put in place adequate processes" to address these issues."
So, it is pretty clear that the viral banner is not about India or the fallout from rising India-Qatar tensions following Nupur Sharma's comments. It's about alleged human rights violations and the upcoming football world cup. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 9, 2022 15:23 IST

title: Fact Check: Heard of the jealous Qatari man who sealed his wife's genitals with glue? It's satire
content:
This is a satirical news story that has no basis in reality. This "report" has been making the rounds since 2017 at least.
Qatar has been a trending issue on social media of late. While many Muslim-majority nations have taken a stand against controversial remarks made by now-suspended BJP national spokesperson Nupur Sharma, supporters of the ruling party have taken particular umbrage at Qatar.
Amid thousands of tweets calling out the country's supposed hypocrisy on "blasphemy" and calls to boycott Qatar Airways, one odd post stuck out. It was a screenshot of an alleged report about a Qatari man who purportedly sealed his wife's genitals with glue to punish her.
The headline in the screenshot read: "Qatar: Jealous husband seals wife's vagina with crazy glue."
Through this screenshot, people are taking a dig at Qatar and its residents. A Twitter user shared this photo with the caption, "Just halal things next door".
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that this story was from a satirical news website. It wasn't a real news report.
Upon close inspection of the screenshot, we noticed " worldnewsdailyreport.com " written at the bottom. Subsequently, we searched for the story on the website and found it.
The report said a 33-year-old man confessed before a court that he glued his wife's genitals shut alleging she had adulterous ideas because she liked a post of his 12-year-old cousin on Facebook and also uploaded a selfie. The judge sentenced the wife to 100 lashes and fined the man 40 riyals or USD 10. It is noteworthy that the website's tagline reads, "Where facts don't matter." The website's 'About' section claims that it is an "American Jewish Zionist newspaper based in Tel Aviv and dedicated on covering biblical archaeology news and other mysteries around the Globe," adding its staff includes "retired Mossad agents and veterans of the Israeli Armed Forces." The 'About' section on the site's Facebook page , however, says in loud and clear terms that it's an independent satirical media organisation. It also states, "All characters appearing in the articles in this website — even those based on real people — are entirely fictional and any resemblance between them and any person, living, dead or undead, is purely a miracle." Incidentally, this screenshot had also gone viral in 2017 . At the time, many mainstream news websites including India Today and Aaj Tak reported on this, mistaking the satirical report for real news. These reports were later retracted. To sum it up, an old screenshot of a satirical news article is now being circulated as a real news report amid anti-Qatar social media trends in India. Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jun 9, 2022 17:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Did a Congress leader from Hyderabad marry his daughter? Old hoax resurfaces
content:
Ayub Khan is a gangster from Hyderabad who is serving a seven-year sentence in prison. He did not marry his daughter.
A shocking Facebook post about a supposed Congress Party member has been making the rounds. The text in the post claims Ayub Khan of Hyderabad married his daughter Tharnum Khan. It also contained the photo of a newspaper report whose headline said: "Muslim man married own daughter, impregnates her." AFWA investigated the post and found it to be misleading. While the newspaper clipping is about a 2017 incident in West Bengal's Jalpaiguri, the claim about Ayub Khan marrying his daughter is an old hoax. The origin of the hoax We found that the claim Ayub Khan married his daughter has been on the internet for at least two years now. Independent fact-checkers in 2020 called out a social media influencer, Tharnum Khan, for circulating the hoax. On her Facebook account, she shared photos of herself in a bridal costume. The caption of the photos read, "Got Married with my Dad Ayub Khan. I'm nervous. I don't have marriage experience." In fact, she changed the caption of the photos several times, finally settling on "White Attire". She had tagged Ayub Khan to the post. But his Facebook profile was later deleted. Scanning through her social media accounts, we also found several videos where she mentions her supposed relationships with public figures. In one such video she referred to herself as the wife of cricketer Virat Kohli. Who is Ayub Khan? According to media reports, Ayub Khan, also known as Ayub Pahelwan, is a wanted criminal and gangster from Hyderabad. Speaking to The Logical Indian in November 2020, Khan's son said that his father had five sons and no daughters. This puts the claims about him marrying his daughter to rest. Is he a Congress leader? We found a video from 2018 where Khan announced contesting the 2019 Telangana Assembly Election from Bahadurpura on a Congress ticket. However, in August 2018, a local court in Hyderabad sentenced the gangster along with his wife to seven years in prison in a fake passport case. The Telangana High Court granted him an interim bail for 15 days in February this year. Also, per MyNeta , Shaik Mohd Kalemmuddin was the Congress candidate in Bahadurpura in 2019. The news report The newspaper report shared in the viral post was about a Muslim man called Afazuddin, who married his daughter. However, the news report was from 2017. The same report was published by the Times of India in November 2017. Thus, we conclude that Ayub Khan, an imprisoned gangster and a supposed member of the Congress party, did not marry his daughter. (With inputs from Yash Mittal) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Jun 10, 2022 21:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Is Qatar deporting Hindu migrant workers after Nupur Sharma's controversial remarks? This video is from March
content:
This video is from a protest held by employees against a company in Qatar for non-payment of salary. The incident happened in March 2022. It is not related to Sharma's recent remarks.
Beyond a well-publicised condemnation of remarks made by now-suspended BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma, have there been material consequences for Indians living in Qatar? One viral video seems to suggest so. The video shows a large group of men standing outside a building. The claim alongside suggests the peninsular Arab country is deporting Hindus back to India in the wake of Sharma's controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad. In the video, a man said that around 7,000 men were boarding a bus to buy tickets. He referred to the place as "Redco International". AFWA found that this video was from March, well before this controversy came into existence, and was thus unrelated to it. AFWA Probe We searched for "Redco International" on YouTube. The same video was shared by the channel QN Qatar on March 29, confirming that it was unrelated to the recent row. In March, the channel also published other videos of men in front of the same area. In another video , several men argued about their pending salaries with another man. We also found a video from March 26 where a man spoke to others in front of a building with the board "Redco International". The description of the video reads, "Redco international company Qatar salary breaking news." We also found similar videos of protests against Redco International uploaded to Facebook in March. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story While we couldn't find any credible reports on Indians, particularly Hindus, getting fired by any of the Muslim-majority countries in the wake of Nupur Sharma's remarks, we could conclude that this video was not related to the ongoing row. Published By: Amreesh Kumar Published On: Jun 11, 2022 17:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Lahore protestors burned the Tricolour over prophet row, not Indians
content:
This photo isn't from India. It shows religious groups burning the Tricolour during a protest against Nupur Sharma's remarks in Pakistan's Lahore on June 9, 2022.
The row over remarks against the Prophet Nabi by BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma refuses to die down even after days. Despite diplomatic pressure from several Muslim nations, protests have erupted in several states, resulting in police action.
Among the videos and photos that are shared on social media of the protests, there is an image of a group burning an upturned Indian Tricolour.
"Peaceful Muslims burning Our Tiranga (National Flag) today in India," one such post on Facebook read.
Similar claims have been archived here and here .
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the claim to be misleading. The photo was taken from Pakistan's Lahore on June 9 during a protest by religious groups over Sharma's remarks. AFWA Probe
The protestors are seen holding a banner in the image. The word "Insults" is seen in bold letters while the half-visible footnote in English reads, "Ulama E Nizamia Pak..."
The rest of the banner was in Urdu and a smaller banner seen in the background was in Urdu too, as confirmed by the Google Translate app.
When the image was run through the reverse search on Google, the top result was a news article by the US news agency, The Associated Press.
The photo that was shared as Indians burning the flag was used in this report that was titled "Pakistanis rally to denounce India over remarks about Islam". Published on June 9, 2022, it narrated the brief scuffle between police and Islamists who took out protests in Islamabad against the remarks made by the now suspended BJP leader.
"Supporters of religious groups burn a representation of the Indian flag during a demonstration to condemn derogatory references to Islam and the Prophet Muhammad recently made by Nupur Sharma, a spokesperson of the governing Indian Hindu nationalist party, in Lahore, Pakistan, Thursday, June 9, 2022," the photo caption read.
The report gave credit to AP photographer KM Chaudary for the image.
We found the photo in question was used by Al Jazeera in an article as well to report protests in South Asia over the issue. Headlined 'South Asia protests over prophet remarks by India's BJP officials', the photo was used in the story below the subhead on reactions in Pakistan. Al Jazeera also used a similar photo caption, citing credit to the AP's KM Chaudary.
The story mentioned demonstrators burning Indian national flags along with the pictures of PM Modi and Nupur Sharma.
Hence, it is clear that the photo shared as that of protestors in India was photographed from Pakistan's Lahore.
(With inputs from Adarsh Singh in New Delhi) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 12, 2022 15:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Two-year-old video of man threatening Muslims with guns goes viral amid Prophet row
content:
This video is from March 2020. The man, identified as Yogendra Singh Chauhan, was arrested by Thakurgunj Police of Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh after his provocative speech went viral on social media. It is unrelated to the ongoing row over Nupur Sharma's remarks.
Amid the protests and controversies over the BJP's Nupur Sharma's remarks on Prophet Muhammad, a video has gone viral on social media where a man is seen threatening the Muslim community while firing a rifle.
In the video (abusive language, viewers' discretion advised), a man in a red t-shirt is heard threatening to kill Muslims and abusing the Prophet. Later, he fires three rounds into the air. This clip was shared by many social media users with a caption that read, "Modi's Hindus are now posting their promise to kill Muslims on social media with total impunity."
CJ Werleman, correspondent of the Byline Times, shared this video quoting the same caption.
Archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found the posts to be misleading as the video is more than 2-years-old and is unrelated to the ongoing row. The man was arrested after the video went viral. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of the screenshots from the viral clip led us to some older tweets of the same video. Abdul Shaik, a Twitter user, had posted a screengrab of the same video on April 26, 2020.
It was the screenshot of a Facebook post from March 1, 2020. We ran the keywords of the caption on Facebook and found the same video was shared by many users between March 2020 and April 2020. After going through the comment section of such a video , we came across a newspaper cutting posted by a user named Malik Ansari. It was reported that the man in question was arrested for spreading provocative and abusive speech on social media. Who is this man? Using advanced Google search, we found multiple news stories from March 2020 about the incident. Articles from ETV Bharat , News18 , and Hindustan confirmed that Yogendra Singh Chauhan was arrested in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh on March 1, 2020, by the Thakurgunj police. According to these reports, police recovered two air pistols and two air guns from Chauhan. A mobile phone was also seized from him. Seeking more details on Chauhan, we reached out to Hari Shankar, the SHO of Thakurgunj Police Station. While talking to AFWA he said, "This video is more than two years old. He was granted bail four months after his arrest. Chauhan went back to his native village, Sitapur and has been living there since then." Therefore, it is safe to conclude that the video going viral on social media claiming to be recent was shot in 2020. Also, the man got arrested following this incident. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 12, 2022 21:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Did cops blame BJP for Kanpur violence? Old video viral with false claims
content:
This video is not related to the recent violence in Kanpur. In July 2021 during UP Block Pramukh Elections, the SP of Etawah was caught on camera talking about an armed mob led by BJP leaders that attacked him.
Kanpur has recently witnessed mob violence followed by police lathi-charge over BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma's controversial remarks on Prophet Muhammad.
A total of 24 people were held and 800 were booked initially by the Uttar Pradesh police related to the incident .
Now a video of a police officer talking over the phone has gone viral with the claim that Uttar Pradesh police are blaming the BJP for the recent violence in Kanpur. The police officer can be heard talking to someone saying, "BJP leaders along with the MLA have come with bombs".
Multiple Facebook users have posted this video alongside a caption in Hindi that translates to, "In Kanpur, the police themselves are saying that a BJP MLA has brought a bomb. He is telling this to one of his senior officers. But still, no one has been arrested, only innocent Muslims are being arrested."
India Today Anti-Fake News War room (AFWA) has found that this video is not related to the recent violence in Kanpur. In July 2021, during Uttar Pradesh's Block Pramukh elections, the SP (City) of Etawah district was allegedly slapped. The officer was caught on camera talking over the phone and saying he has been slapped.
The viral posts are saved here and here . AFWA probe
With the help of a reverse image search, we found a Hindi news report published by NDTV India on July 10, 2021, along with a screenshot from the viral video.
Per this report, a video of the Etawah City SP had gone viral during the UP panchayat elections, where he was heard complaining to his senior over the phone that BJP leaders had slapped him and they had gathered with bombs.
Taking this as a clue, we ran keyword searches and found the longer version of the viral video on the YouTube channel, Mojo Story.
This video was uploaded on July 10, last year. The video description reads, "During the counting of Uttar Pradesh's Block Pramukh elections, SP City of Etawah district was allegedly slapped. The SP City was caught on camera talking on a phone call and saying he has been slapped and the mob came with stones and bombs. He reportedly said that BJP MLA and District President were leading the mob."
The same video was also uploaded on another YouTube news channel and the incident was reported by mainstream news portals last year.
Two BJP workers were arrested for allegedly slapping Prashant Kumar, the city SP of Etawah police, who is seen in the viral video talking on the phone.
So it is clear that the viral video is not related to the recent Kanpur violence. It was shot during the Uttar Pradesh's Block Pramukh elections in Etawah in July 2021. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Jun 12, 2022 23:30 IST

title: Fact Check: This Kolkata cop was NOT killed by people protesting against Nupur Sharma
content:
This video is of a constable who shot and killed himself after opening fire at multiple persons at Park Circus in Kolkata on June 10. A woman was killed and two others were injured.
Protests took place across several Indian cities on June 10 over Nupur Sharma's controversial remarks on Prophet Muhammad. Police resorted to lathi-charge and used teargas to quell protests that turned violent. A shocking video supposedly from protests in Kolkata has gone viral with disturbing claims. The video showed a seemingly dead police officer drenched in blood, lying on a road with a rifle beside him. The video can be seen here . Warning: this video contains graphic footage and may be upsetting to some people. An angry crowd was seen surrounding the body. While most voices were unintelligible because of the cacophony, people appeared to shout angrily at another policeman there. Those sharing the video claimed that a mob of protestors killed the policeman and threatened the other cop present at the scene. India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found that the claim along with the video is misleading. While the video is from June 10, the officer seen in it shot himself dead after firing at multiple persons at Kolkata's Park Circus. AFWA Probe A Google search revealed photos and videos from the same incident carried in multiple media reports from June 10. Per the reports, at around 2.30 pm on June 10, Choudup Lepcha, a constable with the fifth battalion of the Kolkata Armed Police, fired about 10-15 rounds at the public. The incident took place at Lower Range Road, near the Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Park Circus, Kolkata, where the constable was posted. A woman on a bike taxi was killed in the onslaught. Two others were injured. Subsequently, the policeman died by suicide after shooting himself. We did not find any report that claims the constable was shot by anyone in the public. Vineet Kumar Goyal, the commissioner of Kolkata Police, told reporters that Lepcha was recruited in 2021 on compassionate grounds since his father died in service in 2017. He was on a ten-day leave and joined back only on June 9. The commissioner also said that the police were investigating why the constable opened fire and then shot himself. An India Today video report about the incident can be seen below: It is hence clear that the police officer seen in the video was not killed by protestors but died by suicide — he shot himself after opening fire at people. While we were unable to ascertain if the other policeman was being threatened by the crowd, it is likely that the people were only expressing their anger about the incident. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena) READ | Fact Check: Did cops blame BJP for Kanpur violence? Old video viral with false claims Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: Jun 13, 2022 19:34 IST

title: Fact Check: This video is from Khargone Ram Navami violence, NOT ongoing protests against Nupur Sharma
content:
This video was shot in MP's Khargone in April 2022, when violence broke out between Hindus and Muslims during Ram Navami. It's unrelated to the ongoing protests.
Following countrywide (sometimes violent) protests against controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad, social media has been abuzz with videos and photos supposedly capturing said violence. Different people have accused Hindus, Muslims, and even the police of instigating violence.
Among such media is the footage of a group, some donning saffron, pelting stones from the roof of a house. "People of Godsewadi rotten society are clearly visible pelting stones from the top of the roof at a peaceful protest. These are the people who start the real stone-pelting, and if Muslims defend themselves, the media and intelligentsia start talking of violence," a tweet that shared the video read.
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was misleading. The video was not shot during the protests over the comments made by now-suspended BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma. It showed the clashes that broke out in Madhya Pradesh's Khargone in April 2022 during Ram Navami celebrations. AFWA Probe
While the post didn't mention where the video was from, a stamp at the bottom that read, "OPPO Reno6 5G 2022.04.10 18:13." This is a standard feature in Oppo smartphones that can be optionally activated.
If needed, the Oppo logo can be watermarked to media alongside the date and time of the shot, the phone's model, or both. Thus, we could surmise that this video was possibly from the evening of April 10, 2022 — long before Sharma even made the offending comments.
Reverse-searching keyframes of the video led us to a tweet from April 14. User Samiullah Khan claimed the video was from Madhya Pradesh's Khargone, and that it showed "Hindutva Extremists" pelting stones at Muslims in the Taudi Mohalla near Mata Chowk. This further confirmed that the video was old and unrelated to the ongoing protests. #WATCH Video From #Khargone Hindutva Extremists Pelting Stone on Muslim population Taudi Mohalla near Mata Chowk. But they're not arrested yet, and bulldozer is not used to demolish their Houses. @RanaAyyub @RahulGandhi @asadowaisi @milligazette @digvijaya_28 @AdityaMenon22 pic.twitter.com/2mj1Gshgd7 — Samiullah Khan (@SamiullahKhan__) April 14, 2022 What happened in Khargone?
#WATCH Video From #Khargone Hindutva Extremists Pelting Stone on Muslim population Taudi Mohalla near Mata Chowk. But they're not arrested yet, and bulldozer is not used to demolish their Houses. @RanaAyyub @RahulGandhi @asadowaisi @milligazette @digvijaya_28 @AdityaMenon22 pic.twitter.com/2mj1Gshgd7 — Samiullah Khan (@SamiullahKhan__) April 14, 2022
Per reports, 175 people were arrested and 64 FIRs were filed after violence broke out in Khargone, Madhya Pradesh during Ram Navami celebrations on April 10 — the date in the video's watermark. The curfew imposed in the area was only lifted in May , almost 24 days after the violence.
Nasir Ahmed Khan, a resident of the locality reportedly told Newschecker that his house came under attack from those seen in the video. An FIR was filed against eight people.
India Today got in touch with a local, who under the condition of anonymity confirmed that the video was shot in the Taudi Mohalla neighbourhood of Mata Chowki in MP during the April unrest.
''The group pelted stones from the roof. A police complaint was filed naming around 32 people and 8 were arrested. However, no such incident of violence has taken place in the area recently," he said. He shared recent photographs of the building from which the group is seen pelting stones in the video.
With his help, we were also able to geolocate the house in question.
Hence, we concluded that the viral video did not show violence during protests over Nupur Sharma's remarks. It's from MP's Khargone, where communal violence broke out earlier this year during Ram Navami.
(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in New Delhi) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jun 14, 2022 12:42 IST

title: Fact Check: Russia's lost ships in the war against Ukraine but this decommissioned US vessel is not one of them
content:
This video was shot during RIMPAC 2016, a maritime warfare exercise. It shows a decommissioned US frigate being sunk as part of an exercise by joint forces of the US, Canada, Australia, and South Korea.
The Russian navy has reportedly taken several high-profile losses while battling Ukraine since February 2022. Putin's naval forces have so far lost at least several "Raptor" patrol boats, a landing ship, a landing craft, and most notably the Moskva, the flagship of its Black Sea Fleet. As the invasion wages on, a video has gone viral on social media that allegedly shows a missile strike on a Russian ship while at the sea. The video did not, however, mention where the ship was attacked or who attacked it. The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was false. This video shows a sinking exercise performed on a decommissioned US ship during the 2016 Rim of the Pacific drill. AFWA Probe Reverse-searching the video's keyframes on Yandex revealed plenty of results. The top result was an article in popularmechanics.com that featured the same video. The headline for the July 2016 story said, "Watch the Navy Send a Retired Frigate Out With a Bang." The article said the video showed the US Navy along with its allies sinking an old frigate as part of a drill in the Pacific Ocean. While the article confirmed that the video was not recent, we checked for more credible sources to confirm the origin of the video. On the verified YouTube channel called ' AiirSource Military ', we found a longer version of the viral video. The video was titled, "Sinking A Navy Frigate With Missiles And Torpedoes SINKEX Sinking Exercise," and it was uploaded to the channel on July 17, 2016. The description of the video reads, "Aerial video of the sinking exercise (SINKEX) of the decommissioned USS Thach (FFG 43) during Rim of the Pacific 2016. The decommissioned ship is fired at with missiles and torpedoes until they sink." Following this, we ran a keyword search for the Rim of the Pacific or RIMPAC 2016, the world's largest international maritime warfare exercise. According to the Daily Mail , decommissioned ships are stripped of their weapons and used for target practice by the forces of the US, Canada, Australia, and South Korea during the biennial event. The report, which had images of the frigate being taken out in plenty, stated the naval and air units of the United Forces took 12 hours to sink the 2013-retired USS Thach near the Hawaiian Islands. According to news.usni.org , on July 14, 2016, the old frigate fell prey to the missiles and torpedoes of the four allies. CNN's video story on the same that used similar footage can be seen here . Thus, it became clear that the claim that the video showed an attack on a Russian ship was baseless. It showed the sinking of an old US frigate as part of the RIMPAC drills in 2016. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Jun 14, 2022 19:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Is this Nupur Sharma's response to international backlash? Nope, this video is from 2019
content:
This video has nothing to do with the ongoing row. This video featuring Sharma is from 2019 and was about the film "Uri".
The Nupur Sharma row continues to unfold. From death threats to several FIRs to public interest litigation in the Supreme Court, Sharma's controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad have caused a storm.
Amid all this, a video has gone viral with the claim that, despite all the drama, the now-suspended Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson appears fairly nonchalant — defiant even — in the face of all the opposition. The video shows Sharma and a group of people shouting, "How's the Josh?" followed by, "High, sir!" They also chant, "Jai Hind!" a couple of times.
Those sharing the video wrote captions like, "This is what you call, rub salt into wounds. We are proud of the lioness, Nupur Sharma," and, " Queen After Offending 1 Billion ."
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) found the claim was false. The video is from 2019 and has no connection with the ongoing row. AFWA Probe
While investigating the claim, we first reverse-searched frames from the video and found the original video on Sharma's verified Twitter account. She shared it on January 26, 2019. Celebrating # #URITheSurgicalStrike style with old college friends! How's the Josh?? High Sir!! @narendramodi ji #RepublicDay2019 cc: @vickykaushal09 pic.twitter.com/hFzaWtJpYp — Nupur Sharma (@NupurSharmaBJP) January 26, 2019

title: Fact Check: This video of cop thrashing elderly man is NOT from anti-Nupur Sharma protests, it's from 2020
content:
The viral video is two years old and not related to the ongoing row. This video is from Uttar Pradesh's Bareilly and shows police action against Covid-19 lockdown violators.
In the backdrop of ongoing protests surrounding Nupur Sharma's controversial remarks on Prophet Muhammad and police action by the Uttar Pradesh government against the protesters , a video of a man being thrashed by police has gone viral with the claim that "Hindutva radicalised cops" brutally assaulted an elderly Muslim man.
Many on Twitter shared the video where a masked policeman could be seen chasing and thrashing a bearded man with a baton. As the video continued, more officers could also be seen beating up others. The video was shared with hashtags like #AfreenFatima, #MuslimsUnderAttackinIndia, and #MuslimLivesMatter.
The India Today Anti Fake News War Room found that the viral video is two years old and not related to the recent Nupur Sharma controversy. It shows cops punishing people for not following lockdown protocols in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh.
The viral posts are archived here and here .
A reverse image search on Yandex led us to the same video being shared as early as 2020. Several YouTube channels uploaded a longer version of the viral video in April 2020, mentioning it was from Bareilly.
Subsequent searches narrowed down to the aforementioned date and location led us to a News Nation video report. Titled, "Uttar Pradesh: Police Attacked By A Group In Bareilly While Enforcing Lockdown," the report was from April 7, 2020.
Per the report, during the Covid-19 lockdown in April 2020, people from the Izatnagar locality in Bareilly attacked a patrolling police party and violated lockdown protocols. Later, a larger group of policemen raided the area and lathi-charged people violating lockdown norms.
This incident was reported by several mainstream media outlets in 2020 which can be seen here , here , and here .
Recently, following Nupur Sharma's controversial remarks, nationwide protests took place and some of these protests turned violent. However, the viral video is not related to the ongoing row. It's a two-year-old video from Bareilly.
(With input from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 16, 2022 16:36 IST

title: Fact Check: A tale of three letters - How a 2020 letter from Amit Shah has become a template for fraud claims
content:
This letter is fake. No letter with this serial number has been issued by the ministry. Similar fake letters in Amit Shah's name, using the same template, have gone viral in the past.
Immediately following her controversial remarks on the Prophet Muhammad, Nupur Sharma reportedly received numerous threats online. The former Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson's comments have been the subject of international and national outrage.
Amid violent protests against her, several FIRs, and reported death threats, a photo of a letter has been making the rounds that supposedly shows the government providing her family with high-level security.
The purported letter from Home Minister Amit Shah asks Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami to provide Z security to Sharma's family home in Dehradun. The letter also praises Sharma for promoting the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ideology and working towards the ultimate goal of a "Hindu Rashtra".
One such post can be seen below.
AFWA found that the letter in circulation is bogus. The Home Ministry has not asked the Uttarakhand CM to provide Z security to Nupur Sharma. Same letter, new hoax
We couldn't find any media report about Shah writing a letter to Dhami regarding Sharma's security. If the Home Minister had written such a letter, it would have made the news.
On June 14, the Press Information Bureau tweeted that Shah sent no such letter to Dhami. A letter is doing rounds on social media claiming to be written by Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, to CM of Uttarakhand, Pushkar Singh Dhami. #PIBFactCheck This letter is FAKE No such letter has been issued by @HMOIndia Do not share the letter pic.twitter.com/uHM5KGhu3j — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) June 14, 2022
A letter is doing rounds on social media claiming to be written by Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, to CM of Uttarakhand, Pushkar Singh Dhami. #PIBFactCheck This letter is FAKE No such letter has been issued by @HMOIndia Do not share the letter pic.twitter.com/uHM5KGhu3j — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) June 14, 2022
This isn't the first time fake letters in the name of Shah have gone viral. We compared the now-viral letter to another phoney letter that went viral in 2021, supposedly sent by Shah to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.
Both letters had the same serial number, "28647021". But there were other glaring similarities as well. Similar shadows in the centre, a dent at the bottom of the letter, and identical folds and creases in two different parts of the letters were visible.
Despite these blatant similarities, however, we also noticed some inconsistencies. The placement of Shah's signature is different in both letters. So, we used error level analysis (ELA), a forensic method that can highlight digitally-modified portions of an image.
We uploaded both letters to FotoForensics . The website highlighted in white the parts of both letters — 2021 and 2022 — which were edited. The body text of the letters was highlighted as edited, as were the sign-offs. The ELA, however, revealed that the signature of the Home Minister, the national emblem or the details in the header and footer were not digitally altered.
This is the 2022 letter. Tracing the original letter
The ELA analysis revealed that in both letters, the same parts were unaltered. Plus, both letters shared similar physical attributes. Thus, we deduced that there was likely an original letter that was edited to create the fraudulent ones.
Advanced searches led us to the letter. A September 2020 report in " TrueScoop " carried a letter from Amit Shah's office that had multiple visual elements similar to the bogus letters.
This letter was a response from Shah's office to Maharashtra BJP MLA Nitesh Narayan Rane who had written to the MHA requesting security for Disha Salian's partner Rohan Rai. Salian, who was found dead in June 2020, was the former manager of Sushant Singh Rajput. When India Today reached out to Rane, the MLA confirmed that the 2020 letter was real and was sent to him by Shah's office in 2020.
The serial number in Rane's letter was 1864702. The serial numbers in the 2021 and 2022 letters were 28647021. It is clear that in both subsequent letters, the serial numbers were slightly tweaked.
It is noteworthy that in 2021, MHA officials confirmed to India Today that no letter bearing the serial number "28647021" had been issued by them.
Thus, we concluded that the 2022 letter where Shah asked Dhami to provide Z security to Sharma is bogus. The original letter that was digitally altered was issued by Shah's office to Maharashtra MLA Nitesh Rane in 2020.
(With inputs from Pathikrit Sanyal) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 16, 2022 20:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Are senior citizen concessions back in Indian Railways? Viral post is a hoax
content:
This viral claim is a hoax. No such decision has been announced. In fact, the Minister of Railways has expressly stated that there are no plans to resume concessions for senior citizens at the moment.
Will the Indian Railways resume the concessions for senior citizens from July? A viral message on social media claims that from July 1, the Indian Railways will resume discounting tickets for senior citizens. Per the post the concessions will be 40 per cent for males above the age of 60 and 50 per cent for females above the age of 58. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story This post and similar ones have been shared by many on Facebook. AFWA found that the viral claim is a hoax. No such decision has been announced by the Indian Railways or the Ministry of Railways. The viral posts have been archived here and here. Ministry of Railways says no India Today went straight to the horse's mouth and contacted Rajeev Jain , ADG Public Relations, Ministry of Railways. Jain categorically denied this viral post, calling it "fake news". He said, "No such decision has been taken, there will be no change in concessions from July 1. Only the existing concessions will continue." On May 19, this year while speaking to reporters at IIT Madras, Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the concession for senior citizens could not be resumed because the Railways was already operating at a subsidised rate.
Will the Indian Railways resume the concessions for senior citizens from July? A viral message on social media claims that from July 1, the Indian Railways will resume discounting tickets for senior citizens. Per the post the concessions will be 40 per cent for males above the age of 60 and 50 per cent for females above the age of 58.
This post and similar ones have been shared by many on Facebook.
AFWA found that the viral claim is a hoax. No such decision has been announced by the Indian Railways or the Ministry of Railways.
The viral posts have been archived here and here.
India Today went straight to the horse's mouth and contacted Rajeev Jain , ADG Public Relations, Ministry of Railways. Jain categorically denied this viral post, calling it "fake news". He said, "No such decision has been taken, there will be no change in concessions from July 1. Only the existing concessions will continue."
On May 19, this year while speaking to reporters at IIT Madras, Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the concession for senior citizens could not be resumed because the Railways was already operating at a subsidised rate.
"For every Rs. 100 spent towards operational expenses, the Railways collects only Rs. 45 from a passenger. We have to contribute to keeping the railways a sustainable mode of transport," the minister emphasised. Who started this rumour?
A Facebook page named "Rail Mail" claimed in a post that the Indian Railways was set to resume concession for the elderly starting July 1. However, the Facebook page later retracted its claim and apologised for its error.
On June 11, a Twitter user raised a query about the concession for the elderly, to which the official Twitter account of Railway Seva replied, "Presently concessions are being given to 4 categories of Divyangjan, and 11 categories of Patients and Students," reinstating that the claim about the resumption of concessions for elderly was false. What are the present concessions in place?
Indian Railways concessions used to range from 25 per cent to 100 per cent in 53 categories. The details of these concessions can be seen here .
But in view of the pandemic and Covid-19 protocols, with effect from March 20, 2020, the Railways indefinitely discontinued concessions with exception to only four categories of Divyangjan, 11 categories of patients, and students. In March this year, the Railway Minister said in the Lok Sabha that the ministry had no plans to restore the concessions for senior citizens.
Even the Press Information Bureau fact-checked this claim and tweeted that posts like these had no factual basis.
(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Jun 16, 2022 23:10 IST

title: Fact Check: Old RRB-NTPC protest video used to assert RJD's role behind anti-Agnipath violence
content:
This viral video is from January 2022, when Bihar students were protesting against Railway Recruitment Board's decision to hold the Non-Technical Popular Categories (NTPC) exams 2021 in two stages.
Several states like Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar have witnessed violent protests against the recent introduction of the 'Agnipath' scheme . Agitations turned violent and resulted in damage to public property worth hundreds of crores in Bihar .
The main opposition party of Bihar, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) has also supported the ongoing protest. Meanwhile, a video has gone viral on social media questioning RJD's role in prompting the youth to riot.
In the viral video , a man is heard introducing himself as a follower of Lalu Prasad Yadav-- the RJD patron, while talking to the press. He goes on to voice the concerns of the students but loses words and disappears when asked about the cause of the protest. ' ' #_ pic.twitter.com/4g3zcFhNWS — ( ) (@KiranKu76964816) June 17, 2022
' ' #_ pic.twitter.com/4g3zcFhNWS — ( ) (@KiranKu76964816) June 17, 2022
While sharing the video, Twitter users have posted captions that blame the party, whose leader is convicted of 'fodder scams', for orchestrating the ongoing protests.
Archived versions of the similar claims can be seen here and here .
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found these posts to be misleading as the video is not related to the ongoing protest. The video is from January when Bihar witnessed protests over the two-stage RRB-NTPC exams.
A reverse search of the screenshots from the viral clip led us to the same video posted by a Twitter user on January 31, 2022.
In that video, the logo of 'Principle of News' was visible. We ran some keywords and found the YouTube channel 'Principle of News' that covers the developments in Bihar.
We found the original video uploaded on January 28, 2022, from which the viral clip was snipped out. The caption of the video clearly states this protest on the RRB-NTPC row.
This is not the first time that Bihar has seen students' protests going violent and leading to arson of public properties this year. In January, angry students set trains on fire after the Railways decided to hold the Railway Recruitment Board's Non-Technical Popular Categories (RRB-NTPC) exams 2021 in two stages. The agitators claimed the second stage for final selection was tantamount to "cheating" those who appeared and cleared the first stage of the RRB-NTPC for computer-based test (CBT) which was released on January 15.
Meanwhile, the Agnipath scheme was introduced by the government on June 14, 2022 . Since then, the RJD has urged the central government several times to recall this scheme .
Therefore, it is safe to conclude that the viral video is not related to the ongoing protests. The footage from several months before is now shared with misleading claims.
