title: Fact Check: Shiv Sena leader shares photo from Pakistan while taking jibe at India's education system
content:
The viral photo of books being sold on a footpath is from Lahore, Pakistan.
On August 3, Manisha Kayande, a member of the Maharashtra Legislative Council and Shiv Sena spokesperson shared a collage of two photos, taking a jibe at India's education standards. The first photo was of a swanky showroom for shoes and the second one showed books being sold on the street. "This says a lot about how we are heading as a society," a line of text in the post read.
Sharing the post, the Sena spokesperson wrote in Hindi , "If India is educated, only then will it improve." Besides Kayande, several other Twitter users also shared the photos with similar captions.
AFWA's investigation found that the photo of books being sold on a footpath is not from India but from Lahore, Pakistan.
The viral posts have been archived here and here .
We snipped out the image showing books on the footpath from the post and ran a reverse image search on it. The results led us to a website called " Locally Lahore ". Here, we found an article on Lahore's Anarkali Bazaar published in 2017.
The article's headline read, "Gem in The Dirt - Sunday Open Book Bazaar at Anarkali Lahore". This article spoke in detail about the weekly open book bazaar in the city. The viral photo, along with others, was published with the report.
We have found a similar article report that carried the same photo published on the website " Youline magazine " in 2019. In both reports, the photo was credited to Humna Jabbar.
We found Jabbar's Facebook and Instagram . From these, we ascertained she is a resident of Lahore. AFWA reached out to Jabbar through her website and enquired about the viral image. Our story will be updated as and when she responds.
However, it is clear that in an attempt to take a jibe at India's education standards, a Sena spokesperson shared a photo from Pakistan. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Aug 8, 2022 15:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann never claimed farmers owe Rs 294 crore to state govt
content:
This claim is misleading. In his speech, Bhagwant Mann was referring to the amount owed by the Punjab government to the farmers and not the other way around.
A video of Bhagwant Mann's speech is being widely shared online. In the 15-second clip , the Punjab chief minister can be heard saying, "The government's Rs 294.98 crore is outstanding towards farmers. It has been pending for many years." Many on social media shared the video and claimed Mann was referring to the amount farmers owe the state government. For example, one person on Facebook wrote , "He's saying that sugarcane farmers owe Rs. 294 crores to the government. Did the government sell sugarcane to farmers?" AFWA's investigation found that, in reality, Mann was referring to the amount owed by the government to the farmers - and not the other way around. AFWA PROBE We noticed the logo of a Punjabi news platform, Prime Asia TV , in the viral video. Following this, we went through its YouTube channel, where we found the full video of his speech uploaded on August 5. At 27 minutes and 22 seconds, Bhagwant Mann can be heard saying the exact lines which feature in the now viral video. He said, "I want to tell you, the government's Rs 294.98 crores were outstanding towards the farmers. It was pending for many years. The honourable finance minister is sitting here, he handles the co-operative department." "We've deposited Rs 100 crores in the accounts of the sugarcane producers," Mann further said. "On August 15 we'll deposit Rs 100 crores more. And the rest of the Rs 94.98 crores will be deposited on September 7. The government's liability towards the sugarcane farmers will be zero then." This speech was also broadcast live on Bhagwant Mann's official Twitter handle on August 5. , Live. https://t.co/vip13WYExU — Bhagwant Mann (@BhagwantMann) August 5, 2022 Earlier, sugarcane farmers throughout Punjab had proposed agitation on August 3, which was later called off after the chief minister accepted most of their demands, including clearing their pending payments. Thus, it's clear that the amount Mann mentioned in his speech was in reference to the amount the Punjab state government had to pay to the sugarcane farmers. Not the other way around. title: Fact Check: This rioting video DOES NOT show recent fuel price protests in Bangladesh - it's from 2013
content:
Although such protests are indeed going on in Bangladesh against the fuel price hike, the video is from May 5, 2013. It shows protests by Islamic hardliners near Dhaka demanding an anti-blasphemy law.
Bangladesh recently witnessed a massive hike in fuel prices resulting in massive protests and demonstrations across the country. Amid this, a video of violent protests and vandalism began making rounds on social media.
People shared the minute-and-a-half-long clip and claimed the video showed people's anger following their government's decision to hike fuel prices.
A verified Twitter account called "Wall Street Silver" shared this video alongside a caption that said, "Bangladesh. Protests and hard clashes have erupted in several cities after the government decided to increase petrol prices by 51 per cent and diesel by 42 per cent effective from midnight. Huge lines are reported at petrol stations all over Bangladesh." Bangladesh protests and hard clashes have erupted in several cities after the government has decided to increase petrol prices by 51% and diesel by 42% effective midnight. Huge lines are reported at petrol stations all over Bangladesh sound pic.twitter.com/JQmUsLBIAD — Wall Street Silver (@WallStreetSilv) August 7, 2022
Bangladesh protests and hard clashes have erupted in several cities after the government has decided to increase petrol prices by 51% and diesel by 42% effective midnight. Huge lines are reported at petrol stations all over Bangladesh sound pic.twitter.com/JQmUsLBIAD — Wall Street Silver (@WallStreetSilv) August 7, 2022
ABP News and India News also used these visuals in their recent news reports on the Bangladesh crisis. Zee News Gujarati also used a screengrab from the same video to report recent protests in Bangladesh.
, - 51.7% #BangladeshEconomicCrisis #BangladeshProtest #petrolPriceHike @rashid_hashmi pic.twitter.com/cwVT9XcCf1 — India News (@IndiaNews_itv) August 7, 2022
, - 51.7% #BangladeshEconomicCrisis #BangladeshProtest #petrolPriceHike @rashid_hashmi pic.twitter.com/cwVT9XcCf1 — India News (@IndiaNews_itv) August 7, 2022
Archived versions of all these posts can be seen here , here , and here .
AFWA's investigation found this video was shot way back in 2013 during a protest in the country. It had nothing to do with the recent protests. AFWA PROBE
A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video took us to a YouTube video from May 6, 2013. A United Kingdom-based news outlet, Channel 4 News, uploaded this clip. "Bangladesh riots: Islamist hardliners fight with police", the caption of the video said. The description of the video further noted that Islamic hardliners engaged in a fierce battle with the police demanding an anti-blasphemy law. Subsequent searches led us to a report in The New York Times published on May 6, 2013. The report mentioned that clashes took place on May 5, 2013, in the capital city of Dhaka. This resulted in the death of at least 22 people. Per the report, three security officers were beaten to death while a dozen other people were killed, including protesters shot by the police. A CNN report further said that activists of a radical Islamic organisation named Hefazat-e-Islam blocked nearly all the roads leading into Dhaka, pressing a list of demands including the anti-blasphemy statute. The same video was uploaded to the official YouTube channel of The Telegraph on May 6, 2013, confirming that this clip was nearly nine years old. Thus, we can safely conclude that the viral video does not show recent violent protests in Bangladesh against the massive fuel price hike. title: Fact Check: Afghan Army chopper's heart-stirring flood rescue operation shared as Pakistan incident
content:
This video shows a rescue effort in Afghanistan's Kandahar province. Not Pakistan.
Amidst turbulent brown flood waters, lay a vehicle toppled. A survivor desperately climbed to the top with his head fixed to the sky, as a military helicopter arrived. Wasting no time, those inside the bird dropped a rope for the survivor to snatch. This breathtaking scene is from a viral video that claims to show Jawans risking their lives to rescue flood victims in Balochistan. Archived versions of the claim can be seen here and here. An investigation by AFWA found that the rescue was not conducted by the Pakistan army in Balochistan as claimed. It is from Afghanistan's Kandahar. AFWA Probe Monsoon spells have claimed over 170 lives in Balochistan this year. Quoting Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), Dawn reported that Balochistan has received 181.7mm of rain since June 14 — almost 300 per cent above what it normally receives each year. ALSO READ| Fact Check Video: Old video of US naval exercise viral as Pelosi's Taiwan escort Having confirmed the province is battling rain's fury, we turned our attention to the video next. When we reverse searched on Yandex, we found a tweet by Afghanistan-based journalist Mustafa Kazemi from January 4. He used a screenshot from the now-viral video here. "Backstory on Kandahar helicopter flood rescue," the thread began. Backstory on Kandahar helicopter flood rescue. Pilots had gathered to leave to Kabul for holiday. They were in a bus in Kandahar airport when they got the call. Two pilots nakedly "Lt. Edris & Capt. Sami" got off the bus & went to their V-5 and flew the rescue mission. pic.twitter.com/BQZJvGxcl3 — Mustafa KAZEMI (@CombatJourno) January 4, 2022 Mustafa said it was the pilots from the 777 Special Mission Wing that carried out the rescue operation in the "v-5" (Mi-17V-5) helicopter. In the last tweet of the thread, Mustafa included a link and screenshot of a video story by Radio Liberty dated March 4, 2019. "Flash flooding in Afghanistan has left dozens dead," text on the screenshot read. Subsequent refined searches led us to a similar photo on the Agence France-Presse website . "In this photo taken on March 2, 2019, an Afghan military helicopter rescues people from atop an overturned truck in flooded area of Arghandab district in Kandahar province," the caption read. At least 20 people were killed by flash floods in Kandahar, AFP said, quoting the UN. Among the reverse search results of the video, there were a couple of tweets on January 3 . They claimed it was an Afghan Defence Ministry helicopter engaged in a rescue operation in Kandahar. MOD deployed helicopter rescue team to save people from flash floods in Kandahar province pic.twitter.com/uRsAR2xN76 — The 220 Podcast (@The220Podcast) January 3, 2022 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story ALSO READ| Fact Check: Shiv Sena leader shares photo from Pakistan while taking jibe at India's education system AFWA reached out to Kazemi who confirmed the viral video was from the incident in Kandahar and not Balochistan as claimed. So, while the claim was not fully true, we can confirm that the video was in circulation long before the monsoon rains wreaked havoc in Balochistan. title: Fact Check: This almost decade-old video does not show world's largest hydroelectric dam bursting during flood
content:
The Three Gorges Dam in central China is the largest hydroelectric dam in the world. There are no recent reports about it breaking. This video is from Uttarakhand's Srinagar and it is more than nine years old.
A video has been making the rounds on social media with the claim that it shows the world's largest hydroelectric dam bursting. In the video , one can see river water flooding a dam.
AFWA's investigation found that this is an old video from Uttarakhand. The world's largest hydroelectric dam is the Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze River in China. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story AFWA Probe The Three Gorges Dam in central China is the largest hydroelectric dam in the world. In 2012, the dam located in the Hubei province of China took over the first place replacing the Itaipú hydroelectric power plant in Brazil and Paraguay. However, we couldn't find any recent reports about the Three Gorges Dam bursting because of floodwaters. In 2020, the Three Gorges Dam was hit heavily by torrential rain and several of its outlets were opened to discharge water.
The Three Gorges Dam in central China is the largest hydroelectric dam in the world. In 2012, the dam located in the Hubei province of China took over the first place replacing the Itaipú hydroelectric power plant in Brazil and Paraguay.
However, we couldn't find any recent reports about the Three Gorges Dam bursting because of floodwaters. In 2020, the Three Gorges Dam was hit heavily by torrential rain and several of its outlets were opened to discharge water.
At multiple instances in the video in question we can hear people speaking in Hindi. This gave the first cue that the video could be from India.
We then did a reverse search of the video in question on Yandex and found a longer version of the same video uploaded to a YouTube channel in December 2013. According to the description, the video was from the Alaknanda Hydro Electric Power Project located in Srinagar, in the Pauri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand.
According to media reports , a flood in June 2013 affected the hydro project, which was then in the developing stage.
To confirm the location of the video in question we reached out to Tejpal Singh Chauhan, India Today's correspondent in the Pauri Garhwal district. Chauhan confirmed to us that the video is indeed from the Alaknanda Hydro Power Generating Station in Srinagar. He also sent us a recent video shot from the same location as seen in the viral video.
A comparison between the screenshot from the viral video and the one sent by our correspondent can be seen below.
Google geolocation of the spot can be seen here.
It is hence clear that the video in question is from Uttarakhand and does not show the world's largest hydropower plant bursting.

title: Fact Check: This heart-wrenching photo of father-daughter duo is neither recent nor from Israel-Palestine crisis
content:
This photo was taken in March 2017 and shows a father carrying his daughter as he walked from an Islamic State-controlled area toward Iraqi special forces soldiers during a battle in Mosul, Iraq.
Amid the ongoing Israel-Palestine crisis, an image of a weeping man carrying a young girl in his arms has gone viral on social media. This image has been shared with hashtags like "Palestine Will Be Free" and with claims that the man and the girl in the photo are Palestinians.
AFWA's investigation found that the viral image is neither recent nor related to the Israel-Palestine conflict. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story WHERE'S THE PHOTO FROM? Upon reverse searching the photo, we found it in a photo gallery of the Radio Free Europe Radio Library . There, the photo's caption read, "A crying man carries his daughter across enemy lines in the Iraqi city of Mosul from territory controlled by Islamic State militants to positions held by Iraqi special forces." The photo was credited to Reuters photographer Goran Tomasevic. Subsequent refined searches led us to several photos of the same father-daughter duo captured from different angles on the official website of Reuters . Per the website, these images were taken on March 4, 2017. They also carried the same caption. This proves the photos are neither recent nor from the Israel-Palestine crisis.
Upon reverse searching the photo, we found it in a photo gallery of the Radio Free Europe Radio Library . There, the photo's caption read, "A crying man carries his daughter across enemy lines in the Iraqi city of Mosul from territory controlled by Islamic State militants to positions held by Iraqi special forces." Subsequent refined searches led us to several photos of the same father-daughter duo captured from different angles on the official website of Reuters . Per the website, these images were taken on March 4, 2017. They also carried the same caption. This proves the photos are neither recent nor from the Israel-Palestine crisis.
According to a July 2017 Reuters report , photographer Tomasevic described the scene when he took this photograph.
He said, "Both screaming in terror, the father and the young daughter he cradled in his arm fled through the rubble-strewn streets of Wadi Hajar, transformed in a flash into a battleground between Islamic State fighters and Iraqi special forces."
He added, "When they reached the special forces lines, males were ordered to lift their shirts to prove they weren't suicide bombers. The father was so beside himself, so panicked. According to a CNN report , at least 43 Palestinians including 15 children have been killed after the recent round of fighting between Israel and Gaza-based militants. Israel has maintained that most of the people who died in its airstrikes were militants.

title: Fact Check: No, there is no SC-ordered taxpayers' group that will dictate election freebies
content:
While the apex court has recommended a committee that would advise the governments on election freebies, it is yet to assign the powers and limitations of this committee.
If social media is to be believed, then India is all set to have the largest organisation of taxpayers in the world. That too, at the recommendation of the apex court of the country.
Many on social media are claiming that once it is formed, "No matter which Government is ruling, without the approval of this Organisation, no free electricity, free water, free distribution, or loan waivers can be announced by any government implement them[sic]. As the Money belongs to our tax payments, so the taxpayers should have the right to oversee its use."
AFWA's investigation found that while it's true that the Supreme Court recently recommended a committee comprising several stakeholders that would look into the matters related to freebies announced by political parties during elections, however, the apex court is yet to mention the powers and limitations of such a committee.
While investigating the claim, we found a PTI report from August 3. It stated, following a PIL that challenged the practice of political parties promising freebies during elections, a Supreme Court bench suggested a committee comprising different stakeholders that would suggest measures to tackle the issue.
We then searched on the Supreme Court website to find out what the bench has actually ordered.
The order dated August 3 quotes: "Keeping in mind the prayers made in these petitions which relate to distribution of freebies by political parties, we are of the considered view that it would be appropriate to constitute an Expert Body with representatives of all the stakeholders: the beneficiaries, those opposing freebies, Central Government, State Governments, opposition parties, Finance Commission, Reserve Bank of India, Niti Ayog etc., to name a few, to take a holistic and comprehensive view of the matter and making their recommendations." The apex court further ordered that all stakeholders mentioned in the order and veteran advocate Kapil Sibal put their recommendations on the composition of the committee within a week. The National Herald published a piece on this order, talking to various Supreme Court advocates. Sanjay Hegde was quoted saying, "There is only a committee that is being formed. No report has come yet. The issue of jurisdiction will arise only if the apex court decides to act on the recommendations of the committee. As of now, it seems like it will be a burial by committee." No reports also mention this committee either being called or referring to an all-India organisation of taxpayers. Hence, we can conclude that this claim is misleading. Although the Supreme Court has recommended a committee that will advise on issues related to election freebies, it has not yet been mentioned that election freebies can't be implemented without the approval of such a committee. title: Fact Check: Footage of Taliban chopper crash shared as Balochistan mishap that killed Pak Lt General
content:
This video predates the Balochistan incident and reportedly shows a Taliban pilot crashing a chopper in Afghanistan's Kandahar province in January, 2022.
Six Pakistani military personnel, including a Lieutenant-General, died in a helicopter crash in Balochistan on August 1. The crew was conducting relief operations in the flood-hit province when their chopper crashed due to bad weather .
Now, several people are sharing air mishap footage claiming to show how Lieutenant-General Sarfraz Ali and his men lost their lives.
The video shows a chopper wobbling over a flooded road full of vehicles before crashing at a distance. Civilians can be seen shooting the incident on their phones. The post claimed the video was one such piece of footage.
An AFWA investigation revealed that this footage predates the chopper crash in Balochistan. It was viral before, purportedly from Taliban-occupied Afghanistan. AFWA PROBE
While going through the comments on one such post , we found one that said "Wrong video," along with a YouTube link to support the claim.
Uploaded on January 5, 2022, it was the same video. "Crazy Flight helicopter crash funny Taliban helicopter flight video," the video was titled.
This confirmed that the viral video is old and unrelated to the recent Balochistan air crash.
A reverse search of the video's keyframes on Yandex led us to the YouTube channel of Afghanistan-based Aamaj News . The video was uploaded on January 5.
Yandex also led us to Russian and Ukrainian news articles that used Aamaj News screenshots to report that Taliban pilots crashed an American military class MD 530F helicopter in Kandahar. The chopper was reportedly engaged in flood rescue operations in the region.
The same claim was made on Reddit as well.
Agence France-Presse too reported on the viral video, citing Zee News and Mojo TV having used the clip while reporting the incident in January.
AFWA in the past has debunked disinformation pertaining to Balochistan. Some of these reports can be read here and here and here .
It is thus clear that the viral video is unrelated to the recent helicopter clash in Pakistan that killed six, including a top commander.

title: Fact Check: Nitish Kumar attacked the BJP in this 2014 clip — NOT the RJD
content:
The original video dates back to February 18, 2014. In it, Nitish Kumar was not attacking the RJD. Rather, he was calling out the BJP and the NDA.
Bihar is once again going through political turmoil after the Janata Dal (United) chief Nitish Kumar cut off his ties with the National Democratic Alliance. Amid this crisis, a video of the Bihar Chief Minister's speech has started making the rounds on social media. Those sharing it claim that Kumar said he would never join hands with the Rashtriya Janata Dal in this video.
Kumar, in this 28-second-long clip , said, "After this, it does not matter whatever the situation may be, there is no question of going back. No understanding is possible, whether I exist or am buried in the soil. Impossible — this is not possible anymore. The chapter is closed forever, as you have shattered trust." " ... " #___ #BiharPolitics #NitishKumar #_ pic.twitter.com/uZ37gWUKjI — Shivraj Singh Dabi (@ShivrajDabi) August 9, 2022
" ... " #___ #BiharPolitics #NitishKumar #_ pic.twitter.com/uZ37gWUKjI — Shivraj Singh Dabi (@ShivrajDabi) August 9, 2022
Those sharing the video claimed these words to be made for RJD, the party of Lalu Prasad Yadav.
Archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here .
AFWA's investigation found that the video is eight years old and in it, Nitish Kumar was attacking the Bharatiya Janata Party and not the RJD. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video led us to a tweet by the official handle of the RJD. Sharing the same video, this 2019 tweet claimed that Kumar had targeted the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and the BJP in his speech. - ! ! ! pic.twitter.com/6MV60aGWdE — Rashtriya Janata Dal (@RJDforIndia) November 15, 2019
- ! ! ! pic.twitter.com/6MV60aGWdE — Rashtriya Janata Dal (@RJDforIndia) November 15, 2019
The Navbharat Times also published a news report stating the same.
A subsequent refined search for the full-length video took us to First Bihar Jharkhand , a verified YouTube channel dedicated to news. There, we found a four-minute-long video of this same speech by Nitish Kumar.
Around the one-and-half-minute mark, Kumar said, "I trusted. That was the era of Atalji (Atal Bihari Vajpayee). Now it's not there anymore. When we were parting, Advaniji (Lal Krishna Advani) called and said that the promises made by the speaker will be fulfilled. I said that it is not possible for us anymore."
"And the speaker who promised is not there anymore. Who will remember those? That is why we decided to walk on our path. So that era ended then. Now you have come with a new avatar. After this, it does not matter whatever the situation may be, there is no question of going back," Kumar further added, making it clear that these words were aimed at the BJP.
We came across another video on YouTube that dated this speech to be from February 19, 2014.
Further advanced searches led us to a report published in Jagran on February 18, 2014. The report said that Kumar made these comments when he was asked if the JD(U) wanted to form alliances with the BJP again. A Dainik Bhaskar report also stated the same.
However, Nitish Kumar had said in 2017 after parting ways with the RJD that he cannot be with "people who commit the sin of amassing property through corrupt means while hiding behind the shield of secularism." Now, he is all set to form a new government in Bihar with the help of RJD again. Published By: Komal Sharma Published On: Aug 10, 2022 15:20 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of BJP workers getting bashed by TMC in Hooghly falsely shared as JD(U) retaliation in Bihar
content:
This video is from a fight that broke out between Trinamool Congress and BJP workers in West Bengal's Hooghly district on August 5.
A video showing two groups getting into a scuffle has been circulating on social media. It's being claimed that it shows BJP workers in Bihar getting trashed on the road following its split with the Janata Dal (United). In the video , a few people can also be seen holding BJP flags.
The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here .
AFWA's investigation found that this video shows a fight that broke out between Trinamool Congress and BJP workers in West Bengal. DEFINITELY NOT BIHAR
In the video, we can hear people talking in Bangla. Additionally, 20 seconds into the video, "Chinsurah" can be seen written at a roundabout. Chinsurah is in the Hooghly district of West Bengal. This indicated the video was not from Bihar at all.
We were also able to geolocate the viral video on Google. A search on Google Maps for Khadina More Junction led us to a user-uploaded photo that matched the location of the viral video. WHAT HAPPENED?
A reverse search of the keyframes of the video led us to media reports from August 5, 2022.
Per the reports , the video is from a scuffle that broke out between TMC and BJP workers during a rally organised by the BJP at Khadinan More in Chinsurah.
The BJP had accused TMC MLA Asit Majumdar and his supporters of beating up the saffron party's workers without any provocation. Denying the accusation, Majumdar claimed that he and other party workers had confronted BJP workers who were making supposedly false allegations against the TMC.
A video report about the incident by News18 India can be seen below. . , BIP-TMC #BengalNews #TMc #BJP @_poojaLive pic.twitter.com/SaXoCqbiYx — News18 India (@News18India) August 6, 2022

title: Fact Check: Hyderabad, Mumbai or Kolkata? This flyover decked in tricolour lights is actually from Jaipur
content:
This video is not from Hyderabad at all. It shows the newly-constructed Sodala Elevated Road in Jaipur, Rajasthan.
On August 15 this year, India will celebrate its 75th Independence Day. Amid people using the Indian flag as their social media avatars, and various celebrations being planned across the country, a video of a city street has gone viral.
Several people shared a video which shows a flyover illuminated in saffron, white, and green lights. They claimed it was from Bhagyanagar, Hyderabad.
But some also claimed these sights were from other cities. Some said Borivali in Mumbai , while others said it was from Kolkata .
AFWA's investigation found all three claims were false.
We reverse searched the keyframes of the video and found it shared by an Instagram account . The account mentioned it was from Jaipur, Rajasthan. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rajasthan (@rajastha.n)
A post shared by Rajasthan (@rajastha.n)
Subsequent refined searches led us to videos of the same flyover on YouTube. On the YouTube channel of First India News we found a news report from August 4, 2022.
Per the report, this flyover was the Sodala Elevated Road in Jaipur. In the video news story, the reporter interviewed an official from the Jaipur Development Authority (JDA).
Following this, AFWA got in touch with the JDA. "Yes, this is the video of the Sodala Elevated Road connecting Ajmer Road and Tonk Road in Jaipur," JDA chief engineer Sanjeev Jain said.
Hence, we can conclude that this video is neither from Mumbai, nor Hyderabad, nor Kolkata. It's from Jaipur, Rajasthan.

title: Fact Check: New fake doctor scam after teacher recruitment scam in Bengal? This news report is 5 years old!
content:
This scam is not a new one. In 2017, over 500 fake doctors were identified in multiple institutes in West Bengal. Many were arrested.
The Central Bureau of Investigation on August 10 made its first arrests in the alleged School Service Commission scam in West Bengal. And even as this fraud is unravelling, is there another scam related to fake doctors being busted in the state?
A video of a news report has been widely shared on social media. It claims that a fake medical degree racket has been brought down by the authorities.
The news clip claims that several persons with fake medical certificates have been arrested. These people were allegedly practising in the top hospitals of Kolkata, posing as doctors.
One such social media post, alongside the video, claimed: "560 fake medical degrees sold in Kolkata. Fake doctors were arrested from the top hospitals in Kolkata. Out of 560 fake doctors, one doctor got the President's award recently. Only god can save us."
AFWA's investigation found the news clip is not recent at all - in fact, it is more than five years old. AFWA PROBE
We searched for a fake medical degree racket in West Bengal and found several 2017 news reports with similar claims. The Times of India and The Hindu reported in June 2017 that over 500 fake doctors were identified in multiple institutes in West Bengal.
We also found the same viral news clip on YouTube on NDTV's channel, entitled: "6 Fake Doctors Arrested In Bengal In A Month, 3 From Top Kolkata Hospitals".
We also found reports stating that one of the fake doctors arrested around that time was awarded by the President of India.
Per the reports , Subhendu Bhattacharya of Howrah was awarded the lifetime achievement award by President Pranab Mukherjee during the 6th Dr Malati Allen Nobel Award in Kolkata. He was later arrested.
So, we concluded that a five-year-old incident was shared as a recent one on social media.

title: Fact Check: Don't fall for this 'fake' Emirates Airlines free tickets contest — it's another phishing scam!
content:
This is a phishing scam. Emirates Airlines confirmed it is not running any such contest, adding this website has no link to it.
Who wouldn't love free flight tickets for vacationing abroad? Well, a website in the name of Emirates Airlines has been offering free two-way tickets to Europe and Asia. But before you get too excited: it's just another phishing scam! Phishing scams use deception to trick people into divulging sensitive data. Often, they are used for data mining. But sometimes, they are also used for financial fraud. The link to this website is being widely shared on Facebook and WhatsApp. An Emirates Airlines representative confirmed to AFWA that this is a fake website, adding that the airline is not running any such contest. How does the scam work? We tried to open this website on a desktop computer but failed. Ultimately, we realised that it has been created in such a way that it only opens on a phone. Once you access the website, it asks you to take a short quiz to avail the aforementioned free flight tickets. As you answer the questions, you will be redirected to a new page with gift boxes. Upon selecting these boxes, you'll be informed that you've won two round-trip flight tickets to Europe or Asia. Next, you are asked to share the website link with either 30 friends or five (WhatsApp) groups. This is standard in phishing scams. As you do this and click on the "Finish" button, you will be redirected to another web page with the warning: "This page has been reported unsafe." Multiple red flags The website: There are various red flags on this website which indicate that this is not the official website of Emirates Airlines. The search box, the dropdown menu, and the user profiles listed under the "Customer Reviews" section — none of them are clickable. The URL: The website's link " tinyurl5.ru/r284629707/ " resembles a shortened URL made using tinyurl.com . This appears to have been done to bluff people and make them believe that this is a genuine website whose link has just been shortened. When you share this URL on mobile WhatsApp, the preview mentions " fly.emirates.com ". This is quite identical to the actual preview you'd see for the Emirates Airlines website emirates.com . This is what the original Emirates Airlines looks like. Newly-made : Using the GoDaddy WhoIs tool, we found that this website was created on April 6, 2022. Such websites are generally created to run temporary scams and deleted as and when this is done — or if it gets reported. Experts say this is 'Typical'. AFWA spoke to cybersecurity expert Bob Diachenko, who examined it and called it a typical phishing website. He added that about 15 security vendors had already flagged it as malicious. Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Aug 11, 2022 18:41 IST

title: Fact Check: No, 18% GST on house rent is NOT applicable to all tenants
content:
The GST council has indeed levied a GST on house rent. But this 18 per cent tax is not meant for all. It is only applicable to companies or individuals that are registered under GST.
If social media posts are to be believed, one now has to pay a Goods and Service Tax even for renting a house. One such post claims, "Modi promised in 2018 - Every Indian will have a house by 2022. Modi delivered in 2022 - 18% GST on house rent." Modi promised in 2018 - Every Indian will have a house by 2022. Modi delivered in 2022 - 18% GST on house rent.
— Sanghamitra (@AudaciousQuest_) August 12, 2022
Modi promised in 2018 - Every Indian will have a house by 2022. Modi delivered in 2022 - 18% GST on house rent.
— Sanghamitra (@AudaciousQuest_) August 12, 2022
AFWA's investigation found that GST on house rent is not applicable for all. It is only meant for those tenants — business firms or individuals — who are registered under GST. Is there really a tax on renting houses?
The short answer is yes. But this tax does not apply to everyone.
While investigating the claim, we found a detailed report on GST on house rent in the Business Standard . It states that under the new system, 18 per cent GST will be charged on house rent under the reverse charge mechanism (RCM), where the tenant will be liable to pay it.
However, the report clarified that salaried individuals need not pay any such tax. The new rule only applies if the person/company has completed GST registration.
What's more? The report further states that if neither tenant nor landlord is not registered under GST, there is no legal obligation to pay any tax on the rent.
Archit Gupta, founder and CEO at ClearTax, explained to the media: "If any common salaried person has taken a residential house or flat on rent or lease, they do not have to pay GST. However, a GST-registered person who carries out business or profession must incur 18 per cent GST on such rent paid to the owner."
To further confirm the claim, we tried to look for a government report that supported this media report. We found a press release from the PIB on the recommendations of the recently concluded 47th GST Council Meeting. The press release was published on June 29, 2022.
This press release states that the council has withdrawn the exemption on a few services. One such service is renting residential dwellings to business entities (registered persons).
In fact, the PIB also debunked the viral claim about tax on renting houses. Claim: 18% GST on house rent for tenants #PibFactCheck Renting of residential unit taxable only when it is rented to business entity No GST when it is rented to private person for personal use No GST even if proprietor or partner of firm rents residence for personal use pic.twitter.com/3ncVSjkKxP — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) August 12, 2022
Claim: 18% GST on house rent for tenants #PibFactCheck Renting of residential unit taxable only when it is rented to business entity No GST when it is rented to private person for personal use No GST even if proprietor or partner of firm rents residence for personal use pic.twitter.com/3ncVSjkKxP — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) August 12, 2022
Hence, we concluded that this viral claim was misleading. While the GST council has indeed levied a tax on house rent, this 18 per cent tax is not meant for all. It is only for companies or individuals that have completed GST registration. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Aug 13, 2022 12:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Positive 'Dangal' review shared as 'Laal Singh Chaddha's' audience reaction amid controversies
content:
This video is nearly six years old and not related to 'Laal Singh Chaddha'. It shows the public reacting to 'Dangal', which was released in 2016.
Even before its release, Aamir Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan-starrer 'Laal Singh Chaddha', a remake of the Hollywood Oscar-winner 'Forrest Gump', was at the centre of controversy. Many pledged on social media to boycott the film and encouraged others to do so. And now, even after its release, the controversies continue, with myriad allegations of the film being disrespectful to the Indian Army, the Sikh community, and others. Amid all of this, however, many on Twitter have shared a video , claiming it to be the audience's positive reaction to the film. # Baycott . pic.twitter.com/CvkKiS8bnF — Rishi R,Sharma (@RishiSh27706153) August 11, 2022 The video allegedly shows vox pop interviews of audience members after a special screening of 'Laal Singh Chaddha'. People in the video appeared to be all praise for the film and Khan's acting. The same video was shared on Facebook as well. Archived versions of some similar posts can be seen here and here. AFWA's investigation has found this video is nearly six years old. It shows the audience's reaction to 'Dangal', another movie led by Aamir Khan that was released in 2016. AFWA Probe In the video, not a single viewer mentioned "Laal Singh Chaddha" by its name. This made us doubt the authenticity of the claim. We noticed the logo for 'movie talkies.com' was visible in the video. So, we searched for the official YouTube channel of this website . There, we came across the first public review of "Laal Singh Chaddha", uploaded to the YouTube channel on August 11. In this video, the audience's reaction was lukewarm — as opposed to the viral video where the reactions were overwhelmingly positive. While it received praise from some, others stated it was a "waste of money." More importantly, however, the people speaking in the viral video were not in this one. We also noticed the new logo of the channel was different from the logo seen in the viral video. Subsequent searches on the channel took us to a video that was uploaded on December 23, 2016. It showed people reacting to Aamir Khan's "Dangal", a film that smashed box office records. Reportedly, "Dangal" earned a whopping collection of Rs. 2,024 crore worldwide, and remains one of the highest-grossing Indian movies. When we compared this video with the viral one, it became clear that the viral video was cut from this footage. Any mention of the film's name, "Dangal", was removed from the video to give it a false spin. "Laal Singh Chaddha" has received mixed reviews from critics. And its box office collections have not lived up to expectations. It has managed to collect Rs. 18.96 crore in its first two days. #LaalSinghChaddha falls flat on Day 2... Drop at national chains... Mass pockets face steep fall... 2-day total is alarmingly low for an event film... Extremely crucial to score from Sat-Mon... Thu 11.70 cr, Fri 7.26 cr. Total: 18.96 cr. #India biz. Note: #HINDI version. pic.twitter.com/9hwygm6Jrm — taran adarsh (@taran_adarsh) August 13, 2022 Therefore, we concluded that the viral video does not show the audience's reaction to "Laal Singh Chaddha". Published By: Ritika Shah Published On: Aug 13, 2022 17:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Unrelated to India@75-This video of Shivraj Singh Chouhan hoisting BJP flag is from 2018
content:
This video is from 2018 and is unrelated to India's Independence Day celebrations. This took place during a BJP event near Khajuraho, MP.
As India gets ready to celebrate 75 years of its independence, both social media and the streets have been filled with the Indian flag. This has only been boosted by the government of India's "Har Ghar Tiranga" campaign, a part of its Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav initiative. Amid all this, a video featuring Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has been shared widely along with critical comments. The video shows Chouhan unfurling the Bharatiya Janata Party flag as someone can be heard singing the national anthem. Many on Facebook shared the video and wrote captions criticising Chouhan. For example, "Even in old age, you could not understand that the country is before the party! Neither Modiji nor you are following 'Rajdharma'! Only those who fill the party's pocket in the name of the national flag can consider the BJP flag bigger than the tricolour! BJP is insulting the tricolour." AFWA's investigation found that the viral video is old and unrelated to the celebration of 75 years of India's Independence. The viral posts have been archived here and here . AFWA Probe When we searched online for news on this, we found a tweet by journalist Dinesh Shukla from May 14, 2018. Sharing the same video, Shukla wrote that as part of the Chalo Panchayat campaign in Madhya Pradesh, Chouhan hoisted the BJP flag in the Khajua village near Khajuraho. @BJP4India @ChouhanShivraj ... ? pic.twitter.com/QXjPLZ6e0b — Dinesh Shukla (@dineshhshukla) May 14, 2018 Following a subsequent refined search, we found a Patrika report from May 16, 2018, regarding the incident. Per the report, on May 14, 2018, during a "Panchayat Chalo" event, Chouhan hoisted a BJP flag and the national anthem was sung. Opposition leaders criticised him and the party for reciting the national anthem after hoisting the party flag. The report also carried screenshots from the same video. Thus, we were able to conclude that this incident happened four years ago and has nothing to do with the upcoming Independence Day celebrations. title: Fact Check: Video from Kerala shared as crowd thronging Lucknow's Lulu mall to watch 'Laal Singh Chaddha'
content:

Aamir Khan starrer 'Laal Singh Chaddha', the ambitious Hindi remake of Hollywood masterpiece 'Forrest Gump', is receiving a lukewarm response in theatres, say reports .

"People throng to see the film Lal Singh Chaddha at Lulu Mall, Lucknow," a user wrote in Hindi while tweeting the video.

Several netizens had aggressively replied to the tweet saying that the video was from Kerala and not Lucknow as claimed. One such reply had a screenshot of an India Today video with a Hindi report. The partly visible title of the video link read, "Thallumaala promotions can". pic.twitter.com/o70tH12IDd — Vineet Sharma / (@Vini_kushinagar) August 13, 2022
pic.twitter.com/o70tH12IDd — Vineet Sharma / (@Vini_kushinagar) August 13, 2022

title: Fact Check: Old video of teacher thrashing a student in Bihar passed off as that of Jalore incident
content:
A Dalit student has been allegedly killed by a teacher for drinking water in a school in Jalore. But the viral video is of a different incident from Bihar.
A nine-year-old Dalit boy died on Saturday after he was allegedly beaten up by a teacher for drinking water from a pot in a private school in Rajasthan's Jalore district.
Amidst the public outrage over the shocking incident, a Facebook user posted a video of a man brutally thrashing a boy and claimed that this was how the teacher killed the boy for drinking water.
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that the video is unrelated to the Jalore incident. The video was shot in Bihar earlier this year where a tuition teacher was arrested for brutally beating a student.
Using reverse image search, we found the screenshots of the viral video tweeted by the news agency ANI on July 7, 2022. According to the tweet, the incident was from Bihar where a tuition teacher called Amarkant Kumar was arrested for brutally thrashing a six-year-old student. title: Fact Check: Video of Rakesh Jhunjhunwala dancing in wheelchair is NOT his last — it's from July 2021
content:
This was not the last video of Rakesh Jhunjhunwala. The viral video is from July 2021 during his birthday celebrations.
Following the demise of billionaire business magnate Rakesh Jhunjhunwala on August 14, a video of him dancing while sitting in a wheelchair has gone viral on social media. Those sharing it claimed that this was the last video of Jhunjhunwala.
AFWA's investigation found that this was not the last video of Jhunjhunwala — it is old. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Is the video recent? When we reverse-searched frames from the video, we found that many people had shared the video in question last year on social media. A Facebook user shared it on August 17, 2021, and wrote in the caption, "Big Bull...Rakesh Jhunjhunwala dancing at his best He is on wheel chair from last one year Due to Diabetic Foot." This concluded that the video was at least a year old — making it unlikely that this was his last video prior to his death. When is the video from? We found that a YouTube channel called "Stoploss Hunter" shared the video, post the businessman's death, entitled, "Rakesh Jhunjhunwala Funny moments. India will miss you sir." We noticed that the video contained the Business Today logo and the date "July 5, 2021". Overlaid text in the video read, "RJ at his b'day celebration on July 5, 2021." Subsequently, we searched for this video on Business Today's YouTube . The video was uploaded on August 14 and its title read, "A rare video of Rakesh Jhunjhunwala dancing at his birthday celebrations on July 5, 2021."
When we reverse-searched frames from the video, we found that many people had shared the video in question last year on social media. A Facebook user shared it on August 17, 2021, and wrote in the caption, "Big Bull...Rakesh Jhunjhunwala dancing at his best He is on wheel chair from last one year Due to Diabetic Foot."
This concluded that the video was at least a year old — making it unlikely that this was his last video prior to his death.
We found that a YouTube channel called "Stoploss Hunter" shared the video, post the businessman's death, entitled, "Rakesh Jhunjhunwala Funny moments. India will miss you sir." We noticed that the video contained the Business Today logo and the date "July 5, 2021". Overlaid text in the video read, "RJ at his b'day celebration on July 5, 2021."
Subsequently, we searched for this video on Business Today's YouTube . The video was uploaded on August 14 and its title read, "A rare video of Rakesh Jhunjhunwala dancing at his birthday celebrations on July 5, 2021."
This confirmed that the video was from July last year. His last video
Rakesh Jhunjhunwala was wheelchair-bound for over a year due to various diabetes-related ailments. But even then, he was active in business and public life. Per news reports , Jhunjhunwala met Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in October last year.
On August 7, his last public appearance was at an Akasa Air event. Jhunjhunwala held 40 per cent stake in Akasa Air. "Normally, a child is born in nine months. We (Akasa Air) took 12 months. It would not have been possible without the cooperation of the Ministry of Civil Aviation," Jhunjhunwala had said in his short speech at the Mumbai airport. "Nowhere in the world has an airline been conceived and born in 12 months," he had said.
A week before his death, Jhunjhunwala gave an interview to CNBC TV-18. In the interview, he shared his insights on Indian markets and Akasa Air. "Regardless of the global developments, the Indian market will grow, but at a slower pace," he had said.
Thus, it is clear that Jhunjhunwala's last video was most definitely not the July 2021 video of him dancing while using a wheelchair. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Aug 15, 2022 14:46 IST

title: Fact Check: No, the Centre is NOT privatising all public sector banks except SBI!
content:
Two economists Poonam Gupta and Arvind Panagariya have recommended the privatisation of all nationalised banks, except SBI, in a policy paper. However, the government has not approved this recommendation yet.
Ever since Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman proposed to take up the privatisation of two public sector banks in her Budget speech for the fiscal year 2021-22, the issue has been widely debated. However, even as the pros and cons of such a move are being discussed, a few on social media have claimed that all nationalised banks, except the State Bank of India, will be privatised.
One such Facebook post contains a screenshot of a Zee News Hindi headline that claims the same.
AFWA's investigation found that this claim is misleading. The Centre has not announced anything of this sort as of yet. Archived versions of such posts can be seen here .
While investigating the claim, we found a report by The Times of India from July 12, according to which, a policy paper of the Indian Policy Forum recommended privatisation of all nationalised banks. It further stated that due to its better performance, SBI may remain under government control.
The policy paper was written by Poonam Gupta, the Director-General of the National Council of Applied Economic Research and a member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, and Arvind Panagariya, former NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman and Columbia University professor. However, we found no media reports that claimed the Centre approved this recommendation.
We also looked for what Zee News reported, given that its headline was shared by many on social media.
We found the Zee News report from July 13 whose headline went viral. It says that the Centre will privatise two nationalised banks in 2022. It also mentioned the recommendations of Gupta and Panagariya.
However, according to an August 2 report in the Hindu Business Line , the government told the Rajya Sabha that the privatisation of public sector banks will have to wait and a Bill has not been listed for the current session. Minister of State for Finance Bhagwat K Karad said in a written reply: "As per list of business for monsoon session no such bill has been listed for introduction, consideration and passing."
Hence, we can conclude that the viral post is misleading - as was the Zee news headline.
(With input from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Aug 15, 2022 18:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Lucknow school play show 'Bharat Mata' being made to offer namaz? Clip shared out of context
content:
This is a clipped video. The original video shows the same girl offering prayers as per the religious customs of Hinduism, Sikhism, and Christianity as well.
As India celebrated its 76th Independence Day on August 15, a video of school students performing in a play was widely shared on social media. The video shows a girl dressed in a sari and a crown surrounded by boys and girls dressed up in skull caps and hijabs. As the video progresses, the students in skull caps remove the crown from the head of the girl supposedly dressed as "Bharat Mata". They are then seen putting a scarf on her head and all of them start offering namaz. Those sharing the video claimed this video was from the Shishu Bharti Vidyalay in Malviya Nagar, Aishbagh, Lucknow. They also asked for strict action against the school for depicting such a scene in a children's play. Bharatiya Janata Party leader Abhijat Mishra shared this video, tagging Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, seeking his attention on the matter. He has since deleted his tweet. Archived versions of the post can be seen here . AFWA's investigation found that the viral video was trimmed out of context to give it a false and communal spin. AFWA Probe When we searched online, we found a two-minute-20-second-long video of the same play that was recorded from another angle. Arvind Chauhan, a Times of India journalist, shared this video. Here is the complete video of the students offering prayers in various ways (as per the religions) #Lucknow https://t.co/OS99RE0ie8 pic.twitter.com/DIsHq9GB4m — Arvind Chauhan (Silly Soul | ) (@Arv_Ind_Chauhan) August 15, 2022 This video clearly shows how the play featured different groups of students denoting different religious groups offering prayers as per Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, and Christian customs, along with the girl in the sari. It did not just show students removing the crown and making the girl in the sari offer namaz. Subsequent searches led us to a tweet by the Lucknow Police Commissionerate on August 15 confirming that the viral video was clipped from the original context to give it a communal spin. It further stated that action is being taken against those who shared the clipped video. @Uppolice pic.twitter.com/t8a6Ws5B6b — POLICE COMMISSIONERATE LUCKNOW (@lkopolice) August 15, 2022 AWFA reached out to Sunil Sharma, an additional CP in the Lucknow Police Commissionerate. He said, "Following an investigation, we found that on the occasion of Independence Day, the play was staged by children where prayers of all the religions were performed. But someone shared the clipped video on social media. We are taking cognisance of the matter, and action will be taken." Therefore, it is safe to conclude that a viral video from Lucknow's school was shared with a false and communal twist. title: Fact Check: Video of boy dancing FALSELY shared as Jalore Dalit student who died after teacher beat him up
content:
This video shows Harish Bheel, a class 2 student from Barmer, Rajasthan. Bheel's headmaster confirmed this. Meghwal's father also confirmed this was not his son.
A video of a young boy dancing to a Rajasthani song has gone viral on social media. Those sharing it claimed that this boy was Indra Kumar Meghwal, the nine-year-old Dalit student at Saraswati Vidya Mandir in Jalore, Rajasthan, who recently died after he was allegedly assaulted by his schoolteacher.
According to media reports , the accused Chail Singh reportedly saw Meghwal drinking water from an earthen pot that was "reserved for upper-caste teachers", and subsequently beat him up. His family claims the assault took place on July 20. Singh has been arrested and booked for murder and under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
One Facebook user who shared the video wrote, "Some memories of Indra. What innocence! How was this poor child even supposed to know that he would lose his life for merely quenching his thirst! It is hard to believe that this poor child got such brutal punishment. Thousand salutes to him!"
AFWA's investigation found that the boy seen dancing in the viral video is not Indra Kumar Meghwal. He is Harish Bheel, a resident of Barmer, Rajasthan.
We compared the appearance of the boy seen in the viral video with some images and videos of Indra Kumar Meghwal and found that the two looked very different. Subsequently, we scanned the comments sections of the viral posts and found a comment that claimed the boy's name was Harish. The comment added that he was a student at the Gomrakh Dham school in Barmer, Rajasthan. Per the Facebook profile of the commentor, Tr Chela Ram Raika, he is a teacher at the GUPS Gomrakh Dham School in Barmer. We then looked into the official Facebook Page of Government Upper Primary School Gomrakh Dham. There, we found a longer version of the viral dance video shared on July 30 with the caption, "Class 2 student Harish gave a confident performance on the occasion of 'No bag day'." Harish performed on this independence day as well AFWA contacted Gunesha Ram Choudhary, the headmaster of Government Upper Primary School Gomrakh Dham, who confirmed to us that the child in the video is Harish Bheel, a student at his school. "Six-year-old Harish studies in class 2 and has a keen interest in dancing. He gave a rocking performance on August 15 as well," Choudhary added. He also sent us a video of Harish's independence day performance, which can be seen below. As per Choudhary, Bheel's viral dance video was shared on the school's Facebook Page on July 30. However, the school staff was shocked when some people began circulating it in the backdrop of the Jalore incident. He sent us yet another video of Bheel in which he identifies himself. In this video, his face is clearly visible. Looking at this video, one can easily make out that this is the boy from the viral video. India Today's Jalore correspondent Naresh Sarnau Vishnoi further contacted Indra Kumar Meghwal's family members and showed them the viral video. The deceased student's father Devaram Meghwal confirmed that the boy in the viral video was not his son. Thus, we concluded that this video has been shared with a false claim. The boy in the video is not Indra Kumar Meghwal. Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Aug 16, 2022 15:01 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Pfizer CEO did not say his company aims to cut world population by 50%
content:
The clip is doctored. He actually said, "By 2023, we will reduce the number of people in the world that cannot afford our medicines by 50 per cent".
A video of Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla has gone viral on social media, where he can be heard talking about his company's goal of "reducing the number of people in the world."
In the video, Bourla can be heard saying , "I think that is really fulfilling of a dream that we had, together with my leadership team when we started in '19. The first week we met in January of '19 in California to set up the goals for the next five years, and one of them was by 2023 — we will reduce the number of people in the world by 50 per cent. I think today, this dream is becoming a reality."
AFWA's investigation found that this video was both digitally altered and shared out of context to give it a different meaning.
Archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here .
We could see "World Economic Forum" written all over the blue background behind Bourla. So, we searched for talks that the Pfizer CEO had given at the event. We found a video on the official YouTube channel of the World Economic Forum.
This video, more than half an hour long, was uploaded to the channel on May 25. It was a conversation between Bourla and Klaus Schwab, the Executive Director of the World Economic Forum.
While answering Schwab's question about Pfizer's non-profit plan for dispensing drugs to 45 economically disadvantaged nations, Bourla said the following , "I think that is really fulfilling of a dream that we had, together with our leadership team when we started in '19. The first week we met in January of '19 in California to set up the goals for the next five years, and one of them was by 2023, we will reduce the number of people in the world that cannot afford our medicines by 50 per cent. I think today, this dream is becoming a reality."
Thus, it became clear that in the viral video, Bourla's words were cut out. Instead of, "We will reduce the number of people in the world that cannot afford our medicines by 50 per cent," the viral video shows him saying, "We will reduce the number of people in the world by 50 per cent."
(With input from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Aug 17, 2022 19:56 IST

title: FACT CHECK: No, R Madhavan DID NOT lose his house while trying to fund 'Rocketry: The Nambi Effect'
content:
R Madhavan has denied this claim on his Twitter account. However, he said in an earlier interview that he did not own and house and would buy one after the film was completed.
Actor R Madhavan's directorial debut "Rocketry: The Nambi Effect" is a biopic of Nambi Narayanan, a former scientist and aerospace engineer at the Indian Space Research Organisation. While the film was a moderate success, if social media posts are to be believed, its production put a great financial strain on its director. One such post said, "R Madhavan lost his house to fund Rocketry and directed this movie when the original director had opted out due to prior commitments. He had to do other projects just to fund this movie. He had been working on this project for 6 yrs." R Madhavan lost his house to fund Rocketry and directed this movie when the original director had opted out due to prior commitments. He had to do other projects just to fund this movie. He had been working on this project for 6 yrs.
— MKG 2.0 (@MKG_II_0) August 7, 2022 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story AFWA's investigation found this claim is not true. There are no media reports that state Madhavan lost is home while funding the movie. The actor has himself denied this claim. Archived versions of posts with similar claims can be seen here and here. Who produced the film? While investigating the claim, we found a July 20 report in The Telegraph that said the film was jointly produced by Tricolour Films and Varghese Moolan Pictures. We then tried to access the websites of these two production houses. Although the website of Tricolour is not available, a poster on the website of Varghese Moolan Pictures suggests that both companies indeed produced the film. However, a closer look into the company details of the Tricolour Private Limited revealed that this company was incorporated on March 24, 2014, with Madhavan Ranganathan and his wife Sarita Madhavan as the directors of the company. Has Madhavan funded the film? So, now, we tried to find out if Madhavan has spoken about funding the film. We found a YouTube video from June 29 where he spoke about his directorial debut. In the interview, Madhavan was asked if, during the two years of the pandemic, he had no source of income because he was busy writing this film. In response, the actor said, "Not two, it was six years. While I worked on other projects in between, I did that because I wanted to fund 'Rocketry'. I don't have a house of my own. And, I told my wife that we are going to buy a beautiful house after this film." Madhavan, however, has denied losing his house to fund the film. In a tweet, responding to such a claim, the actor wrote, "Oh Yaar. Pls don't over-patronize my sacrifice. I did not lose my house or anything. In fact, all involved in Rocketry will be very proudly paying heavy Income Tax this year. God's grace, we all made very good and proud profits. I still love and live in my house." Oh Yaar. Pls don't over patronize my sacrifice. I did not lose my house or anything. In fact all involved in Rocketry will be very proudly paying heavy Income Tax this year. Gods grace We all made very good and proud profits. I still love and live in my house . https://t.co/5L0h4iBert — Ranganathan Madhavan (@ActorMadhavan) August 17, 2022 Hence, we can conclude that this claim is misleading. R Madhavan did not lose his house while funding "Rocketry: The Nambi Effect". (With inputs from Yash Mittal) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Aug 17, 2022 21:35 IST

title: Fact Check: This 8-year-old video shows YSR Congress members brawling on Independence Day — not INC members
content:
This video is eight years old and shows YSR Congress leaders fighting with each other — not the Indian National Congress leaders.
A peaceful flag-hoisting ceremony suddenly turned into a scuffle. This is a video that has been making the rounds on social media. Per those sharing the video, this incident took place at the Karimnagar Congress office in Telangana.
The video shows the Indian flag being hoisted in the presence of a bunch of people. It then cuts to a woman dressed in a purple sari, supposedly the chief guest at the event, engaged in a fight with a man in white. Another man then hits the man with slippers. The brawl continues for a while as the woman shouts at the man.
AFWA's investigation found this video is eight years old and shows Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party or YSR Congress Party members fighting with each other — not Indian National Congress members from Telangana.
The viral posts have been archived here and here .
Upon reverse-searching frames from the video, we found a 2014 NDTV report entitled "In Fight After Flag Hoisting, Politicians Use Slippers and Slaps". Per the report, two YSR Congress leaders engaged in a brawl after a ceremony to hoist the Independence Day flag at the party office in Telangana's Karimnagar district.
Subsequent searches yielded a longer version of the video on a YouTube channel named "Mango News". Uploaded on August 16, 2014, the video was titled "YSR Congress leader thrashed up publicly by party female leader Karimnagar".
The same incident was also reported by the Deccan Chronicle on August 16, 2014. Per the news report, Ganta Susheela, a woman YSR Congress leader, and her husband Sathish thrashed the party's district president Singireddy Bhaskar Reddy for allegedly not intimating her about Independence Day celebrations at the party office.
She also alleged that Reddy was misbehaving with women workers of the party and using filthy language while talking to them. The report said that the Karimnagar rural police registered a case against Reddy under the SC/ST Atrocities Act for abusing Ganta Susheela in the name of her caste. Thus, it is clear that this eight-year-old video of a scuffle shows YSR Congress Party members engaged in a scuffle — not Indian National Congress members. Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Aug 17, 2022 23:47 IST

title: Fact Check: BCCI parody account claims Hardik Pandya will replace Rohit Sharma as India's T20I skipper
content:
The viral tweet is from a parody account, not from the BCCI's official Twitter handle. Rohit Sharma remains the Indian T20I captain to date.
Indian allrounder Hardik Pandya has been in red-hot form since leading Gujarat Titans to the IPL crown. Following the successful IPL run, Pandya had said that his next goal was "to win the World Cup for India no matter what happens". Meanwhile, a tweet purportedly by the Board of Control for Cricket in India claimed that Indian skipper Rohit Sharma has handed over the Twenty20 International captaincy to Pandya.
"This decision has been taken in the best interest of Indian Cricket going forward. He will continue to lead the side in ODI & Tests," the tweet further said.
AFWA's investigation found the viral tweet was made by an imposter account. AFWA Probe
We started by running multiple keyword combinations on Google to retrieve any authentic information about this. However, there was nothing to be found despite repeated tries. There was no announcement on the official website of the BCCI either.
We couldn't find any information on Sharma stepping down on the Twitter accounts of BCCI secretary Jay Shah and president Sourav Ganguly either. It is highly unlikely for a development like this to not be announced on the official social media accounts of the cricket body or its office bearers.
We checked the viral tweet next. While the display name of the unverified page read "BCCI", the handle name was "@_BCCII". It had a total of 1,315 followers at the time of filing this story.
The BCCI's official handle, on the other hand, is verified and has over 18.3 million followers. We confirmed that the Twitter handle of this account is "@BCCI".
We also found that the bio of the account that had shared the viral tweet read: "Official Twitter Handle of Team India (Parody)".
Meanwhile, we found news reports that suggested Pandya is in contention to be named Sharma's deputy for the T20 World Cup. Leading media outlets reported Sharma will remain the Indian captain for the World Cup. India Today's sports desk was also able to confirm that there has been no official announcement from the BCCI on a captaincy change.
Thus, it is clear that the tweet claiming Rohit Sharma has stepped down as the T20I captain of India for Hardik Pandya is not from an official source — rather, it's from a parody account.
(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena in New Delhi) Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Aug 18, 2022 15:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Bollywood stars aren't boycotting people - these pics are from 2018 Kathua gang rape protest
content:

title: Fact Check: Not J&K, this video shows clashes between coca farmers and police in Bolivia
content:
The video is from Bolivia. It shows a clash between coca farmers and the Bolivian authorities — an ongoing issue in the country.
Disturbing footage of violence has been making the rounds on social media. Shot on what appears to be a cellphone, the video shows a street full of people, some of whom appear to be throwing objects at someone or a group outside the frame. Things escalate with a loud bang and one of the people falls amid what looks like a small explosion. Those sharing the video claimed this scene was from Jammu and Kashmir — security forces retaliating against stone-pelters with bullets. AFWA's investigation found that the video is not from Jammu and Kashmir but from Bolivia. AFWA Probe A reverse image search of the video's frames led us to several Spanish news portals that reported the incident. Per the website of Bolivision TV , this was a recent clash between the coca producers and Bolivian authorities. Per the report, in the video, a protesting coca farmer threw a homemade dynamite stick at the police while holding the other one on another hand. Within a few seconds, the second one burst in his hand, causing him serious injury. According to local Bolivian media , the man lost his left hand in the explosion. The same viral video was uploaded by "Unitel Bolivia" on Dailymotion, entitled in Spanish: "Coca grower injured for handling dynamite is in 'critical situation'". Bolivia has been witnessing a stand-off between the coca growers and the government for the last couple of weeks. The Bolivian city of La Paz witnessed several clashes between the protesting farmers and the police. Per international media reports , the protesting farmers of the Adepcoca Coca Growers Association are demanding the closure of a "parallel market promoted by a group affiliated to the ruling government". The protesters marched and proclaimed that the parallel market was "illegal and enjoys government support". Thus, we conclude that this video was not from Jammu and Kashmir, or from India at all. It's from Bolivia. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: pragya malhotra Published On: Aug 18, 2022 22:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Arjun Kapoor never forced Cristiano Ronaldo to click selfie with him — viral tweet is doctored
content:
This screenshot has been digitally altered. Ronaldo never tweeted any such thing. This selfie was taken during a promotional event in 2018 in Madrid.
Following the #boycottbollywood trend flooding social media, actor Arjun Kapoor issued a statement about the film industry making a mistake by staying silent on this issue. The actor said it was high time the film fraternity came together and did something about it. Consequently, he became the target of online trolling. Around this time, a screenshot of a tweet allegedly made by footballer Cristiano Ronaldo went viral . Featuring Ronaldo's selfie with Kapoor, the tweet reads: "This unknown guy forcefully rushed in to my dressing room and forced me to take a selfie with him the way we look like friends. What a looser." Many online mocked Kapoor as they shared this screenshot. The archived version of this tweet can be seen here . But did Ronaldo tweet this? AFWA's investigation found that the screenshot was digitally altered. Ronaldo never tweeted this. His selfie with Arjun Kapoor dates back to 2018. The telltale signs While the Twitter handle is the correct one, and the account appeared verified, there are subtle hints all over the tweet that point to its lack of authenticity. There are multiple mistakes in the tweet. The words "loser" and "into" have been misspelt as "looser" and "in to" — something that seems suspect. When we searched online, we found that this screenshot was not new at all. It was shared on social media back in 2018 as well. However, we couldn't find any such tweet on Ronaldo's Twitter account. The date mentioned in the screenshot was May 23, 2018. So, we tried to look for Ronaldo's deleted tweets posted around this date on the archiving website, Wayback Machine. However, we couldn't find any such tweet. The selfie Upon reverse searching the viral photo, we found it on Arjun Kapoor's Instagram page in a post from May 16, 2018. Kapoor wrote in the caption: "Amazing feeling meeting & talking football with Cristiano !!! Heck of a player, heck of a guy. All the best for Kiev & Russia." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Arjun Kapoor (@arjunkapoor) Kapoor had tagged the luggage brand American Tourister in the same Instagram post. Subsequent refined searches led us to a video the brand had shared on its YouTube channel on June 22, 2018. In it, Kapoor, among others, could be seen meeting Ronaldo. As per the description on the channel, nineteen influencers from around the world met Ronaldo in Madrid. Indian actor Ayushmann Khurrana was also a part of this event. Khurrana also shared his selfie with Ronaldo on Twitter on May 16, 2018. The backdrop in both selfies features the same advertisement for American Tourister. This clearly points to the fact that the viral photo is from the same event. Did Kapoor and Ronaldo interact? Yes. We found multiple media reports from 2018 about the two. The Hindustan Times reported that when Kapoor met the Portuguese footballer, he told him about his fanbase in India. Responding to this, the latter had said that he would love to visit India, adding that he was aware of how much Indians loved him. It is very unlikely Kapoor "forced" Ronaldo to take a selfie with him in a brand event such as this. Also, had Ronaldo tweeted any such thing about Kapoor, it would have definitely made the news. However, there are no reports indicating this. To further make sure of this, AFWA got in touch with Ronaldo's spokesperson, who said this tweet's screenshot was "fake". Thus, we concluded that the tweet being used to mock Kapoor right now never existed in the first place. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Aug 19, 2022 15:22 IST

title: Fact Check: This cloudburst is NOT from Pakistan! 2020 video from Australia viral with false claim
content:
Although Pakistan has witnessed torrential rains recently, this video is from Perth, Australia. It was recorded on February 25, 2020.
Recent heavy rainfall in Pakistan has resulted in the loss of lives and properties worth crores. Amid this, a video of a heavy cloudburst, supposedly from Jamshoro , a district located in the Sindh province of Pakistan, has gone viral on social media. This 13-second video shows several layers of dark clouds bursting into rain over a road. People shared the video with captions like: "Video showing storm Cloudburst over Jamshoro yesterday. Sindh broke the record of the heaviest rainfall ever in one single day — after receiving more than 355mm breaking the previous record of 238 mm — said Climate Change Minister Sherry Rehman on Friday." Archived versions of some similar claims can be seen here and here . AFWA's investigation found these visuals are more than two-years-old and not from Pakistan at all. AFWA Probe A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral clip led us to the video uploaded to an Instagram page named "Kaneartie Photography" on August 1. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kane Artie ~ Australia (@kaneartie.photography) Although the caption did not state any details regarding the location or time of this video, we noticed the "perthstorm" hashtag in it. Perth is one of the major cities in Australia. ALSO READ| Fact Check: BCCI parody account claims Hardik Pandya will replace Rohit Sharma as India's T20I skipper Subsequent keyword searches took us to the Facebook page of Kane Artie Photography where we found a photo of the cloudburst with a caption, "This is just one of the shots from the storm Timelapse back in February 2020. When these microbursts hit the ground, all the force has to go somewhere and it gets blasted outwards." There, we found the full-frame video of the timelapse where it was mentioned that the video was shot back in 2020. We searched for relevant news articles on Perth cloudbursts and found a Daily Mail report. While featuring the same visuals, the report mentioned that heavy rain smashed the city on the afternoon of February 25, 2020, with some suburbs recording wind speeds of up to 126 kilometres per hour and 14mm of rain within minutes. Another report from ABC News noted that the meteorological department had warned of flash floods and large hailstones. The warning for Perth was cancelled over an hour after it was issued as the storm moved southeast of the city and weakened on its journey inland. Thus, it became clear that a two-year-old video from Perth, Australia, was shared with the claim that it was from Sindh, Pakistan. Published By: Ritika Shah Published On: Aug 22, 2022 09:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Haj pilgrim's video falsely shared as Bhim Army chief's arrival at Jalore over Dalit boy's death
content:
This video shows the walkathon of Kerala man Shihab Chottur who is making his maiden Haj pilgrimage on foot — an 8,640 km journey to Mecca.

In the comments section of one such post, we found a user pointing out that the video is related to Shihab Chottur, a Haj pilgrim from Kerala. In the video, we also noticed a young man wearing a skull cap walking between the crowd, closely followed by a group in pink t-shirts. Police appeared to be guarding the man. The people shooting the video also pointed their fingers at the same man.
Shihab Chottur, a 30-year-old man from Kerala , is on an 8,640 km journey on foot to Mecca. He started his journey on July 2 and is expected to complete the trip in 280 days, walking through six countries.
