title: Fact Check: Not Chambal and not even India! This 2021 video of a boy's rescue is from Bangladesh
content:
This 2021 video is from Chandpur, Bangladesh. Local police dismissed claims of crocodiles in the water.
An unsettling video shows a child struggling to stay afloat in turbulent water. As the child cries for help, a green shape could be seen moving behind him under the water. Thankfully, things then take a turn for the better and a boat arrives. The boy is then pulled out of the water by one of the men on it. This video purportedly shows how a boy narrowly escaped a terrible fate in the Chambal river, a tributary of the Yamuna River in central and northern India. The green shape behind him was supposedly a crocodile. Those sharing the video thanked the State Disaster Response Force for its timely action. Thank You SDRF , SDFR , # @ashokgehlot51 @GovindDotasra @rahulprakashIPS @pankajips2009 @girirajagl @MeenasSugrive @vinodkapri @ajitanjum @ravishndtv pic.twitter.com/h77LbBGXLq — Pintu Lal Meena (@PintuPahadi) August 24, 2022 Many shared the video with similar claims, including IRS officer Dr Bhageerath Choudhary. Subsequently, news outlets such as NDTV , DNA , the Navbharat Times , CNN-News18 , Latestly , the Free Press Journal , and even India Today reported the story. This is real heroic deed. Chambal river, crocodiles and the fighter kid. Salute to the rescue team. #Chambal pic.twitter.com/MvNVLV5pVy — Dr Bhageerath Choudhary IRS (@DrBhageerathIRS) August 24, 2022 But is this video from the Chambal river? AFWA's investigation found that the video is nearly a year old and not even from India. Archived versions of these posts can be seen here and here . SO, WHERE'S THE VIDEO FROM? We first noticed that Dr Choudhary mentioned in a later tweet that he was told this video might not have been from the Chambal river. He wrote, "Some say this video is not from Chambal. Irrespective of the source of this video undoubtedly the most heroic act it is. Any other info about the source. Please share." ALSO READ | Fact Check: Video from Hyderabad in Pakistan FALSELY shared as an attack on Hindus in India Even the India Today report earlier mentioned that it was unable to ascertain if the video actually was from Chambal, going only by Dr Choudhary's original tweet. It later updated the report. Some says this video is not from Chambal. Irrespective of the source of this video undoubtedly the most heroic act it is. Any other info about the source. Please share. @PintuPahadi — Dr Bhageerath Choudhary IRS (@DrBhageerathIRS) August 25, 2022 When we reverse-searched frames from the video, it led us to the same clip posted on June 19 on Facebook. The video was geotagged to Sylhet, Bangladesh. However, no further details were provided. The person who helped pull up the drowning boy was seen wearing a lungi, a popular attire in Bangladesh. It is also unlikely that a member of a disaster management team would carry out such an operation without proper uniform. Subsequent refined searches in Bangla took us to a video uploaded to YouTube on August 27, 2021. It showed a similar boat rescuing a drowning boy from a water body. The caption mentioned this to be an incident from Chandpur Bay, where the Padma and the Meghna rivers meet the Bay of Bengal. When we compared the boat, the boy and the people who were seen rescuing, it became clear that both the incidents were the same. "This boy accidentally fell into the Chandpur Bay — he has now been rescued. Just see how dangerous Chandpur Bay is...", a voice was heard towards the end of the YouTube video speaking in Bangla. When we Googled this place, we found news reports from the Bangladeshi media calling it a "mysterious deathtrap". Multiple news reports stated that drowning is a common occurrence here. We reached out to Mohammad Hossain Tareq , a Bangladesh-based journalist who confirmed to AFWA that this incident is nearly a year old and from Chandpur. "This place is known as the Hilsa Sanctuary. The best quality Hilsa fish of Bangladesh can be found here. Also, as the place is near the ocean, the water current here remains very high, resulting in similar incidents at regular intervals," Tareq said. WAS THERE A CROCODILE BEHIND THE BOY? In the YouTube video, no crocodile was visible. We reached out to the local police from the Chandpur district in Bangladesh for further information. An officer who did not wish to be named dismissed the claim and said, "It is mainly the mischievous kids who sometimes get into trouble after getting into the water to catch Hilsa fish." ALSO READ | Fact Check: Clipped-out Modi speech given false spin — PM was not instigating violence against upper castes Therefore, it is clear that a year-old rescue video from Bangladesh was shared as something that happened in the Chambal river in India. Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Aug 27, 2022 19:41 IST

title: Fact Check: No, a Muslim lawyer DID NOT move Supreme Court to get 'Gadar 2' banned
content:
Adeel Ahmed confirmed to AFWA that he did not file any petition in the Supreme Court against 'Gadar 2'. Also, the film's release date has not been announced yet.
Bollywood, off late, has been facing backlash from audiences. And in retaliation, several actors have spoken up against this supposed boycott. Amid all this, social media has been seeing a large number of posts in support of "Gadar 2". And these posts have been accompanied by some questionable claims.
"Gadar 2" is the official sequel of "Gadar: Ek Prem Katha" released in 2001. While extending support to the upcoming movie that will supposedly be released on September 8, several people claimed that a lawyer named Adeel Ahmed had filed a petition in the Supreme Court to ban the film's release citing that it may hurt Muslim sentiments. View this post on Instagram A post shared by aakash thakur (@only_one_king_1199) 8 " 2" 2, ! pic.twitter.com/ThO66MvrHF — Abhishek Kumar Kushwaha (@AskAbhishek_IND) August 18, 2022
A post shared by aakash thakur (@only_one_king_1199)
8 " 2" 2, ! pic.twitter.com/ThO66MvrHF — Abhishek Kumar Kushwaha (@AskAbhishek_IND) August 18, 2022
Archived versions of these posts can be seen here and here .
AFWA's investigation found that Adeel Ahmed did not file any petition in the apex court to ban "Gadar 2". At the same time, the film's release date has not been announced yet.
With the help of a keyword search, we first looked for the release date of "Gadar 2" . However, we did not find any report stating it will release on September 8. An October 2021 report in The Hindu mentioned that the film will be produced by Zee Studios and Anil Sharma Production.
Subsequent searches took us to the motion poster of this movie that was shared on the official YouTube channel of Zee Studios on October 15, 2021. The video revealed that Sunny Deol, Ameesha Patel, and Utkarsh Sharma, the son of the film's director Anil Sharma will play significant roles in it.
However, we did not see any mention of an official release date either in the caption or description. It was only mentioned that the film will hit theatres in 2022.
Last April, film trade analyst Taran Adarsh confirmed in his tweet that the shooting of "Gadar 2" was 80 per cent done. SUNNY DEOL, ANIL SHARMA, ZEE: 'GADAR 2' 80% COMPLETE... #Gadar2 - the sequel to #Gadar , starring #SunnyDeol , #AmeeshaPatel and #UtkarshSharma - is 80% complete, after #Lucknow shoot... Directed by #AnilSharma ... Produced by #ZeeStudios and #AnilSharmaProductions . pic.twitter.com/ypE88wzDgg — taran adarsh (@taran_adarsh) April 25, 2022 Has there been a petition to ban 'Gadar 2'?
SUNNY DEOL, ANIL SHARMA, ZEE: 'GADAR 2' 80% COMPLETE... #Gadar2 - the sequel to #Gadar , starring #SunnyDeol , #AmeeshaPatel and #UtkarshSharma - is 80% complete, after #Lucknow shoot... Directed by #AnilSharma ... Produced by #ZeeStudios and #AnilSharmaProductions . pic.twitter.com/ypE88wzDgg — taran adarsh (@taran_adarsh) April 25, 2022
When we searched for this, we came across a Times of India report from August 2, 2001. Per this report, the screening of "Gadar" was challenged in the Punjab and Haryana High Courts because it was "violative of Sikh tenets." Apart from that, we did not find any news reports supporting the claim.
We then reached out to Supreme Court advocate Adeel Ahmed . Ahmed dismissed these rumours and said that he was a "big fan" of Sunny Deol and the film "Gadar". He also sent a clarification video to AFWA that can be seen below.
Therefore, it is clear that no such petition has been filed in the Supreme Court to ban the release of "Gadar 2".
(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Aug 30, 2022 16:43 IST

title: Fact Check: Neither UP nor Rajasthan, this video of woman who fell into a pothole is from Delhi
content:
This video is from Begumpur in Delhi, not Prayagraj, UP.
On a waterlogged street, pockmarked with potholes and dark mud, three men successfully pull out a woman from a crevice. As the woman examines her legs covered in dirty water, a man can be heard commenting about a hole in the street. This video has been shared widely online with the claim that it's from Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. However, there seems to be some contention about that. Some shared the video claiming it's from Bhilwara in Rajasthan. The archived versions of a similar post can be seen here . So, where's this video really from? AFWA found that it's from New Delhi. AFWA probe We found a longer version of the same video shared on Twitter by Sumit Agarwal, the national secretary of the Confederation of All India Traders on August 27. He claimed that this video was from Begumpur in New Delhi. Begumpur is a village located in Rohini, in northwest Delhi. In the longer version of the video, we noticed the signboard for a hospital. While the full name of the hospital was not visible, its name ends with "A'S". The board also had "Delhi-86" written on it. Begumpur's pin code is 110086. We then searched for hospital names ending with "A's" in Begumpur. This led us to Hira's Multi Speciality Hospital in Barwala Road, Begum Vihar Extension, Begumpur, Delhi 86. Google street video of Hira's hospital shot in May 2022 can be seen below. A comparison between the viral video and the Google Street View of Barwala Road confirmed that the video is indeed from Begumpur, Delhi. In the viral video, we noticed the signage for "Sahil Fitness Club". However, this was not there in the Google Street View, which was shot in May this year. Instead, we noticed boards for "Indraprastha" clinic and "The Solid Fitness Club". This made us wonder if the video was recent at all. We reached out to Hira's Hospital to figure out when this incident took place. Dr. Hira Kapoor, the director of the hospital confirmed to AFWA that the video was recent and indeed from the road outside his hospital. He also said that the Indraprastha Clinic seen on Google Street View shifted from that location about two months ago and the building was currently occupied by Sahil Fitness Club. It is hence clear the viral video is from New Delhi, and not from either Uttar Pradesh or Rajasthan. (With inputs from Jyoti Dwivedi ) Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: Aug 30, 2022 22:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Fan-wars! Egyptian soccer fans attacking rivals FALSELY shared as violent Al-Sadr supporters
content:
This video is not from Iraq but from Egypt. It shows fans of Ismaily SC, a football club, attacking the fan bus of its rival Al Ahly SC.
Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, is witnessing massive unrest . Reportedly, at least thirty people have been killed in fighting between rival Shia militias, as well as the Iraqi security forces, after the religious leader Muqtada al-Sadr claimed on August 29 that he was withdrawing from politics. The death toll is only expected to rise further. Video purportedly shows Sadr supporters attacking an Iranian bus carrying pilgrims pic.twitter.com/WP5X6F7Pnr — Karwan Faidhi Dri (@KarwanFaidhiDri) August 30, 2022
Video purportedly shows Sadr supporters attacking an Iranian bus carrying pilgrims pic.twitter.com/WP5X6F7Pnr — Karwan Faidhi Dri (@KarwanFaidhiDri) August 30, 2022
A video in the meanwhile has gone viral that shows people attacking a bus by throwing large rocks at it. Supposedly, the people attacking were Al-Sadr's supporters and the passengers on the Iranian bus were pilgrims.
Archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here .
AFWA's investigation found that the video is not from Iraq, but from Egypt. It shows fans of a football club attacking a rival football club's fan bus.
When we reverse-searched frames from the video, it led us to the same clip shared on Twitter from a handle named AL Ahly Stadium on August 21. The Arabic caption roughly translates to, "Ismaily fans attack the buses of Al-Ahly fans."
When we Googled these two names, results suggested that both were football clubs in Egypt, one based in Cairo, and the other in Ismaïlia. Given that the video was shared almost nine days ago, it is clear that it is not related to the ongoing agitation in Iraq.
Subsequent searches led us to multiple news reports from August 21 and 22 carrying photos from the same video
Per the reports, some fans of Ismaily Sporting Club attacked Al Ahly Sporting Club's fan bus before a match between the two teams in the Egyptian League on August 21. Following the attack, the match was postponed. The report further noted that the bus driver was injured.
We also found another YouTube video of the same incident where a logo of a football club could be seen behind the windshield of the bus around the 16-second mark.
When we compared this logo with the profile picture of the official Twitter account of Al Ahly, it became clear that the bus was indeed carrying the fans of Al Ahly.
Al Arabiya Egypt, an Egyptian news outlet, also shared this video, confirming that Ismaily Sporting Club fans indeed attacked Al Ahly fans.
Therefore, we concluded that this video has nothing to do with the ongoing crisis in Baghdad, Iraq.
(With input from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Aug 30, 2022 23:10 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of T Raja Singh viral as suspended BJP MLA eating prison food after recent arrest
content:
The viral video is at least a year old. Moreover, Cherlapally Central Jail authorities have dismissed that it was shot inside its premises.
Suspended Bharatiya Janata Party MLA T Raja Singh was sent to Cherlapally Central Jail after he was booked under the Preventive Detention Act for allegedly trying to disrupt "peace and public tranquillity". This happened two days after the Telangana police arrested him for derogatory remarks against the Prophet Muhammad. Soon after, a video of Singh eating food was widely shared online. The video saw him eating while sitting on what looked like a bench. There were a number of plastic bags and water bottles in front of him. At one point, he smiled and waved at the camera. Those sharing the video on Facebook wrote captions like, "It is not easy to be a hardcore Hindu. You have to eat prison food. Despite this, he has the smile of a lion on his face." AFWA's investigation, however, found that the video was not shot inside Cherlapally Central Jail. The viral posts have been archived here and here . AFWA Probe A combination of reverse image search and Telugu keywords led us to the same clip shared by many on Facebook claiming it to be from 2021. One person on Facebook wrote in Telugu , "The video of MLA T Raja Singh having breakfast in Nampally Court is now going viral on social media." Further searches in Telugu led us to Facebook posts from August 2021. That this video was shared a year ago proves that it has nothing to do with his recent arrest. Per such posts, last year, Singh supposedly had to appear in court once every four days because the state government had slapped several charges against the "Hindu leaders" in the state. However, AFWA found no relevant news reports regarding this claim. Of course, soon after the video went viral recently, Cherlapally Central Jail authorities issued a press statement. Per Telugu news reports , authorities clarified that the viral video was not from the jail at all. Thus, we can say with certainty that this video does not show Singh eating prison food following his recent arrest. Published By: Komal Sharma Published On: Aug 31, 2022 16:54 IST

title: Fact Check: First Indian virtual school in Delhi? Kejriwal govt gets schooled
content:
Virtual schools in India, both private and government-run, have existed in India for a while now — even as early as 2020.
While inaugurating the Delhi Model Virtual School on August 31, Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal claimed that this was the country's first virtual school. Kejriwal said , "Today, we are inaugurating the country's first virtual school in Delhi," adding that it was about a year back that his government had announced this plan. https://t.co/PIms2geisB — Arvind Kejriwal (@ArvindKejriwal) August 31, 2022 Following this, many on social media pointed out that the Delhi Model Virtual School was not India's first virtual school , referring to older headlines referring to other virtual schools in different parts of the country. AFWA's investigation found there is more than enough evidence to suggest Kejriwal's claim does not stand. Archived versions of tweets calling out the Delhi CM's claims can be seen here and here . So, what actually is a virtual school? Virtual school is a broad term and somewhat difficult to define precisely. During the Covid-19 pandemic, most schools in India had shifted to virtual modes — students and teachers interacted online and not in physical classrooms. So for a while, most Indian schools were virtual. Is the Delhi Model Virtual School the first of its kind in India? According to a Delhi government circular , the Delhi Model Virtual School will be governed by the Delhi Schools of Specialised Excellence and is affiliated with the Delhi Board of School Education. The circular claims it is the "first online government school," and it aims to provide "free access to Delhi's education model for children from anywhere" and a "seamless learning experience through live classes, recorded sessions, assignments and assessments, curated videos, tutorials, and personalised mentoring sessions" among other things. However, this is not the first online government school. The Centre launched the National Institute of Open Schooling in August 2021. Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan inaugurated this digital schooling system for eligible students who were unable attend a brick-and-mortar school. "This school is a new model of learning and is an example of how leveraging technology and innovation can facilitate greater inclusion in education," Pradhan said at the time. "The school is the first-of-its-kind initiative in India, which will provide advanced digital learning platforms via virtual live classrooms and labs, etc." This was more than a year ago. AFWA spoke to Professor Saroj Sharma, the chairperson of the National Institute of Open Schooling, who called it the world's largest open school programme. She said about 25 lakhs students had enrolled in it so far. Private initiatives in virtual schooling About two years ago, in October 2020, former Uttarakhand Chief Minister Trivendra Singh Rawat inaugurated Global Seas Institute in Dehradun . The institute's founder Reena Prakash Tyagi told AFWA that it was the first "fully-virtual home school in India." Even in April 2021, when the Aam Aadmi Party government had announced its plans to establish India's first virtual school, his claim was fact-checked . The report mentioned many such ventures already operating at that time. So, whether private or government-run, virtual schools are certainly not a novel concept. Published By: Komal Sharma Published On: Aug 31, 2022 23:23 IST

title: Fact Check: No, PM Modi did not say singing Bhajans could help reduce malnutrition!
content:
In Episode 92 of 'Mann Ki Baat', PM Modi spoke about how in the Datia district of MP, Bhajan events were organised to raise awareness of malnutrition. He also spoke about other facets of these events, such as the 'Matka' program.
Can singing "bhajans" or devotional songs help reduce malnutrition? If social media is to be believed, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said as much on "Mann Ki Baat", his monthly radio programme. One such tweet claimed , "PM of India says in "Man Ki Baat" singing Bhajan can reduce Malnutrition! It happens when too much Malnutrition affects your Brain." Ashok Swain, a professor and the HoD of the Department of Peace and Conflict Research at Uppsala University in Sweden, tweeted , "Modi says singing Bhajan (Hindu devotional song) can solve malnutrition problem. Thankfully Nehru is not alive to witness this stupidity!"
But did Modi really say this? AFWA's investigation found that this was not the case. These appear to be a misreading of the PM's words. Archived versions of such claims can be seen here and here . AFWA Probe We first looked at the latest episode of "Mann Ki Baat". In Episode 92, which aired on August 28, Modi began his address by discussing Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav. Around the 12-minute-mark, he spoke about malnutrition. The relevant section of his address can be read below: "Can you believe that devotional songs can be used to fight malnutrition? In Madhya Pradesh's Datia district, under the 'Mera Bachcha Abhiyan', this was successfully done. 'Bhajan' events were organised in the district where teachers dubbed 'Poshan Gurus' were invited. A 'Matka' program was also organised where women brought fistfuls of grain to their Anganwadi centres and that grain was used to cook the Saturday 'Bal Bhoj'. This not only helped increase the attendance of children at Anganwadi centres, but it also helped reduce malnutrition."
This makes it clear that the PM did not say devotional songs could cure malnutrition. Rather, he spoke about how devotional songs were used as a method for increasing public awareness of malnutrition. Following the episode, an article published by The Wire criticised Modi's approach. It noted, "Cultural and traditional practices are not harmful. But it is in bad faith to make them part of habits that sideline tested and approved solutions to crucial welfare issues." The piece accused Modi of shifting the focus "to devotional music" instead of "dwelling on the role of Indigenous food cultures," dubbing this move counterproductive. It also said that "while many of Prime Minister Modi's other comments in his monologue are well-taken, especially about public participation, neither the need for context-specific interventions nor for evidence-based policies are served by misplaced allusions to bhajans and kirtans." So, while it is matter of opinion if devotional songs are an effective tool in countering malnutrition, it is more than clear that PM Modi did not ever say that singing bhajans could solve or reduce it. (With inputs from Mayank Anandan) Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Aug 31, 2022 23:31 IST

title: Fact Check: Did singer Ranjit Bawa criticise Bhagwant Mann in front of him with a song? Viral video tampered
content:
This video has been tampered with. Bawa performed the theme song for the Khedan Watan Punjab Dian event, and not 'Chitta'.
"Sports is the best antidote to the drug menace. The youth must be encouraged to take up sports," declared Punjab's Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann while inaugurating the sporting event Khedan Watan Punjab Dian at the Guru Gobind Singh stadium in Jalandhar on August 29. Mann, like all Punjab politicians, has promised to tackle the narcotics epidemic in the state. However, a recent video that's been widely shared online seems to suggest that one Punjabi singer criticised the government's role in the spread of this epidemic, right in front of the CM. The video supposedly shows Punjabi singer Ranjit Bawa singing his song "Chitta" — a street name for certain drugs — at an event where Mann and his wife were present. The Punjabi song contains provocative lyrics such as, "The speaker of truth invites many enemies, the speaker of lies thrives. The government is the one that sells drugs, that's why it's everywhere." The text inside the video reads, "Bawa sang the song 'Chitta' in front of Mann. Madam Gurpreet (Mann's wife, Dr. Gurpreet Kaur) seemed pleased with it." AFWA's investigation found that the viral video has been tampered with. Bawa was performing the theme song he had composed for the event, not the song "Chitta". AFWA Probe Searches led us to the full video of this performance. The viral section can be seen at the 4 minutes and 47 seconds mark. However, here Bawa and singer Amrit Mann were singing something else altogether. In fact, it was the theme song for the aforementioned Khedan Watan Punjab Dian event. The event featuring various block, district and state-level tournaments will be held from September 1 to October 21. We did not find any videos or reports that suggest Bawa performed "Chitta" at the event. It's noteworthy, however, that the singer has performed the song at several live shows. Here's a YouTube video from January 2016 where he's performing the song: Thus, we concluded that the viral video was doctored. The song "Chitta" has been added to the clip's audio. (Written by Yash Mittal) Published By: Komal Sharma Published On: Sep 1, 2022 18:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Yes 'Brahmastra' was renamed from 'Dragon', no it had nothing to do with the Pulwama attack
content:
Yes, the movie was renamed, but the title 'Brahmastra' was announced in October 2017. The Pulwama attack took place on February 14, 2019.
Director Ayan Mukerji's "Brahmastra: Part One" is all set to release on September 9 and an online boycott campaign has already started. Amid the ongoing "Boycott Bollywood" campaign, some claimed that the film was initially named "Dragon", and that after the February 14, 2019, suicide bombing in Pulwama, Jammu and Kashmir, the producers decided to rename it to "Brahmastra". They also allegedly renamed the protagonist from Rumi to Shiva . All this, to supposedly attract a wider Hindu audience.
AFWA found that while the movie's name was indeed changed from "Dragon" to "Brahmastra", the title was announced back in October 2017 , much before the Pulwama attack. The archived versions of such claims can be seen here and here . Was it ever called 'Dragon'?
While investigating, we first came across a tweet from the movie's producer, Karan Johar. On October 11, 2017, Johar announced the film titled "Brahmastra". A TRILOGY ...A FANTASY ADVENTURE....A LABOUR OF LOVE....."BRAHMSTRA" pic.twitter.com/8yQ2Y0yWaD — Karan Johar (@karanjohar) October 11, 2017
A TRILOGY ...A FANTASY ADVENTURE....A LABOUR OF LOVE....."BRAHMSTRA" pic.twitter.com/8yQ2Y0yWaD — Karan Johar (@karanjohar) October 11, 2017
At the time, Johar planned to release the film on August 15, 2019. However, it was later postponed several times due to multiple reasons .
Following Johar's tweet in October 2017, we found a news report that suggested the fantasy film was rumoured to be titled "Dragon" before the official announcement. In fact, the report also noted that on October 8, 2017, Johar had said at an event that the film wouldn't be titled "Dragon".
On March 10, 2019, Ayan Mukerji took to Instagram to talk about the film. He shared Kapoor's photo and said that initially, the protagonist was all set to be called Rumi. He wrote, "There was new inspiration, newer thoughts... Dragon became Brahmstra, we gave Ranbir a haircut, and Rumi became... Shiva." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ayan Mukerji (@ayan_mukerji)
A post shared by Ayan Mukerji (@ayan_mukerji)
Per media reports , during the launch of the motion poster for the movie on December 15, 2021, Mukerji told reporters, "When 'Dragon' was the title of the film, that time, we had not thought about it. Shiva, in the film, has the power of fire, so I wrote the name 'Dragon' in the script. But the film was always rooted and inspired by Indian culture and history. So when the time came to give the title, Brahmastra was always the right title for the film."
So, while the film was initially titled "Dragon", it appears to have been a placeholder. The filmmakers' decision to name it "Brahmastra" had nothing to do with the terrorist attack in Pulwama.
(Written by Yash Mittal) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Sep 2, 2022 17:13 IST

title: Fact Check: This video from Japan shows horrific 2011 tsunami, not recent floods in Pakistan
content:
This video is from the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami in Japan, one of the most powerful earthquakes of all time. It was shot in Ishinomaki, a city in Japan.
The devastating floods that hit Pakistan in June have so far affected more than 33 million people and claimed over one thousand lives. Social media is full of videos and photos of the destructive deluge in the country. One such video supposedly from Karachi, Pakistan, shows vehicles on the road being washed away by rushing water. But is this video from Karachi at all? AFWA's investigation found that the video was taken during the 2011 Thoku earthquake and tsunami in Japan, one of the most powerful earthquakes of all time. AFWA Probe Upon reverse-searching frames from the video, we came across a 2014 blog that contained the same shots. It said the footage is from around the Ishinomaki port area. Ishinomaki is a city in Japan's Honshu mainland. It was one of the worst hit cities in 2011. Subsequent searches led us to the same video uploaded to a YouTube channel in April 2012. The title of the video said, "2011 Japan Tsunami: Ishinomaki". As per the description of this video, the footage was shot from the rooftop of Ishinomaki Gas. The channel had also given a link to its source, a different YouTube channel that shared the video in December 2011, proving that the video was more than a decade old. We looked for the area mentioned on Google Street View and found remarkable similarities between the video and the location. This proceed that the video was shot in Japan. It is hence clear that the video is not from Pakistan at all. Published By: Komal Sharma Published On: Sep 2, 2022 20:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Rahul Gandhi goofs up on "litre" for "atta", but corrects himself immediately
content:
Rahul Gandhi indeed used "litre" as a unit for "atta", but he immediately corrected himself. The viral video is clipped and incomplete.
Congress party leaders lambasted the ruling NDA government at the Centre on the issue of price rise and unemployment through its "Halla bol" rally in the capital on Sunday.
While the senior Congress leaders took their turn to attack the BJP, Rahul Gandhi gave out a price list to show how the commodity market has received the heat of inflation.
A video clip of Rahul Gandhi has gone viral where he can be heard goofing up the unit for "flour". In the viral clip, Gandhi is saying, "Atta (flour) was Rs 22 per litre but today it is Rs 40 per litre".
Multiple Facebook users have posted the viral clip of Rahul Gandhi and wrote a caption in Hindi, that translates to, "since when is atta is being sold in litres?"
India Today Anti Fake News War Room ( AFWA) has found that it is true that Rahul Gandhi has indeed goofed up in his speech while comparing the prices of various commodities with earlier years. Gandhi indeed used " litres" as the unit of mass for flour, but he immediately corrected himself. The viral video is incomplete as it shows the clipped version of his speech. AFWA probe
We found the entire speech of Rahul Gandhi delivered at Delhi's Ramlila maidan on September 4 uploaded on the verified YouTube channel of the Indian National Congress.
In the middle of his speech, Rahul Gandhi began comparing the prices of a few essential commodities with their prices in 2014. Gandhi was listing out the prices of various commodities whose units were mostly in litres and he goofed up while calling out the unit price for flour.
From the time stamp 1.52.00 on the YouTube video, Gandhi said, "I have figures from 2014 when an LPG cylinder used to cost Rs 410, today it is Rs 1050. Petrol was Rs 70 per litre. Today it is around Rs 100 per litre. Diesel was Rs 55 per litre, today it is Rs 90 per litre. Mustard oil was Rs 90 per litre, today it is Rs 200 per litre. Milk was Rs 35 per litre, today it is Rs 60 per litre. Atta (flour) was Rs 22 per litre, today it is Rs 40 per litre"
Then immediately, in the next breath, he corrected himself and said "Oh Kgso on one hand you're being hit by unemployment, on the other hand, there is terrible inflation".
But the viral clip does not show the portion where Rahul Gandhi rectifies his mistake. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Sep 4, 2022 18:08 IST

title: Fact Check: This 'astronaut' was highlighting Bengaluru's pothole problem — not Jammu and Kashmir's
content:
This video is not from Jammu and Kashmir, It is from Bengaluru. Baadal Nanjundaswamy, a Bengaluru-based artist and activist, made this video to highlight the city's pothole problem.
An astronaut slowly walks on what looks like a ground pockmarked with craters. Only, the astronaut is not an astronaut. And the ground is not outside the Earth's atmosphere — it's a road full of potholes, supposedly in Jammu and Kashmir.
This video has been widely shared on social media, with many attempting to highlight the lack of infrastructure maintenance in Jammu and Kashmir. One such post reads, "Congratulations to all Kashmiris, especially administration of Jammu and Kashmir to achieve such an achievement of landing on moon. All credit goes to administration of Jammu and Kashmir for their unprovidable [sic] facilities."
But is this video from J&K? No. AFWA found that it was from Bengaluru. The video was created by a Bengaluru-based painter and activist to highlight the condition of roads in the city.
While searching, we came across several news reports from September 2019 that said the video was from Bengaluru's Herohalli and the "astronaut" was Bengaluru-based artist and activist Baadal Nanjundaswamy.
Therein we also found the original September 2, 2019, tweet by Baadal containing the video, shared with hashtags like "Herohalli" and "Namma Bengaluru". At the time of writing this, the video had around 1.7 million views. Hello bbmp @BBMPCOMM @BBMP_MAYOR @bbm #thelatest #streetart #nammabengaluru #herohalli pic.twitter.com/hsizngTpRH — baadal nanjundaswamy (@baadalvirus) September 2, 2019
Hello bbmp @BBMPCOMM @BBMP_MAYOR @bbm #thelatest #streetart #nammabengaluru #herohalli pic.twitter.com/hsizngTpRH — baadal nanjundaswamy (@baadalvirus) September 2, 2019
Per the Indian Express , following the video's popularity, the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP), the city's civic body, took immediate action and began repair work on those roads the very next day.
Baadal himself had shared the video of this response by the civic authorities with the caption, "Thank you people for such a overwhelming response and support! Work in progress. Quick and prompt response from BBMP." Thank you people for such a overwhelming response and support! Work in progress.. Quick and prompt response from @BBMP. Thank you very much @BBMPCOMM @BBMP_MAYOR and Mr. Prabhakar, CE RR Nagar who is overlooking on ground currently. pic.twitter.com/clgoLAIKzU — baadal nanjundaswamy (@baadalvirus) September 3, 2019
Thank you people for such a overwhelming response and support! Work in progress.. Quick and prompt response from @BBMP. Thank you very much @BBMPCOMM @BBMP_MAYOR and Mr. Prabhakar, CE RR Nagar who is overlooking on ground currently. pic.twitter.com/clgoLAIKzU — baadal nanjundaswamy (@baadalvirus) September 3, 2019
Baadal, a gold medalist in Bachelor of Fine Arts at the Chamarajendra Academy of Visual Arts, is known to create artworks to highlight such issues. In 2015, he installed a life-sized model of a crocodile in the middle of a road in a big water-filled pothole to once again highlight the condition of roads in the city. In 2018, he drew a cobweb around a pothole to make civic authorities take notice.
After his artworks gained popularity , he was even invited to draw several portraits, including that of cricketer Sachin Tendulkar at the Students Activity Centre in IIT Bombay.
So, we concluded that the video was not from Jammu and Kashmir at all.
(Written By Yash Mittal) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Sep 5, 2022 15:59 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of fireworks in Kashmir FALSELY shared as Srinagar celebrating Pak victory in Asia Cup
content:
While the video is indeed from Srinagar, it is more than two years old and hence not related to the 2022 Asia Cup at all.
Pakistan won against India by five wickets in their Super 4 game of the 2022 Asia Cup in Dubai on September 4. Soon after the match between the traditional cricket rivals, a video was shared by many online supposedly showing how people in Srinagar celebrated Pakistan's victory against India with firecrackers.
Sudarshan News shared the video on Twitter , along with a provocative message against those supposedly celebrating Pakistan's victory. Sagar Kumar, a journalist from Sudarshan News also tweeted the video with the same claim from his verified account. Both later deleted the tweets, but the video bearing the Sudarshan News watermark has been widely shared since.
AFWA found that the video is at least two years old and not related to the Pakistani cricket squad's latest victory against the Indian team. AFWA Probe
In a reply to Sagar Kumar's now-deleted tweet, the Srinagar police had stated that the video was old and no such incident was reported from the Srinagar area after the recent India-Pakistan cricket match. "Don't spread fake news and sensationalism by circulating old videos. Nothing of this sort reported from anywhere," read the Srinagar police tweet.
The police also added the video in question was around six years old and it was from Srinagar's Nawakadal chowk area. The video is half a decade old from Nawakadal chowk. Don't spread fake news and sensationalism by circulating old videos. Nothing of this sort reported from anywhere. #FakeNewsAlert — Srinagar Police (@SrinagarPolice) September 4, 2022
The video is half a decade old from Nawakadal chowk. Don't spread fake news and sensationalism by circulating old videos. Nothing of this sort reported from anywhere. #FakeNewsAlert — Srinagar Police (@SrinagarPolice) September 4, 2022
The oldest version of the video we could find on the internet was from August 14, 2020. Many on social media had shared the video at the time claiming it showed a celebration of Pakistan's independence day in Srinagar.
It is noteworthy, however, that similar incidents have been reported from Jammu and Kashmir in the past. Jammu and Kashmir Police in October 2021 registered a case about the alleged celebration of the Pakistani cricket team's victory over India in the T20 World Cup.
AFWA couldn't independently verify the context or the date of the video in question. However, it is clear that the video is at least more than two years old and not related to Pakistan's recent victory in the Asia Cup 2022.
(With input from Yash Mittal) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Sep 5, 2022 17:25 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video of crocodile in waterlogged road is NOT from Bengaluru
content:
The viral video is old and from Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh. This happened in August. The croc was later captured.
Incessant rains in Bengaluru have paralysed the Silicon Valley of India. Social media in the last few days has seen an onslaught of videos and photos that show waterlogged streets and flooded homes in the Karnataka capital. One such video supposedly from Bengaluru shows a crocodile crawling through a waterlogged road.
Many on Facebook shared the video, identifying the location as Bellandur, a suburb in southeast Bangalore.
But is it? AFWA's investigation found this video is from Madhya Pradesh. AFWA Probe
In the comments section of one such post, some people pointed out that the video was from Madhya Pradesh. A subsequent search informed us that this particular video has been on the internet since August this year.
Several news websites had reported this. ETV Bharat uploaded this video on its YouTube channel on August 16, 2022, with the title, "Crocodile enters residential colony in Shivpuri in MP, rescued."
Per ETV Bharat, a crocodile wandered into a residential colony in Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district and was later captured by the rescue team from Madhav National Park after an hour-long operation. It was then released into the Sankhya Sagar Lake.
This incident was also reported by the Times of India , the Hindustan Times and News 18 . They all used the same visuals.
Per these reports, the crocodile was eight-foot-long and caused panic among people as it entered a residential area near the old bus stand in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh following heavy monsoon downpours. The crocodile was seen swimming into the area after a nullah overflowed, causing waterlogging.
As floods continue in Bengaluru, many have shared photos of civic volunteers finding catfish in the waterlogged streets.
This too was reported by news websites . However, AFWA did not find any recent news about crocodiles being spotted in Bengaluru. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Sep 6, 2022 19:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Ravi Shastri's mistake did not cost India the toss in Asia Cup 2022 India-Pakistan match
content:
Yes, Ravi Shastri did goof up while announcing the toss call. But his mistake was corrected by the match referee Andy Pycroft on the spot. Pakistan rightly won the toss.
A popular sentiment among Indian cricket fans, "lose the cup but don't lose against Pakistan," perfectly captures the feverish atmosphere around every India-Pakistan match. In such a situation, even the coin toss becomes a prestige issue. And following India's recent defeat against Pakistan in Dubai, the toss has become somewhat controversial.
During the match in the super 4 edition of the Asia Cup 2022, held on September 4, cricketer turned commentator Ravi Shashtri announced the toss. Pakistan won it and elected to bowl first — eventually winning the match by five wickets.
A video of this toss is now being widely shared online. In the clip , Indian skipper Rohit Sharma tossed the coin while Pakistani skipper Babar Azam took the call. As Babar called "tails", Shashtri appeared to announce it as "heads". Many on social media are now blaming Shashtri for calling the toss wrongly in favour of Pakistan, implying that this is what led to the team's victory.
AFWA found that while Shashtri did goof up the toss call, his mistake was corrected by the match referee Andy Pycroft on the spot. The outcome of the toss was not affected by Shastri's mistake.
The archived versions of such tweets can be seen here and here . AFWA Probe
We found a tweet by Star Sports India, the broadcasters of the Asia Cup 2022. The tweet contained the video of the toss where Babar can be clearly heard saying "tails," with Shastri announcing it as "heads". But, after the toss, referee Andy Pycroft announced the outcome as "tails". Rohit Sharma then pointed at Babar, signalling the latter won the toss. The coin has favoured Babar, check out below what Pakistan chose to do! Keep watching #INDvPAK at the DP World #AsiaCup2022 on Star Sports & Disney+Hotstar! #BelieveInBlue #GreatestRivalry - Round2 pic.twitter.com/C2PyULDCRB — Star Sports (@StarSportsIndia) September 4, 2022
The coin has favoured Babar, check out below what Pakistan chose to do! Keep watching #INDvPAK at the DP World #AsiaCup2022 on Star Sports & Disney+Hotstar! #BelieveInBlue #GreatestRivalry - Round2 pic.twitter.com/C2PyULDCRB — Star Sports (@StarSportsIndia) September 4, 2022
Many media reports also confirmed the referee's on-spot correction . Who decides the conditions of the toss?
A BCCI official told AFWA that it is customary that the skipper of the home team tosses the coin while the one visiting calls it. In case both the teams are playing on foreign soil, it's decided beforehand which team will be designated as home and which one as visitors.
Thus we concluded that Shastri's goof-up did not affect the outcome of the toss in the September 4 India-Pakistan match.

title: Fact Check: When Ashish became Ashik — grisly Mysuru murder given false communal spin
content:
Both the accused and victim are Hindus. The woman was allegedly killed by a 29-year-old man called Ashish. His name was falsely shared as "Ashik" by several news reports.
A young woman was found dead in a hotel room. The police took swift action and arrested her boyfriend as the prime suspect. This incident from Mysuru, Karnataka, however, has been discussed on social media in a different context — that of "Love Jihad", a Hindu right-wing conspiracy that believes Muslim men seduce Hindu women in order to convert them.
Those discussing this incident shared the photos of the two involved — a Hindu woman called Apoorva Shetty and a supposedly Muslim man called Ashik. Sagar Kumar, a journalist from Sudarshan News tweeted the photos, calling the man an "Abdul", a popular euphemism for Muslim men used by the Hindu right.
AFWA, however, found that both the victim and the man accused of killing her are Hindu.
The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here , here , and here .
We found that the post that's being shared with the names and photos of the victim and the accused was taken from a news report by Mysuru-based news website Star of Mysore . Per this report and others, Shetty was found dead in a hotel on the night of August 31. She had reportedly checked into the hotel with a man called Ashik. On September 2, the Mysuru police apprehended this man.
Multiple media outlets including News18 Kannada , Zee News , TV9 Kannada reported the incident, calling the accused Ashik, However, none of these reports had any mention of his religion. To get to the bottom of this, AFWA reached out to ACP MN Shashidhar and Inspector Divakar of the Devaraja police station, under whose jurisdiction this case falls. They both told AFWA that the name of the accused was not Ashik — it was Ashish. They said both the accused and the victim are Hindu. Speaking to AFWA, the ACP said, "When rumours started to circulate in the name of the accused's religion, I personally took a look at his details. The name of the man is Ashish and he belongs to the Okkaliga caste. His father's name is Ravikumar and his mother is Gowri. He is a 29-year-old graphic designer." AFWA also obtained a copy of the FIR, which confirms that the name of the accused is Ashish. "The couple had taken a room at a hotel on August 30. Ashish went absconding following the woman's death. He was later arrested after the police traced his mobile. He is currently under police custody and an investigation is underway," the ACP further said. The police also told AFWA that the accused is an alcoholic and has a history of engaging in petty fights, adding that he is married and has been staying away from his wife for some time. He has been charged with murder under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code. It is hence clear that both, the victim and accused, are Hindus. And all allegations of "Love Jihad" are false. Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Sep 7, 2022 15:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Netizens go gaga over incredible wrestling moves! But the grappler is not Olympian Bajrang Punia
content:
The man seen in the viral video is Mosam Ali, a freestyle professional wrestler from Punjab.
Two pehelvans or wrestlers face off against each other in an arena surrounded by hundreds of people. One of the wrestlers shows tremendous dexterity as he rolls and tosses his opponent several times in quick succession — rendering him visibly disoriented and unwilling to fight.
This exciting short video has been widely shared online with the claim that it shows Indian freestyle wrestler and Olympics bronze medallist Bajrang Punia displaying his talent.
AFWA, however, found that the expert wrestler in the video was not Punia. It was Mosam Ali, a professional wrestler from Punjab. The viral post has been archived here . AFWA Probe
Under the viral tweet, several people said that the wrestler in question was Mosam Ali. People also commented that this looked like a staged fight.
A reverse image search on the video's frames revealed that it had been on the internet since 2019. Several people at the time had shared the video on Facebook and YouTube and they can be seen here , here , and here .
We then found Ali's YouTube channel , which is full of similar freestyle wrestling videos. In almost all videos, Ali appears to be the winner. AFWA spoke to Ali over the phone and showed him the viral clip. He recognised the video and immediately identified himself in the viral clip.
Ali is a popular name in freestyle professional wrestling circles in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh. Per news reports , he hails from Malerkot, Punjab, and has won several local or interstate tournaments .
His bouts are popular and get regularly featured on "Kusti" YouTube channels . We found several videos of Ali where he defeats his opponents using his signature wrestling move as seen in the viral clip.
Because some people alleged the video was staged, AFWA asked Ali about it, who said, "Even WWE wrestling is also for entertainment. Yes, if we entertain people with our wrestling what is wrong with that?" On his Instagram page , Ali calls himself an "artist".
In either case, it is amply clear that the video does not show Bajrang Punia. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Sep 7, 2022 19:58 IST

title: Fact Check: 2019 World Cup clash between Afghanistan and Pakistan cricket fans shared as Asia Cup incident
content:
This video does show Afghanistan and Pakistan cricket fans clashing. However, it is old and took place during the ICC Cricket World Cup tournament of 2019.
A video of a brawl inside a cricket stadium that's been widely shared recently supposedly shows violence following the recent Afghanistan-Pakistan Super 4 match of the Asia Cup.
In the video, people were seen shouting, punching, and hurling chairs at one another. A few of those involved in the violence appeared to be wearing Pakistani cricket jerseys and holding Pakistani flags. Security personnel could be seen attempting to control the situation. People shared the video with captions like, "Pakistan fans vs Afghanistan fans fighting in Dubai. Asia Cup 2022."
AFWA's investigation found that this clash took place between Afghanistan and Pakistan supporters during the 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup.
We found that many people had shared the same video in 2019, proving that it definitely was not recent. A YouTuber had captioned one such video as, "Fight during Pakistan vs Afghanistan match 29 June 2019 ICC world cup."
Subsequently, we found a June 2019 report by The Sun , that said after Pakistan defeated Afghanistan in a Cricket World Cup match, clashes erupted between fans. We compared the viral video with the video shared by The Sun report and found striking similarities between the two.
The match where this clash happened took place on June 29, 2019, in the Headingley stadium in Leeds, England. And the brawl was reported by several Indian media outlets .
Reportedly , fans clashed after a plane with political messages like, "Justice for Baluchistan" and "Help end disappearances in Pakistan" flew over the cricket ground.
It's noteworthy that after Pakistan's recent victory against Afghanistan in the Asia Cup Super 4 match , clashes broke out between the fans of the two countries. The Sharjah Stadium was also reportedly vandalised by fans during this.
To sum it up, while Afghanistan and Pakistan cricket fans brawled during the Asia Cup 2022 cricket match, this video does not show that. Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Sep 8, 2022 15:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Sportscar swims through flooded Bengaluru street? This video is not even from India
content:
This video is neither from Bangalore nor from India at all. It has been on the internet since June and was shot in the US, likely in Miami, Florida.
Heavy rains led to floods in several parts of Bengaluru recently. Photos and videos of waterlogged roads and flooded houses from the city have taken over social media. One such was a video of a submerged supercar swimming through a flooded street.
Those sharing the video claimed it was from Bengaluru, and shared it with captions like, "All the unicorn millionaire startup founders in Bangalore right now." All the #unicorn #millionaire #startup founders in Bangalore right now. #bangalorefloods #bangalorerains #Bangalore #bangalorestartups #unicornstartups #founders pic.twitter.com/INc6V3usHd — Besharam ladka (@BesharamLadka) September 5, 2022
All the #unicorn #millionaire #startup founders in Bangalore right now. #bangalorefloods #bangalorerains #Bangalore #bangalorestartups #unicornstartups #founders pic.twitter.com/INc6V3usHd — Besharam ladka (@BesharamLadka) September 5, 2022
The same video has been shared widely on Facebook as well. The archived version of this video can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found that the video was not from Bangalore — or even India.
When we reverse-searched frames from the video, it led us to several articles published on automobile news websites . As these articles were published in June 2022, it became clear that it is in no way related to the recent Bengaluru floods that happened in the first week of September.
The car seen in this video was a Chevrolet C8 Corvette. Per the reports, this video was reportedly shot in Miami, Florida. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Luis Leyva (@superstrong26) Was it shot in Florida? We spotted a man at the beginning of the video holding a green and black umbrella. When we ran a Google Lens search on the umbrella, it took us to a website featuring photos of similar-looking umbrellas. These umbrellas were a promotional product for TD Bank. We went through the official website of TD Bank or Toronto-Dominion Bank which operates in North America and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada. However, we weren't able to find any other markers to identify the location. So, while we were not able to pinpoint the exact place where the video was shot, we are more than certain that it was not in Bengaluru. title: Fact Check: No, dancing Pak fan DID NOT cause Pak-Afg clash at Asia Cup 2022, viral video is from 2021
content:
The video of the dancing Pakistan fan is from a 2021 T20 World Cup match between Pakistan and Afghanistan. It is completely unrelated to the recent clash.
Following the high-octane Asia Cup 2022 match in Sharjah on September 7, where Pakistan defeated Afghanistan, social media has seen a deluge of photos and videos of fans of both teams clashing. One such post shows two videos playing on split-screen.
One shows a man wearing a Pakistan cricket jersey and white shorts, grooving with joy in the middle of the crowd in the stadium. The other video shows a brawl. People could be seen attacking each other and vandalising the stadium.
People sharing the video claimed that the dancing Pakistan supporter instigated and provoked the Afghanistan fans, which resulted in the clashes.
Journalist Aditya Raj Kaul tweeted the video, writing: "A glimpse of Pakistani fans abusing, taunting & mocking Afghan fans inside the stadium which led to an argument and Afghan fans were provoked. Clash erupted. Hope action is taken against Pakistanis who end up indulging in violence everywhere across globe!"
Archives of similar social media posts can be found here , here , and here .
AFWA found that the dancing Pakistan fan's video is from the T20 World Cup 2021.
We found the first part of the viral video shared by a Pakistani YouTube channel "Jaan Kay Geo" on Nov 2, 2021. This proved that the dancing Pakistan supporter had nothing to do with the recent clash.
Another YouTube channel named "All Timez Sports" shared this video with the caption, "Pakistani Fan Mocking Afghanistan People In The Stadium Funny Dance ICC World T20 Cup 2021 #PakvAFG."
The 2021 Men's ICC World Cup match between Afghanistan and Pakistan took place at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, Dubai on October 29, 2021 .
The Asia Cup 2022 match between the two teams, on the other hand, was held at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium in the UAE.
We also compared the clash's video with photos and videos of the two stadiums and found that the video of the clash was from the Sharjah stadium . When we did the same for the dancing man's video, we found it was shot in the Dubai stadium .
To sum it up, the video of a Pakistani fan dancing and teasing Afghanistan supporters is from the T20 World Cup 2021 — it is completely unrelated to the recent clashes that took place during the Asia Cup 2022.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Sep 8, 2022 19:05 IST

title: Fact Check: Bulldozer scooping water out of flooded Pak street? This video is at least 4 years old!
content:
This video is from 2018 and was shot in either Iran or Iraq. It does not show the ongoing climate disaster in Pakistan.
Pakistan's worst climate-induced disaster in years continues to devastate countless as people struggle to find food and shelter amid floods. With its biggest lake, Manchar, bursting its banks, the rescue teams there are racing to evacuate people.
In the middle of this, a rather bizarre video supposedly from Pakistan has started doing the rounds on social media. In the 30-second video, a bulldozer appears to be scooping water from a flooded street and pouring it into a truck. The water, however, continuously drips from the truck. Voices can be heard in the background, laughing at this seemingly unusual activity.
The text in the video reads, "Heavy rain in Pakistan. City is flooded. They are removing water using the latest technology. The whole world is stunned seeing this technology."
Those sharing the video mocked Pakistan's supposed attempts to mitigate the devastation caused by the floods. Archives of these posts can be found here and here .
AFWA has found that this video is neither recent nor of Pakistan. It has been on the internet since at least 2018. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of the keyframes of this video led us to Russian news portals that stated the video was from November 2018 and was shot in Baghdad, Iraq.
We also found the same video tweeted by Al Jazeera Mubasher correspondent Abdulaziz Mujahed on November 28, 2018. pic.twitter.com/iJ5dYHkSzM — |Abdulaziz Mujahed (@elmogahed02) November 28, 2018
pic.twitter.com/iJ5dYHkSzM — |Abdulaziz Mujahed (@elmogahed02) November 28, 2018
While the tweet stated that the video was from Baghdad, Mujahed later followed up with another tweet stating that some of his followers suggested that it was from Ahvaz, a city in Iran. The comments on this tweet also suggested that in the video, the bulldozer wasn't scooping up water, it was removing mud and debris.
We searched for "Ahvaz flood" along with frames from the video and landed on the YouTube channel of Ava News , which also suggested that the video was from Ahvaz.
As per news reports, heavy rains caused floods in parts of both Iran and Iraq in November 2018.
So, while AFWA was not able to verify if it was shot in Iran or Iraq, this 2018 video definitely does not show the recent floods in Pakistan. Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Sep 8, 2022 22:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Rahul Gandhi is being made the butt of a joke — but the truth is something else
content:
This audio in the clip has been tampered with. In January 2021, while showing a booklet on the Farm Laws 2020, Gandhi turned around to mock the BJP, alleging that the party would have hidden this information.
A video being widely shared online shows Rahul Gandhi holding a booklet during a press conference. Gandhi shows the poster and then suddenly turns around, showing his back to the reporters there. Sharing this video , one person wrote, "When Rahul Gandhi was asked to show the backside of the poster, he turned around and showed his own a**."
Others mocked Gandhi similarly, including Maharashtra Bharatiya Janata Party MLA Ram Satpute, who shared the video with the hashtag "Pappu".
AFWA found that the audio has been tampered with in this clip. In reality, while showing a booklet on the Farm Laws 2020, Gandhi turned his back to the press in an attempt to mock the BJP.
The archived versions of these claims can be seen here and here .
We found the full video of this press conference on the Indian National Congress's official YouTube channel. The January 2021 video was titled, "LIVE: Special Press Briefing by Shri Rahul Gandhi at AICC HQ".
Two minutes and 24 seconds into the video, the viral extract shows up. Here, Gandhi can be heard saying, "See how fair we are. We are clearly showing our booklet to each one of you. If the BJP would've been here, they would've done this"
At this point, Gandhi turned his back to the reporters, implying that the BJP would have hidden this information from the press. The audio of the part where he mentioned the BJP was edited out from the viral video.
Per media reports , on January 19, 2021, Gandhi released a booklet named "Kheti Ka Khoon" (Murder of Agriculture), highlighting the "plight" of farmers in the country. The booklet was released at a press event at the Congress headquarters in New Delhi. He alleged that the Centre was misinforming the country about the Farm Laws 2020.
At the time, there was a massive ongoing protest against the BJP-led Centre on the three farm laws which were later rolled back in November 2021.
(Written by Yash Mittal, with inputs from Mayank Anandan)

title: Fact Check: Justin Timberlake wasn't wearing an anti-Trump t-shirt, photo was digitally altered
content:
This photo was digitally altered. In the actual photo, Timberlake was wearing a t-shirt with 'Nike Air' written on it.
In a recent interview, former President Donald Trump said that everyone wants him to run for President in the 2024 elections in the US. He added that Narendra Modi was doing a terrific job as the Indian Prime Minister. In the backdrop of these statements, a photo of singer-songwriter Justin Timberlake has gone viral on social media where he can be seen wearing a t-shirt with that proclaimed, "Keep America Trumpless." Those sharing the photo also shared links to an e-commerce website where one can buy these t-shirts. AFWA's investigation found that the viral image is doctored. In the actual photo, Timberlake was wearing a "Nike Air" t-shirt. AFWA Probe A simple reverse search of the viral image led us to the stock photos website Getty images . In this photo, his t-shirt said "Nike Air". This text appeared to have been digitally removed in the viral photo and replaced with the "Keep America Trumpless." ALSO READ| Fact Check: Rahul Gandhi is being made the butt of a joke — but the truth is something else As per Getty Images, this photo was shot in New York City when Timberlake was going to the gym on August 10, 2017. The same day, GQ magazine published a report on Timberlake's "gym look" with the headline "Justin Timberlake's Chill Gym Style is a Lesson in Layering." In the past, photos of various celebrities like Dwayne ' The Rock' Johnson , former US President Barack Obama, Brad Pitt and Chris Evans were also digitally altered to make them wear similar anti-Trump t-shirts. All of these were debunked. Published By: Ritika Shah Published On: Sep 9, 2022 02:27 IST

title: Fact Check: 2017 pic of Burj Khalifa lit up as Union Jack FALSELY shared as Queen Elizabeth II tribute
content:
This photo is from 2017 when Burj Khalifa was illuminated in the colours of the Union Jack to show solidarity following the suicide bombing attack in Manchester, UK.
As the world mourned the death of Queen Elizabeth II, a photo of Dubai skyscraper Burj Khalifa lit up in the colours of the United Kingdom flag has been widely shared on social media , supposedly as a tribute to the Queen.
People shared the photo on Twitter with captions like, "The latest tribute to the passing of HM #QueenElizabeth at #BurjKhalifa #UAE." The archived version of this post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found that while this photo is real, it's not recent at all — it's from 2017. AFWA probe
A reverse search of the photo led us to a BBC report from May 24, 2017. Per the report, multiple iconic landmarks like Geneva's Jet d'Eau fountain, Dubai's Burj Khalifa, and Australia's Brisbane's Story Bridge were illuminated in the colours of the British flag to pay tribute to the victims of the suicide bombing attack in Manchester, UK. This incident happened at a crowded pop concert leaving 22 people dead and more than 100 injured.
The same photo was used in an Al Arabiya report from the same date. Burj Khalifa was lit up on the Queen's 94th b'day
In 2020, Burj Khalifa was lit up in honour of Queen Elizabeth II on her 94th birthday. Its photo was shared by the official Instagram account of the tower on April 21, 2020. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Burj Khalifa by Emaar (@burjkhalifa) Till the time of writing this story on September 9, 2022, there were no reports of Burj Khalifa lit up in the colours of the British flag as a tribute to Queen Elizabeth II. However, the Empire State Building in New York City in the US shared a photo on its official Twitter account of the skyscraper bathed in purple light. The tweet ( https://twitter.com/EmpireStateBldg/status/1567966413188628480 ) read, "Tonight, our tower lights will shine in purple and sparkle in silver to honour the life and legacy of Her Majesty, Queen Elizabeth II." title: Fact Check: Mourning for Elizabeth did not take violent turn at Wembley! This video is from 2014
content:
This video is from 2014 when football fans disrupted a minute's silence to the Gresford Mining Disaster during the Chester v Wrexham derby.
Tributes poured in from around the world following the demise of Queen Elizabeth II, who took her last breath at the Balmoral Castle in Scotland on September 8. From brands to celebrities, thousands shared photos and videos, paying their respects to the English monarch. One such post is a video that supposedly shows a minute's silence being observed at the Wembley Stadium — that is rudely interrupted. All of a sudden, people got angry and started shouting. Someone in the crowd even lobbed a flare. People shared the video on Twitter with captions like, "Minute's silence for the Queen at Wembley before England vs Germany". Archives of similar posts can be found here and here . AFWA found that this video is from 2014, and is not related to the English Royal Family at all. AFWA PROBE On reverse searching the frames of the viral video, we found a 2019 YouTube video entitled, "Minute silence interrupted, Chester vs Wrexham (bootlegger)". It was the same clip. The video's description listed the original source that landed us on the YouTube channel "Bootlegger", which had shared the video log of the match where the incident actually happened in 2014. The viral video is only a small part of the almost hour-long vlog. A news report about this incident stated that on September 22, 2014, a minute of silence was held prior to the kick-off of a Chester FC-Wrexham AFC football match at the Swansway Chester Stadium to mark 80 years of the 1934 Gresford Mining Disaster that claimed the lives of 266 miners. However, Chester FC fans interrupted the silence by mocking a Wrexham supporter's tragic death. These fans were later banned from watching matches at the stadium for 30 years. It's noteworthy that following the passing of Queen Elizabeth II, there have been reports of similar incidents already. During a Europa Football League match between Arsenal and Zurich, a minute's silence during half-time was interrupted with boos and jeers on September 8. This video, however, does not show that. We also looked up if there was an England-Germany match at the Wembley Stadium as claimed. According to the stadium's website, it is scheduled for September 26, 2022. This completely dismisses what was being claimed. ( Written by Sanjana Saxena ) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Sep 9, 2022 18:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Woman throwing money at colonised kids is NOT Queen Elizabeth, video is 26 years older than her
content:
This video was shot by French filmmaker Gabriel Veyre between 1899 and 1900 in a French colony in Vietnam. Queen Elizabeth II was born in 1926.
Queen Elizabeth II's seven-decade-long reign has been a well-documented one. Following her death, news outlets, among others, have been sharing retrospectives. These feature a lot of monochromatic videos and photos of the monarch in different parts of the once-vast British empire. One such video, that has been shared by many, shows two women throwing what appears to be food at a group of children who can be seen fighting to grab it. One of the women is supposedly Queen Elizabeth II, and this video was allegedly shot in one of Africa's British colonies. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here . AFWA found that the woman in the video is not Queen Elizabeth. In fact, this video is more than two decades older than the English monarch. AFWA PROBE Upon reverse-searching frames from the video, we came across a screenshot from it on a French website called Catalogue Lumière , which archives films made by the Lumière company in Lyon, France. As per the website, the screenshot was from a film by Gabriel Veyre, shot sometime between 1899 and 1900 at the French colony of Annam, French Indochina (now Vietnam). The film was screened on January 20, 1901, in Lyon, France, under the title "Indo-Chine: Annamese children picking up cash in front of the ladies' pagoda." The site said the women in the video were Madame Paul Doumer — the wife of Joseph Athanase Paul Doumer , the Governor-General of French Indochina from 1897 to 1902 — and her daughter. Between 1899 and1900, French filmmaker Gabriel Veyre travelled across the French colonies in Vietnam. He shot around 39 motion pictures and photographs for the French government to exhibit at the 1900 Paris Exposition Universelle. This was 26 years before Queen Elizabeth II was even born. We searched for the film on YouTube and found a better-quality version uploaded to a channel containing a catalogue of films by Lumière. The video was titled, "Lumière: Annamese children picking up coins in front of the Ladies' Pagoda (1900)." It is clear from the video that neither woman in it resembles the now-dead English monarch. Additionally, we can also see Chinese text written on the building behind the woman. The text, per Google Lens, was about Buddha, which would make sense because the building is a pagoda or a Buddhist place of worship. The video was published by multiple other YouTube channels and websites with the same information. Thus, we concluded that this video did not show Elizabeth II. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Sep 9, 2022 19:12 IST

title: Fact Check: These photos of luxury caravans are not from Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra
content:
These photos are old and not related to Bharat Jodo Yatra. They show a luxury caravan belonging to a Maharashtra-based brand. Congress's Jairam Ramesh confirmed no such vehicle was part of the campaign.
As Congress leader Rahul Gandhi began the party's ambitious "Bharat Jodo Yatra" from Kanyakumari to Kashmir, the containers that will serve as accommodations for Gandhi and 230 party workers created some controversy online. Many shared photos of what the interiors of the 60 or so containers mounted on trucks supposedly look like. These photos included what looked like a luxury caravan with high-end interiors.
India TV also used one of the photos shared on social media claiming it was the caravan used by Gandhi during the campaign. The archived version of the post can be seen here and here .
AFWA, however, found that the photos were not of the Bharat Jodo Yatra containers at all. AFWA probe
With a reverse image search, we found the first three photos in a 2013 Indiatimes report . Per this report, the photos were from the interior of a premium motorhome that was introduced in 2013. The same photos and several others from the interior of this motorhome were also shared by multiple Facebook pages in 2013.
The fourth photo in the post was that of a parked caravan. We found the same published in a 2019 article on the website Luxe Camper . More photos of it were available on the website of Maharashtra-based caravan vendor Motohom . To get to the bottom of it, AFWA reached out to Congress leader and general secretary in charge of communication for the party, Jairam Ramesh, who confirmed that Gandhi and other party cadres participating in the campaign were using bare minimum utilitarian containers hired from a Mumbai-based company and the images being circulated online were not of their containers. According to him, Gandhi is using a one-bed container, while other containers have between two and 12 beds. title: Fact Check: Over decade-old image of empty theatre from Argentina goes viral, claiming 'Brahmastra's box office failure
content:
This image is at least 13 years old and was taken in 'Teatro Presidente Alvear', a theatre for performing arts in Buenos Aires, Argentina.
Brahmastra, the purported magnum opus of director Ayan Mukerji, started with a bang at the box office. While it has received a lukewarm response from critics, a section of social media is keen to follow the boycott trend against this movie. Amid this, an image of an empty theatre has gone viral on social media.
People who shared this image claimed this to be from the screening of Brahmastra on the first day of its release. A man can be seen in this image sitting in the middle between the empty chairs, while two others were having a chat in the corner.
This picture was shared with a caption calling for a boycott of this movie. Users also cite this image to claim that Brahmastra flopped on its first day as the theatre remained empty.
An Archived version of such a post can be seen here.
AFWA's investigation has found that the image of this empty theatre is more than a decade old and is from Argentina. AFWA Probe
With the help of a reverse image search on Google, we found the same image in a report by "The Print" published on 10 January 2021, making it clear that the image is not recent, and not related to Brahmastra by any means.
Although the caption did not carry any details about this photograph, it mentioned this as a representational image of an empty theatre.
But where was it shot, and when?
We searched further for this image and found this on Flickr , a website dedicated to sharing photographs online.
There, it mentioned that the photograph was taken by a photographer named Beatrice Murch on August 25, 2009. Although it did not reveal the place where it was shot, it carried some tags like Argentina, Buenos Aires and Teatro Alvear.
With the help of these keywords, we were able to locate a theatre for performing arts named ' Teatro Presidente Alvear ' in Buenos Aires, the capital of Argentina.
Some more searches with keywords took us to a Spanish article on this theatre where we found several images that show the inside of the auditorium. When we compared the seat arrangements and the design of the lighting on the wall of the theatre, it became clear that the viral image was indeed taken here.
