title: Fact Check: No temples were harmed in this video! Dargah demolition in Andhra given communal spin
content:
The structure being demolished in the video is a dargah or a Muslim shrine - not a temple. It was being demolished to construct a mosque in its place. However, the demolition has been put on hold.
"Jihadis demolished an ancient temple in Andhra Pradesh. Wake up Hindus, wake up! This is happening in independent India," screamed an alarming tweet . Alongside it was a video that showed a few men demolishing an archway. The men wore skull caps.Â
This video  was shared by many online, who all made similar claims. Some alleged  without sharing the video that "a Hindu Naga temple" was demolished by Muslims in Andhra Pradesh.
AFWA's investigation, however, found that the structure being demolished in the video was not a temple. In fact, it was the gate of a Muslim shrine or dargah. AFWA PROBE
A keyword search on Google led us to an India Today report . It said that tensions rose in Andhra Pradesh's Guntur after a few people tried to demolish a dargah at LR Nagar to construct a mosque on October 12. Locals intervened and stopped them.
Following this, we spoke to Abdul Basheer, India Today's principal correspondent in Guntur. Basheer confirmed the sequence of events stated in the report. He also shared a different video of the same incident where people could be seen breaking a green wall inside a compound. WHAT HAD HAPPENED?
According to an inspector at the Lalapet Police Station in Guntur, the Baji Baba dargah was established by AS Ratnam alias Rahman, who resided at LR Nagar for 40 years. Per the police, 15 years ago, Rahman set up a shrine for his wife on a piece of land he owned. He also allegedly informed his daughter and neighbours to construct a mosque there after his death.Â
Rahman succumbed to Covid-19 in 2020 and following this, his daughter, who was his legal heir, donated the land for a mosque to be constructed. The police said, however, families in the neighbourhood demanded that it must remain a dargah.Â
"We have not received any complaints. But due to the mild tensions, we have written to the RDO to put a hold on the demolition and also requested people not to enter the disputed area. The arch had a naga structure along with a crescent and a star that represents a dargah. However, as there was no complaint filed, no case has been registered. The situation is peaceful," the inspector said.
Therefore, it is clear that the video being shared is of a dargah, not a temple.

title: Fact Check: Old chopper crash photos and videos go viral after Kedarnath pilgrims' helicopter tragedy
content:
The video is from a 2014 airshow in Russia's Gelendzhik. The photo, on the other hand, has been in circulation for at least seven years. Neither is related to the recent tragedy.
Seven people, including a pilot, were killed after a helicopter carrying Kedarnath pilgrims crashed into a hill in Uttarakhand's Rudraprayag district on September 18 morning. Since the news broke, social media has seen a deluge of photos and videos that allegedly captured the tragic accident. One such video  shows a chopper bursting into flames. This 17-second-long clip shows a chopper landing awkwardly, bouncing on the ground, and then bursting into flames.  The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here . A photo of a helicopter exploding mid-air has also been shared by many on Twitter . Both implicitly and explicitly, people claimed it was a shot of the Kedarnath chopper. An archived version of this post can be seen here . AFWA found that neither was from the Kedarnath tragedy. The video is from a 2014 air show in Russia. The photo of the helicopter has been in circulation for seven years at least.  A Russian crash A reverse search of the video's keyframes on Yandex led us to the same video uploaded to YouTube in September 2014. Per its description, the footage shows a Mi-8 helicopter crash in Gelendzhik, Russia. We searched for the incident online and found multiple news reports from 2014 which carried a longer version of the video. Reportedly , during the international airshow "Gidroavisalon 2014" in Russia's Gelendzhik on September 4, 2014, a chopper crashed. The helicopter belonged to the Russian "Panh Helicopters" aviation company. All three people on board died. The exploding chopper photo The photograph of the helicopter exploding mid-air is also not related to the Kedarnath crash. Using reverse image search, we found the photo on the stock image site iStock . According to iStock, it was uploaded to the website on March 24, 2015. However, the website did not offer any other details regarding it. Over the years, multiple media organisations have used it as a representational photo for stories related to chopper crashes. While we couldn't independently confirm the exact source of the image, it is clear that it is not related to the Kedarnath incident in any way. Kedarnath helicopter crash The chopper, a Bell 407 helicopter VT-RPN owned by Delhi-based Aryan Aviation Private Limited, was travelling with pilgrims from Kedarnath to Guptkashi when it crashed in Garud Chatti, approximately two kilometres from Kedarnath. Per reports , the State Disaster Response Force has cited poor visibility caused by fog as a likely reason for the crash. Published By: Abhishek Chakraborty Published On: Oct 18, 2022 20:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Images from Pune Buddhist event FALSELY shared as mass religious conversion in Jaipur
content:
These photos are not from Jaipur but from Pune, Maharastra. These were shot on October 15 during a socio-religious event organised by the Indian Buddhist Mahasabha. No mass conversions at the event were reported.
On October 5, hundreds of Dalits across Delhi-NCR converted to Buddhism as part of the Buddha Dhamma Deeksha Samaroh, an event organised by the Jai Bheem Mission, founded by the Aam Aadmi Party's former social welfare minister Rajendra Pal Gautam. While the controversy surrounding the event continues to unfold, two photos have started making the rounds on social media. These photos allegedly show a similar mass conversion event in Jaipur, Rajasthan.Â
Those sharing the photos  claimed that on October 16, one lakh people were initiated to Buddhism in Jaipur . Â
AFWA's investigation found that these photos are not from Jaipur. They're from Pune, Maharastra, and shot during a "Dhamma Mela", organised by the Indian Buddhist Mahasabha. AFWA PROBE Â
First, we looked for news reports on recent mass conversions in Jaipur but found none. Following this, we reverse-searched the viral photos. This led us to multiple photos of an event shared by a Facebook page called "We Support Sujat Ambedkar"  on October 15. There, we noticed similar photos as the ones going viral.
The Marathi caption of the album described the event as a "grand Dhamma gathering" organised by the Indian Buddhist Mahasabha in Pimpri Chinchwad on the occasion of the 66th Dhammachakra Pravartan Day.Â
A subsequent refined search led us to a verified Twitter account of Priyadarshi Telang, an "independent researcher and human rights advocate". This account too had shared photos from the aforementioned event on October 15, calling it the "Dhamma Chakra Pravartan Din Celebration." #धम्मक्रांति चिरायु होओ #DhammaChakraPravartanDin Celebrations at Pimpri, Pune pic.twitter.com/GO1o1telkR — Adv Priyadarshi Telang (@priyadarshi07) October 15, 2022
#धम्मक्रांति चिरायु होओ #DhammaChakraPravartanDin Celebrations at Pimpri, Pune pic.twitter.com/GO1o1telkR — Adv Priyadarshi Telang (@priyadarshi07) October 15, 2022
According to a News18 report , Dhammachakra Pravartan Din marks the anniversary of BR Ambedkar and lakhs of his followers embracing Buddhism in 1956. Subsequently, we found photos of this event on the Twitter account of Prabuddh Bharat, a media house founded by Dr BR Ambedkar in 1956. तू उभा सूर्यापरी, राहिले कोठे निशा ! ऐवढे आम्हा कळे, ही तुझी आहे दिशा !! 66व्या धम्मचक्र प्रवर्तन दिनानिमित्त भारतीय बौद्ध महासभा आयोजित भव्य धम्म मेळावा, आज पिंपरी चिंचवडमध्ये लाखोंच्या जनसमुदायाच्या उपस्थित संपन्न झाला. लाखोची जनता, तिचा एकच नेता ! @Prksh_Ambedkar pic.twitter.com/tGV4TIuDbl — Prabuddh Bharat (@PrabuddhBharat2) October 15, 2022
तू उभा सूर्यापरी, राहिले कोठे निशा ! ऐवढे आम्हा कळे, ही तुझी आहे दिशा !! 66व्या धम्मचक्र प्रवर्तन दिनानिमित्त भारतीय बौद्ध महासभा आयोजित भव्य धम्म मेळावा, आज पिंपरी चिंचवडमध्ये लाखोंच्या जनसमुदायाच्या उपस्थित संपन्न झाला. लाखोची जनता, तिचा एकच नेता ! @Prksh_Ambedkar pic.twitter.com/tGV4TIuDbl — Prabuddh Bharat (@PrabuddhBharat2) October 15, 2022
When we compared the Prabuddh Bharat photos with the viral ones, it became clear that the latter were cropped out from the former.Â
 We also found a news report , quoting Prakash Ambedkar, the grandson of BR Ambedkar, who was one of the key speakers at the event. Per this report, during the event, Ambedkar criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, who had recently batted for the abolition of the caste system . However, we did not find any mention of religious conversions in this report. We then reached out to Sameer Shaikh, India Today's stringer from Pune who was present at the event. He confirmed to us that there was no mass conversion there. He added that Ambedkar's speech was more political, and focused less on social issues. Therefore, it is safe to conclude that a socio-religious gathering in Pune was falsely shared as a mass conversion in Jaipur, Rajasthan. (With inputs from Sameer S Shaikh, Pune) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Oct 19, 2022 00:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Did a Russian tank accidentally run over recent conscript? This shocking video is from 2014
content:
This incident is from 2014. News reports from the time, however, have discrepancies in terms of the soldier's name or even how seriously he was injured.
President Vladimir Putin recently said  that Russia should be finished calling up reservists in two weeks, promising an end to its controversial mobilisation drive that has seen hundreds of thousands of men summoned to fight in Ukraine. Reportedly, men in their fifties have been conscripted. The drive has led to many Russians fleeing the country , some even resorting to unusual means to do so.Â
Amid all this, a video  allegedly showing Putin's newly-mobilised recruits taking part in a parade has been shared widely online. What makes the video shocking is that an armoured vehicle tank tramples one of the soldiers during the event.
In this video, soldiers could be seen standing in attention. With audible gunshots in the background, two military vehicles could be seen moving. As one of the vehicles took a sharp turn, it ran over a soldier. The visibly injured soldier managed to get up before ultimately collapsing.  Â
On Facebook , people shared the video with captions like, "During a Russian military procession and 'show of might', a military vehicle runs over a Russian soldier who is part of the parade." Many media outlets , including The Irish Sun , reported this as a recent incident.Â
AFWA's investigation, however, found that the viral video dates back to 2014. AFWA Probe Â
Reverse-searching frames from the video on Tin Eye led us to a report by a Vietnamese news website  that reported on the video on June 17, 2014.Â
We also found a June 16, 2014, Daily Mail report  on the incident.Â
This report identified the soldier as 19-year-old Pavel Touromov, who had just completed his military training in the south-eastern Russian city of Ussuriysk when the accident happened. According to this report, Touromov suffered serious internal injuries after a BMP armoured personnel carrier that weighed 20 tonnes ran him down. An eye witness told the tabloid, "He went down and straight under the wheels, his body making the vehicle bounce. It was sickening to watch. I thought he was killed instantly but then, amazingly, he bounded up and ran off."
However, some Russian reports  have identified the soldier as Alexei Agishin and said that he sustained only just minor injuries. Another 2014 Russian news report , featuring a photo of the soldier in the hospital, quoted him on how he managed to survive.Â
Named here as Anatoly Agishin, the soldier reportedly said, "I stood with my back to this armored personnel carrier. At the last moment, I turned around and a second later there was a blow. I don't remember how the front two wheels drove over me. But I remember that when I saw a gap between the wheels, I grouped up and crawled under the hull of the armored personnel carrier. I waited for him to pass and then only tried to get to my feet. But then I don't remember anything."
So, while there are some discrepancies in how the story has been reported, it is nonetheless clear that it is in no way a recent incident. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Oct 19, 2022 19:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Video game footage mistaken for Ukrainian missile attack on Russian tanks — once again!
content:
This video does not show a real incident. It has been taken from a military video game called Arma 3.
Almost eight months in, as Russia's invasion of Ukraine continues, Russian General Sergei Surovikin admitted on October 18 that the situation in areas Russia claims to have annexed was 'tensed' .
As the war rages on, a video allegedly showing a Ukrainian missile attack on Russian tanks has been widely shared. On Twitter, people shared the video , with captions like: "American FGM-148 Javelin missiles attacking Russian tanks. Too bad they didn't have them earlier. It's no longer a walk in the park for the Soviets."
The FGM-148 Javelin or Advanced Anti-Tank Weapon System-Medium (AAWS-M) is an American-made portable anti-tank missile The Javelin made its debut in 1996 and has been in service for nearly three decades. Similar posts have been archived here , here , and here . Â
AFWA found that this video is not authentic footage from Ukraine, but from a video game called Arma 3 — a video game whose videos have been mistaken for war footage over the years.Â
A keyword search about Ukraine firing at Russian Tanks with Javelin missiles took us to a YouTube video on a channel called "MILMAN". This video  showed military attacks in a similar setting as the viral clip.Â
Further, we looked into other videos on this channel and found one that was an extended version of the viral clip. The description of the video stated that it is a military simulation and not real footage. The channel also added a disclaimer in the comment section that read: "All events in this video are not real. This is just a video game ARMA 3."  It's noteworthy that Javelin anti-tank missiles  are among the arms sent to Ukraine by the US as part of its military assistance packages. In fact, footage  of Ukrainian troops blowing up a Russian tank attack to smithereens using American Javelin anti-tank guided missiles has made the news earlier this year. But the viral video clearly does not show that. That footage is from a video game that has interestingly become somewhat enmeshed in the war footage misinformation machine. Back in July, footage  from the same game was falsely shared as Ukrainian drones attacking Russian subs. Back in 2020, videos from the game went viral as an Azerbaijani MiG-25 being shot down by Armenian defence forces. And the year before that, footage from the game was mistaken for a demonstration of Israel's anti-missile defence system. AFWA has debunked all three claims. (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Oct 19, 2022 22:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Kejriwal isn't talking about punishing rapists here, this 2020 presser was about Delhi riots
content:
This video is clipped from a 2020 press meet where Kejriwal spoke about how people found guilty of participating in the 2020 Delhi riots should be punished. He was not talking about those accused or convicted on rape charges.
Manish Sisodia, while campaigning in Gujarat for the Aam Aadmi Party, responded to a question from a journalist about Bilkis Bano. Documents have revealed  that the Union Home Ministry fast-tracked the early release of 11 men convicted of raping Bilkis Bano and killing her family during the 2002 Gujarat riots despite the CBI's strong objections. The journalist asked the Delhi Deputy Chief Minister why the AAP was silent on Bilkis Bano and issues related to Muslims, alleging that the party has been accused of "soft Hindutva". To this, Sisodia answered , "Our main focus is on development such as education, schools, hospitals, and employment. We are concerned about these issues." Sisodia's answer has since courted criticism on social media . Countering the backlash, several AAP members and supporters , including the party's MLA Naresh Balyan  shared a video of Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal. They claimed the AAP supremo's words in the video clarified the party's stance on rape and rapists. The archived versions of such posts can be seen here  and here . In this 24-second-long video from a press conference, Kejriwal can be heard saying: "Nobody should be spared. Take strict action against them. Why are you seeking public opinion on this? Will these opinions lead to punishment for the rioters? Is this how our criminal justice system works? Jail the ones who are guilty." AFWA found that this video has been clipped from a longer statement he made about the 2020 Delhi riots. AFWA Probe A reverse search of the keyframes of the viral video led us to its longer version uploaded by NDTV to its YouTube channel on February 27, 2020. The headline of the video reads, "Arvind Kejriwal said, 'Strict action should be taken against the rioters without seeing the party'." As per its description, the press conference was called by Kejriwal to talk about riots that broke out in parts of Northeast Delhi in February 2020. In this video, the Delhi Chief Minister can be heard saying, "The ones who tried to instigate riots should not be spared. Whoever it is, even if it's someone from my cabinet, nobody should be spared. Take the strictest of actions against them." "Why are you seeking public opinion? Will the opinions lead to punishments? Is this how our criminal justice system works? Jail the ones who are guilty. If these people are guilty, punish them. If our people are guilty, punish them doubly. Don't spare anyone. Stop politicising national security," he added. We also found multiple media reports  from February 2020 about this presser. Per these reports , Kejriwal held the meeting after former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain was accused of inciting violence during violent clashes in Delhi on February 24 and 25, 2020. It is hence clear that the video in question is from a press meeting related to the 2020 Delhi riots. It was taken out of context and shared with misleading claims. (With input from Yash Mittal) Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Oct 19, 2022 23:20 IST

title: Fact Check: Chilling video of snake coiled around sniper is NOT from Arunachal, it's from Indonesia
content:
This video is not from India at all. It's from Indonesia.
A sniper lay still covered in camouflage in a forest at an elevation, aiming into the distance. What made the scene chilling was that a snake had coiled itself around the sniper and the gun. But the sniper looked unaffected.Â
This video, allegedly from around Arunachal Pradesh, has been widely shared online. Rohit Upadhyay, the Bharatiya Janata Party's social media head for Delhi shared it as well and wrote, "Indian Army Sniper Armed With Sako TRG 42 .338 Lapua Magnum Sniper Rifle Along A King Cobra Somewhere Near LAC At Arunachal Pradesh". The archived version of this video can be seen here .
Even Zee News Marathi reported on this video, writing it was from Arunachal Pradesh's border.Â
AFWA's investigation found that the viral video is not from India at all, but from Indonesia.
Upon reverse-searching the keyframes of the video, we found it in a September 18 video report by the Indonesian news outlet Tribun Timur.
As per the YouTube video's description, the person seen in the video was part of the Indonesian National Armed Forces, also known as the TNI (Tentara Nasional Indonesia). The video was credited to a TikTok user @luxydwipriyanto0.
Multiple Indonesian news websites also cited the TikTok account as a source while reporting the story.Â
On TikTok, we found that this video was shared with the hashtags "Kopasgat TNI Au" and "TNI Indonesia". Kopasgat TNI Au is the infantry and special forces corps of the Indonesian Air Force. However, we couldn't independently verify if this video showed this particular branch of the Indonesian Air Force. We found another similar video of a person covered with grass, standing while holding a gun on the same TikTok account. Using keyword search, we found an Instagram and a Facebook account that most likely belonged to the same TikTok user. Upon comparing the kind of content shared on these three handles, one can see many similarities.  The account mentions the name Luxy Dwi Priyanto on Instagram and Facebook. In 2016, the person running the accounts had written in a Facebook post that he was associated with the 'Special Forces Corp Command'.  In most of his posts, he can be seen wearing a military uniform. In one of the videos shared by him , some people can be seen jumping out of an aircraft with parachutes.  While we cannot say with certainty that this is the person in the viral video, it is likely. We also couldn't find any evidence that this video shows an Indian Army soldier. Thus, we conclude that this video from Indonesia has been falsely shared with the claim it shows an Indian soldier in Arunachal Pradesh. advertisement (With inputs from Mayank Anandan) Also Read | Fact Check: Decade-old Nigerian photo FALSELY shared as Bharat Jodo Yatra scene Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Oct 20, 2022 17:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Grisly video of woman's naked corpse in suitcase in Gurgaon given FALSE communal spin
content:
The woman in the video has been identified as Priyanka. Her husband, Rahul Kushwaha, has been charged with murder. Both husband and wife were Hindus.
A video  making the rounds on social media shows cops examining an abandoned suitcase and discovering a naked corpse stuffed inside. Many sharing the video claimed the woman whose corpse was discovered was Hindu and that her Muslim boyfriend murdered her. Such tweets used the word "Abdul" while referring to the murderer. It is a euphemism for Muslim men that is regularly used by the Hindu right. The archived versions of such claims can be seen here , here , and here . AFWA found that both the victim and accused in this case were Hindu. This grisly murder was given a false communal spin. AFWA Probe According to the viral post, the suitcase was discovered in IFFCO Chowk, Gurugram. A keyword search on Twitter revealed two ANI tweets about the incident. In one of the tweets, the news agency used images similar to the visuals seen in the viral video. According to ANI, a woman's body was found in a suitcase near IFFCO Chowk in Gurugram on October 17. Per ANI, Gurugram's ACP Crime Preet Pal Singh said that the woman's husband was arrested in the case and later confessed to the crime. The agency, however, made no mention of the names or religions of the victim and the accused. Gurugram, Haryana | Body of a woman aged between 20-25 found in a suitcase, dumped near Iffco Chowk. Woman was murdered elsewhere. Body is fresh & has been sent to hospital, FIR filed. We're trying to establish identity of woman. Further probe on: DCP West Deepak Saharan pic.twitter.com/j1EOjaasCT — ANI (@ANI) October 17, 2022  Haryana | On October 17, a woman's body was found in a suitcase near IFFCO Chowk. The woman's husband was arrested in the case and later confessed his crime. There was a fight between the two after which the accused killed his wife: Preet Pal Singh, ACP Crime, Gurugram pic.twitter.com/7PFCcYp9ng — ANI (@ANI) October 19, 2022 AFWA then reached out to Singh, who confirmed to us that the woman's husband, who has been charged with her murder, is Hindu. Singh said, "Both the husband and wife were Hindus. The man's name is Rahul Kushwaha and the woman's name was Priyanka. So far there is no communal angle in this matter." Aaj Tak's Gurugram correspondent also confirmed to AFWA that the woman was from the Yadav caste.  According to the postmortem report , the woman was strangled to death. The police also said there was evidence of torture on her body, including her private parts. They also haven't ruled out rape. During police interrogation, the husband, Rahul, claimed that his wife used to make expensive demands that were unaffordable to him. This led to regular fights. According to police, on the night of October 16, Priyanka slapped Rahul. This enraged him and he strangled her to death. On the morning of October 17, he stuffed her corpse into a big suitcase and abandoned it at IFFCO Chowk. It is, hence, clear that both the accused and victim are Hindus, and the communal narrative being presented on social media is a false one. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Oct 20, 2022 20:19 IST

title: Fact Check: Rape convict whose life sentence was reduced by MP High Court is NOT a Muslim man, he's Hindu
content:
The name of the convict is Ramu aka Ramsingh, and he is a Hindu man. While the court called the crime "a demonic act", it reduced his sentence to 20 years saying that he was "kind enough" to spare the child's life.
A recent judgement by the Indore Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court reduced the life sentence of a rape convict to 20 years. The bench reportedly noted that while the crime was heinous, the convict was "kind enough" to spare the life of the four-year-old survivor. This move was criticised by many on social media, some of whom also claimed that the convict was a Muslim man called Mohammad Firoz. One such claim was made by Sudarshan News journalist Santosh Chauhan . The same claim was also tweeted by Sudarshan News journalist Ashish Vyas and Panchjanya, a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh publication. Panchjanya later deleted the tweet. The archived versions of these posts can be seen here , here  and here . AFWA's investigation found that the convict is Ramsingh, a Hindu man — not Mohammad Firoz. AFWA probe According to reports published by media organisations including The Indian Express , the Hindustan Times , and The Hindu , the name of the convict was Ramu alias Ramsingh. The Indore Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court reduced his sentence of life imprisonment, which was awarded to him in 2009, to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment. While the bench of Justices Subodh Abhyankar and Satyendra Kumar Singh called the crime "a demonic act", it reduced the life imprisonment stating the convict was "kind enough" to spare the child's life. The bench said, "In such circumstances, this Court does not find any error in appreciation of evidence by the trial Court and considering the demonic act of the appellant who appears to have no respect for the dignity of a woman and has the propensity to commit sexual offence even with a girl child aged four years, this Court does not find it to be a fit case where the sentence can be reduced to the sentence already undergone by him, however, considering the fact that he was kind enough to leave the prosecutrix alive, this court is of the opinion that the life imprisonment can be reduced to 20 years rigorous imprisonment." Ramsingh was arrested on charges of raping a four-year-old girl in Indore in 2007. He was convicted and sentenced to life term imprisonment by an Additional Sessions Judge, Indore in April 2009. In May 2009 he made a criminal appeal challenging the judgement in the Madhya Pradesh High Court, The incident reportedly took place near ITI ground in Indore on May 31, 2007. Ram Singh, then 25, resided in a tent nearby. He called the minor girl inside the tent under the pretext of giving her a rupee and raped her. AFWA accessed the judgement copy of the case dated October 18, 2022, to confirm the name of the convict. Per the judgement, which is available on the website of the Madhya Pradesh High Court, the name of the convict is Ramu aka Ramsingh, the son of Kishansingh. Ramsingh's advocate Sharmila Sharma also confirmed to AFWA that Ramsingh is Hindu. She also sent us a photo of his court surrender memo that identified Ramsingh as a "Marwari Rajput". It is hence clear that the name of the convict whose life imprisonment was reduced by the Madhya Pradesh High Court is not Mohammad Firoz. Also, the convict is a Hindu. Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 25, 2022 18:51 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Babar Azam DIDN'T accuse umpires of helping India with 'no-ball' call, fake quote goes viral
content:
Although Babar Azam initially argued with the on-field umpires over the no-ball call, he did not criticise the umpires' decision on any public platform.
Following India's nail-biting victory against Pakistan in the T20 World Cup, social media saw a deluge of photos and videos from the match, especially from Virat Kohli's innings. There has also been some controversy and outrage about the " no-ball " call in the last over of the match.Â
At a time when India needed 13 runs from three balls, Pakistani left-arm spinner Mohammad Nawaz offered Kohli a full toss which the latter sent over the boundary line. The umpires called it a 'no-ball' for its height, helping India get a free hit on the next ball. This obviously contributed to India's victory. Â
Many online also shared Babar Azam's alleged quote, where the Pakistani skipper supposedly took a dig at the umpires for favouring India. A Facebook page named "Best Hindi News" shared a photo of Babar Azam alongside the alleged quote, "It was the umpires who led to India's victory. The ball that Kohli hit for a six was not a no-ball."
AFWA's investigation has found that Babar Azam made no such comments. We also found no evidence that he criticised the umpires' calls in front of the media.Â
We found an Indian Express report quoting Pakistani cricketers like Wasim Akram, Waqar Younis, and Shoaib Malik who asked why the on-field umpires did not consult with the third umpire before calling the delivery a no-ball during such a crucial moment in the match. There were no reports, however, that quoted Babar Azam making such accusations.Â
On the contrary, Babar Azam admitted to Pakistan's "mistakes" in the last over. During a post-match press conference, the Pakistan skipper was asked if he thought strike bowlers like Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah should have bowled the last over instead of Mohammad Nawaz.Â
Babar explained that he wanted to pick up wickets from his strike bowlers early by giving away fewer runs so that Mohammad Nawaz got maximum runs to defend. He added, "Indian batsmen played sensibly as they knew that we have an over left from a spinner. There too, we bowled a no-ball and a couple of wides." The part where Babar speaks about the 'no-ball' can be heard around the 6-minute mark.Â
Aside from this press conference, Babar spoke during the post-match presentation ceremony , but did not mention anything about the no-ball call.Â
He was also seen giving a pep talk to the team in the dressing room following his team's defeat. There, he specially mentioned the name of Mohammad Nawaz and told his teammates not to lose heart as it was just the beginning of the tournament.
We also reached out to Sumit Ghosh, a sports journalist with a leading Bengali daily newspaper. He added that "although Babar was seen getting into an argument with the umpire when the no-ball was called, he did not get vocal about it after the match."
Therefore, it is more than evident that a fictional comment quoting Babar Azam has gone viral on social media. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Oct 25, 2022 22:04 IST

title: Fact Check: This stunning video of fireworks is OLD, not from Delhi's 2022 Diwali celebrations
content:
This video has been on the internet since January 2022 at least. Many claim it shows New Year's celebrations in Naples, Italy. However, we haven't been able to independently verify that.
A day after Diwali, on October 25, Delhi's air quality dropped to "very poor". While a number of factors like stubble burning, construction dust, and vehicular pollution account for Delhi's annual deterioration of air quality, firecrackers on Diwali play their part as well. The Delhi government had earlier announced a fine and/or imprisonment for those found bursting or selling firecrackers on Diwali this year. However, many flouted this ban across the city. Several people on social media shared a video  of a city skyline dominated by a stunning display of fireworks. Those sharing it  claimed this was how Delhi celebrated Diwali night. AFWA found that the video has been on the internet since January this year at least, and therefore could not have been from Diwali 2022. AFWA PROBE A number of people who claimed the video was from Delhi were quote-tweeting the Twitter account "@WokePandemic", which shared the video on October 24 with the caption, "Happy Diwali MiLords". Happy Diwali MiLords pic.twitter.com/8zgdx1DVXA — Eminent Woke (@WokePandemic) October 24, 2022 We found that the same account on January 3 had shared the same video claiming it to be from Italy's Naples. Italy: Naples, The mayor banned Crackers on New Year's eve, due to Covid restrictions. Mayor said €500 fine for anyone who violates the rules. This is how the Italians responded to Mayor on #CrackerBan @coolfunnytshirt Do share. pic.twitter.com/ndHNHZYKRh — Eminent Woke (@WokePandemic) January 3, 2022 We further reverse-searched the video's keyframes and found the video shared by multiple people on Twitter , Facebook and YouTube  in the first week of January 2022, all of whom claimed it was from Naples. The video and its screenshots were also carried by multiple media reports  from January 2022, that said despite a ban issued by the mayor of Naples Gaetano Manfredi, people had celebrated the new year with fireworks. There are several other videos of fireworks from the 2022 new year's celebrations in Naples available on social media. We couldn't independently verify the location of the viral video. AFWA has reached out to people from Naples to verify its location. This story will be updated as and when we receive a response. It is, however, clear that the video is at least ten months old and not related to Diwali celebrations in Delhi in 2022. (With inputs from Mayank Anandan in New Delhi) Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Oct 25, 2022 23:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Rishi Sunak seeking Hindu monk's blessings is from August, not after PM appointment
content:
This video is from Rishi Sunak's visit to an ISKCON temple in August 2022. He made the visit ahead of Janmashtami in 2022.
Rishi Sunak, the first person of Indian origin to become the British Prime Minister, has been largely cheered by Indians, both at home and abroad. Sunak, back in 2019, took oath as a member of the parliament holding the Bhagwad Gita . He also proudly displayed his religious roots when he sported the sacred Hindu 'Kalawa' thread  during his first address after taking charge as the PM. Time and again, he has embraced his Hindu heritage — something that has earned him both praise and criticism. Now, many on social media are claiming that Sunak took the blessing of a Hindu monk before swearing in as the Prime Minister. Those making the claim shared a video  where Sunak  can be seen kneeling in front of a saffron-clad man. In the clip, Sunak and his wife Akshata Murty could also be seen interacting with various people, some also dressed in saffron. The archived version of one such post can be seen here . AFWA found that the video is from Sunak's visit to an ISKCON temple in August 2022. AFWA Probe A keyword search on the recent temple visits made by Sunak led us to a tweet made by him on August 18. This tweet carried a photo of Sunak and his wife wearing saffron shawls. As per this tweet, the image was from Sunak's visit to the Bhaktivedanta Manor temple ahead of Janmashtami. Bhaktivedanta Manor is an ISKON temple in the UK's Watford. He also shared the same photo, and others, on his Instagram account . Today I visited the Bhaktivedanta Manor temple with my wife Akshata to celebrate Janmashtami, in advance of the popular Hindu festival celebrating Lord Krishna's birthday. pic.twitter.com/WL3FQVk0oU — Rishi Sunak (@RishiSunak) August 18, 2022 A set of images from Sunak's visit to Bhaktivedanta Manor was also shared by the temple on its Facebook page  on August 18. In these photos, one can see the same people and backgrounds as seen in the viral video. In August, Sunak was running for the Prime Minister's post in the United Kingdom. The same set of photos was also shared by the Instagram page of Bhaktivedanta Manor . The page also shared several other photos of the monk seen in the viral video. As per the page, he is Keshava Swami We further searched the Instagram profile of the monk and found the viral video uploaded by him on September 18, 2022. The caption to the video reads, "Was a pleasure to meet [Rishi Sunak] & Akshata Murthy a few weeks ago. 'Rishi' means a sage, a great thinker, derived from 'drsya' which means 'spiritual vision.' We talked about the need for wisdom that breathes in a world that's suffocating from materialism."     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by S.B. Keshava Swami (@keshavaswami) It is hence clear that the video in question is months old, and definitely not from after his appointment as the British Prime Minister. Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 26, 2022 20:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Months-old photo used to publicise low pollution levels in Delhi during Diwali 2022
content:
This is an old photo that was used in news reports as early as August 2022. Therefore, it cannot show Delhi's pollution levels on Diwali this year.
Over the years, Delhi's pollution has been a big concern for all. Between 2017 and 2021, Delhi was among the top five most polluted cities in the world. On October 27, 2022, it was in the number two position ( https://bit.ly/3DjUJw6 ). Â
On October 26, however, the Indian Express reported  how Delhi saw its cleanest day-after-Diwali air since 2015. As per this report, the air quality index in Delhi on Diwali day was 312, while it was 303 the day after. Even Delhi's Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal tweeted on this matter. These two graphs show how pollution has been decreasing over the years due to constant efforts of Delhiites. pic.twitter.com/wFxfB9h78Z — Arvind Kejriwal (@ArvindKejriwal) October 24, 2022
These two graphs show how pollution has been decreasing over the years due to constant efforts of Delhiites. pic.twitter.com/wFxfB9h78Z — Arvind Kejriwal (@ArvindKejriwal) October 24, 2022
Soon, people shared a photo, supposedly shot at Dhaula Kuan in Delhi, showing clear skies.
One such post claimed, "This is the latest scene of South Delhi's Dhaula Kuan Road on the cleanest Diwali day". Many shared  the same photo with the same claim . The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found this photo was old and not taken on Diwali or the day after in 2022. AFWA Probe
Upon reverse-searching the photo, we found that it was used earlier in many news reports. On August 29, the Economic Times used this particular photo in an article. While the report did not contain a description or attribution for the photo, its headline — "Dhaula Kuan-Delhi airport road beautification project to be finished in 3 months: LG" — suggested it was shot at Dhaula Kuan. After that, with the help of keyword searching, we found two more news reports that used the same image. On August 11, these reports were published on "socialnews.xyz"  and "prokerala.com" . "Socialnews" captioned the photo, "New Delhi: Traffic moves slow at Dhaula Kuan area due to Raksha Bandhan festival, in New Delhi on Thursday, Aug 11, 2022." It was credited to photojournalist Wasim Sarvar of the news agency IANS. AFWA has contacted Sarvar regarding how old the photo was and where it was shot. This story will be updated as and when we receive a response. We compared the viral photo with the original one and they are the same. A comparison can be seen below. Therefore, it is clear that this is an old photo and is not taken on the day of Diwali 2022 or the day after. Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Oct 27, 2022 21:21 IST

title: Fact Check: 2021 video of Ramiz Raja lambasting Pak team FALSELY shared as reaction to recent T20 WC defeats
content:
This video of Raja criticising the Pakistani team is from April 23, 2021. Raja has not yet made any official comment following Pakistan's defeat against Zimbabwe in the ongoing T20 World Cup.
After losing to India in a belter of a contest in Melbourne on October 23, Pakistan again faced an embarrassing defeat against Zimbabwe on October 27. Following this, the squad has faced harsh criticism  from former Pakistani cricketers.Â
Amid this, many on social media shared a video  of Pakistani Cricket Board chairman Ramiz Raja criticising his team for their poor performance.Â
In this video, Raja called the players' performance "embarrassing" and "shameful". He further compared Zimbabwe with a "club level" team. Raja also sought answers from those responsible for this. #ZimVsPak #PakistanCricket Ye to julum hai 😀 Ramiz Raza after big blow by Zimbabwe pic.twitter.com/OmHiiM7R6F — Umesh Chandra (@umeshkodopi) October 28, 2022
#ZimVsPak #PakistanCricket Ye to julum hai 😀 Ramiz Raza after big blow by Zimbabwe pic.twitter.com/OmHiiM7R6F — Umesh Chandra (@umeshkodopi) October 28, 2022
People on Facebook and Twitter shared the video with captions like, "Ramiz Raza very upset and angry for lost match Pakistan vs Zimbabwe in World Cup 2022." An archived version of such a post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found that this video is more than a year old and not related to Pakistan's recent defeat against Zimbabwe in the ongoing T20 World Cup. AFWA ProbeÂ
We first searched for news reports to find out if Raja made any comments following Pakistan's defeat against Zimbabwe. We found none. On the contrary, we came across several news reports  quoting former Pakistani players who demanded Raja's resignation after the humiliating defeat in Perth.
Subsequently, we looked at Pakistan's poor show against Zimbabwe prior to this World Cup. A T20 clash between both teams on April 23, 2021, in Harare, Zimbabwe, saw Pakistan reach 99 all-out while chasing 119.Â
When we searched for news reports around the April 2021 timeline, we found a WION report that quoted Ramiz Raja stating, "I'm shocked as to whether I should analyse this or express anger over this. This clearly is a very dark moment in our history."Â
As these words were familiar with the viral video, we searched for the original one and found it on "Ramiz Speaks", the official YouTube channel  of the former Pakistani cricketer. It was uploaded to YouTube on April 23, 2021, making it clear that the video is more than a year old and not related to the ongoing World Cup.Â
Per the ICC website , Ramiz Raja was formally elected as PCB Chairman on September 13, 2021, almost six months after this match.Â
While back-to-back defeats have made the road to the semi-final for Pakistan even more challenging, this video certainly has nothing to do with it. Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Oct 29, 2022 17:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video of man kicking Morbi bridge cable is recent - not years old as some have claimed
content:
This video is not from 2018 or 2021. While we could not find an exact date, it was most likely shot recently. But it does not also show the events leading up to the collapse.
At least 141 people died after a British-era bridge in Gujarat's Morbi collapsed on the evening of October 30. The bridge reopened to the public on October 26 after renovation. While an investigation is still underway, many videos of the bridge flooded social media with a conspiracy theory - that some people deliberately tried to sabotage it.Â
One such video is that of the crowded bridge (with a black arrow pointing at the crowd) where some people can be seen pulling the suspension cables and kicking the safety fence.
However, countering this claim, several people asserted that the viral video is actually a few years old - possibly from either 2018 or 2021, implying it couldn't possibly have anything to do with the bridge's collapse. The counterclaims were backed by two videos of the Morbi Bridge that have been available on the internet at least since 2018 and 2021 respectively. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here .
In these videos as well, people can be seen pulling the suspension cables of the 150-year-old bridge. Many came to this conclusion based on the colours of a group of people's clothes in the different videos.
AFWA found that the viral video is not old and that it was likely shot days ago after the Morbi Bridge was reopened to the public. However, AFWA in any way is NOT suggesting that the bridge could have collapsed due to pulling and kicking at the fence and cables. The collapse is a matter of a detailed probe and beyond the scope of our investigation. AFWA PROBE
Watching the CCTV footage of the Morbi bridge collapse, we noticed that the bridge's fence was taller than the people standing on it. The fence looked approximately 6.5 feet tall. A few other videos of the bridge shot after the renovation also confirmed that the new fence is taller than the height of an average person. In the viral video as well, the fence is taller than the people. Chilling CCTV visuals of Gujarat's Morbi bridge collapse. Will guilty be booked for murder? #5iveLive #MorbiCableBridge | @ShivAroor @JournoAshutosh pic.twitter.com/keQgBcUcx9 — IndiaToday (@IndiaToday) October 31, 2022
Chilling CCTV visuals of Gujarat's Morbi bridge collapse. Will guilty be booked for murder? #5iveLive #MorbiCableBridge | @ShivAroor @JournoAshutosh pic.twitter.com/keQgBcUcx9 — IndiaToday (@IndiaToday) October 31, 2022
However, the Morbi Bridge's fence was shorter before its renovation. Images and videos of the bridge shot before the renovation confirm that the fence was then approximately four feet. The fencing also appears short in the aforementioned 2018 and 2021 videos that are being shared as counterclaims. In the viral video, a boundary wall can be seen on the bank of the river at the end of the bridge. Historical satellite imagery and old videos from the spot show the wall used to be shorter till 2019. It was made taller by the end of 2020. In the viral video, the boundary is taller, suggesting it is not old. Images from live coverage of the accident also show there is a bush on a pillar at the right end of the bridge. In the viral video, too, we spotted a bush of roughly the same size. This bush was also present at the same spot on the pillar in the 2018 and 2021 videos - but was less prominent. advertisement Thus, we conclude that the viral video (with the black arrow) is not from 2018 or 2021. It was most likely shot recently. But it also does not show the events leading up to the collapse. title: Fact Check: Obama DID NOT lose control of crowd, pro-Obama chants replaced with profane anti-Biden slogans
content:
This video is doctored. In the original video, the crowd chanted in support of Barack Obama as he addressed a heckler during his rally.
With about a week left until the midterm elections, which will set the stage for the 2024 presidential elections in the United States, a video of former US President Barack Obama being shouted down by the crowd with profane chants has gone viral online. "But this is what I mean, this is what I mean. We are having a conversation. Hold on, listen, everybody," Obama was seen saying in the video before his voice was muffled by loud chants of "F*** Joe Biden". Sharing this video, one person  wrote on Twitter, "Breaking News. Barack Obama can't control his crowd as they chant FJB. He is really upset and throwing a fit on stage. They say he wanted to stop the filming so people wouldn't share and tweet this clip. FJB." Archives of similar posts can be found here  and here .  AFWA found that this video is doctored. In the original video, the crowd was chanting Obama's name in his support after he was interrupted by a heckler.  AFWA PROBE A keyword search led us to a CNN report about a recent Obama speech being interrupted, featuring an extended version of the viral video. According to this report, on October 29, Obama was interrupted by a heckler as he discussed political civility while rallying to support Democrat Gretchen Whitmer, the Governor of Michigan, in Detroit. In the extended version of the video, Obama can be seen talking about the recent attack  on Paul Pelosi, the 82-year-old husband of US Speaker Nancy Pelosi, and condemning hostility in American politics. A minute and a half into the video, a man from the crowd was heard yelling "Mr. President", interrupting Obama's speech. The heckler could not be heard properly but he continued to speak, bringing the speech to a halt. Following this, Obama confronted the heckler, and this is the part that can be seen in the viral video. However, contrary to the viral video, the crowd present at the rally started chanting Obama's name in his support — not profanities.   We also found another video from the incident tweeted  by Dylan Wells, a Washington Post reporter. In this video as well, the crowd could be heard chanting in support of Obama after he was interrupted by someone from the crowd. "Sir, this is what I'm saying. We've got a process that we set up in our democracy. Right now, I'm talking. You'll have a chance to talk sometime later. You wouldn't do that in a workplace", said Obama addressing the heckler as the heckler's voice was muffled by raucous applause and "Obama, Obama" chants from the crowd. Another video tweeted by journalist Rachel Louise Just showed the interruption, followed by the heckler being escorted out. As former President Barack Obama acknowledges the attack on Paul Pelosi, he is interrupted by a heckler in Detroit, who is then pointed out by the audience and escorted out. pic.twitter.com/Ffax9P0tWW — Rachel Louise Just (@RLJnews) October 29, 2022  Interestingly, videos from the rally suggest that following this incident, Obama was interrupted by yet another heckler during this speech, a woman this time. However, she was similarly escorted out. Thus, it is clear that the widely circulating video of anti-Biden chants during Obama's rally is not only doctored but also misrepresents the actual response of the crowd at Obama's Michigan rally.  (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 3, 2022 11:57 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Imran Khan stutter over questions about human testing for cancer research in his hospital?
content:
This video is digitally altered. When Khan was asked about these allegations made by former Pakistani cricketer Sarfaraz Nawaz, he replied by calling his former teammate is 'stupid'.
A video of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan has been making rounds on social media, where he can be seen mumbling while answering questions asked by journalist Rajat Sharma. Many on Twitter shared this interview clip alongside conspiracy theories. In this video, Sharma questioned Khan about a Jewish pharmaceutical company owned by his former in-laws that wanted to conduct a cancer drug experiment on living humans in his hospital . Sharma further asked Khan if an ample amount of money was spent to make this experiment a success. Khan, in the video, first stammered and responded that he did not want to talk about this. یہودی فارماسیوٹیکل کمپنیز ہیں جو آپ Ú©Û' سابق Brother In Law Ú©ÛŒ کمپنیز ہیں جنہیں کینسر ریسرچ Ú©Û' سلسلے میں Ú©Ú†Ú¾ لوگ چاہیئے تھے جن پر وہ تجربہ کرسکیں۔ اس لیئے یہاں یہ پیسہ خرچ کیا گیا 🤔 رجت شرما Ù†Û' بھی 90 Ú©ÛŒ دہائی میں اس سازش Ú©Ùˆ بھانپ لیا تھا جو ڈاکٹر اسرار اور حکیم سعید بتا کر گئے pic.twitter.com/WGkS88VZzg — Junaid Raza Zaidi (@junaidraza01) November 1, 2022 Several people shared this video with Urdu captions that accused Khan of a conspiracy in his hospitals in the 90s. An archived version can be seen here . AFWA investigation found that the video was digitally altered to give it a false spin. AFWA Probe With the help of a search with some keywords, we came across the original video uploaded to the YouTube channel of India TV four years ago. Titled "Imran Khan in Aap Ki Adalat", this 39-minute-long video was part of a court-room themed interview hosted by journalist Rajat Sharma. Around the 16-minute mark, Sharma is heard referring to an allegation made by Sarfaraz Nawaz, a former Pakistani cricketer and teammate of Khan, before asking the question that has gone viral. Replying to this, Khan promptly said, "As I have mentioned earlier, he (Sarfaraz Nawaz) has sunk below the beast's level. There is a saying in English — 'gone case'. So, there is no point talking because he is a stupid man. Apart from being stupid, he is a man with ill intentions," making it clear that his response was something else compared to the viral video. In this interview, Khan also responded to some other allegations raised by his former dressing room companion Javed Miandad. While his counter was more polite towards Miandad, Khan went all guns blazing against Nawaz and compared him to a "thief". Therefore, it is safe to conclude that the video of Imran Khan was shared with clipped answers to give it a misleading spin. Also Read: Fact Check: Obama DID NOT lose control of crowd, pro-Obama chants replaced with profane anti-Biden slogans Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 3, 2022 16:45 IST

title: Fact Check: Ashok Gehlot did not criticise Congress rule in Rajasthan, clipped video shared out of context
content:
This video was clipped out of context. Gehlot was criticising the Centre and said people across India, including Rajasthan, are fed up because of violence, inflation, and unemployment.
Rajasthan, one of the few Congress-ruled states in India, has been plagued with controversies for some time now. Between communal tensions and a power struggle in the Congress leadership, the state has constantly in the spotlight. Now, a video of Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot has been widely shared on social media.
Those sharing the video  claimed that the veteran Congress leader was admitting that all was not well in the Congress-ruled state. The short Gehlot clip was also tweeted  by the Bharatiya Janata Party's Laxmikant Bhardwaj, who wrote, "The Chief Minister of Rajasthan is saying that the people of Rajasthan are fed up… with whom?"
AFWA found that this video was clipped out of context. In the original video, Gehlot said that across India, including Rajasthan, people were fed up with the Central government.Â
A reverse search of the viral video's frames led us to a longer version of the video uploaded to Twitter on November 2. In this longer version, a reporter asked Gehlot for his reaction to Sachin Pilot's recent statement. गुटबाजी और सियासी बयानबाजी से त्रस्त राजस्थान की जनता की अब एक ही पुकार राजस्थान में भी केजरीवाल । #SachinPilot #Congress #kejriwal @AamAadmiParty @ArvindKejriwal pic.twitter.com/gQgLaLEpeO — Saurabh Choudhary (@Saurabh_aap007) November 2, 2022 On November 1, Prime Minister Narendra Modi heaped praise on Gehlot calling him one of the senior-most chief ministers and an experienced politician. The PM was sharing a dais with Gehlot at a government function in Banswara, Rajasthan.Â
गुटबाजी और सियासी बयानबाजी से त्रस्त राजस्थान की जनता की अब एक ही पुकार राजस्थान में भी केजरीवाल । #SachinPilot #Congress #kejriwal @AamAadmiParty @ArvindKejriwal pic.twitter.com/gQgLaLEpeO — Saurabh Choudhary (@Saurabh_aap007) November 2, 2022
On November 1, Prime Minister Narendra Modi heaped praise on Gehlot calling him one of the senior-most chief ministers and an experienced politician. The PM was sharing a dais with Gehlot at a government function in Banswara, Rajasthan.Â
However, this remark did not go well with everyone in the Congress party. Sachin Pilot called PM Modi's praise of Gehlot an "interesting development" that needed to be taken seriously by the party. The former deputy CM of Rajasthan also said Ghulam Nabi Azad, who recently left Congress, had also received similar praise from the PM.Â
Responding to the reporter's question in the video, Gehlot said, "Such statements should not be made. Our General Secretary Venugopal had asked party members not to comment on this. Right now, we should have only one mission in front of us. People are fed up in Rajasthan and all over the country. There is tension, violence, inflation, and unemployment." Gehlot also spoke about the Bharat Jodo Yatra, the schemes Congress had implemented in Rajasthan, and how his state managed the Covid-19 pandemic.Â
From this video, it is evident that the viral video was clipped and shared out of context. ANI also tweeted a screenshot from the viral video, reporting that this was Gehlot's reaction to Pilot's statement. Alwar, Rajasthan | They should not make such remarks. KC Venugopal has asked everybody in the party to not make any such remarks. We want that everybody should follow discipline: Rajasthan CM Ashok Gehlot on Sachin Pilot's remarks https://t.co/ptGGHUY7M3 pic.twitter.com/ELTQLrNG3K — ANI (@ANI) November 2, 2022
Alwar, Rajasthan | They should not make such remarks. KC Venugopal has asked everybody in the party to not make any such remarks. We want that everybody should follow discipline: Rajasthan CM Ashok Gehlot on Sachin Pilot's remarks https://t.co/ptGGHUY7M3 pic.twitter.com/ELTQLrNG3K — ANI (@ANI) November 2, 2022
We also found multiple media reports  that reported on Gehlot's reaction. A longer version of the viral clip was also shared by India Today  and News 18 Rajasthan  in their video reports.Â
It is hence clear that a video of Gehlot was clipped and shared out of context to make it look like he was criticising the Congress party. Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Nov 3, 2022 23:33 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of Kerala woman who joined ISIS is clipped from film teaser for 'The Kerala Story'
content:
This video is from the teaser of an upcoming movie titled "The Kerala Story" by Vipul Amrutlal Shah.
A monologue video of a woman donning a burqa has been widely shared on social media by many people who claimed that she was a Hindu woman who ended up in jail in Afghanistan after being radicalised by ISIS. In the video , the woman can be heard saying, "My name was Shalini Unnikrishnan. I wanted to be a nurse to serve humanity. Today I'm Fatima Ba. An ISIS terrorist in Afghanistan jail. I'm not alone. Like me, 32,000 women have already been converted and buried in the deserts of Syria and Yemen." She alleged  that this was openly happening in Kerala, pleading to people to put an end to this. The archived versions of similar posts (  ) can be seen here  and here .  AFWA found that the video was from the teaser of an upcoming movie titled "The Kerala Story".  AFWA probe At the end of the viral video, one can see "The Kerala Story" written on a black background. Several people on social media had shared the same video with the hashtag #TheKeralaStory. Many on Twitter  also claimed the clip is from an upcoming movie. We also found multiple media reports about the viral video. Per an India Today report published on November 4, the woman in the video is actor Adah Sharma. The report also says the scene was from a teaser of her upcoming movie "The Kerala Story", directed by Sudipto Sen. According to reports, the movie is about women from Kerala who were radicalised to join ISIS. A longer version of the viral video was tweeted by Sharma on November 3. Heart breaking and gut wrenching stories of 32000 females in Kerala! #ComingSoon #VipulAmrutlalShah @sudiptoSENtlm @adah_sharma @Aashin_A_Shah #SunshinePictures #TheKeralaStory #UpcomingMovie #TrueStory #AdahSharma pic.twitter.com/M6oROuGGSu — Adah Sharma (@adah_sharma) November 3, 2022 This longer version video says the movie was directed by Sudipto Sen and produced by Vipul Amrutlal Shah under the banner of Sunshine Pictures. A "Coming Soon" text also appears at the end of the video. The teaser was also uploaded to the YouTube channel Sunshine Pictures on November 3. The caption to the video reads, "Heartbreaking and gut-wrenching stories of 32,000 females in Kerala! Coming Soon!" Whether 32,000 women from Kerala were trafficked by the terrorist outfit, a claim that has been debated on social media, is not the focus of this investigation. It should also be noted that of the many people sharing the video, only a handful seemed to have confused the film teaser for a real incident. title: Fact Check: Old photo of dead man is NOT from rally where Imran Khan was shot
content:
This is an old photo that was shared by many in 2021, who claimed it was from Afghanistan.
In an assassination attempt, former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan was shot during a rally last Thursday at Wazirabad's Allahwala Chowk. Reportedly, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf chief was hit by four bullets, and is now in a stable condition. One of his supporters was killed and many were injured during this attack.
Following this, Pakistan saw PTI supporters  protesting both online and offline. Amid this, many on social media shared  a heartbreaking photo of a boy sitting beside a body. While sharing this photo, people claimed that the person in this image lost his life during the attack. The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
Many shared  the same photo with the same claim  on Facebook as well.Â
AFWA's investigation found the photo is not from Khan's recent rally.  This image has been on the internet for more than a year at least.
Upon reverse-searching the photo, we found a social media post  using the same photo on July 30, 2021. The image was shared with a caption: "Painful image Thousands of #Afghan kids have experienced this in their lifetime! Lost in the world of hopelessness and crying over the dead body of your father. If you don't see our suffering and pain and what we have gone through in the last 4 decades, I doubt your humanity! Stop supporting terrorism in my country." On July 29, 2021, another person posted this imag e with the caption: "Tears of an Afghan child over the dead body of his father killed in Helmand province. Where are the human rights and children's rights organizations Or they are silent because Afghan lives don't matter to them." IS THIS PHOTO FROM AFGHANISTAN'S HELMAND PROVINCE? We found two more similar posts on Twitter. A journalist named Fehim TaÅŸtekin shared  this image on July 30, 2021, entitled "Baba ve oÄŸul! Helmand-Afghanistan." In that post, he tagged Bilal Sarwary, a journalist from BBC. Sarwary also posted this  image claiming, "As children, we're taught to honour our parents and as parents to protect our children - but this violence makes mourners out of us all. #AFGHANISTAN #Helmand." AFWA reached out to Sarwary to confirm how old the photo was and where it was shot. The story will be updated as and when we receive a response. Therefore, it is clear that this is an old photo that was falsely shared with the claim that it was from the recent attack on Khan's rally in Pakistan. title: Fact Check: 'Golden Dragon' from China becomes 'Deepotsavam' from Hyderabad and Kerala
content:
This video shows 'Golden Dragon', a fleet of boats with golden lights, cruising on the Yulong river in south China's Guangxi, held as part of China Tourism Day celebrations.
A video making the rounds on social media shows a glamorously lit fleet of boats cruising on a river in a zigzag motion. The text along the video reads, "Sri Mahankaleshwara Devalayam, Miralam Mandi," a temple located in Hyderabad. The same video, however, was also shared with the claim that it is from Kerala. Bhawana Somaaya, a film critic and author, tweeted the video , writing, "Deepotsavam in Kerala. 240 boats sailing in the river with lamps. Diwali celebrations continue." Archives of similar posts can be found here and here . AFWA found that this video is neither from Hyderabad nor from Kerala. In fact, it is not even from India, but from China. AFWA Probe A reverse search of the video's frames on Yandex led us to an August 29 tweet . Alongside the viral video, a Turkish caption roughly translates to, "A 'golden dragon' consisting of 88 bamboo rafts was spotted sailing on the Yulong River in southern China. Chinese dragons traditionally symbolize mercy and the power of glory and represent the power to rule water, rain, storms, and floods." 88 bambu saldan oluÅŸan bir ''altın ejderha'', Çin'in güneyinde yer alan Yulong Nehri'nde seyir halindeyken görüntülendi. Çin ejderhaları geleneksel olarak; merhameti ve ihtiÅŸamın kudretini sembolize edip suyu, yağışı, fırtına ve seli yönetme gücünü temsil eder pic.twitter.com/yq3IZt0f0u — Dr Şükran 💎 (@SukranDr) August 29, 2022 Using this clue, with a keyword search, we landed on the government website of Guangxi China . The website had a news article featuring images of similarly lit boats. Guangxi is an autonomous region in southern China, bordering Vietnam.   According to it, on May 19, eighty bamboo rafts with golden lights formed a 70-meter-long dragon-like structure and wandered along the Yulong river, a small tributary of the larger Li River in China's Guangxi. The event was held as part of the 12th China Tourism Day, a commemorative day that aims to improve Yulong River's reputation and create new night tourism models.  We also found similar videos of this annual event shared by the Daily Mail  and Chinese state-controlled media outlets like CGTN , China Plus Culture , and Xi's Moments  this year on Facebook. This rules out the possibility of the video being from India. Talking about the possibility of a similar event in Hyderabad, on November 6, Union Minister For Culture, Tourism, And Development Of North Eastern Region, G Kishan Reddy, tweeted  a video showing glimpses of the "Koti Deepotsavam" held in Hyderabad. This event reportedly started  on October 31 and will continue till November 14. In this event, while lamps were lit by devotees at the NTR Stadium along with some temples of Hyderabad, we could not find any footage of this incident showing a fleet of boats with lamps similar to that in the viral video.   In Kerala, however, an annual ritual  does take place at Sabarimala temple where a lamp is lit in the river. This ceremony takes place in connection with Mandal Puja, which occurs in January, during which a lamp is lit in the Pamba River and an offering is made to it. However, videos from this incident also do not feature a dragon-like structure. Thus, it is clear that the video of the "Golden Dragon" from China is being shared with misleading claims. title: Fact Check: Picture of Mazar photoshopped to a highway to push FALSE 'Land Jihad' claim
content:

The hashtag "Stop Land Jihad" has been trending on Twitter for the past few days. Several Twitter accounts have shared photos of public property and land being encroached upon. title: Fact Check: Video of earthquake hitting busy junction in Nepal is from 2015, NOT recent
content:
This video from Kathmandu's Tripureshwor Chowk shows the deadly April 2015 earthquake in Nepal that killed nearly 9,000 people.
Nepal was struck by a 6.3 magnitude earthquake in the wee hours of November 9. Tremors were also felt across North India, including Delhi, Gurugram, Ghaziabad, and Lucknow.Â
Following this, CCTV footage of a busy junction being rocked by an earthquake has been shared by some on social media. It shows a structure in the middle of the junction collapsing because of the tremors, bringing traffic to a halt. Those sharing it claimed it was from the recent earthquake in Nepal.Â
AFWA found that the video is from the 2015 Nepal earthquake, which killed nearly 9,000 people and injured many more. AFWA probe
A reverse search of the viral video screenshots led us to multiple media reports  and YouTube channels which had shared either the same video or screen grabs from it in 2015. According to an India Today report from the time , that used a screenshot from the same video, the footage was from a quake that struck Nepal on the afternoon of April 25, 2015.Â
The 7.8 magnitude quake killed nearly 9,000 people and thousands were injured. It also left a trail of destruction, with 600,000 structures destroyed in Kathmandu and other nearby areas. The earthquake was felt in parts of northern India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Tibet. The same video was also uploaded to the YouTube channel WildFilmsIndia. Per the channel, it was shot at Tripureshwor Chowk in Nepal's Kathmandu. The footage was also used in a documentary film on the 2015 Nepal earthquake.Â
The same video was also uploaded to the YouTube channel WildFilmsIndia. Per the channel, it was shot at Tripureshwor Chowk in Nepal's Kathmandu. The footage was also used in a documentary film on the 2015 Nepal earthquake.Â
A comparison of the viral video with Google Street View of Tripureshwor Chowk  confirmed that the video is indeed from the same roundabout. As per Google Maps and media reports from Nepal , the statue seen under the destroyed structure was that of the late king Tribhuvan Shah. Â
Moreover, on November 9 the earthquake occurred at 2:12 am Nepal time. However, the viral video is clearly from the daytime. Also, the epicentre of the recent earthquake was the Doti district which is about 430 km west of the capital, Kathmandu.
It is hence clear that the video in circulation is more than seven years old and not related to the earthquake which hit Nepal on November 9. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 9, 2022 21:21 IST

title: Fact Check: How a 2017 survey was doctored to project victory for Congress in 2022 Himachal elections
content:
This viral video was doctored. The original video is from October 2017 and predicted 39-45 seats for the BJP and 22-28 seats for the Congress in the assembly elections that year.
In less than 24 hours, the people of Himachal Pradesh will cast their votes for the assembly elections. The incumbent Bhartiya Janta Party, Congress, and the new entrant Aam Aadmi Party have left no stone unturned during their campaigns in the state.Â
Meanwhile, a video of an opinion poll from ABP News has been shared by many social media users - including Congress leader Alka Lamba. The clip purportedly shows an opinion poll from Himachal Pradesh, predicting a clear majority for the Congress party with 39-45 seats in its kitty. On the other hand, the BJP's projected seat share can be seen falling between 22-28 seats.Â
Lamba shared this 22-second-long video on November 10, expressing her gratitude to the people of the state. An archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â
AFWA's investigation found the viral videos were edited. Originally from 2017, it predicted a majority for the BJP.Â
We first searched for what exactly the ABP News opinion poll predicted for the 2022 Himachal Pradesh assembly polls. We found that ABP News and C-Voter hinted at a hung assembly with both BJP and Congress winning an equal share. The Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly has a total of 68 seats. A party needs to cross the 35-seat mark to form a government in the state. The survey predicted the BJP's seat share between 31-39 and 29-37 for Congress. Notably, the report, based on this opinion poll, was published by the ABP group on November 9, a day before Lamba tweeted this video. TRUTH BEHIND THE VIRAL VIDEO
The Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly has a total of 68 seats. A party needs to cross the 35-seat mark to form a government in the state. The survey predicted the BJP's seat share between 31-39 and 29-37 for Congress. Notably, the report, based on this opinion poll, was published by the ABP group on November 9, a day before Lamba tweeted this video. TRUTH BEHIND THE VIRAL VIDEO
We took some screengrabs from the viral video and ran a reverse search on Google. This led us to a clip uploaded to ABP Live's YouTube channel on October 31, 2017. When we compared the frames of the viral video with the original, it became clear that a five-year-old clip was shared as a recent one.Â
Moreover, the predicted figures shown in the viral video for the Congress party were not the same. The original video projected 39-45 seats for the BJP and 22-28 seats for the Congress, making it evident that the viral video was doctored.
Therefore, it is safe to conclude that a five-year-old opinion poll video was doctored to spread lies ahead of the Himachal Pradesh assembly elections.Â

title: Fact Check: This is NOT Arunachal's 'bamboo airport', viral video is from new Bengaluru airport terminal
content:

Under one of the viral posts, people pointed out that the visuals were from the Bengaluru airport.
