title: Fact Check: Videos of young men harassing women at two Tamil Nadu colleges FALSELY given communal twist
content:
This video shows two different incidents in Tamil Nadu, both of which had no communal angle to them. Police constables from the two areas where the incidents took place have confirmed this to AFWA.
A video of young men rashly riding bikes and hooting as they allegedly barge through the gates of a women's college has been doing the rounds on social media. The video captured utter chaos as young women on the road ran away from the men, who could be seen thrashing an old man on the road later in the video. Those sharing the video claimed that it showed Muslim men harassing Hindu women in Tamil Nadu. Tweeting the video , a person wrote, "No, these are not behind the scenes (BTS) of a Bollywood movie where hero ends up saving the girls. This is happening at a women's college in Tamil Nadu, where Muslim boys are eve-teasing Hindu girls. This is what a state without law and order and Muslim appeasement looks like." Another Twitter user  made a similar claim about the incident, tagging K. Annamalai, the president of the Bharatiya Janata Party in Tamil Nadu, requesting him to help the women. Archives of similar posts can be found here , here , and here . AFWA found that this video shows two different incidents in Tamil Nadu, both of which had no communal angle to them. Police constables from both areas have confirmed this. The viral video also used footage from two different incidents — one in which bikers trespassed into a women's college, and the other where men beat up a man who had come to pick his daughter up from the college. We will cover them one by one. Trespassing into girls' college We first ran a reverse search of the first part of the viral video. This led us to a news report published by the Times of India on November 5, featuring a keyframe from the viral video. According to the report, on October 30, nine men were arrested by the Madurai city police who forcibly entered the Lady Doak College in Madurai's Tallakulam on Thevar Jayanthi. The young bikers reportedly harassed the students as well as assaulted a college security guard. Nowhere in this report could we find the mention of the young men being Muslim. We found a video news report about this incident on Thanthi TV , a Tamil News Channel. The video showed boys gesticulating wildly as they barged through the gates on two-wheelers, hooting and screaming — the visuals as seen at the beginning of the viral video. This confirms that the first part of the video indeed shows the Lady Doak College incident. The Deputy Commissioner of Police for Madurai North told ANI on November 5 that ten people had been arrested following the incident, out of whom five were college students. Apart from that, police also seized four two-wheelers. Here as well, there was no mention of the men's religion. Tamil Nadu | An incident of harassment of girls by some men on bike was reported at Lady Dok College, Madurai on Oct 30 on Jayanti of Muthuramalinga Thevar. Case filed against 11 people. 10 people arrested,4 two-wheelers seized. 5 arrested are colleges students:DCP, Madurai North pic.twitter.com/UwwTGq19kR — ANI (@ANI) November 5, 2022 The thrashing of a student's father The latter part of the viral video shows an old man being beaten up by a group of men. A reverse search of a keyframe from this part led us to a tweet by ANI that contained the same clip. According to it, on November 2, a group of young men assaulted a parent who had come to pick up his daughter from Sri Meenakshi Government Arts College in Madurai's Sellur. #WATCH | TN:Some youths assaulted a parent who'd come to pick up his daughter from Sri Meenakshi Govt Arts College for Women in Madurai on Nov 2 6 people arrested so far; case filed u/s 341,308,506(ii) &TN Prohibition of Harassment of Woman Act:Madurai CP (Note:Abusive language) pic.twitter.com/SNspntoPYN — ANI (@ANI) November 5, 2022  The ANI news report on this incident stated that six out of the seven people involved were arrested for assaulting a 50-year-old man. The man had asked the boys to pass quietly as a funeral procession was passing by. No communal angle was mentioned in this case as well.  As per the Commissioner of Police T. Senthil Kumar , the parents of the young men involved in both incidents would be counselled and patrolling in the surrounding areas would also be strengthened.  AFWA contacted India Today's Madurai stringer Marisami, who gave us the press releases of both incidents that mentioned the names of the culprits involved and those arrested in these cases. The press release for the Lady Doak College incident can be found here , and that for the Meenakshi College incident can be found here . This information was also shared on the Facebook page of the Madurai City Police, and can be found here  and here .  Moreover, AFWA reached out to police constables in Sellur and Tallakulam. Both confirmed there was no communal angle in the two incidents and all those arrested for creating a ruckus in the colleges were non-Muslims.  Thus, it is clear that two separate incidents were conflated and falsely shared with a communal spin on social media. (Written by Sanjana Saxena, with inputs from Marisami) Published By: Komal Sharma Published On: Nov 11, 2022 00:14 IST

title: Fact Check: PM Modi DID NOT mock people who suffered after demonetisation, doctored video viral
content:
The viral video is edited from Modi's 2016 speech in Japan. In the unedited original video, it is clear that PM Modi did not make fun of the people who suffered after demonetisation.
On the evening of November 8, 2016, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the demonetisation drive, making the legal tenders for Rs. 500 and Rs 1,000 null and void. What followed was a nationwide cash crunch, long queues at banks and ATMs for weeks, and economic distress for many, many people (especially vulnerable social classes) across India. Even deaths.
On the sixth anniversary of demonetisation, many on social media shared a video of Modi , alleging that the PM took sadistic pleasure in the people's suffering. The video showed Modi speaking to an audience. He spoke about demonetisation. And then he said, "Wedding at your home, and no money." परपीड़ा सुख का क्रूरतम उदाहरण "हे हे हे हे...बेटी की शादी है, पैसे नहीं हैं..." यह उस देश में हुआ जहां के गांव-जवांर में किसी की बेटी की शादी हो तो गरीब से गरीब आदमी भी अपनी पहुंच भर योगदान देता है। इस क्रूर सुख के अलावा नोटबंदी का क्या हासिल रहा? #DemonetisationDisaster pic.twitter.com/AN3sTNsq6Z — Krishna Kant (@kkjourno) November 8, 2022
परपीड़ा सुख का क्रूरतम उदाहरण "हे हे हे हे...बेटी की शादी है, पैसे नहीं हैं..." यह उस देश में हुआ जहां के गांव-जवांर में किसी की बेटी की शादी हो तो गरीब से गरीब आदमी भी अपनी पहुंच भर योगदान देता है। इस क्रूर सुख के अलावा नोटबंदी का क्या हासिल रहा? #DemonetisationDisaster pic.twitter.com/AN3sTNsq6Z — Krishna Kant (@kkjourno) November 8, 2022
While sharing the 39-second-long video , one person on Twitter wrote: "The cruellest example of sadistic pleasure. When someone is suffering, he is laughing... " The archived version of this post is here .
AFWA's investigation found that the viral video was edited. It joined two parts of the PM's original speech, changing its context and meaning.Â
In the viral video, a news clip from ABP, we noticed the words, "PM Narendra Modi in Japan LIVE," written in Hindi. Subsequent searches with relevant keywords led us to news reports about his visit to Japan following the demonetisation announcement. Reportedly, On November 12, 2016, Modi visited Japan for the annual Summit meeting . There he met the Indian community and addressed a gathering in Kobe . We also found the longer version of the same clip, uploaded to the ABP News YouTube channel . The 21-minute-long video was titled, "FULL SPEECH: Similar scheme could be launched after December 30: PM Modi warns black money holders". We found the first part of the viral video between the 7.35-minute and 8-minute marks in the original one. The second part of the viral video was edited. In the unedited version, PM said in Hindi, "Someone has no money for his daughter's marriage, someone has no money for his mother's treatment. But despite having too many problems people have welcomed the move (demonetisation). I salute them. For the betterment of the country, they are coming forward just like Japan did in 2011." This part was between 8.25 minutes and 9.37 minutes in the video. The same video was uploaded on PMO's official Youtube channel  on 12 November 2016, captioned, "PM Narendra Modi's Speech: interaction with Indian Community in Japan". advertisement On November 13, 2016, India Today  reported on this. The piece was titled "PM Modi in Japan: I salute the people of India for supporting demonetisation despite inconvenience." Thus, we concluded that the viral video was from Modi's 2016 speech in Japan. From the unedited or original video, it is clear that PM Modi did not make fun of people who suffered following demonetisation. Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Nov 11, 2022 00:30 IST

title: Fact Check: These images DO NOT show Chelsea star Didier Drogba converting to Islam
content:
Didier Drogba himself has clarified that he has not converted to Islam. It was a prayer where he took part with his Muslim brothers in his native village.
A post has recently gone viral on social media that shows former Chelsea footballer Didier Drogba making a hand gesture that looks similar to Islamic prayer. The set of photos being shared  shows Drogba seated with another man who is also doing the same. While sharing these photos, several Facebook pages and people claimed that Drogba converted from Christianity to Islam.Â
"ALLLAHU AKBAR. Former Ivorian star Didier Drogba converts to Islam. Oh ALLAH make him steadfast on Islam," read one such post alongside the photos.
AFWA's investigation found that such posts are misleading and that Drogba himself has denied these claims. AFWA Probe
With the help of a few searches, we found a report on a Ghana-based website  that featured Drogba's reactions after such posts went viral. Per this report, Drogba denied reports of him converting to Islam and cleared the air by stating that it was just a prayer for his Muslim brothers in his village.Â
We also found a tweet posted by Drogba himself, where he categorically mentioned that he has not changed his religion. This story is going viral 😅 but I haven't changed religion. This was just me paying respect to my Muslim brothers i was visiting in my village. A moment of togetherness. Much love and blessings to all 🙏🏾
— Didier Drogba (@didierdrogba) November 7, 2022 "This story is going viral but I haven't changed religion. This was just me paying respect to my Muslim brothers I was visiting in my village. A moment of togetherness. Much love and blessings to all," Drogba wrote while making his religious beliefs clear. Therefore, it is clear that such claims are nothing but baseless rumours. Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Nov 11, 2022 17:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Kohli's post-match presser FALSELY shared as retirement announcement
content:
The video is not related to T20 World Cup 2022. It is a post-match press conference from the Asia Cup 2022 held in September.
India's defeat against England in the T20 World Cup 2022's second semi-final on November 10 has stung fans across the country. Both online and offline, fans and experts lambasted the Indian squad for its poor performance that brought India's World Cup campaign to a startling halt.
Amid this, many on social media shared a video of a press conference and claimed that after losing to England in semi-finals, Virat Kohli announced his retirement from cricket. Many shared the video  the video with Hindi captions like, "Virat Kohli announces retirement from cricket after semi-final loss."
AFWA's investigation, however, found this misleading. The video has no link with ICC T20 World Cup 2022 — it was a post-match press conference held during the Asia Cup 2022. AFWA PROBE Â
Upon reverse-searching a keyframe of the video, we found the same clip on ESPNcricinfo  uploaded on September 4, 2022. The same video was shared by Gulf News on its YouTube, titled "Asia Cup 2022: Virat Kohli post-match press conference".
During the conference, Kohli said he did not think about answering his critics when he returned to competitive action at Asia Cup 2022, saying he was focused on working hard and giving his "120 per cent" towards the team's cause. He said he was absolutely fine with people having opinions about his game but that doesn't, in any way, affect his happiness. Kohli said, "Never really paid attention to these things (answering the critics). I have played for 14 years and it doesn't happen by chance. My job is to work hard on my game, something that I am keen to do, keen to improve for my team and that's something that I am going to continue to do so." After Team India's poor performance in T20 World Cup 2022, there is speculation that many senior players like Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Ravichandran Ashwin, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Shami may say goodbye to the shortest form of the game.  However, India's head coach Rahul Dravid said , "It's too early to talk about it, just after a semi-final game... These guys have been terrific performers for us. We've got a couple of years to reflect on it. These are some really quality players here. Not the right time to talk about or think about this stuff now. We'll have enough time, enough matches as we go on ahead and try to prepare for the next World Cup." Therefore, it is clear that the video being shared is not related to the T20 World Cup 2022. It is a post-match press conference from the Asia Cup 2022. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Nov 11, 2022 19:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Did PM Modi demand T20 World Cup Ind vs Eng rematch? Viral claim absolutely FALSE
content:
This is absolutely false. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has not reacted to India's loss in the semi-final.
India's unfortunate loss against England in the 2022 Men's T20 World Cup semi-final has left cricket experts and fans performing a postmortem on the Indian squad's performance . I don't mind India losing: victory & defeat are part of sports. But I do mind India not showing up today. #T20WorldCup — Shashi Tharoor (@ShashiTharoor) November 10, 2022
I don't mind India losing: victory & defeat are part of sports. But I do mind India not showing up today. #T20WorldCup — Shashi Tharoor (@ShashiTharoor) November 10, 2022
Amid this, a video is being widely shared on social media with Hindi captions like, "England has won the semi-final by foul play. So, Ind vs Eng semi-final match will be played again and Prime Minister Narendra Modi has made this demand to ICC. Rohit is happy."
AFWA's investigation found it was absolutely false. PM Modi has not said anything about Team India's defeat. AFWA Probe
This 3.33-minute-long video claimed in Hindi, "In the second semi-final, Indian Team lost to England by ten wickets. Indian batsmen like Virat Kohli and Hardik Pandya played well and India finished his innings at 168/6 after 20 overs. Indian bowlers, however, failed to take wickets. England made 170 runs without losing any wickets, Jos Buttler scored 80, and Alex Hales 86."Â
It added, "But England's performance surprised everybody. How could they do this? The umpires' wrong decision made England win this match. After this, PM Narendra Modi made a big demand to the ICC. Modi said if England won the match by foul play, then I should approach ICC to organise an England vs India second semi-final again."
We did not find such posts on PM Modi's social media, be it Twitter or Facebook . In fact, after Team India's win against Pakistan in the 2022 Men's T20 World Cup, Modi congratulated Indian cricketers, specifically Virat Kohli. We found news reports about this on news websites like Hindustan Times and NDTV , among many others . The India team bags a well fought victory! Congratulations for an outstanding performance today. A special mention to @imVkohli for a spectacular innings in which he demonstrated remarkable tenacity. Best wishes for the games ahead.
— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) October 23, 2022
The India team bags a well fought victory! Congratulations for an outstanding performance today. A special mention to @imVkohli for a spectacular innings in which he demonstrated remarkable tenacity. Best wishes for the games ahead.
— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) October 23, 2022
We also found no news reports about PM Modi's reaction to the semi-final loss. To further verify this, AFWA spoke to sports journalist Subhapam Saha, who said that nothing of this sort had happened.Â
Therefore, it is clear that the claim made by the viral video is absolutely false. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has not called for a rematch of the 2022 Men's T20 World Cup semi-final. Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Nov 12, 2022 18:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Six-year-old CCTV footage from Taksim Square falsely shared as Nov 13 Istanbul blast
content:
This video shows a March 2016 explosion in Istanbul. While both explosions occurred around the same area — Taksim Square — the one in the viral video is six years old.
At least six people were killed and 81 wounded in an explosion in the Taksim Square area of Istanbul, Turkey, on November 13. Reportedly, one person has been arrested  and 21 have been detained in relation to a blast. The Turkish government has blamed Kurdish militants for the incident. Following this, CCTV footage of an explosion has gone viral  on social media, with many  claiming  it showed the deadly blast in question. One Facebook user shared the video with the caption, "Bomb blast footage at Taksim Square Istanbul this evening." ALSO READ | Fact Check: Did PM Modi demand T20 World Cup Ind vs Eng rematch? Viral claim absolutely FALSE   AFWA found that the viral footage is not recent at all. It shows an explosion that occurred in Turkey in 2016.  AFWA RROBE One can see "19/03/2016" written towards the end of the viral video. This hinted at the fact that this video may be from 2016. On reverse searching the keyframes of the video, we found it in a March 2016 report published in the Turkish news website "Milliyet". Upon comparing the viral video with the one in the report, one can easily see their similarities. According to this report, the footage shows a suicide bomber who had caused an explosion in the Taksim Square area of Istanbul on March 19, 2016. Other Turkish news portals like "Diken" , "Cumhuriyet"  and "Haberturk"  had also carried grabs from this video in their reports about the incident. At least four people died and 36 were injured in this incident, as per the BBC .  Thus, it is clear that while the video shows an explosion at Taksim Square in Istanbul — the same area where the recent blast occurred — it is more than six years old. Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Nov 14, 2022 15:02 IST

title: Fact Check: This woman DID NOT hold a 'Go Back Modi' placard in Bali during G20, viral photo is morphed
content:
This photo is morphed. The original, likely from the US, was shared online months ahead of the summit. The placard originally appealed to US citizens to vote for Democrats.
The two-day G20 summit in Bali, Indonesia, concluded with the intergovernmental organisation's presidency being handed over to India on November 16. Amid all this, a photo of a woman  holding a placard reading, "Go Back Modi. Again. Go Back Modi," was shared by many on Twitter. Those sharing the photo claimed that this photo was from Bali, shot during the summit.
Some said  the photo was shot on November 15. One person  wrote sarcastically, "This is how red-suited Saheb was welcomed." Many also criticised the Indian media  for not including this opposition to PM Modi as part of its G20 coverage. The archives of such posts can be found here , here , here  and here. Â
AFWA found that this photo is morphed. In the original photo, the placard appealed to vote Republican candidates out in the recently-concluded US midterm elections. AFWA PROBE
A reverse search of the image led us to a tweet  from July 1, featuring the same woman holding a blue placard. The tweet read, "Want to save American democracy? Read this sign and comply! #ElectDemocrats2022 up and down every ballot! ⁦@CasaDemocrats." Want to save American democracy? Read this sign and comply! #ElectDemocrats2022 up and down every ballot! ⁦ @CasaDemocrats ⁩ pic.twitter.com/pFm6PbF94D — Ralph Atchue (@Atchue4AZDems) July 1, 2022 Both photos appeared to be the same in every respect aside from the contents of the placard. The placard's text in the older photo read, "Democrats and Independents must unite to vote out Republicans. Vote Blue this November. Paid for by concerned citizen." This indicated three things: One, the Bali photo was not from Bali at all — most likely it was shot somewhere in the US. Two, it was taken months before the G20 Summit. And three, the contents of the placard were digitally altered. A comparison of the viral image with the one found in the tweet can be found below. We also found more tweets  and posts  on Imgur, an American image-sharing website, containing the original photo.  Further searches led us to a tweet  by journalist Wajahat Ali, who also shared the original photo on July 1, writing, "This lady has been holding this sign at the middle of the intersection, stone cold, not a word uttered. I still think the country is underestimating the anger of women and Gen Z. They won't take this sitting down. They won't go back."  This lady has been holding this sign at the middle of the intersection, stone cold, not a word uttered. I still think the country is underestimating the anger of women and Gen Z. They won't take this sitting down. They won't go back. pic.twitter.com/kfUgK6Y4hS — Wajahat Ali (@WajahatAli) June 30, 2022 AFWA has reached out to Ali for more information regarding the photo and the woman featured in it. This story will be updated as and when he responds. Thus, while we could not find where exactly this photograph was shot, it is clear that the photo of the woman holding the "Go Back Modi" placard is morphed and not from Indonesia. (Written by Sanjana Saxena)  Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Nov 17, 2022 18:33 IST

title: Fact Check: Modi was not ignored at this G20 meet - Here's why he is missing from pic of world leaders
content:
The emergency meeting was convened by NATO and G7 members following a missile strike in Poland. India is part of neither organisation.
The just-concluded G20 Summit in Bali, Indonesia, was keenly observed in India. The two-day summit saw Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping exchange courtesies — a big deal considering the two leaders have not met for bilateral discussions since 2020. Also, on November 16, Modi was handed over the presidency of the intergovernmental forum by Indonesian President Joko Widodo. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story As photos and videos from the summit flooded social media, pictures from one particular meeting received much attention. These featured French President Emmanuel Macron, Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, U.S. President Joe Biden, and British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, among others, sitting at a table. Modi was not present at the meeting, and thus was missing from the photos. A lot of hay has been made about the absence of Modi in this meeting by his critics. "Biden called an emergency meeting at #G20 - India's so-called Vishwaguru Modi is missing," read one such tweet . Another asked  , "Where is Vishwaguru?". The Sanskrit term "Vishwaguru" roughly translates to "world leader" and is often used by supporters of Modi to praise him and by his detractors to mock him. The implication of such tweets here is that while the PM positions himself as a global statesman, he was ignored for this seemingly crucial meeting of world leaders. Biden called an emergency meeting at #G20 - India's so-called Vishwaguru Modi is missing! pic.twitter.com/PSkLlLLz7x — Ashok Swain (@ashoswai) November 16, 2022 Archives of similar tweets can be found here , here , here  and here . Looking into the facts, we found that the exclusion of Modi from this meeting has nothing to do about his stature on the global stage. WHAT WAS THE MEETING ABOUT?  According to news reports , on November 15, a missile struck the village of Przewodów in Poland, near the border with Ukraine. The incident occurred amid ongoing Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy facilities. In its aftermath, an emergency meeting was convened by members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) and the intergovernmental political forum G7 who were present at Bali during the G20 Summit. At the time of this meeting, it was suspected that Russia was now also attacking Poland — a development that can escalate geopolitical tensions further. Following this emergency meeting in Bali, the White House  and the Council of the European Union  issued a joint statement signed by the leaders of Canada, the European Commission, the European Council, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Earlier, I met with G20 and NATO Leaders to discuss the explosion in Eastern Poland near the Ukrainian border. We offer our full support for and assistance with Poland's ongoing investigation. pic.twitter.com/KZcWZBo4VI — President Biden (@POTUS) November 16, 2022 It said,  "We discussed the explosion that took place in the eastern part of Poland near the border with Ukraine. We offer our full support for and assistance with Poland's ongoing investigation. We agree to remain in close touch to determine appropriate next steps as the investigation proceeds." The leaders reaffirmed their commitment to "hold Russia accountable for its brazen attacks on Ukrainian communities, even as the G20 meets to deal with the wider impacts of the war." advertisement It's noteworthy that Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov  left Bali a day ahead of the scheduled conclusion of the G20 Summit. Lavrov took the flight home apparently hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky virtually addressed the leaders, repeatedly referring to them as the G19 and calling for the war to end "justly". WHO ATTENDED THE MEETING?  According to Reuters , the people present in the photo were European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Germany's Chancellor Olaf Scholz, France's President Emmanuel Macron, Canada's Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, U.S. President Joe Biden, British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, Netherland's Prime Minister Mark Rutte, Japanese Prime Minister Fumio Kishida, U.S. Secretary of State Anthony Blinken, and European Council President Charles Michel. advertisement WHY WAS MODI NOT THERE? Modi was not part of the meeting because India is not a part of either NATO or G7. NATO has thirty members  and representatives from all member countries were not present at the meeting. This is because it was an emergency meeting that was called during the G20 Summit and several NATO members were not in Bali by virtue of not being part of the G20. G7 members  include Germany, France, the U.K., Italy, Japan, Canada, the U.S., and the European Union. This is why Japan, which is not part of NATO, was present at the meeting. WHAT IS INDIA'S POSITION ON RUSSIA AND UKRAINE?  India has largely kept its position neutral on the Russia-Ukraine conflict and abstained from resolutions against Moscow. Most recently on November 14 , when the United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution calling for Russia to be held accountable for violations of international law India was among the 73 countries that abstained from the voting. Thus, it is clear that Narendra Modi was not excluded from the meeting as a rebuff to either India or the Prime Minister. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Nov 17, 2022 22:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Old explosion video from Russian Belgorod region FALSELY shared as recent blast in Crimea
content:
The video has no links with the reported explosions in Dzhankoi, Crimea. The original video is from the Russian Belgorod region and it was shot in August 2022.
The ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine has resulted in a major geopolitical crisis — not just in these two countries but across the globe. Recently, a missile hit the Polish village of Przewodow near the Ukrainian border and escalated tensions further.  Amid all this, many on social media  and even some news outlets have claimed that Ukraine has destroyed a Russian-occupied airfield in Dzhankoi in Crimea. Temporarily occupied Dzhankoy, Crimea. There is an attack on the airfield, Russian aircraft, Su-25 attack aircraft and Su-34 bombers are on fire and detonating. The strike was carried out by new Ukrainian kamikaze drones #Crimea #ukrainecounteroffensive #Kherson #Ukraine pic.twitter.com/VQRVIqOmwe — Ukraine-Russia war (@UkraineRussia2) November 16, 2022 One person on Twitter shared a video with the caption, "In Crimea, there were explosions near the military airport and now there is a fire there". Another did the s ame and captioned it , "There were explosions in Dzhankoy (Crimea). There is information that the Ukrainian armed forces struck the airfield. There were around 80 pieces of military equipment there." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Archived versions of similar tweets can be found here and here . But AFWA's investigation found the claim misleading. The video has no link with the explosions in Dzhankoi, Crimea. The original video is from August 2022. AFWA Probe Reportedly in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin publicly admitted his desire to take over Crimea, and immediately he did so. On the other hand, back in August, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also made it very clear that Ukraine had set a goal to take back Crimea . On October 2022, a huge explosion destroyed part of the Kerch bridge from Russia to Crimea and hit Vladimir Putin's prestige projects and a vital logistical link for the Russian military. Does this viral video have any link to the explosion site of Dzhankoi, Crimea? A reverse search of a keyframe of the viral video led us to more videos. The first one was uploaded to the official YouTube channel of The Sun on August 19. It was titled "Russian ammo depot EXPLODES near the city of Belgorod inside Russia border." The same can be seen on Guardian's YouTube channel as well. Reportedly, fires blazed after explosions at a military base near the city of Belgorod inside the Russian border on or before August 19. Thus, it is clear that the shared video has no link with the explosions in Dzhankoi, Crimea. The original video is from the Russian Belgorod region from August. Published By: Ritika Shah Published On: Nov 20, 2022 15:25 IST

title: Fact Check: Bill Gates DID NOT ask for 'Death Panels' during G20, decade-old video shared with false claims
content:
Gates mentioned the 'Death panel' as a passing remark in July 2010 during an event. He did not talk about it becoming a requirement in the future.
Following the recent G20 summit in Bali, Indonesia, many on social media shared a postcard alleging that Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates made a shocking statement. They claimed that Gates has advocated for a "Death Panel" for sick people to cut "high medical costs."
The postcard features a photo of Gates and the text, "Bill Gates Tells G20 World Leaders That 'Death Panels' Will Soon Be Required." According to Gates, death panels will be necessary in the near future in order to end the lives of sick and unwell people due to "very, very high medical costs". pic.twitter.com/Ct6vjergaO — Clown World â"¢ 🤡 (@ClownWorld_) November 18, 2022
According to Gates, death panels will be necessary in the near future in order to end the lives of sick and unwell people due to "very, very high medical costs". pic.twitter.com/Ct6vjergaO — Clown World â"¢ 🤡 (@ClownWorld_) November 18, 2022
It further adds, "Unelected world health czar Bill Gates has used his appearance at the G20 Summit in Bali, Indonesia, to raise a discussion about 'death panels'. According to Gates, death panels will be necessary in the near future in order to end the lives of sick and unwell people due to 'very, very high medical costs'." An archived version of this postcard can be seen here .
A video that makes the same claim has gone viral as well. It was shared with captions like, "Watch: Bill Gates' sick message about a disturbing 'death panel' was caught on tape at the G20 summit."
In the video, a voice can be heard saying, "He said something very alarming last evening at the G20 summit." Following that, Gates can be heard saying: "Because of very, very high medical costs and a lack of willingness to say, 'is spending a million dollars on that last three months of life for that patient, would it be better not to lay off those ten teachers and to make that trade-off in medical costs?'"Â Watch: Bill Gates' sick message about a disturbing 'death panel' was caught on tape at the G20 summit. Full episode: https://t.co/pq6vGgkdiE pic.twitter.com/CSO0TouSpo — The Western Journal (@WestJournalism) November 16, 2022
Watch: Bill Gates' sick message about a disturbing 'death panel' was caught on tape at the G20 summit. Full episode: https://t.co/pq6vGgkdiE pic.twitter.com/CSO0TouSpo — The Western Journal (@WestJournalism) November 16, 2022
"But that's called the death panel, and you are not supposed to have that discussion," Gates was heard adding. An anchor appeared after this and said, "Bill Gates continues to play with people's lives like they are his own experiment."Â
AFWA's investigation found that the viral video is not from Indonesia's G20 summit but is almost a decade old. Also, Gates never said that a "Death Panel will soon be required."Â AFWA Probe
Had Gates made such a shocking statement at the G20 Summit, it would have been in the headlines. However, we found no news reports that suggested he made such a statement there. We then tried looking for the source of the video.
The logo for "FORA.tv" was clearly visible in the viral video. So, we searched for the video with relevant keywords and came across a video uploaded to the same channel in September 2010. It looked similar to the viral video.
Entitled "Bill Gates: End-of-Life Care vs. Saving Teachers' Jobs", the introductory part of the video noted that it was shot on July 10, 2010, at the Aspen Institute — a non-profit organisation for human studies. This made it clear that it had nothing to do with the recent G20 summit.
We found that nowhere in the video did Gates talk about the requirement of a "Death Panel." He discussed how the US had spent 17 per cent of its GDP on healthcare, making roads stressful for other sectors like education.Â
Gates then went on to suggest a public discussion about a "Death Panel" while making the statement that has now gone viral. However, Gates did not say that these so-called panels would be "necessary in the near future" as suggested.Â
According to an Associated Press story debunking the same claim , the term "death panels" refers to the way critics characterised a provision in Barack Obama's Affordable Care Act in the US, when it was still a proposal. This provision would allow Medicare to pay doctors for voluntary counselling sessions that address end-of-life issues.
Therefore, it is safe to conclude that the "death panel" argument is being taken out of context and presented as recent. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 20, 2022 15:39 IST

title: Fact Check: A witch flying around at night? Video made using VFX makes headlines across the world
content:
This video does not show a real incident. It was created by Zambian VFX artist Joseph Njovu.
Waking up in the middle of the night to look out the window only to find a ghostly creature floating in the sky — a nightmare for many — has supposedly been caught on camera by a man. A video  recorded by an unidentified man in the middle of the night is doing the rounds on social media that has left people from different nooks and corners of the world alarmed.Â
The video  shows an old rusted white van parked in front of the window. A strange noise, resembling that of a weeping animal can be heard in the background. Suddenly, a creature appears floating in the sky, reaching the parked vehicle. Watching this, the person shooting the video hides behind the curtains.Â
When the man re-opens the blinds, the creature can be seen standing still and looking right into the camera with its glowing eyes. Then, it starts moving again, this time towards the person recording the video who, watching this, runs away from the window. Social media users have attributed the video of this floating "witch" to many different places. A Facebook user  claimed that the video was shot near a Bihar crematorium. Others said  that it was from Meerut, shot yet again near a crematorium.Â
News 18  and Zee News  reported this incident, claiming that it went viral from Kalna, a town in the Purba Bardhaman district of West Bengal, days before "Bhoot Chaturdashi" in October. While reverse-searching the keyframes of the video, we found it was shared  along with photos of a Pakistani news report about a supposed ghost-sighting. Apart from Pakistan , the video has also been attributed to Columbia  , Nigeria , Malaysia  and the Phillipines . AFWA's investigation found that this video does not show a real incident at all. It was created by Zambian VFX artist Joseph Njovu. AFWA PROBE Â
The reverse search of a keyframe from the viral video led us to a video  posted on September 24, titled, "VFX tutorial. Flying witch caught on camera. Cinema 4d and after effects." This tutorial was made by Joseph Njovu, a visual effects artist based in Zambia, in which he shows a breakdown of how he made the viral video. At the start of the video, Njovu mentions how the video he made just for fun has been going viral in Nigeria with people mistaking it for a real incident.Â
Then he showed the original clip that he shot before adding the creature to it. The clip was not shot at night but in the early evening and was later edited using Marvelous Designer, a software used by 3D artists. A comparison of the raw clip and the viral video can be seen below. Â
Njovu also showed the female avatar , which later became the "witch", and how he added elements like long hair, an oversized robe-like cloth, and sound effects to the video to make it realistic and scary. Njovu also made use of his voice and that of his wife in the background, talking to each other as they saw the scary creature. However, the viral video has a different spooky voice played on repeat in the background. Most probably, the audio has been tampered with to make it scarier. So, it is clear that the witches and ghosts supposedly sighted in various parts of India and the world was just a video made by a VFX artist.  (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Nov 20, 2022 15:49 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi didn't say 'I want power, not truth', viral video was clipped out of context
content:
The original video is from Congress 'Mehngai Hatao Maha Rally', which was organised in Rajasthan's Jaipur on December 13, 2021. Here, Gandhi was not talking about himself, rather he was targeting BJP leaders.
On September 7, 2022, Rahul Gandhi started the Bharat Jodo Yatra in Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu. Having moved through six states, the Yatra  is right now in Maharashtra as neighbouring Gujarat is in full election mode.Â
A 15-second-long video clip  featuring Gandhi has been widely shared online, amid all this. During a rally, the Congress leader is saying, "I want power. I don't care about the truth. The truth can go to hell. I just want the seat." Â
Many shared the clip , with captions in Hindi  like: "Rahul Ji only wants power. He doesn't care about the truth". The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found that in the original video, Gandhi was referring to Bharatiya Janata Party leaders, not himself.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to a video that was uploaded to the YouTube channel of The Indian Express , titled "Rahul Gandhi Slams BJP: 'I Am a Hindu, Not Hindutvawadi". It was from the Congress party's "Mehangai Hatao Maha Rally", organised in Rajasthan's Jaipur on December 13, 2021. We also found a much longer version of the same video on the Congress's official YouTube channel. The video was titled, "Shri Rahul Gandhi addresses the 'Mehangai Hatao Maha Rally' in Jaipur, Rajasthan".Â
In the latter video, between the 11.28- and 12-minute-marks, Gandhi can be heard saying in Hindi, "Hindutwavadis want power at any cost. Just like Mahatma Gandhi once said, 'I want the truth. I look for the truth. I don't want power', the same way, they (the BJP) say, 'I want power. I don't care about the truth. The truth can go to hell. I just want the seat'."
The rally and Gandhi's speech were widely reported by news outlets. According to The Hindu  aside from Gandhi, Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot, Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel, Mallikarjun Kharge, Bhupinder Singh Hooda, Kamal Nath, Sachin Pilot, Ajay Maken, Adhir Ranjan Chowhdhury, among others, attended the rally.
Thus, it is clear that in the viral clip, Gandhi was not talking about himself, rather he was targeting Bharatiya Janata Party leaders. Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Nov 21, 2022 14:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video FALSELY shared as Zakir Naik converting people to Islam during FIFA
content:
This video is from May 2016, when Naik visited Qatar to give a lecture. Thus, it has no connection with the ongoing Football World Cup.
Controversial Islamic televangelist Zakir Naik, a fugitive who has been charged in India with hate speech, promoting enmity between groups, and money laundering, has reportedly been invited to Qatar to give talks during the FIFA World Cup 2022.
As people condemned the Qatari government for inviting Naik , videos of people allegedly converting to Islam after listening to the preacher talk in Qatar have been widely shared. In one video, a person resembling Naik can be seen reciting Islamic verses and four others repeating them.Â
A Facebook user shared the video with the caption, "#FifaWorldCup2022: People accepted Islam after listening Zakir Naik in Qatar at Fifa World Cup 2022." Several Twitter accounts also shared this video , linking it to the World Cup.Â
In another video, people can be seen repeating Islamic verses being recited by a man wearing a white robe. This video was filmed in an outdoor location. A Facebook user shared this video , writing: "Update on the FIFA World Cup. So far more than 1000 people have converted to Islam, even though the event has not even started yet. Today is the first match."Â
AFWA found that both videos are old and have no connection with the ongoing FIFA World Cup. At the time of filing this story, there were no reports of anyone converting to Islam during the FIFA World Cup in Qatar.Â
India Today had earlier erroneously cited this video as Naik proselytising people in Qatar during the FIFA World Cup 2022. However, the report was corrected soon after. AFWA Probe
Let us look at these videos one by one. In the comments section of the first one on Facebook, we noticed that many had pointed out that this video was from 2016 . Subsequently, we conducted a keyword search that led us to a May 27, 2016, tweet by a Qatar journalist. The Arabic tweet said, "Four people declare their conversion to Islam after a lecture by Dr. Zakir Naik." 4 أشخاص يعلنون إسلامهم بعد محاضرة د.ذاكر نايك في #كتارا .. #قطر pic.twitter.com/nUYUWZxbwp — جابر الحرمي (@jaberalharmi) May 27, 2016
4 أشخاص يعلنون إسلامهم بعد محاضرة د.ذاكر نايك في #كتارا .. #قطر pic.twitter.com/nUYUWZxbwp — جابر الحرمي (@jaberalharmi) May 27, 2016
The Doha-based channel Al Jazeera Mubasher also shared a similar video on its Facebook page  on May 27, 2016. It was the live broadcast of a lecture by Naik, titled "Does God Exist?"
On comparing a screengrab of the viral video with the Aljazeera video, similarities between them could be easily seen.Â
As per reports, Naik had visited the Cultural Village Foundation in Doha , Qatar, in May 2016. There, he presented this lecture to a large audience of around 13,000 people. Reportedly, the lecture ended with the conversion of eight people to Islam.
For the second video, we reverse-searched keyframes from it and found that it had been shared on YouTube on March 14, 2018. Its title read: "60 Filipinos convert to Islam."
On comparing the second viral video with this one, it becomes clear that they are the same.Â
We could not verify the exact date or the location of this video. However, since it has been on the internet at least since 2018, we concluded that it was not related to the FIFA World Cup 2022.Â
To sum it up, two old videos are being falsely peddled as people converting to Islam at the FIFA World Cup 2022 in Qatar. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 21, 2022 19:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Is Donyi Polo Arunachal Pradesh's first airport post-independence? Viral claim is wrong
content:
Donyi Polo is the first greenfield airport in Arunachal Pradesh. The northeastern state has two more operational airports, Pasighat and Tezu, inaugurated in 2018 and 2019.
On November 19, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Donyi Polo Airport in Itanagar, the capital of Arunachal Pradesh. Since then, several people on social media  have made the surprising claim that it took more than seven decades of India's independence for the northeastern state to have an airport. आजादी के 70 साल बाद पहली बार अरुणांचल प्रदेश में एयरपोर्ट बना यह होता है असली भारत जोड़ो 💪 pic.twitter.com/FUjeFFEQno — बिपिन भारद्वाज (@vipinbharadwaj2) November 21, 2022
आजादी के 70 साल बाद पहली बार अरुणांचल प्रदेश में एयरपोर्ट बना यह होता है असली भारत जोड़ो 💪 pic.twitter.com/FUjeFFEQno — बिपिन भारद्वाज (@vipinbharadwaj2) November 21, 2022
With a sarcastic jab at the Congress party's Bharat Jodo Yatra, some the photo of an airstrip with captions  like, "This is the real 'Bharat Jodo'. The first ever airport has been built in Arunachal Pradesh since independence." The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found these posts to be misleading. Donyi Polo is not the first commercial airport in the state but is the first greenfield airport. There are two more existing operational airports in Arunachal Pradesh.
When we reverse-searched the photo of the airstrip, it took us to an NDTV report published on November 18, a day before the inauguration of Donyi Polo Airport. The report mentioned that the airport will be the first greenfield airport in Arunachal Pradesh and the first in its capital city Itanagar. It further noted that this will be the third operational airport in Arunachal Pradesh after Pasighat and Tezu. Despite the presence of the other two airports, however, passengers often opt for either Dibrugarh or Guwahati in Assam due to the long travel time needed to reach these airports, the report added.
It further noted that this will be the third operational airport in Arunachal Pradesh after Pasighat and Tezu. Despite the presence of the other two airports, however, passengers often opt for either Dibrugarh or Guwahati in Assam due to the long travel time needed to reach these airports, the report added.
Per a press release  from the Prime Minister's Office, PM Modi said that Donyi Polo Airport will be the fourth operational airport in Arunachal Pradesh, taking the total airport count in the North-East region to 16 during the inaugural event.
The official data provided by the Airport Authority of India , however, contradicts the claim made in the Press Information Bureau press release — it showed Zero Airport or Ziro Airport, the fourth airport as "non-operational." Pasighat and Tezu airports were 'operational' per this chart.
When did Arunachal Pradesh enter India's aviation map?
The Hindu reported on May 21, 2018, that after Arunachal Chief Minister Pema Khandu flew to Pasighat airport from Kolkata via Guwahati with some other passengers, it became the last of the eight northeastern states to enter India's aviation map. An Indian Express fact-check report noted, however, that it was during the 1980s when the first-ever commercial flight touched down in Arunachal Pradesh.
On February 9, 2019, Zee Biz reported that Prime Minister Modi inaugurated the Tezu airport and laid the foundation for the construction of a greenfield Airport at Hollongi, Itanagar.Â
Therefore, it is more than clear that Donyi Polo is not the first airport to be built in Arunachal Pradesh following India's independence. Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Nov 22, 2022 11:38 IST

title: Fact Check: NO 'Love Jihad', photos of Hindu woman killed by her father falsely given communal twist
content:
These photos show a Hindu woman called Ayushi Yadav who was murdered by her father Nitesh Yadav. The police confirmed to AFWA that there was no 'love jihad' angle to the story.
In the aftermath of the recent grisly story of Aaftab Poonawala being accused of murdering his partner Shraddha Walkar and later chopping up her corpse to dispose it, stories of alleged "love jihad" have been widely shared on social media. Love jihad is a far-right conspiracy theory that purports Muslim men target non-Muslim women to convert them to Islam by means of seduction, feigning love, kidnapping, and marriage.Â
One such story of alleged "love jihad" came with a gruesome set of photos  of a dead woman wrapped in a plastic sheet lying alongside a red trolley bag. These photos were shared with captions like, "Another woman, found packed in a suitcase, becomes the victim of love jihad. Keep sleeping, Hindus. This is how women will keep dying." Those sharing the posts also claimed  that the body was discovered on the Yamuna Expressway in Uttar Pradesh.Â
Some shared photos of the incident without mentioning "love jihad". However, they used euphemisms like "Abdul"  to imply that the woman seen in the photos was killed by a Muslim man. This post has been archived here.
AFWA's investigation found that all such claims were categorically false. According to the police, Nitesh Yadav, the father of Ayushi Yadav, the dead woman seen in the photos, confessed to killing her.Â
When we looked for reports of any such recent incident on the Yamuna Expressway, we found a tweet by the Mathura Police that said the dead woman from the viral photos was found  stuffed in a trolley bag on November 18 on the Yamuna Expressway in the Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh. The police later identified her as Ayushi Yadav, a resident of Delhi's Badarpur. The Mathura police tweeted on November 21 that Ayushi was murdered by her father Nitesh Yadav and that her mother Brijbala helped him dispose of the body. The police said in a statement that Ayushi had married a man called Chatrapal against the wishes of her family. According to the statement, there was a heated argument between Ayushi and her father on November 17 during which he shot her twice using his revolver. Later in the dead of the night, Nitesh and Brijbala transported her corpse in their car, disposed of it on the Yamuna Expressway, and returned home. लाल ट्राली बैग में अज्ञात बालिका की जघन्य हत्याकाण्ड (आनर किलिंग) का सफल अनावरण करते हुये बालिका के माता पिता को मय आलाकत्ल व घटना मे प्रयुक्त कार सहित गिरफ्तार करने के सम्बन्ध में अपर पुलिस अधीक्षक नगर,मथुरा द्वारा दी गयी बाइट । pic.twitter.com/nmHnbLuUHX — MATHURA POLICE (@mathurapolice) November 21, 2022 advertisement Mathura police also tweeted that the revolver used to kill Ayushi and the car that was used to dispose of her body had been recovered. थाना राया व स्वाट टीम लाल ट्राली बैग में अज्ञात बालिका की जघन्य हत्याकाण्ड (आनर किलिंग) का सफल अनावरण करते हुये बालिका के माता पिता को मय आलाकत्ल व घटना मे प्रयुक्त कार सहित किया गिरफ्तार¬- pic.twitter.com/aKbaY9kcKI — MATHURA POLICE (@mathurapolice) November 21, 2022 AFWA contacted Mathura's assistant superintendent of police MP Singh who rubbished any claims of an interfaith relationship and "love jihad". He said that Ayushi had married a man called Chatrapal Singh Gurjar, who belonged to a different caste. Singh added that Ayushi would often leave home without informing the family. Her father Nitesh was worried that she would bring dishonour to the family. This, Singh said, was what led to the murder. The Indian Express , Outlook  and The Times of India  also reported that Ayushi was killed by her father Nitesh Yadav. Thus, it is clear that this grisly tale was falsely given a communal spin by many on social media. (With inputs from Ashish Kashyap) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Nov 22, 2022 15:36 IST

title: Fact Check: 2018 clip of Imam praying amid earthquake resurfaces after recent deadly tremors in Indonesia
content:
This video is four years old. It is from August 5, 2018, shot in Bali's Musholla As-Syuhada mosque when a 6.9 magnitude earthquake rocked Indonesia claiming the lives of at least 98 people.
A devastating earthquake in the West Java province of Indonesia on November 11 left at least 160 people dead, with nearly a thousand injured and damage worth crores. According to the United States Geological Survey , the magnitude of the quake was 5.6 and it hit Indonesia around 1:21 pm local time.Â
Following this, a video has been circulating on social media that allegedly shows a man dressed in white praying inside a mosque amid heavy tremors. This clip begins with chants of prayer on the loudspeaker. As soon as the tremors started, several people ran away. #Earthquake of 5.6 magnitude hits Indonesia, 56 died and 700 injured so far. worshipers continued to pray Salah. SubhanAllah. May Allah bless them and have mercy on them 😥 pic.twitter.com/zDMMGCnDdb — Quran & Hadith (@QuranAndHadithh) November 21, 2022
#Earthquake of 5.6 magnitude hits Indonesia, 56 died and 700 injured so far. worshipers continued to pray Salah. SubhanAllah. May Allah bless them and have mercy on them 😥 pic.twitter.com/zDMMGCnDdb — Quran & Hadith (@QuranAndHadithh) November 21, 2022
The man in white and a few others, however, stood still and continued to pray, holding the walls for support. This video was shared by many on Twitter, with captions like, "Earthquake of 5.6 magnitude hits Indonesia, 56 died and 700 injured so far. worshipers continued to pray Salah. SubhanAllah. May Allah bless them and have mercy on them." The archived version of such a post can be seen here .Â
AFWA's investigation found that this video was at least four years old, and thus, not from the recent earthquake.Â
A reverse search of screengrabs from the viral video took us to a BBC report from August 7, 2018, that carried the same image of the man in white holding the wall for support. Reportedly, he was an Imam named Arafat and the video was from the Musholla As-Syuhada mosque in Bali, Indonesia.Â
A spokesman for the mosque told BBC News that worshippers heard sounds from "the ceiling and the roof like it was going to fall, so we ran". But the imam stayed as he believed "his life was only for God to take" and so the mosque was "the best place to take shelter".
An August 2018 report in Outlook  noted that the clip went viral after the mosque authorities posted it on Facebook.Â
The Guardian also shared the video on its YouTube channel on August 6, 2018. It was titled, "Footage of an imam reciting evening prayers in Bali while a deadly earthquake struck the neighbouring island of Lombok has gone viral, with people praising him for his unwavering faith."
As per a New York Times report from August 6, 2018, this devastating earthquake claimed at least 98 lives and left at least 20,000 people homeless. Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 22, 2022 21:36 IST

title: Fact Check: Are fans sneaking beer into Qatar stadiums by disguising them as Coke, Pepsi? Viral pics are old

title: Fact Check: Not earthquake, this video shows an accident in Istanbul hours before the tremors
content:
This video from Istanbul shows an accident that occurred a few hours before the earthquake.
An earthquake of magnitude 5.9 shook northwest Turkey on November 23. Reportedly , at least 50 people were injured and buildings in the Duzce province. The epicentre of the earthquake was in Golyaka, a district in Duzce, about 200 km east of Istanbul.
Following this, a video  of several cars, stranded in the middle of a road in a haphazard manner, has gone viral on social media . Some of these cars appeared damaged and smoke could also be seen coming out of some of them. Vehicles that looked like ambulances could also be seen.Â
Many who shared the video claimed it showed the devastation caused by the recent earthquake. One such tweet  read, "A magnitude 6.0 Earthquake has struck an area of western Turkey near the town of #Duzce, about 210km (130 miles) east of #Turkey largest city #Istanbul." The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .
AFWA found that the viral video shows an accident that occurred in the Mecidiyekoy area of Istanbul's Sisli district hours before the earthquake — and thus, unrelated to its AFWA Probe.
In one of the viral tweets, we noticed that a person had pointed out that the viral video shows an accident that happened in Istanbul and not the earthquake. Subsequently, we conducted a reverse search of the video's keyframes alongside relevant Turkish keywords. We found that the video was posted by the Turkish newspaper Sabah on its verified Facebook page on November 23. As per its description, the clip shows a traffic accident that occurred on the E-5 highway. Twelve vehicles had reportedly collided with each other in an accident that injured at least eight people.  Other Turkish-language media websites like TRT Haber , Yeni Akit  and Haber Global  also reported on this. As per these reports, this accident occurred in the Mecidiyekoy area of Istanbul's Sisli district.  According to the Turkish news portal B Gazete , a car that was speeding on the E-5 highway of Istanbul crashed into a commercial taxi and caused the accident. Time difference It is noteworthy that while both, the accident and the earthquake, occurred in Turkey on the same date, they occurred at different times. According to Reuters , the earthquake hit Turkey at 04:08 am local time. An official Twitter account of the Turkish Police  also mentioned the same time in a tweet. News outlets that reported the Mecidiyekoy accident mentioned that it occurred  at 01:20 at night . That it did not occur during the day is also clear from the video. Thus, it is clear that while the viral video is from Turkey and from the day of the earthquake, it preceded the natural disaster by at least a few hours. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 23, 2022 21:05 IST

title: Fact Check: This clip shows music video shoot, NOT Ukrainian soldier creating propaganda video about Russia
content:
This footage is from behind the scenes of a music video shoot for Ukrainian singer Anna Khanina's song 'Lullaby'.
Almost nine months into the Russian invasion of Ukraine, an end to the war is not yet on the horizon. As hostilities continue, a video  of an aged soldier, screaming in pain and hitting his head as a man records the whole thing on camera has been shared widely online. Those sharing it claimed that it showed Ukrainians creating propaganda videos about Russian chemical warfare. The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
Does this clip really show Ukrainians making propaganda videos? AFWA's investigation found that this video was from behind-the-scenes footage of a Ukrainian music video. Â AFWA probe
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes with relevant keywords led us to a ten-minute-long behind-the-scenes video. This was, per the video's title, for a music video. It was uploaded to the YouTube channel "Petr Sherekin" on October 14.Â
The title of the video in Russian read, "As filmed in the music video of the singer Anna Khanina". Anna Khanina is a Ukranian singer. While we could not find the viral clip anywhere inside this video, we noticed a number of similarities between them.Â
In the YouTube video, the man in a Ukrainian soldier's uniform can be seen introducing the viewers to the crew members. The cameraman seen in the viral clip is also present in this video wearing a similar-looking blue jacket and holding similar-looking camera equipment. The channel also has several other videos of the same man. The YouTube channel of Anna Khanina shared the music video for her new single "Lullaby" on October 22. The video description notes that the actor in the video is Petr Sherekin. Again, while the scene from the viral clip was not in the final video, it featured multiple scenes of Sherekin in the same uniform.  The same claim was earlier debunked by other fact-checkers . In fact, Reuters spoke to Khanina, who said that the viral clip was from the same music video shoot. "I was present at the shooting when these shots were being taken for my new song 'Lullaby'," she said. (With inputs from Ashish Kumar) Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Nov 23, 2022 22:47 IST

title: Fact Check: The GOAT asked to embrace Islam? Viral video of Messi and Al-Bulayhi is doctored
content:
This video is doctored. The audio from a 2014 Pakistan-Sri Lanka cricket match was added to the video of the Saudi defender talking to Messi.
Saudi Arabia on November 22 clinched a remarkable victory over Argentina at the opening game of the FIFA World Cup 2022. This triumph against one of the world's top-ranked teams was followed by the announcement of a snap public holiday on November 23 in its celebration. Videos of jubilant Saudi football fans celebrating this massive victory have been flooding social media platforms ever since.Â
Amid the celebrations, a video that has been making the rounds on Facebook and Twitter shows a confrontation between two players from the two teams during this much-talked-about match. If the viral video is to be believed, it shows Saudi defender Ali Al-Bulayhi asking Lionel Messi to embrace Islam in the middle of the match.Â
Al-Bulayhi can be seen approaching Messi in the video, giving him a pat on his back, following which he can be heard saying, "If you non-Muslim, and you turn Muslim, no matter whatever you do in life, straight to heaven." Following this, the conversation becomes inaudible for a few seconds as Messi looks away and chuckles. Towards the end, Al-Bulayhi can be heard saying, "Be ready for the fire," before concluding the conversation. Archives of social media posts showing this supposed conversation between the rival players can be found here , here and here .
Archives of social media posts showing this supposed conversation between the rival players can be found here , here and here .
AFWA found that this video is doctored. The audio of the conversation between two cricket players from an eight-year-old match was added to the video of the Saudi defender and Messi.Â
With the help of a keyword search, we found a 2014 Hindustan Times report titled "Pakistan opener asks Dilshan to embrace Islam." It stated that on August 30, 2014, Pakistan cricketer Ahmed Shehzad was caught on camera asking Tillakaratne Dilshan, a Sri Lankan cricketer to embrace Islam. This happened in 2014, during the last one-day international match of Pakistan's tour of Sri Lanka. The report contained the exact words spoken by Shehzad, which were the same as what can be heard in the viral video.
ABP News, on its YouTube channel, shared the clip from the match showing Shehzad making his religious pitch to the Sri Lankan player as they were exiting the field. It is worth noting, that the conversation taking place between the players in this video matches that in the viral video beat for beat. Â
The comments by the Pakistan batsman were investigated by the Pakistan Cricket Board, who summoned Shehzad for an explanation and also issued him an official reprimand. The Sri Lankan cricketer was, however, unconcerned about the religion-focused comments and did not lodge a complaint regarding the incident. Shehzad, on the other hand, dubbed the conversation a "personal chat" with Dilshan.
This confirms that the audio from a 2014 cricket match has been digitally added to the clip going viral.
But what happened between Messi and Al-Bulayhi?
A keyword search about the recent confrontation between Messi and the Saudi player led us to reports about Al-Bulayhi approaching Messi by slapping his back and shouting at him in the middle of the match. The visuals of the viral clip were shot immediately after Saudi Arabia took a shock lead with two goals in five minutes at the start of the second half. This is when Al-Bulayhi decided to turn and shout at Messi. The report also shared a tweet featuring the actual clip from the match. The conversation between the two, however, could not be heard in it. KKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKK ISSO AQUI pic.twitter.com/j3Sonbv65u — TWITTEIRO ARARENSE (@leonardomed) November 22, 2022
KKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKK ISSO AQUI pic.twitter.com/j3Sonbv65u — TWITTEIRO ARARENSE (@leonardomed) November 22, 2022
After the game, the Saudi defender revealed that he squared up to the Argentina legend and screamed: "You will not win, you will not win," a prediction that came true.Â
Thus, it is clear that a doctored video was shared with misleading claims about a conversation between the two players.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: Nov 24, 2022 15:05 IST

title: Fact Check: 2016 video of England fans mocking children FALSELY shared as a FIFA World Cup 2022 incident
content:
The viral video has no relation to the FIFA World Cup 2022. This video is from France and was shot during UEFA Euro 2016. It showed England fans mocking migrant children outside a bar in Lille.
In their very first FIFA World Cup 2022 match, England faced Iran on November 21 at the Khalifa International Stadium in Doha, Qatar. The English squad's Bukayo Saka scored a twin, while Raheem Sterling, Jack Grealish, Jude Bellingham, and Marcus Rashford all scored one goal a piece, beating Iran 6-2 . Videos of English fans celebrating this victory have been shared by thousands online.
Alongside these celebratory videos, however, people also shared one disturbing clip that shows a group of people harassing four children.
Those sharing the video claimed that English fans bullied local Qatari children after the match. One person who shared the video , wrote on Twitter, "I am at the #Qatar2022 fan zone and I have just witnessed #ENG supporters bully a small group of local children. They are seen throwing coins at their heads while chanting, 'f*ck off ISIS, it's coming home.' Dreadful scenes. #FIFAWorld Cup." The archived version of this post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation, however, found that this video was from France, shot during UEFA Euro 2016. Here, England's fans were mocking migrant children outside a bar in Lille.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to a June 2016 Reddit post titled "England fans accused of mocking refugee children in France as they pay one to down a pint and have others 'fight' over handfuls of coins." It contained a Telegraph report from June 16, 2016.
According to the report, drunk England fans were accused of mocking refugee children, aged between seven and nine, in France after paying one to drink alcohol and others to fight over handfuls of coins. Other news outlets like Mashable also reported the same.Â
When we searched online, we also found several tweets from the time that contained the video. One such tweet read: "English fans are mocking gipsy children throwing them coins."
 English fans are mocking at gipsy children throwing them coins pic.twitter.com/vWMuGrq0QV — Max Allanazarov (@KyKyPyKy22) June 14, 2016
English fans are mocking at gipsy children throwing them coins pic.twitter.com/vWMuGrq0QV — Max Allanazarov (@KyKyPyKy22) June 14, 2016
According to a Mirror report  from June 2016, this disturbing video was captured during the UEFA Euro 2016, outside a bar in Lille, France.
The Washington Post also reported the same.Â
Thus, we concluded that the viral video is not from the FIFA World Cup 2022 in Qatar. Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 24, 2022 21:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Terrifying video of giant wave crashing into ship is NOT from Indonesia--it's a decade old
content:
This video is more than a decade old and shows the Royal New Zealand Navy's HMNZS Wellington sailing to Antarctica for sea trials.
A 5.6 magnitude earthquake left more than 260 dead and hundreds injured on Indonesia's main island of Java on November 21 . Among the many videos of the natural disaster and its aftermath shared on social media was that of a ship caught in a giant wave.
The terrifying video  shot from the ship itself, shows a giant wave crashing into its bow. The intensity of the water at one point even cuts off the camera's view. Those sharing it claimed that it was from Cianjur, a town and district in the West Java province of Indonesia.
Some claimed that over 50 people died while others said the number was 160. Archived versions of such a post can be seen here  and here.  It's noteworthy that the hardest-hit city during the earthquake was reportedly Cianjur. AFWA found that the video in question shows the New Royal New Zealand Navy Offshore patrol vessel HMNZS Wellington sailing to Antarctica and is from about a decade ago. AFWA PROBE A reverse image search of the video's keyframes led us to a 2016 report published on the website Marine Insight  According to this report, this footage showed the Royal New Zealand Navy's vessel HMNZS Otago being hit by waves as tall as 20 metres. The vessel, reportedly, was on a three-week patrol in the Southern Ocean or the Antarctic Ocean when it encountered these waves. The report also included the YouTube video  that was shared by someone called Alex Croucher on December 24, 2015. The same was reported by the Daily Mail in 2016. Its report  too, included the same YouTube video. Based on the idea that the ship was part of the Royal New Zealand Navy, we ran a keyword search and found a similar video shared on the Royal New Zealand Navy's YouTube channel. This 2012 video, which contained the viral clip, however, did not list the vessel as HMNZS Otago. Rather, the video mentioned it was the HMNZS Wellington. Per the video's description, the clip was shot during a sea trial by the Navy. The video begins with text about testing the Navy's new offshore patrol vessel in the Southern Ocean or the Antarctic Ocean in February 2011. Simon Griffith, the Commanding Officer of HMNZS Wellington, described the journey in the video. Both the HMNZS Wellington  and HMNZS Otago  are Offshore Patrol Vessels, "designed for maritime surveillance, supply and support and patrol missions around New Zealand's 15,000-kilometre coast, the Southern Ocean and into the Pacific." Thus, it is clear that this video has nothing to do with the earthquake in Indonesia. (With inputs from Ashish Kumar) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Nov 24, 2022 23:44 IST

title: Fact Check: Fans DID NOT sing in support of Palestine during FIFA World Cup, this clip is from Morocco
content:
This is a 2019 video from Morocco. It shows the supporters of FC Raja Casablanca expressing their support for the Palestinian cause during a match against Palestine's Hilal Al-Qud
Ever since the kick-off of the 2022 FIFA World Cup match in Qatar, social media has been awash with photos and videos from the tournament. One such video  allegedly shows thousands of people in a stadium singing in support of Palestine, while waving Palestinian flags and banners. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here  and here.
AFWA's investigation, however, found that this video is from the 2019 Arab Club Champions Cup in Morocco — and definitely not the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar. AFWA PROBEÂ
We ran a reverse search of the viral video's keyframes and found the same video and longer versions of it uploaded to YouTube  and Facebook in 2019. This confirms that the viral video is not from the ongoing FIFA World Cup.
Per the description of these videos, it shows supporters of Raja Casablanca, a football club based in Casablanca, Morocco, singing in support of Palestine during a match against the Palestinian club Hilal Al-Quds.Â
We also found multiple media reports about Raja Casablanca fans expressing solidarity with Palestinians against the numerous human rights violations in the country. According to a report by Morocco World News , the video is from Casablanca's Mohammed V stadium. Fans sang in solidarity with Palestine during a match that was held as part of the Mohammed VI Arab Champions Cup (also known as the Arab Club Champions Cup) on September 23, 2019. The banner of Ultras Eagles, a fan club of Raja Casablanca can also be seen in the viral video. A comparison between the viral videos and photos of Morocco's Mohammed V Stadium available on Google Maps  confirms that the video is indeed from the same stadium. It is hence clear that the video in question is old and from a football match in Morocco. It is not related to the ongoing FIFA World Cup 2022 in Qatar. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Nov 25, 2022 00:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Musk has not announced plans to buy Snapchat, viral screenshot is fake
content:
This screenshot was digitally altered. Elon Musk has not said or tweeted anything about buying Snapchat as of yet.
Twitter has been in the news for all the wrong reasons since Elon Musk bought the social media company. Musk's policy changes have been criticised by ex-employees, users of the site, politicians, and more. As the future of the website hangs by a thread, many online have begun claiming that Musk is now eyeing another social media app: Snapchat.Â
Many shared a screenshot of a tweet allegedly made by Musk. It read, "Next I'm buying Snapchat and deleting all the filters. Welcome back to reality, ladies."
This screenshot was shared by many on Facebook and Twitter . It was even reported as news on the website Modern Ghana .Â
AFWA's investigation, however, found that the screenshot of the tweet is a fake one. Musk has not made such an announcement.Â
Had Elon Musk announced his intentions to buy Snapchat on Twitter, it would have made headlines in the mainstream media. We, however, could not find any relevant reports from reputable media outlets. Subsequently, we checked Musk's Twitter account.Â
Per the viral screenshot, Musk tweeted about this on November 20. However, when we checked, we did not find any such tweet from that date. On November 20 , Musk made three tweets and retweeted two videos. The three tweets he made were about the FIFA World Cup in Qatar, the reinstation of Donald Trump on Twitter, and one about Twitter itself. We also looked for an archived version of Musk's tweets on November 20 but did not find anything on or about Snapchat there. With the help of an advanced keyword search, we came across only one tweet  made by Musk that featured the word "Snapchat" in it. On May 22, he tweeted in a response to a Twitter user: "This would be a super bad idea, since stocks can swing wildly from one day to the next, eg Snapchat dropping 43%. Tesla is ~40% below ATH! However, eliminating estate tax dodges like GRATs would be good, since the probability of kids being effective stewards of capital is lower." This would be a super bad idea, since stocks can swing wildly from one day to the next, eg Snapchat dropping 43%. Tesla is ~40% below ATH! However, eliminating estate tax dodges like GRATs would be good, since probability of kids being effective stewards of capital is lower.
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) May 27, 2022 Examining the viral screenshot We compared the viral screenshot with tweets and found several inconsistencies in terms of its look. The most immediately visible difference was in the profile picture of Elon Musk. His avatar in the viral screenshot sees him wearing sunglasses. That's not the same as his current Twitter avatar. Apart from that, the time and date stamps align with the text — something that's standard in tweets. While a dot features between the standard time and date format in tweets, the viral screenshot contained a hyphen instead of it. Additionally, the date in the viral post read "NOV 20". But the month format on Twitter is usually not in the upper case. It's in the title case. Thus, it became clear that the viral screenshot was digitally manipulated to spread a false claim. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Nov 25, 2022 22:43 IST

title: Fact check: No, players didn't pause match following an Azan call at FIFA World Cup 2022
content:

Football players busy during a match suddenly pause after the call of Adhan is sounded around the stadium. Once the prayer ends, the game is revived with loud applause from the fans at the gallery. We ran a reverse search of the viral video's keyframes on Google and found that the same video  on multiple social media platforms,  all shared in January 2018. As per these posts , the video was from a football match in Saudi Arabia.
Taking a cue from this, we searched and found news reports about it on several media outlets ,  including BBC and Arab News  from January 2018. According to a BBC report , from January 25, 2018, the video was from King Salman Sport City Stadium in Saudi Arabia.
