title: Fact Check: 2018 satellite view of disaster-hit Indonesia FALSELY shared as recent
content:
The viral clip is from 2018 when back-to-back natural disasters, a massive earthquake, and a tsunami hit the Indonesian coastal island of Sulawesi.
A deadly earthquake shook Indonesia's main island of Java on November 21, reportedly killing at least 272 people . As search and rescue operations continued, many on social media shared a satellite view of what they claimed was the quake. The terrifying video shows land moving almost like liquid.Â
One person shared this clip and wrote  on Twitter, "Satellite image of the earthquake taking place in Indonesia. No escape for those caught in the active earthquake zone. Everything was destroyed in the path of the earthquake." The archived version of this post can be seen here .
However, AFWA's investigation found that the viral clip had no link with Indonesia's recent earthquake. The original video was from 2018 when back-to-back natural disasters, a massive earthquake, and a tsunami hit the Indonesian coastal island of Sulawesi.Â
A reverse search of the clip's keyframes led us to various news articles. On October 9, 2018, the Associated Press  published a report titled, "10 minutes of terror: A quake, a tsunami, and a missing son". It contained a similar video.
The Weather Channel's website also shared this clip in a report titled, "12 GIFs That Show How Weather Left Its Mark in 2018" on December 28, 2018. Per the report, on September 28, a magnitude 7.5 earthquake rocked the island of Sulawesi in Indonesia, triggering a tsunami and killing more than 2,000 people in the twin disasters. Other websites like Yahoo shared this clip as well. On YouTube, we found the same video uploaded to the Hindustan Times' channel on October 2, 2018, titled, "Watch: Satellite images of massive earthquake and tsunami that hit the Indonesian Island."Â Thus, we conclude that the viral video, while from Indonesia, is four years old. (With inputs from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Nov 26, 2022 07:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Ukrainians making fake videos about Russian attack? This is BTS footage from a 2019 sci-fi film
content:
This video is neither recent nor from Ukraine. It's behind-the-scenes footage from the production of the 2019 sci-fi film 'Invasion Planet Earth', which was shot in Birmingham, England.
Ever since Russia invaded Ukraine back in February, social media has witnessed a surge of questionable media regarding the war, be it gory visuals from other countries or high-octane war videos that are really footage from video games.Â
One particular kind of media that's often widely shared online claims to show the creation of propaganda videos or fake visuals from the war. One such is a 28-second-long clip  that allegedly shows Ukrainians filming panicked civilians running and screaming. El circ d'Ucraïna, el espectacle te de continuar els noticiaris no poden parar https://t.co/HipuJH1tir — Carles Codina Calm (@xiricc) November 17, 2022

title: Fact Check: No, Japan DID NOT leave dressing room dirty after losing to Costa Rica in FIFA World Cup 2022
content:
These photos show the state of the Italian football team's dressing room after its defeat against North Macedonia in March 2022 during a World Cup playoff semi-final match.
Costa Rica secured a 1-0 win over Japan on November 27, putting a dent in Japan's hopes of reaching the 2022 FIFA World Cup's last 16. Following this, a set of photos showing garbage scattered in a room has gone viral. Those sharing them said this was how the Japanese squad left its dressing room after suffering the defeat against Costa Rica. A Facebook user  shared these photos with the caption, "Japan's dressing room after Costa Rica match". The archived version of one such post can be seen here .Â
This came as a surprise to many, considering how Japanese football fans were praised in Qatar after they stayed behind following their team's win over Germany and helped to clean up the Khalifa International Stadium. In fact, such a thing has been a trend with Japanese soccer fans. During the 2018 World Cup in Russia, following Japan's loss against Belgium, the team's fans did not let the defeat detract them from helping clean afterwards.
AFWA found that these photos are from March 2022 when the Italian football team had left its dressing room in a shabby condition after its defeat against North Macedonia in a World Cup play-off semifinal match. AFWA Probe
When we reverse-searched the photos, we found in a news report from March 28, 2022, by The Sun. Per the report, the Italian national football team's players had left the dressing room at Stadio Renzo Barbera in Palermo, Italy, in a mess after the squad's shocking 1-0 defeat against North Macedonia that ended Italy's hopes of qualifying for the 2022 FIFA World Cup. Videos of the dirty dressing room had gone viral on social media at the time.Â
Many Italian news outlets like Libero Quotidiano , Rompipallone.it , and Corriere dello Sport  had also carried these images in their reports back then. Following this, Leonardo Bonucci, the captain of the Italian national squad had apologised on behalf of his team, as per the Daily Mail .Â
"It was a big mistake, next time, we'll pay more attention. We were very disappointed and we didn't think that these details make the difference sometimes. We'll pay more attention in the next matches, we apologize", he had said. The Italian squad's communication chief, Paolo Corbi, had also apologised. However, he added that the dressing room wasn't left in as bad a condition by the team as was shown in the pictures.
There has been a lot of misinformation around the FIFA World Cup since it began. AFWA's fact-check stories debunking several such instances of misinformation can be read here . Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 28, 2022 19:34 IST

title: Fact Check: 6-month-old Isudan Gadhvi road show FALSELY shared as AAP CM candidate's recent rally
content:
This video was recorded on May 17 this year, six months before Gadhvi was announced as the chief ministerial candidate in Gujarat on November 4.
Even as winter approaches, the political temperature seems to be soaring in poll-bound Gujarat every passing day. The incumbent Bharatiya Janta Party, the Congress, and the new entrant Aam Aadmi Party have left no stone unturned while campaigning across the state. Amid this, a video of the AAP's chief ministerial candidate Isudan Gadhvi has been making rounds on social media.Â
The video shows Gadhvi leading a road show, waving from atop a moving vehicle. The road, however, looks empty on both sides, with no sign of a visible crowd. Those sharing the video, including Congress leaders, used it to mock the AAP leader. AAP के गुजरात CM उम्मीदवार के रोड शो की तस्वीरें, मानो पूरा गुजरात उमड़ आया 👇 pic.twitter.com/QDuGCM3Mtx — Srinivas BV (@srinivasiyc) November 26, 2022
AAP के गुजरात CM उम्मीदवार के रोड शो की तस्वीरें, मानो पूरा गुजरात उमड़ आया 👇 pic.twitter.com/QDuGCM3Mtx — Srinivas BV (@srinivasiyc) November 26, 2022
"Visuals from AAP's Gujarat CM candidate's roadshow, as if the entirety of Gujarat turned up," wrote Congress leaders Srinivas BV and Keshav Chand Yadav on social media.Â
Alongside the same caption, the video was shared from the official Facebook pages of the Himachal Pradesh Youth Congress , the Madhya Pradesh Youth Congress , and the UP-West Youth Congress . Archived versions of such posts can be seen here .  AFWA's investigation found these posts to be misleading as the video was more than six months old, much before Gadhvi was announced as AAP's chief ministerial candidate in Gujarat.  AFWA Probe  In the responses to Srinivas BV's tweet, we noticed people pointing out that the video was old . They compared frames from the viral video with a six-month older video uploaded to AAP Gujarat's YouTube page. With the help of this clue, we searched with relevant keywords on YouTube and came across a similar roadshow video uploaded to AAP Gujarat's channel in May this year. In this video, Gadhvi could be seen leading a rally in similar attire. However, we could not spot a similar frame that matched the viral one. Subsequent searches with a few more keywords in Gujarati helped us find the original video uploaded to the official Facebook page of AAP Gujarat, six months ago. The Gujarati caption suggested this was captured during the "Parivartan Yatra" in Porbandar. After comparing frames from the original video with the viral one, it became clear that both videos were the same. Notably, this live video was shared by AAP Gujarat's Facebook page on May 17 this year, nearly six months before the official name of the CM candidate was announced. Reportedly, AAP chief and Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal announced Gadhvi's name on November 4 . Therefore, it is evident that Gadhvi was not AAP's CM candidate for Gujarat at the time of this road show.  Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Nov 28, 2022 23:19 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT from FIFA World Cup 2022, video of fan attacking soccer player is from Turkey
content:
This video is from a football match between Turkish football clubs Göztepe and Altay that was interrupted after a fan attacked Altay goalkeeper Ozan Evrim Ozenc.
The FIFA World Cup 2022 has been mired in controversies ever since Qatar was declared the host nation. Adding to the laundry list of negative spotlights on the country and the sporting event is a short video that shows a man running across a football field and attacking a football player with a pole.Â
The video has been circulated with the claim that the incident took place during a match between Germany and Brazil in the ongoing FIFA World Cup. The archived version of the post can be seen here .
This, however, is false. AFWA's investigation found that the video is from a football match in Turkey. AFWA probe
We ran a reverse search of the viral video's screengrabs and found the same video on The Guardian . A report published on November 27, 2022, noted that this video was from a Turkish derby between the Turkish professional football clubs Goztepe and Altay. Reportedly, it showed a Goztepe supporter attacking the latter's goalkeeper, Ozan Evrim Ozenc. Goztepe and Altay are longstanding Anatolian rivals from the city of Izmir.
According to the BBC, the incident took place on November 27 in Izmir, a city on Turkey's Aegean. The man attacked the goalkeeper while a fan was receiving treatment  after being injured by fireworks that were thrown from the crowd. As per reports , following the assault, the goalkeeper suffered a hemorrhage and had to be taken to hospital. The match was abandoned following the incident.
The video was also shared by a few media outlets on Facebook  and Twitter . In a shocking incident, the goalkeeper of a #Turkish #football club, Altay , was attacked by a fan. The incident took place on Sunday during a match between Goztepe and Altay in Izmir. Atlay's goalkeeper Ozan Evrim Ozen was attacked with a corner flag. pic.twitter.com/71r6AWL87s — KUWAIT TIMES (@kuwaittimesnews) November 28, 2022
In a shocking incident, the goalkeeper of a #Turkish #football club, Altay , was attacked by a fan. The incident took place on Sunday during a match between Goztepe and Altay in Izmir. Atlay's goalkeeper Ozan Evrim Ozen was attacked with a corner flag. pic.twitter.com/71r6AWL87s — KUWAIT TIMES (@kuwaittimesnews) November 28, 2022
It is hence clear that the video in question is from Turkey and not related to the ongoing FIFA World Cup in Qatar. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 28, 2022 23:34 IST

title: Fact Check: 2017 aerial view of LA traffic shared as giant turnout for Imran Khan rally
content:
The viral aerial video of the traffic jam is not from Pakistan but from Los Angeles in the United States. The aerial footage shows a massive traffic jam ahead of Thanksgiving.
Following the reported assassination attempt earlier in November, former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan attended his first rally on November 26 . The "Pindi Jalsa" or "Haqeeqi Azadi March Jalsa", in Rawalpindi, Pakistan witnessed frenzy from Khan's fans and supporters as they screamed and cheered him. Following the rally, many shared a bird's eye view of a congested road  and claimed that it was from the same rally. One Twitter user wrote alongside the video  , "EXCLUSIVE — Live scenes in and around Murree Road, Rawalpindi, for the Haqeeqi Azaadi March." Even the former Minister for Interior of Pakistan Sheikh Rashid Ahmed shared the same video on November 27 — though without any context. The archived version of these posts can be seen here  and here . AFWA's investigation found that this video is not from Rawalpindi or from Pakistan at all. It's from Los Angeles in the United States. AFWA PROBE A reverse search of the clip's keyframes led us to various news articles featuring the same video. On November 24, 2017, the Indian Express reported that amid Thanksgiving celebrations that year, a Los Angeles traffic video went viral. The same aerial view was used in an India Today report  from November 22, 2017. The report said that ABC News tweeted aerial footage of a traffic jam on the Los Angeles 405 Freeway to show how "stuck" people could get if they planned to travel by road. Other news outlets like The Independent  and the Telegraph reported the same.  On November 22, 2017, ABC News shared this video on its YouTube alongside the description: "Aerial footage shows incredible bumper-to-bumper traffic in Los Angeles as Americans travel for Thanksgiving." Thus, we conclude that the viral aerial video of a traffic jam is not from Pakistan and it has no links to Khan's recent rally. It's from Los Angeles in the United States. Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 29, 2022 00:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Japanese fans DID NOT trash stadiums at 2022 FIFA World Cup, viral video played in reverse
content:
This video was played in reverse. The original video shows Japan fans cleaning up a Qatar stadium after their World Cup win over Germany.
Fans of the Japanese squad have been winning hearts at the ongoing 2022 FIFA World Cup for staying behind after matches to help clean up stadiums. However, a video  that has been shared by many online seems to contradict this behaviour. It shows people taking the rubbish out of a bag and leaving it littered around a stadium. Those sharing it claimed that this was what Japanese fans had been doing in Qatar. At the time of filing this story, one such video  poster by a verified Twitter user called Andy Ha had received more than 9000 shares. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here , here , and here . AFWA's investigation found that the viral video was played in reverse. The original video shows Japanese fans cleaning a stadium after Japan played against Germany at the World Cup. AFWA probe At the 17-second mark in the viral video, we noticed a man in the background climbing stairs backwards. Multiple other people are also seen walking backwards in the viral clip. This hinted that the video could have been shared in reverse. We further did a keyword search on Twitter and found similar videos shared on November 24. However, unlike the viral clip, in these videos, the same group of people could be seen picking trash scattered around the gallery and placing them in garbage bags. Japan fans cleaning up the stadium after their famous World Cup win over Germany. Most respectful country in the world. 👏 #JPN | #GER | #FIFAWorldCup pic.twitter.com/bPH2vXt7YS — Football Tweet ⚽ (@Football__Tweet) November 23, 2022 The video was also tweeted by Alkass, a Qatar-based group of sports channels, on its official Twitter account. رغم الفوز على ألمانيا.. جماهير اليابان لا تنسى تقاليدها بعد نهاية المباراة. #كأس_العالم #قطر2022 #Qatar2022 #FIFAWorldCup pic.twitter.com/l9o1BnrXRk — قنوات الكاس (@alkasschannel) November 23, 2022 As per Alkass and several others , the video shows Japan fans cleaning the stadium after a match with Germany in the ongoing FIFA World Cup. Japan had a 2-1 win against Germany at the Khalifa International Stadium in Doha on November 23. Posts featuring Japanese football fans cleaning up stadiums started doing the rounds on social media after the tournament's opening match between Qatar and Ecuador at Al Bayt Stadium. After Japan's stunning victory over Germany as well as its loss to Costa Rica, the fans were spotted cleaning the stadium. It is, hence, clear that the viral video is reversed and does not show soccer fans from Japan littering a stadium during the FIFA World Cup 2022. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Nov 30, 2022 15:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Did cops in China run over protestors with cars? This 2021 video is from the US
content:
This video is neither recent nor from China. It's a January 2021 video from the US and shows how a police officer ploughed through a crowd in Tacoma, Washington.
Protests broke out across China over the weekend against the country's draconian zero-Covid policy. Reportedly , citizens from Beijing to Shanghai to Chengdu took to the streets after a building fire killed ten people in Urumqi, Xinjiang, an area that had been locked down for months. Reports say that the protestors believe the state's anti-Covid protocols prevented those people from being saved. According to a Politico report , the government's response to this mass mobilisation has been to flood the protest zones with thousands of police personnel. Social media has since seen a flurry of photos and videos supposedly showing such protests. One such video  was tweeted with the Chinese caption: "Shanghai police kills." The video shows what looks like a police car running over a bunch of people in a crowded street at night time. This video  was also shared with captions like, "No one is reporting this. Police brutality in China running over protestors." Archived versions of these posts can be seen here and here . AFWA, however, found that this video was neither recent nor from China at all. It's from January 2021 when a police officer in Tacoma, US, ploughed through a crowd. AFWA Probe The first thing we noticed was the people in the video were talking in English. This hinted at the fact that the video may not have been from China. Also, under the viral tweet were a bunch of comments that contradicted its claims. One such tweet  read, "Bro, this is NOT from Shanghai, this is from 2021 in Tacoma. Stop spreading misinformation." It linked back to a twee t by Russian state media, Russia Today. This tweet contained a video that looked similar to the viral one. The Russia Today report alongside the video noted that on January 23, 2021, a police SUV was filmed ploughing through a crowd of people and running over at least one person in Tacoma, Washington, in the US. [WARNING, GRAPHIC] Police SUV plows through crowd of troublemakers in #Tacoma Details: https://t.co/VqnDNgpSd8 pic.twitter.com/S0kfup3gBz — RT (@RT_com) January 24, 2021 Subsequently, we looked for news reports on this incident. On MSNBC's website, we found the same footage. According to the news report , a street race was going on when this happened. According to an NBC News report  from January 24, 2021, the police officer ran over at least one person, who was hospitalised. A crowd of about 100 people and several cars were blocking an intersection when the cops arrived, according to a police statement. One Tacoma police car was then surrounded by the crowd and the officer inside reportedly struggled to remove himself. This is when the shocking incident seen in the video took place. "People hit the body of the police vehicle and its windows as the officer was stopped in the street," Tacoma police said. "The officer, fearing for his safety, tried to back up, but was unable to do so because of the crowd." Interim Tacoma Police Chief Mike Ake said at the time, "I am concerned that our department is experiencing another use of deadly force incident." Thus, it became amply clear that this video was not from China where protests have broken out over the state's harsh anti-Covid policies. (With input from Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Nov 30, 2022 19:27 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Hardik Patel DID NOT swear to not vote for BJP in 2022 Gujarat polls, this clip is from 2017
content:
This video is from a rally held by Patel ahead of the 2017 Gujarat assembly elections. At the time, he had backed the Congress party. Patel joined the BJP in June 2022.
With only hours left for phase one of the assembly elections in Gujarat, a video of Bharatiya Janata Party leader Hardik Patel vowing not to vote for the saffron party has been widely shared on social media. The video was shared by the Aam Aadmi Party's Delhi MLA Naresh Balyan on Twitter, who wrote: "Big ruckus in the BJP before Gujarat elections. Hardik Patel swore by his ancestral God that he will not vote for BJP. They have tortured our people and committed murders."
In the video, Patel can be seen speaking to a large crowd. "We take oath on our ancestral God that whoever did atrocity on us, bullied us, and those who are filled with arrogance, we will teach such people a lesson by not voting for BJP," Patel said in the video. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here and here .
AFWA's investigation found that the video in question is from 2017, long before Patel joined the BJP. AFWA PROBE
In the viral video, the words "Jan Sankalp Sabha" and "Bhavnagar" can be seen written in Gujarati. With the help of relevant keywords, we found a longer version of the viral video uploaded to Patel's official Facebook page on December 7, 2017. Per the description of this video, the event was held in Gujarat's Bhavnagar. Â
The original video was also uploaded by multiple YouTube channels on December 7 that year. A 360-degree view of the event was also shared by India Today on Facebook . Per this post, the video was from a rally held during the 2017 Gujarat assembly elections. Â
Patel, who made OBC status for the Patidar caste his political plank , supported the Congress during the 2017 Gujarat assembly elections. As per reports , the young leader was campaigning across the state, mostly in Patidar-dominated areas, to create an anti-BJP atmosphere, prior to the 2017 polls. In fact, Patel formally joined the BJP on June 2, 2022, almost five years after this video was shot.
We couldn't find any credible reports about a recent tussle between Patel and the BJP. On his social media , Patel has been sharing photos and videos  from the BJP's election rallies.Â
It is hence clear that an old video of Patel was taken out of context and shared with misleading claims ahead of the Gujarat assembly elections.Â

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show Indian martial artist Puja Tomar becoming 'World Champion'
content:
This video is almost four years old and is from a One Championship event in Jakarta. Tomar recently won against Bi Nyugen at the Matrix Fight Night Martial Arts competition held in the UAE. But she did not become the 'World Champion'.
A video that has been making the rounds on social media recently shows two women and a male referee standing in a cage ring that is often used for mixed martial arts or MMA. As an announcer calls "Puja Tomar" the winner, one of the women jumps in celebration. Those sharing this video congratulated Tomar for becoming the "World Champion in Martial Arts".
Tomar is a National Wushu Champion and has represented India in the Wushu World Championship. Wushu is a full-contact sport derived from traditional Chinese martial arts. Â
AFWA found that the video is from 2019 and shows Tomar's victory during a ONE Championship event in Jakarta, Indonesia. AFWA PROBE
When we searched for news of Tomar being crowned "World Champion in Martial Arts" on Google, we found news reports about her victory over Bi Nguyen of the US in the Strawweight Title fight at the Matrix Fight Night Martial Arts competition held in the UAE on November 18. Tomar shared this news on her official Instagram page as well.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Puja Tomar (@tomar_puja)
A post shared by Puja Tomar (@tomar_puja)
We found a video of the match uploaded to YouTube by an unofficial account . When we compared the victory announcement in this video with the viral one, we realised they were not the same.Â
Subsequently, we reverse-searched keyframes from the viral video. This led us to a 20-minute-long video uploaded to the Official Youtube Channel of ONE Championship on January 21, 2019. It was a match between Tomar and Indonesian martial artist Priscilla Hertati Lumban Gaol. The match took place at the Istora Senayan Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Per the video's description, "In the end, two of the three judges saw the bout in the Indian star's favour, giving Tomar her first win on the global stage."Â
In this video, at the 19.34-minute mark, one can see Tomar jumping with joy after being crowned the winner. This was the same scene that we saw in the viral video. This made it clear that the video being shared online right now is almost four years old.Â
Did Tomar become the 'World Champion in Martial Arts'?
Tomar, who hails from Uttar Pradesh's Muzaffarnagar , has not yet won the World Championship in Martial Arts, as claimed by a number of people on social media. The last International Mixed Martial Arts Federation World Championship was held in January this year in the UAE, and the only Indian participant who won bronze medal in the event was Vridhi Kumari.
The World Wushu Championship is an international tournament for wushu and sanda (Chinese kickboxing). The WWC has been held once every two years since its inception in 1991. The last Championship was held in 2019 in Shanghai, China. However, because of the Covid-19 pandemic, the event has not taken place since. It is next scheduled to happen in 2023 in the US. While India won two golds, one silver, and one bronze at the WWC in 2019, Tomar was not among the winners there.Â
Thus, it is clear that the video being shared widely online does not show Tomar becoming the World Champion of Martial Arts. In fact, the video is almost four years old.Â

title: Fact Check: Terrifying 2018 video of superfast lava flow shared as Hawaii's recent Mauna Loa eruption
content:
This video shows Kilauea's Fissure 8, a 2018 volcanic eruption that happened miles away from Mauna Loa.
The world's largest active volcano, Hawaii's Mauna Loa, erupted for the first time in nearly 40 years on November 27 , ending its longest quiet period in recorded history. Reportedly ejecting 30 to 60 metres of lava into the air , Mauna Loa has joined its neighbour Kilauea — an active volcano 21 miles away that has been erupting for more than a year now. This unusual dual-eruption event has grabbed the attention of many because the last time these volcanoes erupted simultaneously was back in 1984 .
Amid the deluge of videos and photos of this "sacred event", one video making the rounds on social media shows fast-pacing streams of incandescent lava. In the video, two men can be seen witnessing an orange-red stream of lava flowing at an alarming speed. People sharing this video on social media platforms claimed that it showed the recent Mauna Loa eruption in Hawaii.
One Twitter user sharing this video wrote: "Watch: Fountains of lava up to 200 feet (60 meters) high have been fired into the air from Hawaii's Mauna Loa, geologists say, generating rivers of molten rock from the world's largest active volcano." A Mexico-based journalist also shared this video, writing in Spanish: "Lava fountains up to 60 meters high shoot out of the Mauna Loa volcano in Hawaii." Another such tweet read in Spanish: "This is how they captured the volcano Mauna Loa in Hawaii in the last hours."
A Mexico-based journalist also shared this video, writing in Spanish: "Lava fountains up to 60 meters high shoot out of the Mauna Loa volcano in Hawaii." Another such tweet read in Spanish: "This is how they captured the volcano Mauna Loa in Hawaii in the last hours."
The archives of such posts can be found here , here , and here . #AlMomento 🌋 Fuentes de lava de hasta 60 metros de altura salen disparadas del volcán #MaunaLoa en #Hawái . pic.twitter.com/EqVguRCIhJ — Adela Micha (@Adela_Micha) November 29, 2022
#AlMomento 🌋 Fuentes de lava de hasta 60 metros de altura salen disparadas del volcán #MaunaLoa en #Hawái . pic.twitter.com/EqVguRCIhJ — Adela Micha (@Adela_Micha) November 29, 2022
AFWA found that this video is not recent. It also does not show Mauna Loa's eruption, but rather that of its neighbour — Kilauea. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a 2018 Facebook post by the Daily Mail that contained an extended version of the viral clip. Text in the video stated that it was the Kilauea volcano in Hawaii, and this lava flow supposedly destroyed over 467 homes in its path. This confirmed that the video is not from the recent volcanic eruption.
With a keyword search, we landed on a tweet featuring the viral clip that stated that it shows Kilauea's fissure eight, that took place on June 16, 2018. In addition to this, we found multiple tweets featuring the same video crediting someone called Ken Boyer for capturing it.Â
We then found the Facebook page of Ken Boyer, a photographer based in Hawaii, who shared the same video in 2018. He mentioned the date of the video as June 15, 2018. He also shared the same clip on his YouTube channel , stating that it is from Leilani Estates, a census-designated place in Hawaii County, Hawaii, located in the District of Puna.Â
News reports from 2018 about the Kilauea eruption shared photographs of the fiery stream of lava from the same location as the viral video.
Starting around May 3, 2018, a series of volcanic eruptions and strong earthquakes struck Hawaii, causing major damage to the easternmost portion of the Big Island. A continuous flow of lava from Fissure Eight reportedly poured into the ocean at Kapoho Bay, that reached heights up to 180 feet, destroying more than 700 homes and causing a massive evacuation.Â
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Dec 1, 2022 22:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Voter fraud at Gujarat Assembly elections 2022? This video is months old
content:
This video has been on the internet since February 2022 at least. According to media reports, it was from the 2022 Municipal Elections in West Bengal.
Voting for the first phase of the Gujarat Assembly elections took place on December 1, 2022. While political parties have already started campaigning for phase two of the polls, a video  of a man allegedly committing voting fraud in Gujarat has been circulated widely on social media. In the video, a man standing near an electronic voting machine (EVM) allegedly stopped voters and cast votes on their behalf. The archived link of a similar post can be seen here .Â
AFWA's investigation found that the video has been on the internet since February 2022 at least. At the time, the West Bengal Municipal Elections were on and this video was reported to be from the South Dum Dum municipality.  AFWA PROBE
In the video, people could be heard speaking in Bangla, hinting that it was likely shot in West Bengal and not Gujarat. Subsequently, upon reverse-searching the video's keyframes, we found that the same video has been on the internet   at least since February 27, 2022. It was uploaded to the official Facebook page of CPIM West Bengal  on February 27. Per the caption provided by the page, the video showed voter fraud happening in booth number 108 in the Lakeview School of Ward 33 in South Dum Dum. Â
Around the same time, this video was also tweeted by the Twitter accounts of the Bharatiya Janata Party Bengal  and West Bengal Congress , accusing the Trinamool Congress (TMC) of committing election fraud. Elections were held for 108 municipalities in West Bengal  on February 27.Â
We also found this video carried by media outlets , including TV9 Bangla , on the same date. Per these reports as well, the video was from municipal elections in South Dum Dum.Â
The video was earlier fact-checked by Factly  when it was circulated with claims that it was from the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in March 2022. While we couldn't independently verify whether the video is from South Dum Dum, it is evident that the video is months old and not related to the ongoing Gujarat Assembly elections 2022. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Dec 1, 2022 23:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Brazilian star footballer Neymar seen walking around Doha? Nope, it's his lookalike
content:
The man seen in the video is not Neymar. It's Eigon Oliver, a man famous on social media for being Neymar's lookalike.
In Brazil's opening game against Serbia at the FIFA World Cup 2022, star footballer Neymar da Silva Santos Júnior, known popularly through the mononym Neymar, suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out for the rest of the group stage matches. Brazil will reportedly  make a decision on his further involvement in the World Cup after the squad's final group-stage match against Cameroon.Â
Amid this, even as Neymar shared a photo of his injury on his Instagram Story, a video  began making the rounds on social media that allegedly showed the footballer walking around in Qatar's capital Doha, surrounded by fans. Even the official Twitter account of FOX Soccer, the football news website of Fox News, tweeted this video, identifying the man in it as Neymar .Â
AFWA found that the person seen walking in the viral video is not Neymar. It's a man called Eigon Oliver, who is famous for being the footballer's doppelgänger.
First, we searched online for news reports on Neymar seen walking around in Doha. This led us to a bunch of news reports that said a "Neymar lookalike" was seen in Qatar during the World Cup. We also noticed that under its original tweet, FOX Soccer had issued a clarification. The tweet  said: "UPDATE: we got got," adding, "Neymar has a very convincing doppelgänger." UPDATE: we got got Neymar has a very convincing doppelgänger 😅🤣
— FOX Soccer (@FOXSoccer) November 27, 2022
UPDATE: we got got Neymar has a very convincing doppelgänger 😅🤣
— FOX Soccer (@FOXSoccer) November 27, 2022
Subsequently, we looked for this supposed lookalike of the footballer. When we searched on Facebook, we found a video uploaded to the official page of the international football news website Goal . The video titled "The Neymar lookalike who is ready to get on the pitch" featured the doppelgänger. His Instagram handle was mentioned in the video: @sosiadoney.Â
 On his verified Instagram account , we found that his name was Eigon Oliver. In the Goal video, Oliver said that he did not even know who Neymar was and was surprised when people asked him for photos. Soon, he started to match his hairstyle and looks with that of the footballer, and started impersonating the star athlete for fun.Â
We also found a Reuters tweet  that contained a video of Oliver. It said, "Eigon Oliver is delighting soccer fans in Qatar thanks to his resemblance to Brazilian forward Neymar." Thus, it's clear that Neymar was not walking around Doha while he was injured. It was his lookalike, Eigon Oliver.  (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 2, 2022 21:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of man prostrating in an aeroplane aisle is NOT from India, it's from a Pak-UAE flight
content:
This incident happened on a Pakistan International Airlines flight going from Peshawar to Dubai earlier this year in September.
A bizarre video making the rounds on social media shows a man prostrating in the aisle inside an aircraft as everyone in the flight looks at him. A man in what looks like a pilot's uniform then walks up to him, helps him get up, and makes him sit in his assigned seat. The uniformed man also warns him to not get up again. A voice can be heard saying, "All the passengers are looking at him. Sometimes he calls azaan, sometimes he lies down."Â
In the next scene, a man wearing a sleeveless vest is seen standing, surrounded by the flight staff. Here, a person can be heard saying, "At the time of departure from Peshawar, he was fine. Right after the takeoff, he started acting like this."  After some time, the man in the vest climbs up the seats of the plane and kicks a window.
Those sharing this video alluded to it being from India. One such post read, "First a Namazi wanted to perform Namaz right inside the Aisle of a flying Plane. When passengers & captain of the flight intervened, he took off his shirt & wanted to break the glass. It would have been disastrous for many passengers." One person quoted this tweet and wrote, "Hope a serious action will be taken," while tagging the Airport Authority of India, the Ministry of Home Affairs in India, and the Aviation Safety Network. Another person quoted it , tagging a bunch of Indian news channels and journalists, and the Twitter accounts of the Bharatiya Janata Party in Uttar Pradesh and the Vishva Hindu Parishad. The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â

Another person quoted it , tagging a bunch of Indian news channels and journalists, and the Twitter accounts of the Bharatiya Janata Party in Uttar Pradesh and the Vishva Hindu Parishad. The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â
AFWA found that the viral video is not from India at all. It shows an incident that happened on a Pakistan International Airlines flight earlier this year in September.   AFWA PROBE
Using a keyword search, we found that the viral video was shared by Pakistani journalist Ghulam Abbas Shah on September 19, 2022. As per his tweet, this incident happened on a Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) Peshawar-Dubai PK-283 flight. Â #Video A passenger created extreme trouble on a Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) Peshawar-Dubai PK-283 flight as he suddenly started punching seats and kicking the aircraft's window. pic.twitter.com/bUZ0ZTVNxw — Ghulam Abbas Shah (@ghulamabbasshah) September 19, 2022

The Daily Mail also reported on this incident on September 19. According to the report, this incident happened on a flight that was going from Pakistan to Dubai. Flight attendants reportedly tried to calm the person seen in the video, who was punching and kicking seats, and alarming other passengers.Â
As per the Pakistani daily Dawn , the man was arrested and later deported to Pakistan by authorities at the Dubai airport. Multiple news outlets like The Daily Times and The Tribune had also reported this incident in September.Â
On comparing the uniform of the aircraft staff seen in the viral video with photos of the Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) staff posted on its Facebook page , we found many similarities.Â
Thus, it's clear that this video is from Pakistan, and not from any part of India as has been implied in the tweets.Â

title: Fact Check: Not Gujarat, this video of a cop thrashing a cart-puller is from Patna
content:
This video is not from Gujarat. It's from Rajendra Nagar in Patna, Bihar.
Even though Phase-I of the Gujarat Assembly polls is over, political parties in the state are still in full-fledged campaign mode. After all, the state will go to the polls for its second and final phase on December 5. Meanwhile, a video  of cops thrashing a man pulling a loaded cart has been shared by many. Those sharing the video shot from inside a car said it was from Gujarat. The video was shared with captions like, "#GujaratModel hurts the people... #Gujrat_Boycott_BJP #GujaratElections2022 #BJPCheatsGujarat" The archived version of the post can be seen here  AFWA's investigation found that this clip is not from Gujarat — it's from Patna, Bihar. AFWA PROBE Under the viral posts, many people claimed that the video was not from Gujarat at all. They said it was from Patna, Bihar. Subsequently, a relevant keyword search on Twitter led us to various posts where people shared the same video on November 27 and 28 and claimed that the incident took place in Patna. The posts can be seen here , here  and here. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Even actor Nitu Chandra Srivastava shared   it on her official Twitter account and wrote, "We are in 21st century. Is dis the kind of image #Biharpolice wants to portray? All hard work being done in Bihar, for #Bihar gets washed off, If a poor Thela wala can be attacked mindlessly like this dn can we really claim for a better Bihar. I am disturbed n angry @yadavtejashwi." We also found a November 26 tweet by journalist Anand Singh who claimed that this incident happened in front of his own eyes. Singh wrote on Twitter, "Dear @bihar_police can you justify this act of your men in uniform? This happened infront of my eyes at Rajendranagar Bahdurpur Bridge in Patna just few minutes ago. When I asked, why they beat the rickshawpuller, your men were more keen to know who we are and why we filmed?" Dear @bihar_police can you justify this act of your men in uniform? This happened infront of my eyes at Rajendranagar Bahdurpur Bridge in Patna just few minutes ago. When I asked, why they beat the rickshawpuller, your men were more keen to know who we are and why we filmed? pic.twitter.com/bn1Sai0qiE — Anand Singh (@Anand_Journ) November 26, 2022 AFWA has reached out to Singh to know about the incident. This story will be updated as and when we receive a response. Further, AFWA spoke to India Today's Patna correspondent Rajesh Kumar Jha, who confirmed that this video was from Patna. He identified the area as Rajendra Nagar in Patna. We noticed a huge red-coloured billboard in the viral video, where the words "Now in PATNA" were clearly written. It also featured a phone number. We called the number and discovered that the billboard featured an advertisement for a bakery company. Ashok Kumar Singh, the company's sales and marketing executive, confirmed to AFWA that the location of the billboard was Rajendra Nagar in Patna. We also noticed another ad with the word "Magadh" and a logo alongside it in the video. We searched online for logos of organisations or companies called "Magadh" in Patna and found the same logo used by the Magadh Hospital. Per its website, the hospital is located in Rajendra Nagar, Patna. We called the numbers listed on its website and an employee there confirmed to AFWA that the hospital had only one branch, and the billboard featuring the hospital's name was indeed from the same area. Thus, it is clear that the video was from Patna in Bihar and not from any part of Gujarat. title: Fact Check: This video of Uma Bharti calling PM Modi 'Vinash Purush' is more than a decade old
content:
This video is more than a decade old. According to media reports, and Bharti herself, the remarks were made at a time when she was not part of the BJP.
As Gujarat prepares for its second and final phase of polling for the assembly elections, a video  of Bharatiya Janata Party leader Uma Bharti calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi a "Vinash Purush" or a "man of destruction" is being widely circulated on social media. In the video likely from a press meeting, Bharti can be heard criticising Modi.Â
"I have known him since 1973. He is not a vikas purush, he is a vinash purush. His claim of GDP growth and uplifting people from the BPL to the APL category is fake. Gujarat has neither Ram nor roti. It should be freed from the vinash purush. It is the media that has made Modi so big," Bharti can be heard saying in the video. The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
Many people on social media have shared this video sans context. AFWA found that this video is more than a decade old, and at the time when Bharti made these comments, she was not part of the BJP.Â
Also Read |Â 'Communist quit India': JNU campus walls defaced with slogans by Hindu Raksha Dal
A search with relevant keywords led us to the same video on YouTube, shared on July 27, 2011.Â
Per media reports, ahead of the 2014 Lok Sabha Elections, the same video was shared by Congress leaders to take potshots at Modi, who was then the BJP's prime ministerial candidate. According to the Indian Express , screening the video, then Congress spokesperson Abhishek Manu Singhvi had clarified at the time that Bharti was not in the BJP when she made those remarks.Â
Bharti was expelled from the BJP in 2005 for indiscipline after a public spat with senior leader LK Advani, who was then the president of the saffron party. Reportedly , she asked for the removal of Advani, saying that he had broken the discipline of the party.
In response, Bharti floated her own political party, the Bharatiya Janshakti Party. However, the party failed to gain public support and Bharti returned to the BJP in June 2011. In 2014, she was elected to the Lok Sabha from the Jhansi constituency and served as the Minister for Water Resources from May 26, 2014, to September 1, 2017.Â
When Bharti was asked about the veracity of the viral video on journalist Rajat Sharma's show, Aap Ki Adalat, she said that she had indeed said those things when she was part of the Bhartiya Janshakti Party. The episode was shared by India TV on its YouTube channel on July 11, 2015.
According to a 2014 NDTV report as well, Bharti said that she had made the comments after being expelled from the party.
It is hence clear that the video of Bharti which is now viral on social media is more than a decade old. According to media reports, and Bharti herself, the remarks were made at a time when she was not part of the BJP.Â

title: Fact Check: Video of Lucknow road cave-in FALSELY passed off as that from Gujarat amid assembly polls
content:
This video is not from Gujarat, but from Uttar Pradesh, where a road caved in because of a damaged sewer line in the state's capital Lucknow.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi wrapped up campaigning for the Bharatiya Janata Party on December 3, the day that marked the end of campaigning for the second phase of the Gujarat Assembly Elections. The usual bipolar contest between Congress and the BJP in the state has turned into a triangular one with the Aam Aadmi Party campaigning heavily in the state this time.Â
Amid all this, a video has been shared by many on social media with the purpose of condemning the incumbent BJP's rule in the state. It shows a road that can be seen caving in, forming a pit. Those sharing it wrote captions like, "Pathetic 27 yrs of Modi model," referring to the victory streak that BJP has maintained in Gujarat. Archives of such posts can be found here and here . Â
AFWA found that this video is not from the poll-bound state but from Uttar Pradesh. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a December 2 tweet by Y Sathish Reddy, the social media convener for the Telangana Rashtra Samithi that was recently renamed as the Bharat Rashtra Samithi. The tweet featured the same viral clip with the caption: "While Yogi is busy meditating in Gujarat, the roads in Uttar Pradesh continue to break down." An Amar Ujala photojournalist  also tweeted the same video clip. In the responses under this tweet, we found a tweet from Gyan Tiwari, a BJP MLA from Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh, who said that this incident was caused by a sewer line bursting. लखनऊ का विकास pic.twitter.com/d9kjbZmLXl — Mohammad Imran (@ImranTG1) November 30, 2022
लखनऊ का विकास pic.twitter.com/d9kjbZmLXl — Mohammad Imran (@ImranTG1) November 30, 2022
With the help of this clue, we found a Hindustan Times report regarding an incident where a portion of a road in Lucknow's Vikas Nagar caved in. The report stated that a part of the Mama Crossing to Gulacheen Mandir route in Vikas Nagar caved in on November 28, forming a pit and affecting traffic.
It further mentioned that the trunk line of the sewer line for Jal Nigam, which passes through the middle of this road, was damaged. Leakage in the underground sewage line eroded the soil below the road, resulting in the cave-in.
According to another report , the pit formed was around 25 feet deep. The report featured a different video of the damaged road featuring UP Police barricades around the hole. One of the news reports also stated that two people fell in the pit, adding that they were not injured. A few reportedly also stated that it was the third such instance in the area in the last three years.Â

title: Fact Check: Was Paresh Rawal pressed by a mob after fish remarks in Gujarat? Viral video is 5 years old
content:
This video is from November 2017 when Rawal apologised to the Rajput community following remarks that were then called derogatory.
Actor-turned-politician Paresh Rawal landed in hot water following his recent remark on Bengalis  and the consumption of fish. While campaigning for the Bharatiya Janata Party in Gujarat, Rawal said, "Gas cylinders are expensive but the prices will come down. People will get employment too. But what will happen if Rohingya migrants and Bangladeshis start living around you, like in Delhi? What will you do with gas cylinders? Cook fish for the Bengalis?"
Following this, a video of the veteran actor apologising to a mob has been making the rounds on social media.Â
Retired IAS officer Surya Pratap Singh tweeted the video , writing, "Voters have hit him back, now he is apologising in every street," alongside hashtags for Gujarat and Paresh Rawal. The video he shared also contained the Gujarati text, "If you stay within your limits, there will be no need to ask for forgiveness." वोटर्स ने रपटा दिया...अब गिड़गिड़ाकर माफ़ी मांगता फिर रहा...गली गली। #गुजरात #PareshRawal pic.twitter.com/5KDByc76Lm — Surya Pratap Singh IAS Rtd. (@suryapsingh_IAS) December 2, 2022
वोटर्स ने रपटा दिया...अब गिड़गिड़ाकर माफ़ी मांगता फिर रहा...गली गली। #गुजरात #PareshRawal pic.twitter.com/5KDByc76Lm — Surya Pratap Singh IAS Rtd. (@suryapsingh_IAS) December 2, 2022
Some who shared the video  also claimed that this video from Gujarat shows how locals pressed Rawal on unemployment and inflation, resulting in Rawal abandoning campaigning in the state amid the ongoing assembly polls. In this video, Rawal could be seen trying to calm a mob, offering an "unconditional apology" in Gujarati for his remarks. The archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here .
AFWA's investigation found that this clip is five years old and is now being shared with misleading claims. AFWA PROBE
We searched online to check if Rawal and recently apologised to a crowd. This led us to an NDTV report  from December 2 that he had apologised for his comments on Bengalis. He clarified that in his remarks, he was referring to "illegal Bangladeshis" and "Rohingyas", adding that he did not mean to hurt Bengali sentiments. of course the fish is not the issue AS GUJARATIS DO COOK AND EAT FISH . BUT LET ME CLARIFY BY BENGALI I MEANT ILLEGAL BANGLA DESHI N ROHINGYA. BUT STILL IF I HAVE HURT YOUR FEELINGS AND SENTIMENTS I DO APOLOGISE. 🙏 https://t.co/MQZ674wTzq — Paresh Rawal (@SirPareshRawal) December 2, 2022
of course the fish is not the issue AS GUJARATIS DO COOK AND EAT FISH . BUT LET ME CLARIFY BY BENGALI I MEANT ILLEGAL BANGLA DESHI N ROHINGYA. BUT STILL IF I HAVE HURT YOUR FEELINGS AND SENTIMENTS I DO APOLOGISE. 🙏 https://t.co/MQZ674wTzq — Paresh Rawal (@SirPareshRawal) December 2, 2022
However, we found no videos of Rawal tendering this apology in front of a mob. Subsequently, we reverse-searched keyframes from the viral video and that led us to a video uploaded to a YouTube channel  on November 30, 2017, making it clear that the clip was at least five years old. The caption of the video suggested that Rawal offered his "unconditional apology" to the Rajput community. WHY DID PARESH RAWAL APOLOGISE? A keyword search led us to a DNA report from November 26, 2017, which said that Rawal apologised following remarks where he spoke about Sardar Patel at a rally in Rajkot, and compared the royals (raja) and music (vaja) to monkeys (vandra). Rawal, however, later tried to clarify and said that these words were addressed at the Nizam of Hyderabad and not Rajputs. He said, "I apologise unconditionally to all the members of the Rajput community. I don't know why I spoke those words. I never intended to hurt the sentiments of any community," adding, "My statement was not on the Rajput community. They are a splendour community in India and they make us proud. Nothing wrong will come out of my mouth against such a brave community." The news agency ANI also tweeted this, along with a photo where Rawal could be seen in the same attire he wore in the viral video. I apologise unconditionally to all the members of Rajput community. I don't know why I spoke those words. I never intended to hurt sentiments of any community: Paresh Rawal on his earlier statement allegedly comparing royals and music with monkeys pic.twitter.com/Z0lITUWEvn — ANI (@ANI) November 26, 2017 Therefore, it is safe to conclude that the viral video of Paresh Rawal offering an apology is five-years-old. title: Fact Check: Not Rahul Gandhi, Supriya Shrinate called PM Modi a 'Dhongee Hindu' in this viral clip!
content:
The viral clip was edited to give it a false spin. Supriya Shrinate, in the 2021 video, was calling PM Narendra Modi a 'Dhongee Hindu', not Rahul Gandhi.
In Madhya Pradesh, Rahul Gandhi and other participants of the Congress party's Bharat Jodo Yatra visited the Mahakal Temple in Ujjain on November 29. Reacting to photos of Gandhi offering prayers there, the Bharatiya Janata Party took potshots at the Congress leader, calling him a "Chunavi Hindu" or an opportunist who uses his Hindu identity only during election campaigns .
 Rahul Gandhi Offers Prayers At Mahakal Temple In Ujjain. #TNShorts #RahulGandhi #Ujjain pic.twitter.com/cnZhYvAP2o — TIMES NOW (@TimesNow) November 30, 2022

Meanwhile, a video  of Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate has been widely shared on social media, with captions like, "Congratulations @SupriyaShrinate Ji for finally mustering the courage to speak against your boss and a dhongi hindu @RahulGandhi .. more power to you!!"
The video contained two separate clips. In one, Rahul Gandhi could be seen offering prayers in Mahakal Temple in front of cameras. And in the other, Shrinate could be heard saying in Hindi, "Despite the priests' strong protest, hiding behind the Hindu dharma, the 'Hindu Imposter' entered the sanctum sanctorum of the temple with cameras." Those sharing the video  alleged that Shrinate was criticising Gandhi's recent temple visit. The archived version of such a claim can be seen here .
The Bharatiya Janata Party's Amit Malviya , the Delhi BJP's vice president Sunil Yadav , and other party members like Priti Gandhi  also shared the same video on Twitter.
Did Supriya Shrinate criticise Rahul Gandhi and call him a 'Dhongee Hindu'? AFWA's investigation found that Shirnate's comments in the video were not about Rahul Gandhi at all. They were about Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The video was edited to give it a different context.
A keyword search on Twitter led us to Rahul Gandhi's tweet about his recent Mahakal Temple visit . On November 29 and 30, news outlets like News18 MP-Chhattisgarh  and India Today  published reports using the same clip from the viral video where Gandhi could be seen praying. . @RahulGandhi offers prayers at Mahakaleshwar Temple in Ujjain; BJP slams RaGa's Mahakal visit | #GujaratElections #GujaratElections2022 #ITVideo | @PoulomiMSaha pic.twitter.com/JKBF17jqRL — IndiaToday (@IndiaToday) November 30, 2022

Next, we looked for the source of the Supriya Shrinate'clip. A keyword search on Google led us to a video  that was uploaded on her official Facebook Page on November 11, 2021. She had appeared in a debate show on Aaj Tak and while sharing the video she titled it in Hindi, "The BJP is diverting attention from the real issues of unemployment, hunger, and exploitation of farmers. Modi Ji has made a mockery of religion by carrying a camera inside the sanctum sanctorum, doing Parikrama wearing leather shoes, despite priests' strong protest."
On the same day, the same video was uploaded on the official Youtube channel of Aaj Tak . At the 3.40 minutes mark, Shrinate could be heard saying in Hindi, "Despite the priests' strong oppose, hiding behind the Hindu Dharm, the 'Hindu Imposter', Our Prime Minister entered the sanctum sanctorum of the temple with cameras. He did Parikrama wearing leather shoes. He will teach us Hindu Dharm?" After comparing the viral clip  with the original ( https://youtu.be/Ngyyppt4z9M  ) one, it became clear that the words "Our Prime Minister" was omitted.Â
Thus, it was apparent that Shrinate's target here was PM Narendra Modi, not Rahul Gandhi. Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Dec 5, 2022 17:06 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of a man in BJP attire distributing alcohol is OLD, unrelated to Bihar bypoll
content:
The viral video is old and was shared in December 2021 with the claim that it was from Haridwar. It has nothing to do with the bypoll in Bihar.
On December 5, one Lok Sabha seat and some assembly seats in Bihar witnessed bylections, including Kurhani . Reportedly, on December 3, Lok Janshakti Party leader Chirag Paswan along with Bharatiya Janata Party MP Ravi Kishan, while campaigning in Kurhani, attacked Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. Meanwhile, a video  that's been shared widely on social media shows a man donning a BJP cap and scarf distributing alcohol . Those sharing the video claimed it was from the aforementioned BJP and LJP rallies in Kurhani. One such tweet said in Hindi, "BJP's full form has changed in the 93-Kurhani assembly by-election. B=Bottle, J=Jamke, P=Piyyo. Today, BJP and Chirag Ji have started the drink and vote campaign in an election rally at Kerma Maidan." The archived version of such a post can be seen here . Satish Kumar, the Rashtriya Janata Dal MLA from Makhdumpur  also shared the same video with the same claims. The archived version of his post can be seen here . AFWA's investigation found that the viral video has no link to the Kurhani by-election and that it is old. AFWA Probe Under the viral tweets, we noticed that many had commented that this video clip was old. A subsequent search on Twitter with relevant keywords led to many who shared this video in 2021. On December 20, 2021, the video was shared on the Uttar Pradesh Congress's official Twitter account. On the same day, Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi  and Youth Congress President Srinivas BV  also shared the same clip. In a video, Srinivas even claimed that this incident happened in Haridwar during a JP Nadda rally. देवभूमि हरिद्वार में जिस तरह भाजपाइयों ने शराब की नदियां बहाई, क्या उनके कपड़े देखकर प्रधानमंत्री या स्मृति ईरानी उन्हें अभी तक पहचान पाये है? pic.twitter.com/aitz6iMVaY — Srinivas BV (@srinivasiyc) December 21, 2021 From around the same time, we found a Dainik Bhaskar  report that also said the incident was allegedly from JP Nadda's rally in Haridwar. On December 21, 2021, UP Tak also shared the same video on its official YouTube channel in the "Aaj Kya Hai Viral" segment. However, none of the news reports we found could identify the location and the date of the incident for sure and reported only what the tweets claimed. This is not the first time this video has gone viral with false claims. Earlier this year, lawyer Prashant Bhushan  and Congress leader Kirti Azad  claim this was from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's July 4 rally in Telangana. At the time, AFWA had debunked this. Thus, it is clear that the viral video is in no way related to the Kurhani by-election. It was shared on social media as early as 2021.
