title: Fact Check: News cards predicting AAP win in Gujarat Assembly Elections are morphed!
content:
These graphics were digitally altered from a December 2 ABP News segment. The ABP News-CVoter Exit Poll Results 2022 predicted a 128-140 seat win for the BJP in the Gujarat polls.
The Gujarat Assembly Elections this time witnessed a largely triangular contest with the Aam Aadmi Party trying to encroach upon what have traditionally been Bharatiya Janata Party and Congress bastions. While various exit polls have been predicting yet another BJP victory, one particular set of news graphics making the rounds on social media seems to be telling a very different story altogether.Â
These news graphics supposedly from an exit poll, projected a big majority for the AAP in Gujarat. The first graphic predicted the AAP winning 49 to 54 seats in the first phase of the Gujarat assembly elections. The second graphic said the Congress was likely to win two to four seats and BJP, 35 to 38 seats.Â
AFWA found that both the graphics used in the post were digitally altered from a news report by ABP News. The original report makes no such projection.Â
Closely observing the two graphics, we noticed the letter "P" and a triangular object on the left bottom corners. These matched the logo of ABP News. We could also see part of the news ticker that said in Hindi, "Prime Minister Modi today at Banaskantha, Patan." As per media reports, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on December 2 visited both the Banaskantha and the Patan districts of Gujarat while campaigning in the state.Â
We could also see part of the news ticker that said in Hindi, "Prime Minister Modi today at Banaskantha, Patan." As per media reports, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on December 2 visited both the Banaskantha and the Patan districts of Gujarat while campaigning in the state.Â
We then searched for ABP News video reports published on December 2. This led us to a five-hour-long live stream uploaded by ABP News to its YouTube channel on the same day. Around the 18 minutes 33 seconds mark, we could see frames similar to those in the viral photos. Except for the main text, all other elements in these farmers appeared similar.
We did not find any mention of the 49-54 seat prediction for the AAP in the entire video. Also, the ABP News-CVoter Exit Poll Results 2022 predicted a 128-140 seat-win for the BJP. Per this survey, the Congress is expected to bag 31-43 seats and AAP, 3-11 seats. The channel's opinion poll also predicted the BJP as the probable winner with 134-142 seats. It also predicted 28-36 seats for the Congress and 7-15 seats for the AAP.
The Gujarat Assembly polls were held in two phases on December 1 and 5. Results will be announced on December 8. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Dec 6, 2022 22:00 IST

title: Fact Check: Highway pic from Thailand FALSELY shared as newly built Mumbai-Nagpur Samruddhi Mahamarg
content:
This photo is at least three years old and from Bangkok, Thailand. Not Maharashtra.
In a drive to boost roadway connectivity, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the first phase of the Samruddhi Mahamarg or the Nagpur-Mumbai Super Communication Expressway on December 11. Reportedly , of the 701-km-long stretch of highway, 520 km has already been constructed. The remaining 181 km stretch will be ready by 2024.Â
Following the announcement of the inaugural day, several people on social media shared a postcard that contained what appears to be an aerial view of interconnected highways. They claimed that this photo showed the aforementioned expressway.Â
The postcard also featured a photo of Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis alongside text that mentioned that the project had begun when he was the chief minister of the state between 2014 and 2019.
A local e-newspaper called Nagpur Toda y also used the same photo in a news report about the expressway.Â
AFWA's investigation found that the photo of the roads is not from India but from Bangkok, Thailand.Â
Upon reverse-searching the viral image on Google, we came across a similar aerial shot used in a three-year-old Mumbai Live report . It mentioned that the work for the then "proposed" Mumbai-Nagpur Expressway, was delayed due to concerns over land acquisition. This makes it quite clear that the image existed on the web even before the completion of the stretch that is supposed to be inaugurated on Sunday, December 11. Where is the photo from? When we reverse-searched the photo we found on Mumbai Live, the results contained a similar aerial view of a highway on Shutterstock . The caption mentioned that it was from Thailand. Though it did not mention any other details. A comparison between the viral photo and the Shutterstock photo highlights several similarities, especially the pattern of the bushes, a small waterbody on the left, and the dividers between the highways. We also found a bird's-eye-view timelapse video capturing the movement of vehicles from a different angle on Shutterstock. The caption here read, "Time-lapse aerial view above of circus road traffic cars in Bangkok, Thailand." Another comparison of a screenshot from the timelapse with the viral image makes it evident that both roadways are the same. We also looked for verified footage of the newly built Mumbai-Nagpur Expressway and came across multiple news reports by ABP Majha and BBC Marathi. Both videos can be seen below. Although we could not pinpoint the location of the highway seen in the viral image, it is safe to conclude that it is from Bangkok, Thailand — and not Maharashtra. Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: Dec 8, 2022 14:58 IST

title: Fact Check: Don't wish for a 'skyfall' on your house, it won't make you a millionaire
content:
It is true that a country is liable to pay compensation for damage caused by its space object in another country. However, the amount is not fixed. Nowhere do international space laws mention Rs. 74 crore or its equivalent in other currencies.
The rebel Gallic tribe that made life hell for the Roman army in the "Asterix" comics feared absolutely nothing. Well, almost nothing. They were deathly scared of one thing: that the sky would fall on their heads. The chances of all hell breaking loose from the sky are quite rare, but not impossible.
More than forty years ago, Indians (and many others around the world), at least for a brief bit, experienced something similar. Not the sky, they feared that Skylab would come crashing down on them.Â
On July 11, 1979, the Skylab space station scattered debris across a sparsely populated 150 km-wide section of Western Australia. But media reports in the run-up to the crash instilled a sense of impending doom in the populace. In many parts of India , it led to lockdowns (of the kind we saw during the first wave of the Covid-19 pandemic). People sold their possessions and relocated.  All in all, there was much ado about something that was improbable at best.
But improbability is not the same as an impossibility. While India was spared giant pieces of Skylab crashing down from the heavens, the chances of man-made debris from space falling on you are not absolutely zero. It has happened, and with an ever-increasing number of man-made satellites populating the outer layers of our atmosphere, incidents of these sorts will only increase with time.Â
And while the idea of a piece of space machinery falling on you sounds scary, some on social media seem to suggest that a "skyfall" could translate into a windfall - if you survive, that is!
Take for instance, a post on the Instagram page of Abhay Gupta or @7echnical_life. This page informed its more than 75,000 followers on December 5 that if an artificial satellite crashed on your house, space laws guarantee you a compensation of Rs. 74 crore from the government.Â
Others on different social media platforms also asserted the same. The archived version of other such posts can be seen here .Â
If the amount sounds outrageous to you, that's because it is. While you may be entitled to some compensation, nothing in this territory is simple or definitive. The compensation amount is also not a fixed one (if you are compensated at all). If your eyes lit up at the possibility of windfall gains, the odds are definitely not in your favour here. Before we even get to the supposed Rs. 74 crores waiting for you, let's first examine just how often this happens.Â
How frequently does spacecraft debris fall on earth?
According to a 2018 report by the American scientific and regulatory agency , the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, "A total of between 200-400 tracked objects enter Earth's atmosphere every year." However, the report added that because human populations live on only a small percentage of the Earth's total surface area, "any objects that do not burn up and disintegrate upon atmosphere re-entry are likely to fall into the ocean" or a sparsely populated land area.
According to experts at the Aerospace Corporation , an American nonprofit, up to 40 per cent of the mass of a large space object falling from orbit will reach the ground — the rest burns up in the atmosphere. About once a week, an object that weighs at least one tonne falls from orbit and reenters the atmosphere, said Ted Muelhaupt, a consultant for the Aerospace Corporation's Chief Engineer's Office.Â
A July 2022 paper published in the journal Nature calculated that there is roughly a ten per cent chance that debris will strike one or more people within a ten-year period. Another estimate suggested that the overall risk of being hit and injured by a piece of reentering debris is estimated to be less than one in one trillion. Â
Suffice it to say, it's a rarest-of-rare event.Â
If the debris from a space object launched by a country causes damage in another country or hits a flying aircraft, it would be considered an intergovernmental issue as per the 1967 Outer Space Treaty and 1 972 Liability Convention . If two countries have jointly launched the space object, they will be jointly liable to compensate the aggrieved party. Â Who can claim compensation?
If a space object falls into a property, the government of the country where the damage was caused will have to make a claim for compensation through diplomatic channels.Â
What about the compensation amount?
As mentioned in a paper in the Poznan University of Economics journal there is no cap on the amount of compensation. However, this amount should be assessed in accordance with international law and principles of justice and equity.
So far has anyone received such compensation?
According to the 2006 paper titled "Examples of space damages in the light of international space law" , the second stage of a Thor Able Star rocket fell to the ground in Cuba in 1960 and killed a cow, following which, the US Government had to pay Cuba $2 million in compensation. In 2002, a boy in northern China was reportedly injured when a ten kg fragment from a satellite launch fell on his remote village in Shaanxi province. The government only compensated his medical bill of around $48.Â
Coming full circle, when parts of Skylab crashed in Western Australia in 1979, a local government fined NASA $400 for littering. This fine was ignored for years, however. In 2009, near the 30th anniversary of the crash , Scott Barley, a radio host on California's Highway Radio, heard about the fine and issued an appeal on his morning show for funds. Listeners raised the amount and paid the fine in full. Â Â Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Dec 8, 2022 19:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of paper plane gliding from stands to goalpost is not from Qatar World Cup
content:
The video was shot during a UEFA Nations League in June 2022 in Munich, Germany.
The 2022 FIFA World Cup's quarter-finals   will begin on December 9. Brazil, Argentina, France, England, Netherlands, Portugal, Croatia, and Morocco will now compete to reach the semi-finals.Â
As fans gear up for an exciting set of matches, on social media, a video  of one particular fan has been shared with much excitement. The video shows a man launching a paper plane from the galleries to the football field. As the plane glided through the air, fans around cheered it on. Finally, the plane landed inside the goalpost. Those sharing the video  claimed it was from Qatar. An archived version of such a post can be seen here .Â
AFWA's investigation found that this video is from a June 2022 UEFA Nations League match between Germany and England at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany. AFWA PROBE Â
A keyword search on the internet led us to a news report on a Greek website called Videoman   from June 14. It contained the same video. Per the report, on June 7, during a UEFA Nations League match between Germany and England, a fan threw a paper plane to the ground at the Allianz Arena Stadium in Munich, Germany.Â
Just after the start of the FIFA World Cup in Qatar, this video was widely shared on social media. At that time, NDTV , and Indiatimes  reported that this video was shot during the UEFA Nations League match between Germany and England. On November 26, News 18  also reported on the video, with the headline, "Watch: When a Bored Football Fan Scored 'Airplane Goal' With a Paper Aircraft."Â
On December 1, USA TODAY Sports also shared the same video on its Twitter account, and captioned it: "This guy has aim! A fan turned his admissions ticket into a paper airplane at the match between Germany and England at Munich's Allianz Arena."  This guy has aim! A fan turned his admissions ticket into a paper airplane at the match between Germany and England at Munich's Allianz Arena. pic.twitter.com/sla297KYrh — USA TODAY Sports (@usatodaysports) December 1, 2022
This guy has aim! A fan turned his admissions ticket into a paper airplane at the match between Germany and England at Munich's Allianz Arena. pic.twitter.com/sla297KYrh — USA TODAY Sports (@usatodaysports) December 1, 2022
Following this, we looked for photos of the stadium on Google Maps  We then compared the Allianz Arena stadium's roof and reserve bench area's structure with the viral video. The similarities were striking. Â
Thus, we concluded that the viral video is not from the FIFA World Cup in Qatar. It's a months-old video from the UEFA Nations League in Munich, Germany. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Dec 8, 2022 21:59 IST

title: Fact Check: Horrific photos DO NOT show gang-raped Hindu woman in Assam - they're old and not from India
content:
Assam police have confirmed that no such incident has taken place in the state. The photos being shared are more than ten years old and not from India.
[Content warning: sexual assault/nudity]
Already a pernicious conspiracy theory that plagues social media, it seems that allegations of "Love Jihad" have increased exponentially on websites like Facebook and Twitter following the recently uncovered murder of Shraddha Walkar. Most of these allegations follow the same trope. A Muslim man, a Hindu woman, and grisly murder. And A lot of such posts online present falsehoods. The one ahead is no different.Â
A set of photos of a woman's naked corpse stored inside a freezer has been shared by many on social media. Those sharing the photos claimed that Kajal, a woman from Assam, was gang-raped by seven Muslim men. They also claimed that she was stored alive in the freezer and repeatedly raped till she died. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here , here , and here .
AFWA's investigation found that these photos are more than a decade old and not from India at all. Assam police have also dismissed the claims made in the posts.Â
We couldn't find any media report from Assam substantiating the viral claim. A reverse search of one of the images used in the viral posts led us to a blog post in Portuguese published in March 2010. Per this blog, the images were from a murder that took place in Osasco, a municipality in the São Paulo State, Brazil. According to the information provided in this blog, the woman was killed by her partner.Â
A keyword search in Portuguese led us to multiple media reports  from January 2010 regarding the incident. As per these reports, José Lopes da Silva, a 45-year-old man, was arrested on charges of killing his 28-year-old partner Katiana de Souza Moura and placing her body in the freezer in his home.
Also Read |Â Shraddha would've been alive had Maha cops acted earlier, says father in 1st public appearance
According to Brazil's Secretariat of Public Security , the woman's body was found frozen, in a foetal position, inside the freezer. Some reports also said that the woman was kept inside the freezer for three months. The images of the woman, including the ones used in the viral posts , were also uploaded to the website "Documenting Reality" in August 2010.
We also found that the official Twitter account of the Assam Police had dismissed the viral claims, saying the photos were from "a Portuguese blog of 2010," adding that "Appropriate action will be taken against those found sharing such messages." #FakeAlert An image from a Portuguese blog of 2010 is being shared with a completely false context on Social Media. Appropriate action will be taken against those found sharing such messages. Original source of image: https://t.co/XXRwBjiKve pic.twitter.com/r6dcGnIXAK — Assam Police (@assampolice) December 7, 2022
#FakeAlert An image from a Portuguese blog of 2010 is being shared with a completely false context on Social Media. Appropriate action will be taken against those found sharing such messages. Original source of image: https://t.co/XXRwBjiKve pic.twitter.com/r6dcGnIXAK — Assam Police (@assampolice) December 7, 2022
So, while we couldn't independently verify whether the images in circulation are from the murder case in Brazil, we can safely conclude that they are more than a decade old, and were shared alongside a false communally-charged story.
Also Read |Â Bombay HC allows cutting of 22k trees for bullet train project, subject to conditions Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Dec 9, 2022 15:26 IST

title: Fact Check: Video from remote Chinese village viral as Arunachal residents taking precarious journey
content:
This video is from the Atulie'er village in China's Sichuan province. The vine ladder made by the villagers seen in the video was later replaced by a safer steel ladder. It has since become a tourist spot.
"We keep complaining about the transportation facilities in our areas. This is a small village in Arunachal Pradesh. Look at the challenges people face in their daily lives," read the caption of a video , making the rounds on social media. The video shows people climbing very steep cliffs, some on foot, while others scaling up and down a long ladder. People could also be seen carrying toddlers on their backs.
A person who shared the video   on Facebook, wrote in Hindi, "We keep complaining about the facilities of aeroplane, metro, train, bus, ola, uber, auto in our city, whereas this is a small village in Arunachal Pradesh, where life is no less than a formidable challenge."
Archived versions of such posts can be found here , here  and here.  AFWA found that this video does not show Arunachal Pradesh at all. It's from a remote village in China. AFWA PROBE
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a tweet from April 2020. The caption written in Mandarin, loosely translates to: "This video from Daliang Mountain was shared by an Italian. The foreigner asked me if it was true. After watching it, I said it was true. The foreigner asked why China donated so much money to foreign countries, and I couldn't answer." 这个来自大凉山的视频,还是一个意大利人分享我的,老外问我是真的吗,看完后我说是真的。老外又问那中国为什么捐那么多钱给外国,我无法回答。 pic.twitter.com/Vdz2h2homn — 李方 (@stanleynordic) April 24, 2020
这个来自大凉山的视频,还是一个意大利人分享我的,老外问我是真的吗,看完后我说是真的。老外又问那中国为什么捐那么多钱给外国,我无法回答。 pic.twitter.com/Vdz2h2homn — 李方 (@stanleynordic) April 24, 2020
We also found a 2020 Facebook post, featuring the viral clip , mentioning the name of the location as Atulier'er cliff village in the Sichuan province of China. Several others  also shared the same clip , mentioning that it showed the struggle of villagers in this remote Chinese village.
With the help of this clue, we found a video from July 5, 2019  on the Facebook page of China Xinhua News, a state-controlled media outlet in the country, that featured a few shots seen in the viral video. "Residents of this 'cliff village' in Sichuan, China have been scaling the cliff for generations. In recent years, a steel ladder makes the 800-meter climb much easier," the caption alongside the video said.
In another video  shared by China Plus Culture in 2020, we could find some other clips of people climbing up a cliff with bare hands, followed by the clips of the long staircase that could be seen in the viral video. This post also mentioned the location as the Atulie'er village in the Liangshan Yi autonomous prefecture in China's Sichuan province. It further mentioned that the village is located on a cliff 1,400 meters above sea level. The villagers used to use a series of handmade ladders to scale the 800-metre-high cliff. Later, a steel staircase was built that improved the travel conditions for the locals.  Using this information, we found a CNN news report  from October 26, 2016, about a steel ladder connecting the cliff-top mountain village of China with the outside world. The village reportedly started constructing the ladder in August 2016, with an investment of 1 million yuan ($147,928). The report mentioned that the decision came after the state-run Beijing News published harrowing pictures  of around 15 school children, some as young as six, using an unsteady vine ladder to reach their school in the valley below, making the remote village famous on the internet. Back in May 2020, as part of China's poverty relief program, around 84 poor households in Atulie'er village were reportedly relocated  to apartment buildings near the town centre of Zhaojue County in the province of Sichuan. Bidding farewell to their cliff-top houses, they relocated for better access to schools, medical care, and other basic services. However, as per recent reports , the nearly three-km-long steel ladder of the village has now become a tourist spot after the steady improvement in infrastructure. Having been covered by 5G signals, the village became more widely known through live streams and saw a bump in tourism. (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Dec 9, 2022 21:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Students dancing in burqas in viral video are not Hindu, incident falsely communalised
content:
The students seen dancing in burqas in the viral video were Muslim, not Hindu. This was confirmed by the college's In-Charge Principal.
A video of four students, purportedly from Mangaluru's St Joseph's Engineering College, wearing burqas and dancing to the Bollywood song "Fevicol Se", has been shared by many on social media. Reportedly , following this, the college authorities suspended them.
Some who shared the video claimed  that these students were Hindu and they were trying to mock Muslims when they did this. The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
People tweeted  that "Strict action should be taken against St. Joseph engineering college, Mangalore, Karnataka for such an event organised for mocking Muslims." The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation, however, found that the students seen dancing in the viral video were Muslim, and not Hindu.
A keyword search on Twitter led us to an account that claimed to be the official handle for St Joseph Engineering College in Mangaluru . On December 8, 2022, a thread of tweets  from this account claimed that the students seen in that viral video were Muslim and that strict action had been taken against them. Subsequently, AFWA contacted Sagay Raj , India Today's Mangaluru correspondent, who also confirmed that the students were Muslim. He also provided us with a press note from Mangaluru's St Joseph Engineering College after the controversy dated December 8.
Subsequently, AFWA contacted Sagay Raj , India Today's Mangaluru correspondent, who also confirmed that the students were Muslim. He also provided us with a press note from Mangaluru's St Joseph Engineering College after the controversy dated December 8.
The note signed by Dr Sudheer M, the college's In-Charge Principal said, "The video clip being circulated on social media has captured a part of the dance by students of the Muslim community itself who barged on stage during the informal part of the students' association inaugural. It was not part of the approved program and the students involved have been suspended pending an enquiry. The college does not support or condone any activities that could harm the harmony between communities and everyone on campus knows that strict guidelines are in place in this regard."Â
Dr Sudheer M also told India Today, "We came to know about that video which was gone viral. It was a part of a dance program. Actually, students wanted to present a ghost. During that presentation, it was a few seconds and there was not one dance, there was a sequence of dances students were performing, frequently they were changing their dress and, in that process, this has come. Students wanted to present a horror dance. That was not at all the intention of hurting any of the community. Students have already apologised for this and given it in writing also. I also heard that the students themselves regretted and apologised for that particular act."
On December 9, news outlets like ANI , Hindustan Times , and Zee News  also reported the students were Muslims.
Thus, it is clear that the students seen dancing in burqas in the viral video were Muslim and not Hindu. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Dec 10, 2022 14:25 IST

title: Fact Check: Old photo from Pakistan falsely shared as woman protestor tortured by Iranian regime
content:
This 2021 photo shows a Pakistani dancer who was assaulted. Several suspects were arrested by the Peshawar police in its aftermath.
Iran reportedly hanged the anti-hijab protester Mohsen Shekari for "waging war against God" on December 8. This is the first known execution in relation to the anti-government protests, where thousands of Iranians have been demonstrating against mandatory hijab and other regressive laws in the theocratic nation.
Amid this, a photo of a woman showing her badly-bruised back has gone viral on social media. Those sharing the photo claimed the woman was a protester in Iran. One such tweet said, "Iranian female demonstrator beaten up by regime's thugs during #IranRevoIution. This is why @UN_HRC demands investigation." The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â
AFWA found that this photo is from 2021 when Wafa Khan, a dancer from Pakistan, was assaulted. AFWA PROBE
Reverse-searching the viral photo, we found it in a tweet from March 5, 2021 , that said in Urdu, "This is a dancing girl named Wafa Khan. She was called by a miscreant named Mansoor Khan in the limits of Varsak Road Police Station Machni Gate. Then they tortured him there. The police are also not registering their report."
The same account also shared other photos of the same woman where one could see the full extent of her injuries. Responding to this tweet, the Capital City Police in Peshawar, Pakistan, wrote in Urdu, "Immediate action was taken against the named accused in the incident of violence against dancer Wafa. Police force under the leadership of DSP Regi has detained 19 suspects from the house of a man named Mansoor." The Capital City Police of Peshawar have also posted photos of the arrested suspects. It stated that 19 suspects were arrested from the house of a man named Mansoor in the Mullazai village in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Upon searching, the police found arms, ammunition, liquor and other contraband in the house.Â
The Capital City Police of Peshawar have also posted photos of the arrested suspects. It stated that 19 suspects were arrested from the house of a man named Mansoor in the Mullazai village in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Upon searching, the police found arms, ammunition, liquor and other contraband in the house.Â
Many on social media had shared photos of the victim and the suspects following this. We could not find any credible news reports about the incident from Pakistani news outlets.Â
What is clear, however, is that an old photo from Pakistan is being falsely linked to the Iran protests. Â Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 10, 2022 16:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Rahul Gandhi not visit a single temple in TN and Kerala? Viral claims are only half-true
content:
While there are no records of Rahul Gandhi visiting Hindu temples in Tamil Nadu, he did visit several in Kerala during the Yatra.
The Bharat Jodo Yatra that began on September 7 from Tamil Nadu's Kanyakumari has passed through more than 40 districts in eight states as of December 9. The Yatra has received a lot of attention on both, news channels and social media. However, there has been a lot of misinformation surrounding it as well.
Recently, the Bharatiya Janata Party's Information and Technology Department head Amit Malviya took a dig at Gandhi and the Yatra. Following the Congress leader's visit to the Mahakaleshwar temple in Madhya Pradesh's Ujjain last month, Malviya wrote on Twitter, "Rahul Gandhi, son of a Catholic mother and a Parsi father, should stop this fancy dress drama in Hindi heartland. When in Kerala or TN, he never bothered to visit a single Hindu temple. Visited minority religious places though. His beliefs change depending on electoral maths."
Malviya's tweet was widely shared, with its screenshots being circulated on other social media platforms as well. Many such posts can be seen archived here , here , and here . AFWA's investigations, however, found this claim misleading. While Rahul Gandhi visited no Hindu temples in Tamil Nadu, he did visit temples in Kerala as part of the Bharat Jodo Yatra.
The Yatra began on September 7 in Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu. On the same day, Gandhi paid homage at the Vivekananda Memorial  in the city. The official Twitter account of the Congress party also shared a video from there. However, we could not find any record of Gandhi visiting Hindu temples in the state during the Yatra at all. Shri @RahulGandhi paid his respects at the Vivekananda Memorial earlier today. #BharatJodoBegins pic.twitter.com/RVQSzKdWC4 — Congress (@INCIndia) September 7, 2022 On September 10, the Yatra entered Kerala. Gandhi visited the Kannammoola Chattambi Swami temple in Thiruvananthapuram on September 12. Gandhi also met with Swamis of Sivagiri Mutt  on September 14 at Varkala, Thiruvananthapuram. Sivagiri Mutt is the shrine of Sree Narayana Guru, a social reformer who led a movement against the inequalities of the caste system. He then paid a visit to the Mata Amritanandamayi Ashram  in Vallikkavu, Kollam on September 16. On September 20, Gandhi visited the 1300-year-old Thuravoor Mahakshethram temple in Cherthala, Alappuzha. Among the artists performing Chenda Melam was Padma Shri awardee Peruvanam Kuttan Marar. Aside from these visits, Gandhi also met with pastor George Ponnaiah  at the Muttidichan Parai Church, Puliyoorkurichy in Tamil Nadu. When he met, Archbishop Thomas J Netto, Father Ujin Periera, and Pushpam Simon, Gandhi discussed the adverse living, working and economic conditions of fishermen in Thiruvananthapuram. He also visited  the Parambayam Jum'a Masjid in Aluva, Ernakulam, and the St. Francis Xavier's Forane Church in Wadakkanchery, Thrissur. Hence it is clear that such assertions are misleading. While we could not find evidence of Rahul Gandhi visiting any Hindu temples in Tamil Nadu, he did visit several in Kerala. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Dec 12, 2022 13:38 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of public flogging of woman in Afghanistan viral as recent incident
content:
This video is not recent. While it is from Afghanistan, it is at least four years old.
Since Kabul's sudden fall to the Taliban in August 2021, the fundamentalist group has imposed heavy restrictions on women. Regressive rules for women have now become the norm in Afghanistan. Incidents of gender-based violence have also risen steeply in the nation.Â
With this in the backdrop, a video of a woman being publicly flogged has been making the rounds on social media.
This video was shared with captions like, "This video was taken yesterday, I am not sure exact location! But here how terrorist #Taliban are publicly flogging a woman, while she is being beaten up by few men, you can hear (Allah ho Akabar) in the background! As disturbing as this video is, I can assure you worse things are."
The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â
AFWA found that the video is not recent. We could trace the video back to as early as 2018. AFWA PROBE
We ran a reverse search of the viral video's screengrabs. This led us to a video uploaded on February 5, 2018, to the official YouTube channel of Ariana news, a private television network based in Kabul, Afghanistan. The video's title read in Persian, 'Soraya: My mother slandered me / Police arrested 7 people on charges of Soraya field court'. As per the video's description, a woman called Soraya was beaten by her relatives in the Chah Ab district in the Takhar province. The woman claims that she had not committed any crime. Takhar police later reportedly arrested seven people for trying her in a kangaroo court and punishing her. We also found the same video on the website of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. The video story was titled "Video Shows Mob Beating Afghan Woman" and was published on February 2, 2018. As per the story, witnesses said the attack took place after clerics issued a fatwa calling for the woman to be punished for an extramarital affair. Thus, it is clear that the video of the public flogging is at least four years old and not recent at all. Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 12, 2022 21:07 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Pfizer CEO did not resign saying mRNA vaccines were unsafe
content:
This video is from March 2022. In it, he did not say that the mRNA technology was unsafe. He has also not resigned as CEO.
It's been almost three years since the Covid-19 pandemic nearly paralysed the world. With vaccinations and herd immunity, a glint of normalcy is visible on the horizon. But this hope for normalcy is seemingly being challenged by a video that's been shared widely on social media. It features Albert Bourla, the CEO of Pfizer.
Those sharing this 45-second-long video claimed that Bourla admitted that vaccines developed using mRNA technology were unsafe. These vaccines use mRNA created in a laboratory to teach our cells how to make a protein that triggers an immune response inside our bodies.Â
"Pfizer CEO Albert Burla is stepping down and now says the mRNA technology was not sufficiently proven when they launched ... He says they convinced him, but he wasn't sure. He admits it's not safe," wrote a Twitter user while sharing the video. An archived version of such a claim can be seen here . 🇺🇸 Pfizer CEO Albert Burla is stepping down and now says the mRNA technology was not sufficiently proven when they launched ... He says they convinced him, but he wasn't sure. He admits it's not safe. pic.twitter.com/1zHLQEZulZ — nikola 3 (@ronin19217435) December 10, 2022 Those sharing the video also claimed that Bourla is now stepping down as CEO. In the video, Bourla could be heard saying, "I was surprised when they suggested to me that this is the way to go, and I questioned it. And I asked them to justify how can you say something like that, but they came, and they were very, very convinced that this is the right way to go."
🇺🇸 Pfizer CEO Albert Burla is stepping down and now says the mRNA technology was not sufficiently proven when they launched ... He says they convinced him, but he wasn't sure. He admits it's not safe. pic.twitter.com/1zHLQEZulZ — nikola 3 (@ronin19217435) December 10, 2022
Those sharing the video also claimed that Bourla is now stepping down as CEO. In the video, Bourla could be heard saying, "I was surprised when they suggested to me that this is the way to go, and I questioned it. And I asked them to justify how can you say something like that, but they came, and they were very, very convinced that this is the right way to go."
He added, "They felt that the two years of work on mRNA since 2018 together with BioNTech to develop the flu vaccine made them believe that the technology is mature and we are at the cusp of delivering a product. So they convinced me. I followed my instinct that they know what they are saying. They are very good, and we made this very difficult."
AFWA's investigation found that the video was shared out of context with misleading claims. Bourla did not admit to vaccines being unsafe. Also, he had not announced his resignation from the pharmaceutical company at the time of publishing this story. AFWA ProbeÂ
At first, we looked for news reports to make sure if Albert Bourla has tendered his resignation from Pfizer, but found none. We also visited Pfizer's official website and found Bourla still listed as the Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the pharmaceutical company, making it clear that he has not stepped down. Subsequently, we searched for the source of the original video. As the logo of 'WP Live" is somehow visible at the bottom of the viral video, we ran keywords and came across the original one uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Washington Post Live. This video from March 11 was titled: "Albert Bourla on why mRNA technology was 'counterintuitive' to producing an effective vaccine." We also found a transcript of the entire interview on the Washington Post website . We searched for the relevant bit and found that Bourla was responding to the interviewer's question: " When you and your colleagues were trying to decide which route to go down, the traditional vaccine route or the mRNA route, you write that it was, quote, 'most counterintuitive to go the mRNA route,' and yet you went that route. Explain why." advertisement Bourla said, "It was counterintuitive because Pfizer was mustering on the table, had very good experience and expertise with multiple technologies that could give a vaccine, and the Novartis that some of the vaccines are, we were very good in doing that. Protein vaccines, we were very good in doing that and plus many other technologies," adding, that "mRNA was a technology, but we had less experience, only two years working on this, and actually, mRNA was a technology that never delivered a single product until that day, not vaccine, not any other medicine. So, it was very counterintuitive." Following this, the section in the viral clip begins. He concluded the answer with, "I followed my instinct that they know what they are saying, they are very good, and we made this very difficult decision at that time." Thus, it becomes clear that Bourla was admitting to the vaccines being unsafe in this video. The first mRNA vaccine was jointly developed by Pfizer and BioNTech and was approved by the FDA for emergency use in the US on December 2020. As per the FDA , mRNA or RNA is the genetic material and the vaccine contains a small piece of the SARS-CoV-2 virus's mRNA that instructs cells in the body to make the virus's distinctive "spike" protein. When a person receives this vaccine, their body produces copies of the spike protein, which does not cause disease but triggers the immune system to learn to react defensively, producing an immune response against SARS-CoV-2.   Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Dec 12, 2022 22:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Not Cyclone Mandous! This video shows 4-month-old Kerala boat accident
content:
This video shows an accident that happened in Kollam, Kerala, back in August. It has nothing to do with Cyclone Mandous.
Cyclone Mandous, which emerged from the Bay of Bengal, made its landfall in Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu, nearly 30 kilometres away from Chennai on December 9. It has since wreaked havoc in many parts of both Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, killing at least four people so far. Â
Of the many photos and videos of the cyclone on social media was a short clip of a boat being rocked by huge waves. The boat could be seen tilting because of the water's force and one person could be seen falling overboard as a result.Â
A Twitter user shared the video, writing, "High tides in Kakinada Uppada Beach due to cyclone Mandous #CycloneMandous #AndhraPradesh". Â
AFWA found that the viral video shows a boat accident that happened in August this year. It is not related to Cyclone Mandous.Â
Upon reverse searching frames from the video, we found it in an August 1 report by ETV Bharat . Per the report, the accident seen in the viral video happened at Neendakara, Kollam in Kerala. Four fishermen reportedly fell into the sea as waves rocked the boat. Later on, however, they were rescued.Â
India Today and Mathrubhumi also reported this incident at the time. This made it clear that the video is not related to the cyclone at all.Â
However, it is also true that in Kakinada, police blocked the entry of tourists on the Uppada Beach Road on December 10 because of the high tide. The Hindu reported that the local police warned that travelling on the Kakinada-Uppada road could be risky for vehicles because of unfavourable weather and weak roads being eroded by the cyclone.

title: Fact Check: Video of water overflowing out of AC vent is NOT from inside Vande Bharat Express
content:
This is a 2019 video shot inside the Bengaluru-Patna Sanghmitra Express. The issue was reportedly sorted out within hours of the video going viral.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on December 11 flagged off the sixth Vande Bharat Express that will run between Maharashtra's Nagpur and Chhattisgarh's Bilaspur. These trains, from the very beginning, have been mired in some negative press following a series of cattle accidents.Â
Now, a video allegedly showing water flooding a Vande Bharat train is being circulated on social media. In the video , water can be seen gushing out from an air conditioning vent. The person recording the video can be heard saying, "Water from the bathroom has entered the coach and soaked the luggage. The TT is here but no mechanic has come so far." The archived versions of one such post can be seen here .
AFWA found that the video is more than three years old and not from inside a Vande Bharat train. AFWA probe
The interior of the train seen in the viral video does not look like that of the Vande Bharat Express which has chair-car seating. A reverse search of the video's screengrab led us to multiple media reports from July 2019 that had carried the same video. According to a report by the Indian Express , the video was from the A-1 coach of the Bengaluru-Patna Sanghmitra Express.
The report cited videos and photos  shared by a Twitter user called @RaiSuyagya on June 29, 2019, as the source. संगमित्रा सुपर फ़ास्ट A1 का हाल, यात्री परेशान, pic.twitter.com/6pSzqKPjmB — सुयज्ञ काशी🇮🇳 (@RaiSuyagya) June 29, 2019 As per reports, the accumulation of leaves in the drain hole of the air conditioning plant and consequent water accumulation in its tray had caused the problem. Quoting a railway official, India TV  reported that the issue was resolved within two hours of the video being shared by the passenger.
संगमित्रा सुपर फ़ास्ट A1 का हाल, यात्री परेशान, pic.twitter.com/6pSzqKPjmB — सुयज्ञ काशी🇮🇳 (@RaiSuyagya) June 29, 2019
As per reports, the accumulation of leaves in the drain hole of the air conditioning plant and consequent water accumulation in its tray had caused the problem. Quoting a railway official, India TV  reported that the issue was resolved within two hours of the video being shared by the passenger.
The train returning from Patna was passing through the Nagpur section when the incident occurred.
The video in question was also uploaded to the YouTube channels of the Hindustan Times and Times of India in July 2019.
While the first Vande Bharat Express was inaugurated on February 15, 2019, from the New Delhi Railway station, it is clear that this video is not from one of those engineless trains. Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Dec 12, 2022 22:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Old videos flood social media claiming to show recent Tawang clash
content:
This video shows a brawl between Indian and Chinese soldiers in Sikkim. It has been on the internet at least since June 2020.
Indian troops foiled an incursion attempt by the Chinese army along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the Tawang sector of Arunachal Pradesh on December 9.Â
Speaking on the matter in Lok Sabha on December 13, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said that the Indian Army had resisted an attempt by China to change the status quo on the LAC and pushed back People's Liberation Army soldiers to their posts. The minister also informed the House that no Indian soldier lost his life or was seriously injured in the clash.
While no official footage of the incident has come out so far, several images and videos are floating around on social media claiming to show the recent Tawang clash. One such video  purportedly shows a brawl between Indian and Chinese soldiers at a snow-clad location. Â
In another video , we can see a Chinese soldier with a serious head injury being nursed. The archived versions of the posts can be seen here and here .
AFWA's investigation, however, found that both the videos are old and not related to the recent clash in Tawang.Â
Video 1: Clash between Indian, Chinese troops
We did a reverse search of the viral video's keyframes and found the same video was carried by multiple media organisations in June 2020.Â
According to a NDTV report published on June 22, 2020, the video was from Sikkim. It emerged a few days after a deadly face-off in Ladakh at that time. The video shows Indian and Chinese soldiers shouting and pushing at each other. We can see them saying "go back" and "don't fight ''. As per media reports, sources from the army have also confirmed the video to be genuine and from Sikkim.Â
Video 2: Chinese army nursing a wounded soldier
The second video supposedly shows the Chinese troops taking care of a badly injured soldier. We could not verify the actual time and place of this video. However, this video has been on the internet at least since February 2021.
The video had surfaced a few months after the deadly Galwan valley clash in Ladakh between the Indian and Chinese armies in which many lives were lost on both sides. The clash was one of the worst in 45 years .Â
Chinese government affiliated channel China Global Television Network (CGTN) had also published this video in 2021 claiming it to be from Galwan.
It is hence clear that both the videos are old and not related to the recent India-China clash in Tawang.

title: Fact Check: This old video from Spain DOES NOT show fans celebrating Croatia's win against Brazil
content:
The viral video does not show Croatian fans celebrating their football team's win over Brazil. It's from Pamplona, Spain, shot during the famous San Fermin festival.
Croatia defeated Brazil 4-2 in the quarter-finals of the 2022 FIFA World Cup on December 9. Following this, a video showing a large crowd celebrating on the street was shared by many who claimed it showed Croatian fans celebrating the football squad's victory. The archived version of such a tweet can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found that the video is not linked to Croatia's recent win at the FIFA World Cup in any way. This video is from Spain and is likely from 2018. AFWA Probe
Reverse-searching screengrabs from the video led us to the same video  uploaded to Imgur in July 2018. The video was titled "Croatia is ready to go." The person who shared the video, however, wrote in an update: "Edit: As pointed out by other imgurians this is not Croatia but Spain. Sorry about the incorrect info." When we checked the comments, we saw that many had pointed out that the video was from Spain's Pamplona, and showed the San Fermin Festival. The San Fermin Festival is a nine-day-long celebration held in July every year, historically rooted in the city of Pamplona, Navarre, in northern Spain. We searched for the festival on YouTube and found many such videos from 2018  that looked similar to the viral clip. A video titled in French , "Pamplona Festivities 2018: The Gaitas play in the heart of the crowd," was uploaded on July 6, 2018, to the official YouTube channel of Sud Ouest, a French daily.Â
The San Fermin Festival is a nine-day-long celebration held in July every year, historically rooted in the city of Pamplona, Navarre, in northern Spain. We searched for the festival on YouTube and found many such videos from 2018  that looked similar to the viral clip. A video titled in French , "Pamplona Festivities 2018: The Gaitas play in the heart of the crowd," was uploaded on July 6, 2018, to the official YouTube channel of Sud Ouest, a French daily.Â
We came across another video of the same performance shot from a different angle. It can be seen below.
We compared these photos with the viral video and found many similarities between them, such as a banner that read "Ohlala! Peluqueria".
Thus, it is clear that the viral video does not show Croatian fans celebrating their football team's win over Brazil. And while we could not independently verify the exact date on which the video was shot, it is clear that it is from an annual Spanish festival.
(Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Dec 14, 2022 22:25 IST

title: Fact Check: Deepika in tears amid 'Pathaan' controversy? No, old video shows her talking about depression
content:
The video is completely unrelated to the ongoing 'Pathaan' controversy. On October 10, 2018, on World Mental Health Day, Padukone opened up about her struggles with clinical depression in this video.
The Shah Rukh Khan-Deepika Padukone starrer "Pathaan" has been at the centre of outrage on social media. The film's song "Besharam Rang" has been criticised heavily by the Hindu right for featuring Padukone in an orange bikini, supposedly an insult to the Hndu religion. Amid this, a video of Padukone crying has been widely shared.Â
In that short clip, the actor can be seen crying while speaking. She said , "I do not think I was able to communicate internally what I was feeling. I knew I had this pit-ish feeling in my stomach. I knew I was scared to wake up. I did not want to wake up. I found comfort in sleep because I felt that was my escape."Â
She further said, "Like waking up in the opposite struggle. That is something I am still scared of. I do not like the sound of an alarm. I think waking up was tough. I do not want to face the day. Every day I had to wake up to something I did not enjoy that feeling of waking up to an alarm and then going to work. I think I had to do it. I was working every day. Every day was a challenge. I did not know how the day was going to pan out for me. I would be extremely conscious of being surrounded by people. If I needed to break down I did not know where I could do that."
Those sharing the video claimed that this was Padukone's reaction to the incessant trolling over the song and its music video.Â
On December 16, 2022, Samajwadi Party leader and Ex-State Minister Of Uttar Pradesh IP Singh shared the video and wrote in Hindi on Twitter, "Deepika Padukone is the daughter of Mr. Prakash Padukone and the wife of film star Mr. Ranveer. BJP and their government created an atmosphere in the country regarding the film. Now tears in her eyes... This film (Pathaan) will get fame all over the world and this film will do business for more than 500 crores." An archived version of such a post can be seen here.Â
AFWA's investigation found that the video is completely unrelated to the ongoing "Pathaan" controversy. It's from 2018, when Padukone opened up about her struggles with clinical depression on World Mental Health Day. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of the clip's keyframes led us to a video that was uploaded on the YouTube channel of The Live Love Laugh Foundation  on October 10, 2018, titled "Deepika is #NotAshamed"
In that video, at the 28-second mark, the actor can be heard saying the words she said in the viral video. Per the description of the video, Padukone had opened up about her mental health struggles. Subsequent searches led us to various news reports on this. On October 10, 2018, NDTV published a report with the headline, "On World Mental Health Day, Emotional Deepika Padukone Says She's #NotAshamed". The story also contained the same video. Time magazine , the Express Tribune , the Logical Indian  and many others reported on the video around the same time. Per these reports, on World Mental Health Day, Padukone opened up about battling depression. Thus, it's clear that the video in question has nothing to do with "Pathaan".  Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Dec 19, 2022 14:40 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Elon Musk never tweeted that ex-Pak PM Imran Khan has most 'fake' Twitter followers
content:
Musk made no such comments. In fact, we found that the Twitter CEO had never mentioned either Khan or Pakistan in any of his tweets.
Did Elon Musk declare that former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan had the maximum number of fake followers on Twitter? Well, some people on the social media site certainly seem to think so. A screenshot of a tweet allegedly made by Twitter's CEO Musk has been shared widely online .Â
It reads, "I am confirming that Pakistan's veteran cricketer Imran Khan has the largest number of fake followers on Twitter." The screenshot also contained a grab from a Twitter analytics tool that showed that more than 60 per cent of Khan's followers were fake.Â
People shared the screenshot with captions like, "More than 60 per cent of #PTI Chief #ImranKhan's followers were fake and they have been removed from his account by #Twitter after #ElonMusk's crackdown on fake accounts on bots".
The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â
AFWA found that Elon Musk did not tweet any such thing. Â AFWA PROBE
The date of the tweet in the viral screenshot appeared to be December 13. So, we did a thorough scan of Musk's Twitter timeline but didn't find any tweet about Khan or an analysis of his followers on the site.
We also checked the archived version of Musk's Twitter account in the event he had deleted the tweet. We found nothing there as well. Using Twitter advanced search, we found that Musk has never mentioned either " Imran Khan " or " Pakistan " in any of his tweets.  Â
Additionally, had Musk made such a comment, it would certainly have been covered by mainstream media outlets. We found no news reports about this.Â
After examining different Twitter follower analysis tools, we found that the photo in the viral tweet was from Sparktoro , an audience research tool. We used this tool to analyse Khan's Twitter followers and it showed that 62.1 per cent of his followers on Twitter were supposedly "fake" — bots, spam accounts, inactive users, propaganda, or other non-engaged/non-real users. This number was close to that in the viral screenshot. However, there is more than meets the eye.  Another tool Follower Audit showed that Khan has just 2.7 per cent fake followers. What causes this disparity? It is important to note that each Twitter analysis tool has its own definition of fake accounts. They use a plethora of factors to decide whether an account is fake or not. For example, accounts which have been inactive for a certain period of time, or accounts with a suspiciously small number of followers can be part of the calculation. However, this does not necessarily mean that all such Twitter accounts are "fake". Additionally, Sparktoro audits a sample of 2,000 random followers for any given account and runs diagnostics on them. This sample size is often too small to provide any meaningful insight into the actual number of fake followers one may have. It is noteworthy that a few months back, several news outlets had reported that around 70 per cent of Musk's followers on Twitter were "fake", based on audits done using Sparktoro. advertisement Thus, to sum up, Musk did not tweet about Khan or his followers on Twitter. The viral screenshot is a doctored one. (With inputs from Ashish Kumar) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Dec 19, 2022 17:07 IST

title: Fact Check: 2018 pic wrongly shared as Ronaldo watching FIFA World Cup final in Qatar
content:
This 2018 image shows Ronaldo and his girlfriend Georgina Rodriguez watching a UEFA Champions League match in Turin, Italy.
Lionel Messi led Argentina to a remarkable victory against France in the FIFA World Cup 2022 final on December 18 at the Lusail Stadium in Qatar. Soon after, "Ronaldo" began trending on Twitter, with many claiming that Messi has finally put an end to the most talked-about debate in football: who is the GOAT (Greatest of all time) soccer player?
Meanwhile, a photo was widely shared online showed a seemingly-unhappy Cristiano Ronaldo watching the final at the venue.Â
AFWA found that this photo is from 2018 and shows Ronaldo watching a UEFA Champions League match in Italy. AFWA PROBE
Using reverse search, we found this photo on Getty Images . According to its description there, this photo from on October 2, 2018, shows Ronaldo and his girlfriend Georgina Rodriguez watching the Group H match of the UEFA Champions League between Juventus and BSC Young Boys at the Allianz Stadium in Turin, Italy. Several news websites also carried this photo in their 2018 reports.Â
Reportedly, Ronaldo and his family left Qatar soon after the Portugal football squad's exit from the FIFA World Cup 2022. As per news reports , the soccer star was spotted training in the Spanish capital of Madrid after leaving Qatar. Following this, he also reportedly visited Dubai to step up his search for a new club. We found no reports of Ronaldo arriving in Qatar to watch the FIFA World Cup 2022 finals.Â
The 37-year-old left the Manchester United football club in November after an explosive TV interview where he criticised the club's manager Erik ten Hag and other club administrators. Since then, he has been searching for a home. Â
Thus, it's clear that a 2018 photo is being falsely shared as Ronaldo watching the FIFA World Cup 2022 final in Qatar.    Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 19, 2022 19:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Cristiano Ronaldo throwing reporter's mic is from 2016, NOT related to World Cup
content:
This is a 2016 video from Lyon in France. At the time of writing this story, Ronaldo did not comment on Argentina's victory.
Argentina's nail-biting victory against France in the FIFA World Cup final on December 18 has the team's fans across the world celebrating, and how. Amid this, a video of Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo throwing a reporter's microphone into a lake , allegedly his reaction to Argentina's win, has gone viral on social media. The Ronaldo-led Portugal squad crashed out of the 2022 World Cup in the quarter-final match against Morocco. The archived version of the post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found that the video is years old and not related to the 2022 FIFA World Cup at all. AFWA Probe
Multiple people on Twitter pointed out that the video in question was old. With the help of a keyword search, we found the same video carried by media organisations including the BBC  and The Guardian in June 2016.Â
Per the news reports, this video is from Lyon in France. The incident happened when Ronaldo was on a morning team walk, just hours before Portugal's final Euro 2016 Group F game against Hungary. A reporter from the Portuguese media outlet Correio da Manha approached Ronaldo and asked whether he was prepared for the day's match. Ronaldo, who was visibly frustrated, grabbed the reporter's microphone and threw it into a nearby lake. Reports also said the soccer player's frustrations stemmed from his poor performance in the opening games.Â
Meanwhile, Ronaldo has so far not made any comments  on Argentina's victory. The soccer player has also refrained from publicly congratulating his rival, Lionel Messi. It is hence clear that the video in question is more than six years old and does not show Ronaldo's reaction to Argentina's win in the FIFA World Cup. Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Dec 19, 2022 21:42 IST

title: Fact Check: This 5-year-old video shows a Maratha Kranti Morcha rally, NOT the MVA's recent march
content:
This video is more than five years old. On August 9, 2017, the Maratha Kranti Morcha staged a protest rally in Mumbai. This video shows that.
Hundreds joined the Maha Vikas Aghadi's Halla Bol rally on December 17, marching and raising slogans against the Eknath Shinde government, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, rising prices, and more. The rally was led by Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, Leader of Opposition in the state Assembly, the Nationalist Congress Party's Ajit Pawar, and state president of the Indian National Congress Nana Patole. Many other leaders from these parties and other factions participated as well. Following the march, Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis called it a " nano morcha ", implying poor turnout at the rally. In retaliation, many on social media shared a short clip of what the rally allegedly looked like . People shared the video, where a sea of people could be seen marching on a flyover, with captions like, "This is the one, Devendra Fadnavis is trolling as Nano Morcha! This is the voice of Maharashtra lovers. Devendra ji. This behavior is not good. Jai Maharashtra!" On December 18, the Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Raut also shared the same video on Twitter and wrote, "This is what Devendra Fadnavis is calling Nano Morcha! The loud voice of the loving people of Maharashtra. Devendra ji.. this behavior is not good. Jai Maharashtra!" The archived version of this tweet can be seen here . AFWA's investigation found that the video was on social media from 2017. In August 2017, the Maratha Kranti Morcha staged a protest rally in Mumbai, the shared video is from there. AFWA Probe A reverse search of the clip's keyframes led us to the same video shared on Instagram . On August 9, 2017, on the same day, this clip was also posted on the Facebook group " Maratha Kranti Morcha Maharashtra" , which has almost three lakh followers. It was captioned, "J J Flyover Mumbai, Maratha Sagar." We compared the two videos and found many similarities between them. Thus, it became clear that this video has been on social media since as early as August 2017.  Subsequently, a keyword search online led us to media reports from the same time that contained similar videos and photos. On August 9, 2017, a similar video was posted by  TOI Plus's Twitter account , with the caption, "#MarathaKrantiMorcha: The community members chanting slogans as they pass-by the JJ flyover." Other news outlets like the Financial Express , and Firstpost published reports that carried similar images. The news agency Associated Press also published a similar photo on August 9, 2017 , with the description, "Members of Maratha Kranti Morcha or Maratha Revolutionary Front take out a silent march in Mumbai, India, Wednesday, Aug. 9, 2017. Tens of thousands of people waving saffron flags are marching through Mumbai demanding quotas in government jobs and education for the Maratha community in western India." Thus, it is clear that the viral video has no link with the MVA's recent protest rally. Published By: Ritika Shah Published On: Dec 20, 2022 15:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Underwater Messi cut-out is not from Kerala at all - It's from Lakshadweep
content:
The cut-out was installed underwater by Argentina fans in Kavaratti, Lakshadweep. All participants were locals, as per Mohammed Swadikh, a vlogger who organised this.
Ahead of the 2022 FIFA World Cup, football fans in Kerala adorned streets in the state with cut-outs of famous soccer players. In fact, so famous were these cut-outs of players like Neymar Jr, Cristiano Ronaldo, and Lionel Messi, that even the official Twitter account of FIFA  gave the state a shout-out.Â
Following Argentina's victory over France in the World Cup final, a video of one such cut-out went viral. And for good reason. The video supposedly shows fans of the Argentine squad in Kerala placing a cut-out of Lionel Messi underwater. It was shared  with captions like, "Kerala's (India) Craziest Football fans have proved it again… They had promised if #Argentina reaches the Finals, they'll place Messi's cutout under the sea among reefs and they did it… I think #Messi should visit Kerala."
AFWA's investigation found that this video is from Kavaratti, Lakshadweep, not from Kerala. AFWA PROBE  Â
We reverse-searched keyframes from the viral video and that led us to several news reports about it. According to the New Indian Express , this video was shot at Kavaratti in Lakshadweep by Mohammed Swadikh, a physical education teacher, vlogger, and a fan of Messi and the Argentine football squad. Before the semifinal match between Argentina and Croatia, Swadikh declared on social media  "If my team wins, I'll plant a Lionel Messi cut-out in the sea." And he kept his word. Per the report, Swadikh sought the help of the Lakshadweep Scuba Adventure team, a group of 15, who organise scuba diving for tourists who visit the island. To further clarify this, AFWA spoke to Mohammed Swadikh. He said. "I was born and brought up in Lakshadweep. We depend on Kerala for education, treatment and to buy things. I have done my graduation from MES College in Aluva, Kerala. The team that was involved with me to install Messi's cut-out comprise natives of Lakshadweep. Only local people from Lakshadweep participated in this and no Keralites were involved with us." He further said, "After my team [Argentina] reached the final, with the help of Ammathi Scuba and Lakshadweep adventures we took Messi's four-metre-high cut-out to the Wall of Wonder area and installed it among the rocks and coral reefs," adding that they had "arranged many programmes to welcome the FIFA World Cup. We erected cut-outs of Messi, Neymar and Ronaldo. Every time we want to do something special, we have done it." It is worth noting that some news organisations, including India Today  and Business Today  had erroneously reported that this video was from Kerala. This error has been rectified since. So, while Kerala has its fair share of enthusiastic football fans (and Argentina fans in particular), this feat was carried out by fans of Messi in Lakshadweep.    Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Dec 20, 2022 20:10 IST

title: Fact Check: This terrifying video of a giant wave is from Durban, BUT it's 5 years old!
content:
This video is from Durban but was shot on March 12, 2017, when a gigantic wave hit the city. No casualties were reported at the time.
A large wave reportedly  killed at least three people and injured over a dozen in South Africa's Durban on December 17. According to reports, the beach was full of people when a "freak wave" hit it. In its aftermath, a video  of a gigantic wave crashing into a beach has been making the rounds on social media. People on Twitter and Facebook who shared this video  claimed it showed the aforementioned freak wave that hit Durban. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The viral video , supposedly recorded from a high-rise building, showed people running away from the coast as a massive wave crashed into the beach. An archived version of such a post can be seen here.  AFWA's investigation found that this video is more than five-years-old. AFWA PROBE Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip uploaded to a YouTube channel called "Sun Newspapers"  on March 12, 2017, making it clear that the viral video was unrelated to the recent incident. The video was titled, "Durban beach closed due to high waves DRAMATIC AERIAL VIDEO."
In its aftermath, a video  of a gigantic wave crashing into a beach has been making the rounds on social media. People on Twitter and Facebook who shared this video  claimed it showed the aforementioned freak wave that hit Durban.Â
The viral video , supposedly recorded from a high-rise building, showed people running away from the coast as a massive wave crashed into the beach. An archived version of such a post can be seen here. Â
AFWA's investigation found that this video is more than five-years-old. AFWA PROBE
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip uploaded to a YouTube channel called "Sun Newspapers"  on March 12, 2017, making it clear that the viral video was unrelated to the recent incident. The video was titled, "Durban beach closed due to high waves DRAMATIC AERIAL VIDEO."
We also found a screenshot of the same video featured in a South African news report  published on March 12, 2017. It mentioned that cyclonic weather in Madagascar caused havoc along Durban's North Beach, forcing the authorities to shut the beach. However, no casualties were reported at the time. IS IT REALLY FROM DURBAN?  As we did not find any concrete evidence from leading media sources to prove the authenticity of the location, we tried to geo-locate the spot seen in the viral video. As a round swimming pool and a causeway were clearly visible in the video, we tried locating them in Google Maps. While searching for the exact location in Google Maps, we came across a similar-looking round pool on the coast of the Durban beach near Durban Funworld , an amusement park. We also noticed a causeway and palm trees on the beach that appeared similar to the visuals in the viral video. These similarities, as illustrated in the image below, helped us conclude that this beach was indeed in Durban. Thus, it is clear that while this terrifying video is from Durban in South Africa, it's not recent at all. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Dec 20, 2022 23:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Don't touch this "Jio scratch card" hoping for a free gift - you'll end up scratching your head in despair
content:
This is an imposter website. Reliance Jio is not running any such scheme.
If an offer looks too good to be true, it's most likely just that - fake.
Is Reliance Jio giving away Rs 999 to everyone on the occasion of their seventh anniversary? Well, you may have already guessed it's junk. But if you think, this is one of those numerous fraudulent websites which cast their net on social media hoping to scrape some personal data - read on. This one is much more serious. If you're not careful, you may actually end up paying Rs.999 to the fraudster.Â
Also Read |Â Bulldozers will run in Bengal like UP: Suvendu Adhikari
The offer floating around, looks genuine at first glance. It is in the form of a scratch card, complete with the logo of Jio, a photo of Mukesh Ambani saying Jio has completed seven years, and a promise of Rs 999 gift. All you need to do to get lucky, is to scratch the card and claim your prize.
As soon as you scratch the card, it congratulates you for winning Rs.999. If you do not want to take the risk of navigating through a fraudulent website, find below the screen recording to see how it actually looks and what happens next.
Ultimately, the offer card wants you to "click here to transfer the prize money into your account". The moment you click on it, you end up being redirected to the Paytm app (if you've the app already installed on your phone). But we'll come back to it later on. Let's first try to peek at what happens behind the scenes.
Also Read |Â States ramp up Covid protocols as China case surge puts India on alert
If you pay attention to the url before the offer opens the Paytm app, you can see that the address looks somewhat weird. The url of the website is ' cartbag.xyz '. Why on earth would Jio use this url for any of their offers? First red flag. You will also notice that the website has been designed to work properly only on mobile phones and the links don't work properly if you open it on a computer. There are two reasons for that. First, you don't install Paytm on your computer where the links want to redirect you. Second, it's easy to investigate a weblink on a computer.
The archived version of this website can be seen here .Â
It is important to note that the website 'cartbag.xyz' uses the same royal blue color scheme as the official Jio website jio.com . That could be one of the reasons many people are assuming this to be a genuine offer and sharing it on WhatsApp as well as Facebook .Â
What does the website ' cartbag.xyz ' reveal:
We found that the website was created barely three months ago. Disposing a fraudulent website soon after duping people is a common practice. According to GoDaddy Whois , the domain 'cartbag.xyz' was created on September 26, 2022. Here is the trap: Assuming that you fell for the bait and clicked the link to "transfer Rs.999 into your bank account", this is how things unfold. As we discussed earlier, it automatically opens the Paytm app installed on your phone. You'll notice, the amount is pre-filled with 'Rs. 999'. Just below the amount, a message deceptively says,"TRANSFER-TO-YOUR-BANK'. The moment someone punches their four-digit UPI pin - just the opposite happens. You end up paying Rs 999 to one "Lakhi Mallick". Also Read | Rishab Shetty's Kantara sent for Oscars nomination, confirms Hombale Productions | Exclusive Wondering who Lakhi Mallick is? We managed to unmask the conman - at least partially. We have all been warned by our banks that we DO NOT need to punch the secret UPI pin to "receive money". It is not difficult to imagine there would be many gullible people falling into this cleverly laid trap. advertisement The man/woman behind the scam: Hidden within the link, which directs you to the Paytm app and opens the payment window, is the UPI ID where the payment is going in case you made the mistake of keying your UPI pin. Also Read | Jet Airways CEO tweets in support of IndiGo air hostess who stood up to rude passenger on flight The ID is  '8327049816@okbizaxis'. The name associated with this Id is 'Lakhi Repair Shop'. The  blue tick along with the name indicates that it is a verified account  which has completed the KYC process . As per the ' National Payment Corporation Of India ' '@okbizaxis' is the format of Google Pay UPI Ids. We cross-checked on Google pay and found that the UPI ID '8327049816@okbizaxis' is indeed associated with "Lakhi Repair Shop". We further scrutinized the phone number '8327049816' through Paytm and True caller apps. This is most probably a Vodafone Idea (Vi) number registered in West Bengal & Andaman Nicobar circle. According to Paytm, this No. and the associated account belong to one Lakhi Mallick. advertisement By the way, Jio is not celebrating its seventh anniversary. It completed six years on September 5 this year. Obviously, there is no such free gift offer on the official website of Jio. And the only person getting lucky by scratching the card is the conman - Lakhi Mallick.
