title: PM Modi wore traditional Khasi attire in Shillong - photo of similar women's dress is morphed!
content:
Modi was wearing a traditional Khasi outfit along with a traditional Garo hat during his Meghalaya visit. The photo of the woman shared along with the post was digitally altered.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's attires, especially some of the more exotic ones, have always made the news.
When Modi visited Shillong, Meghalaya  on December 18 to inaugurate various projects, his outfit, once again, was at the centre of the coverage. The PM has always made his attires part of his political messaging, and this time, he wore a traditional Khasi outfit along with a traditional Garo hat to show his respect for both the main tribes of the state.
Of course, Modi's outfits have also often been the object of mockery by his critics. So, following the Meghalaya visit, people started sharing a photo  that supposedly showed the listing of Modi's attire on an e-commerce platform.Â
To add to the mockery, those sharing the photo suggested that Modi wore a women's outfit. These posts juxtaposed a photo of Modi in the aforementioned attire with a similar-looking dress  that cost $35. It also contained the description, "Multi Floral Embroidered Dress."
The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here  and here .
AFWA's investigation found that this photo was digitally altered. The dress listed on the clothing website was digitally replaced with Modi's attire to falsely imply Modi wore women's clothing.Â
We found several people  reacting to the tweets claiming the image of the woman was digitally altered .
We noticed multiple creases on the outfit worn by Modi in the viral photo. Identical creases could be seen on the listed dress as well. The dress in the latter photo also had blurry edges, hinting at some digital alterations.Â
A search for "Multi Floral Embroidered Dress" on Google led us to the website for Shoreline Wear , a company that has its registered offices  in the US but claims to manufacture "products from competitive Asian markets."
The product that we found was a black dress with floral embroidery that cost $35. When we compared the photo on the website with the viral image, we found that the original product's neckline was visible in the viral photo.
Thus, we concluded that the attire in Modi's photo was cut and added to this product digitally.Â
It's noteworthy that following Modi's Shillong visit, former cricketer and Trinamool Congress leader Kirti Azad mocked the PM , saying that he was "neither male nor female". This comment earned Azad a lot of flak, who then said that he did not intend to disrespect the attire and was only commenting on Modi's "fashion".Â
(With inputs from Ashish Kumar) Published By: Vani Mehrotra Published On: Dec 22, 2022 19:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Not Muslims performing namaz on streets in France, this video shows climate activists protesting
content:
This video from Paris shows environmental activists being forcefully removed for blocking traffic.
A video shows a group of people wearing reflective vests sitting in the middle of the road, blocking the traffic. Soon, they were seen being forcefully dragged away by a bunch of people. This video was shared on social media by many, who claimed it showed people in France forcefully removing Muslims who were praying in the middle of the road. It was by the former governor of Meghalaya, Tathagata Roy, who later deleted it.Â
Right-wing activist and scholar Madhu Purnima Kishwar  also tweeted the same video asserting the same. Kishwar wrote, "France. People are getting down from their cars& clearing roads occupied by the Namazis. Govts in all democracies are cowardly coz they're held hostage by vote banks. Citizen action alone can save us from lethal spread of MuzzBees." The archived version of such posts can be seen here  and here. Â
AFWA's investigation found that the video is from a protest organised by environmental activists in Paris. It does not show Muslims blocking traffic while performing namaz.  AFWA PROBE Â
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a report by the Daily Express  that contained the same video. As per this report published on December 2, the video shows drivers in Paris dragging climate activists off the road on the Levallois bridge in Levallois-Perret. The activist group was identified as "Dernière Rénovation" (Last Renovation) and they were reportedly demanding thermal renovation of buildings in Paris. The protesters brought traffic to a standstill and earned the wrath of commuters. A subsequent search led us to multiple reports  about the incident that used the same video or screenshots from it. Several people on Twitter also shared the same video in early December, calling it an environmental protest. HOW-TO: French drivers show how to safely remove climate activists from major roadways. pic.twitter.com/NvPpUXXtVS — Hananya Naftali (@HananyaNaftali) December 3, 2022 We also found several media report  from France about members of Dernière Rénovation blocking roads at several places while protesting. The group  has demanded the French government ensure better building insulation, which it said could massively cut carbon emissions in the country. It is hence clear that the video in question does not show Muslims in France being removed for performing namaz in the middle of the road. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Dec 22, 2022 23:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Butt obviously, the viral pic of Biden 'groping' Zelenskyy is bad photoshop
content:
This photo has been digitally altered. In the original image shared by First Lady Jill Biden, the US President's hand can be clearly seen resting on Zelenskyy's back.
On December 21, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the White House, where he met with US President Biden and First Lady Jill Biden. This historic moment - Zelenskyy leaving war-torn Ukraine for the first time since Russia's invasion - drew the attention of the international press.Â
Unlike other world leaders, the Ukrainian president arrived at the White House dressed in his usual green military fatigues sweatshirt, a de facto uniform for Zelenskyy. But it wasn't just his attire that grabbed eyeballs.
 A picture  that made people scratch their heads, and has been shared widely across social media, showed Zelenskyy flanked by the Bidens as they faced the press. The photo shot from behind, showed President Biden's hand resting on the Ukrainian commander's buttocks. In fact, it looked like Biden was grabbing Zelenskyy.Â
The photo was accompanied by many suggestive remarks. One such tweet read, "So that's why Zelensky was pulling a vinegar face yesterday. I guess Biden thinks that $44 billion buys him exclusive groping rights."
Biden's reputation, when it comes to being "handsy", precedes him. Both the right-wing and the liberal press in the US have noted Biden's habit of touching people. So, was this incident yet another such example? Not really.
AFWA's investigation found that the photo in question was digitally altered.
We first looked for photos of Zelenskyy's White House visit in the Associated Press and Reuters . All the photos from this particular interaction were taken from the front.Â
Subsequently, we reverse-searched the photo and found it was originally shared  from the official Twitter account of the First Lady of the United States. However, the original photo had one key difference. Biden's hand here appeared to be resting on Zelenskyy's back, not his rear. In fact, Jill Biden's hand placed right above also touched her husband's hand. President Zelenskyy, we hope you take our love and support back to Olena and your children, and all the families of Ukraine. 💕 pic.twitter.com/z1uqAAl8B8 — Jill Biden (@FLOTUS) December 22, 2022
President Zelenskyy, we hope you take our love and support back to Olena and your children, and all the families of Ukraine. 💕 pic.twitter.com/z1uqAAl8B8 — Jill Biden (@FLOTUS) December 22, 2022
Following this, we compared both photos to examine if they were indeed the same. We noticed a bunch of similarities, including the pattern of creases on Biden's sleeve and Zelenskyy's sweatshirt. All three of them appeared to be in the same posture. Photographers visible, though out of focus, in front of them also appeared to be in the exact same positions in both photos. The shadows of all three also appeared to be the same. Then, we focussed on Biden's arm in both photos because, in the viral photo, the arm in question looked slightly awkward. In the original one, Biden's thumb appeared beneath the First Lady's hand. In the viral one, a portion of Biden's thumb is still visible between his wife's fingers. If you look closely, you can see that the tip of Biden's thumb is missing in the photo where his hand is on Zelenskyy's butt. We also compared the length of the US Commander-in-Chief's arms in both photos and noticed that in the viral photo, it was visibly (and unnaturally) longer. This made it clear that the viral photo was digitally altered. And pretty badly, at that. Behind the scenes However, we can't be sure whether Biden's hands could have brushed against Zelenskyy's rear at some point during this event. We found a video  of the interaction shared by the official Twitter account of the cable news network C-SPAN. It's shot from various angles barring from the back. The moment where Zelenskyy and Jill Biden face each other, while Mr and Mrs Biden placed their hands on the Ukrainian leader's back appears at the 40-second mark. President Biden and first lady Jill Biden welcome Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky ( @ZelenskyyUa ) to the White House on his first foreign trip since the Russian invasion. pic.twitter.com/OhKxek3oQM — CSPAN (@cspan) December 21, 2022 advertisement While it is clear from the position and level of Joe Biden's arm that his hand was on Zelenskyy's back at the time, there are several moments in the video where Biden's hand is not visible at all. Judging by the position of the security guards in the viral photo, and comparing them with what is visible in the video, the photo was likely taken from inside the doors behind them by a White House photographer. Given that the photo was shared by the First Lady, and that no other photos from that angle, even if Biden's hand touched the Ukrainian leader's buttocks, the White House would not release such a photo. title: Fact Check: Don't fall for viral pic of Zelenskyy's wife sporting Gucci, Rolex, and LV in a jet, it's fake
content:
This photo is morphed. The original picture is of Richard Heart, a popular cryptocurrency influencer and YouTuber. Olena's face was digitally added to the photo.
"It warms the heart knowing that billions of our hard-earned tax dollars are going towards good causes this holiday season", read a tweet sharing the photo of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's wife Olena. The First Lady of Ukraine, in the viral photo, could be seen sitting alone in a private jet. In the photo, Olena sported a vest and jogging pants that people claimed were from Gucci, a Rolex watch, and a suspected Louis Vuitton bag.
Those sharing the viral photo criticised Olena's extravagant attire, calling it inappropriate for the wife of a war-torn country's president who has been seeking international help.
One Twitter user wrote , "Olena went for the eccentric homeless look with an oligarch's budget. Goes to show how cringe these people are. Having a blast while their people are dying. Disgusting."
The archive of such posts can be found here and here .Â
AFWA found that this photo is morphed. The original photo is of Richard Heart. Olena's face was photoshopped to it. AFWA PROBE
A reverse search of the viral photo took us to a tweet from November 20. The Twitter thread, which was about a big shot from the cryptocurrency space, contained a photo very similar to the viral one. In terms of the person's attire, accessories, and background in the photograph, everything appeared to be the same except for one thing — the face. As it turns out, the person in the original photo is Richard Heart, the founder of HEX Crypto.Â
Further searches led us to the same picture tweeted by Heart on August 19, while replying to Cory Klippsten, the CEO of a Bitcoin financial services firm Swan. A comparison of the original picture tweeted by Heart with the viral one can be seen below.
The same day, Heart tweeted another photo of himself in the same attire and location. Also, the cover photo of his Twitter profile features him holding the same bag.Â
Richard Heart is a popular crypto influencer and YouTuber . He is the founder of the Ethereum-based crypto token HEX. According to his website , Heart owns the world's largest cut diamond called "The Enigma", the quickest Ferrari, and the most expensive Rolex ever made.Â
Olena Zelenska went for a two-day visit to the French Republic where she held a meeting with the First Lady of France Brigitte Macron, on December 13. This was her first international visit since the Russia-Ukraine war began. She was also joined by Ukrainian Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal among other Ukrainian officials. There, about 70 countries and institutions worldwide pledged more than 1 billion euros ($1.05 billion) in immediate aid to help Ukraine get through a harsh winter.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Dec 23, 2022 21:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Ex-Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal NOT arrested for child porn, satire goes viral
content:
The article being shared is from a satirical news website. A note at the end of the article states that there is no truth to it.
Billionaire Elon Musk is actively looking  for a new Chief Executive Officer for Twitter after a clear majority of users voted for him to step down in a poll conducted by him. Ever since he announced  the golden vacancy on December 21, renowned personalities  ranging from popular YouTuber MrBeast to VA Shiva Ayyadurai, the holder of the first US Copyright for email, started applying  for the role.Â
Amid speculations about the next Twitter boss, a purported news article  about a former CEO of the social media website has been widely shared, leaving many enraged. "Former Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal arrested for child porn", read the headline of the viral screenshot . The report also went on to state that the arrest was made after a tip-off from Musk.Â
AFWA found this article was published on vancouvertimes.org , a satire news website. AFWA PROBE Â
We noticed that people called this "news report"  false, with some even claiming this was from a satire news website . We then looked for news about Agrawal's arrest but could not find any media reports related to this. Some people had also shared the link to this supposed news report . Upon visiting the website of "Vancouver Times", we noticed a note at the bottom of the article, stating that it was satirical. It further read, "To ease confusion, the article has been added to the satire section, and a note has been added to the bottom of the article." We checked the "About Us" page of the Vancouver Times  which stated that it was a satirical website. The site said, "Vancouver Times is the most trusted source for satire on the West Coast. We write satirical stories about issues that affect conservatives." The website's "Disclaimer"  page stated that it took no responsibility for the accuracy of the information it shared. "All information in the Service is provided 'as is', with no guarantee of completeness, accuracy, timeliness or of the results obtained from the use of this information," it said. Twitter's battle to suppress the spread of child sexual abuse on its site predates Musk's takeover. In 2021, a civil suit was filed  against Twitter for allegedly refusing to act and take down the child sexual abuse material on behalf of a minor claiming that the site made money off it. On December 16, the Senate Judiciary Committee Chair Dick Durbin sent a letter  to Musk, seeking answers within a fortnight about the platform's plan to stop the spread of child abuse material. title: Fact Check: Did Kanhaiya Kumar call Rahul Gandhi a fool? Video viral with MISLEADING context
content:
Kanhaiya Kumar did not call Rahul Gandhi a fool. Kumar was talking about the BJP when he made the remarks and soon after praised Rahul Gandhi as well.
The highly transmissible BF.7 strain of the Omicron variant of Covid-19 seems to be behind the latest surge in infection globally. India logged 196 new coronavirus cases, with active cases increasing to 3,428, the Union Health Ministry notified on December 26.
Amid fears about another wave of infections in India, Congress and the ruling Bhartiya Janta Party have been locking the horn over the ongoing Bharat Jodo Yatra led by Rahul Gandhi . Now, a video of Gandhi and the Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar  has been shared by many on social media. In that 30-second-long clip, Gandhi can be heard saying in Hindi, "They are framing new excuses to stop the Yatra. They are saying: wear the mask, stop the Yatra, Covid-19 cases are rising again. All these are silly excuses." This is followed by a video of Kumar saying in Hindi, "Someone please explain to these fools that Corona is not an excuse, it is a disease."Â
Those sharing the video  claimed that Kumar was calling Gandhi a fool . Archives of such tweets can be seen here and here .Â
AFWA's investigation found that in the original videos, both Congress leaders were targeting the BJP and the Centre.Â

The tweet read "...It's their (BJP) new idea, they wrote a letter to me saying COVID is coming & stop the Yatra. Responding to that letter, Gandhi hit back at the BJP and Cente and said, "They (the BJP) are scared".Â
On December 23, a video of Kanhaiya Kumar's speech was uploaded to Times Now's official YouTube channel with the title, "Kanhaiya Kumar Mocks COVID-19 Norms | Calls Centre's Advisory A Bid To Derail Bharat Jodo Yatra." At the 20-second mark, the Congress leader can be seen targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and saying "He (Prime Minister Narendra Modi) does not wear a mask while addressing any gathering. During the delta variant, he went to West Bengal for election but did not wear a mask. On the other hand, when he has online meetings with Chief Ministers on Zoom Calls, he puts a mask on his face. He thinks people are fools. Now they bring new excuses. Someone, please explain to these fools that Corona is not an excuse, it is a disease. It is a childish excuse. Rahul Gandhi was the first leader in this country who wrote a letter to the Government about this disease."       Â
On the same day, The Quint and The Telegraph also reported on Kumar's statement. Both reports noted that Kumar was targeting the BJP.Â
Thus, it is clear that Kanhaiya Kumar did not call Rahul Gandhi a fool. He was talking about the BJP-led Centre.

title: Fact Check: This video of ransacked Walmart is old, and NOT from blizzard-hit New York state
content:
This is a 2020 video from Pennsylvania's Philadelphia. While there were two incidents of looting in Buffalo, the video in question is not from New York state.
At least 60 lives have been lost in weather-related incidents, according to news reports, following a blizzard in the US. The death toll of confirmed storm-related deaths reached 27 in Buffalo on December 27. Fatalities reportedly included cases of people found in snow banks and in cars or who had died from cardiac stress while ploughing or blowing snow. According to a viral social media post , taking advantage of the blizzard which pummeled western New York, a people looted a Walmart store. The video  showed the interior of a flooded store, left almost in shambles, with damaged goods and shelves. AFWA's investigation, however, found that the video is more than two years old and not from Buffalo, New York. AFWA probe As per local news reports , the New York State Police confirmed two incidents of retail shop looting in Buffalo amid the December 25 storm. But is the viral video from Buffalo? A keyword search about looting incidents in Walmart led us to similar videos of what appears to be the same store uploaded to multiple YouTube channels  in October 2020. Per the description provided by these channels, the video was from a Walmart in Pennsylvania's Philadelphia. We compared the viral video with the 2020 videos. We noticed several similarities, like the flooded floor and the kind of debris and the placement of wares on shelves. We also found several news reports  about this incident of ransacking from 2020. According to Reuters , two nights of violent unrest and looting took place in west Philadelphia after Walter Wallace Jr, a Black man armed with a knife, was gunned down by law enforcement. According to his relatives, the man was suffering from bipolar disorder. Following the incident, hundreds of people marched across the city demanding racial justice. It is hence clear that while there were two incidents of looting in Buffalo, the video in question is old and not from New York state. Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: Dec 27, 2022 14:42 IST

title: Fact Check: This boy is not a Russia-Ukraine war survivor, Ukrainian MP shares years old and unrelated photo
content:
This photograph is at least a decade old and not related to the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine.
The Russia-Ukraine war is about to enter a new calendar year. Peace between the two nations, however, remains elusive. Since the beginning of Russia's invasion in February 2022, social media has been flooded with videos and photos of the devastation caused by the war, especially its human cost. Photos of Ukrainian children, in particular, have been shared very widely. Of course, not all photos such as these are from Ukraine. And in this story, we will debunk one such photo shared on Twitter  by Ukrainian MP Lesia Vasylenko. Vasylenko tweeted a picture of a boy with a torn t-shirt and bruises and dirt on his face. She claimed that the child is an eight-year-old named Marc, who recently survived a Russian artillery attack in Ukraine. At the time of filing this story, the post had received more than 11,500 retweets. The archived version of the post can be seen here . Screenshots of Vasylenko's tweet  were also shared by many on Facebook . AFWA's investigation, however, found that the photo is around a decade old and not related to the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. AFWA probe Multiple people responded to Vasylenko's tweet, stating the photo was old. A reverse search of the boy's photograph led us to social media posts from April 2022. These posts, too, claimed the photograph was of a Ukrainian victim of Russia's invasion.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Orthodox Wisdom (@orthodox_wisdom) Around the same time, several people on Twitter pointed out that the photo of the boy was very old, and said that it was used by Irish author Christina McKenna on her book's cover. Searching further, we found the photo in a video uploaded to YouTube in October 2014. In this video, we found the boy's photo on the cover of the Spanish translation of McKenna's book "The Misremembered Man" — (El Hombre En El Olvido). The 2008 novel is set in Northern Ireland. We found the same cover photo on an Amazon listing  for the book as well. We also searched for the photograph on TinEye. As per TinEye , the photo first appeared on Flickr in March 2012. However, the photo is no longer available on the Flickr accounts mentioned by TinEye. While the source of the photograph is unclear, it is clear that it is at least around a decade old and not related to the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Dec 28, 2022 15:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Videos from 2015 earthquake viral as latest Nepal tremors caught in camera
content:
Although the first video is from Nepal, it dates back to 2015. The other clips are old and not from Nepal at all.
Two earthquakes  of magnitude 4.7 and 5.3 jolted Nepal in the early hours of December 28. While no loss of lives or property has been reported yet, social media has already seen a bunch of shocking videos that supposedly caught the natural disaster in action. One such video  shared by many on Twitter  features three clips showing tremours caught on camera. Powerful #Earthquake at #Nepal , I hope there is no damage to the people of Nepal, I pray for everyone's recovery. .. @EONIndia pic.twitter.com/venbtQAT3s — Sourabh (@OfficialSRGupta) December 28, 2022
Powerful #Earthquake at #Nepal , I hope there is no damage to the people of Nepal, I pray for everyone's recovery. .. @EONIndia pic.twitter.com/venbtQAT3s — Sourabh (@OfficialSRGupta) December 28, 2022
The first clip of the three videos features a busy road with vehicles passing by. All of a sudden, the frame begins to shake and the vehicles on the road come to a halt. Some pedestrians start running and riders can be seen falling off their bikes.Â
The second clip in the viral video appears shot inside a departmental store. It shows goods on racks falling because of tremors.  The third clip shows a parked car and trees shaking because of a quake. The archived version of such a post can be seen here.
 The third clip shows a parked car and trees shaking because of a quake. The archived version of such a post can be seen here.
AFWA's investigation has found all three clips are old and unrelated to the earthquake that shook Nepal on December 28. AFWA PROBE Â
Per media reports, the earthquake hit Nepal Tuesday night at 01:23 local time . So, it is very unlikely that videos of the quake would feature daylight. This hinted at the videos either being old or not from Nepal at all. A reverse search of the first clip's keyframes led us to the same video uploaded  to the YouTube channel of Wild Films India on April 13, 2020. The original video was more than three minutes long and featured the same clip as the viral one. The caption of this video read, "Nepal Earthquake CCTV footage from Darbar Marg, Kathmandu 25 April 2015", making it quite clear that it was unrelated to recent developments. Reuters Japan also fact-checked  this video last June when it went viral as scenes from a Peru earthquake. While searching for the source of the second video shot inside a departmental store using reverse search, we came across a video shared  by the Facebook page Radio Farra 95.7 FM on November 23, 2021, making it evident it wasn't recent. The video's caption stated that this footage was from a 4.52 magnitude earthquake in Quito, Ecuador's capital. A comparison between the viral video and this one made it clear that both were the same. We also found multiple reports about tremours around the country on November 17  and November 20, 2021 . While we could not verify the date, time, or location of the second clip, it is more than clear that it's not from the recent Nepal earthquake. A reverse search of frames from the third clip led us to a YouTube video  featuring the same scene, only laterally reversed. This video was uploaded to the site on October 2021, making it clear that it is not from the recent Nepal earthquake. The video's caption said that it was from Greece. We searched for news on earthquakes in Greece in 2021 and came across a video report  from September of that year featuring the same video uploaded to YouTube. Per the report, Crete, a Greek island was hit by 23 tremours in seven hours on September 27, 2021. Reuters  reported that a 5.8 magnitude earthquake shook Greece's largest island, killing one person and injuring several. Therefore, it is safe to conclude that the visuals making rounds on the internet are unrelated to the recent Nepal earthquake. (With inputs from Ashish Kumar) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Dec 28, 2022 21:57 IST

title: Fact Check: KCR said he is PM Modi's 'best friend', but NOT after his daughter was grilled in liquor scam
content:
This video is from 2018 and thus, has nothing to do with his daughter being grilled by the CBI. Many times, over the years, KCR has made similar remarks about Modi.
Did Telangana Chief Minister K Chandrasekhar Rao praise Prime Minister Narendra Modi after his daughter came under the Enforcement Directorate scanner in the Delhi excise policy scam? A 30-second video that's been shared on social media shows KCR, the Baharat Rashtra Samithi supremo, saying he was PM Modi's "best friend". Among others, this video was shared on Twitter by the Bharatiya Janata Party's Priti Gandhi .Â
"After his daughter has been named in the Delhi liquor excise scam, KCR is suddenly singing like a canary!!," read Gandhi's tweet. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here , here  and here. Â
KCR's daughter K Kavitha, an MLC and a former MP, was named in a remand report by the ED in connection with the alleged Delhi excise policy scam. According to the ED , Kavitha and two others allegedly paid Rs 100 crore to the Aam Aadmi Party to avail the benefits of the now-scrapped Delhi excise policy. She was questioned by a six-member Central Bureau of Investigation team on December 11.   AFWA found that this KCR video is more than four years old and therefore not related to Kavitha's supposed involvement in the alleged scam. AFWA PROBE With the help of relevant keywords, we found the same video of the Telangana CM uploaded to a YouTube channel on March 4, 2018. In the video, responding to a journalist's question (whose audio was unclear), KCR said, "I have nothing against Narendra Modi and have respect for him… I am his best friend." He further added that he is only against "the slow progress of the country". This confirmed that the video is old. On the same date, multiple media organisations also reported on KCR's remark. According to the Times of India ,  KCR made this statement at a presser, days after his alleged remarks against the PM at a public meeting in Telangana's Karimnagar and Adilabad. Meanwhile, multiple times over the years, the BRS supremo has praised Modi  and and called him his "friend". The CM has also come down on Modi on several occasions. KCR recently had accused  the PM of threatening to topple his government in Telangana. KCR has, so far, not made any public statement about Kavitha's alleged involvement in the Delhi liquor policy scam. Reportedly,  Telangana BJP president Bandi Sanjay Kumar on December 12 had questioned KCR's continued silence on the matter. It is hence clear that the video shared by Gandhi is old. KCR's comments were not made in wake of his daughter's alleged involvement in any scam.  Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Dec 29, 2022 19:03 IST

title: How bluffmasters scripted, cooked up and filtered fake news in 2022 — top tricks exposed
content:
Tired of the same old kind of obvious, easy-to-spot "fake news"? We were as well. But thanks to the concerted efforts of a determined few, misinformation came to us in many innovative ways in 2022. Let's take a look at some, shall we? 1. FaceApp Ke Hain Koun?
Who hasn't wanted to see shiny happy celebrities stripped of their glitz and glamour? They look just like us without makeup (or maybe worse), we have told ourselves. Well, this year, we did get to see what the trio of Bollywood Khans — Aamir, Salman, and Shah Rukh — looked like once the foundation was wiped off their faces. And boy, did they look old . Only, these ancient versions of their faces were not theirs at all; face filters on Snapchat, Instagram, FaceApp, and other applications made this happen in a jiffy.Â
This also became the common link between a tearful Shiv Sena leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut and a visibly emotional Lucknow Super Giants captain KL Rahul , two names we are very unlikely to read in one sentence together. Earlier this year, the sad faces of the two men made the rounds on social media. Of course, neither was actually crying. It was face filters all over again. To them, we shall say: Don't cry because it happened, smile because we debunked it.Â
Dinosaurs don't exist anymore. There is no John Hammond who invested a boatload of money into recreating dinosaurs. There is no Jurassic Park. We all know that, right? Yet, when a video of supposed tiny dinos frolicking across a stream went viral earlier this year, we all paused to think. So, what was up with this clip? This excellent video did not require complex sci-fi technology or high-end CGI to accomplish. It was something annoyingly rudimentary. Whoever shared the dino clip just reversed a video of a band of coatis running around. Imagine bamboozling the world for a few seconds with something so simple.Â
This infuriatingly easy method was also used by people to attempt to tarnish the image of Japanese football fans at the FIFA World Cup in Qatar. Japanese soccer fans at the event made the news globally for staying behind after matches to help clean up stadiums. But during the event, a video of Japanese fans littering in a stadium was shared by many, many people. And of course, the video that originally showed them cleaning up was reversed to make it look otherwise. A clear cartoon villain move by someone who hates cleaning up after themselves; who is to know? 3. War Games
We've all seen horrific videos and photos from the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The human cost of war, the scary shelling, and at least one bizarre photo of an unexploded missile stuck in someone's kitchen sink. Suffice it to say, there is enough shocking (and real) stuff there. Yet, there are also people who have shared footage from a video game, claiming it showed the war in action. In fact, at least one Indian TV channel fell for this repeatedly.
"Arma 3" is a pretty good video game with very realistic visuals. But it's not more real-looking than actual videos from the war. Despite that, on at least two occasions, videos from this very game were widely shared on social media as Ukraine kicking Russia's butt in the war! 4. True Lies
Consuming laced "prasad", losing consciousness, and getting robbed . A child getting kidnapped in a crowded public area . Someone mixing toxic stuff into the street food we love to eat . When we encounter videos capturing these scenarios, we are inclined to immediately believe them to be true. Because these are real fears people have. These are things we have been cautioned against all our lives.Â
And 2022 saw a bunch of these so-called "public awareness" videos that do little to inform audiences that they are scripted and staged, save a blink-and-miss disclaimer at the end. Content creators have capitalised on the real anxieties of people, creating videos that show incidents like these shot from a single vantage point, giving them the appearance of CCTV footage or hidden camera footage. And in doing so, these "awareness" videos only create more hysteria. The not-so-old adage comes to mind: Don't believe everything that's shared on your WhatsApp group. title: 2022 in 'rear' view - why did we fact-check these? Most WTF stories of 2022
content: Normally, "fake news" is a deathly serious business. However, not all fake news stories have high stakes. Some were so absurd and bizarre that they just made us scratch our heads. These weird stories involved world leaders, witches, and even drinking one's own blood. Read at your own risk, these stories may make you question your sanity. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story A 'REAR' SIGHT When Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the White House, US President Joe Biden grabbed his butt . While this is, according to trusted Illuminati sources, the secret world leader handshake, the photo shared online was just disappointingly bad editing. Maybe, AI art can help them do better someday. BLOODY MARY A man allegedly drank the blood he donated   after he was denied biscuits. A totally reasonable action, right? Sadly, this never happened. This viral incident was the figment of a satirical news writer's imagination. HISS MISTAKE Fashion is a dangerous thing. For instance, a man attacked  his wife's legs because he mistook her weird snake-like stockings for a real snake. This act of bravery, alas was just fiction. The photos had nothing to do with this story — if we can ever be reasonably sure this happened at all. WITCH COUNTRY Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal. Then in Karachi, Pakistan. Then Colombia, Nigeria, Malaysia, and the Philippines. This video of a witch  making spooky noises outside a window at night is apparently from all these places. If this story made you feel pain, you can take some solace in knowing that at least in the case of this viral post, the incident was not real. While even the greatest icons are bound to commit a faux pas once in a while, Trudeau appears immune to such mortal flaws. title: Fake News Favourites! These people dominated the space in 2022
content: More than anything else, fake news always vies for eyeballs and therefore follows the famous. This year was no exception. Major events like the FIFA World Cup in Qatar and the Russia-Ukraine war obviously attracted plenty of mis/disinformation, and conspiracy theories like "love jihad" found much in terms of falsehoods around it. But public figures were still the main targets. Sometimes, they were made targets. At other times, their supporters attempted to airbrush their auras. Let's look at top four politicians who were at the epicenter of misinformation. Rahul Gandhi The Congress party scion has, year after year, been targeted with fake news. This year, because of myriad polls across India, and the Bharat Jodo Yatra, Gandhi has been in the public eye almost constantly. Misinformation marched along with the Yatra. Photos of large crowds, like one from a Christian evangelical gathering in Nigeria , were shared (falsely) as the sights and sounds from the Congress party's march. Gandhi, who has often also been the target of the Hindu-right, was also attacked. For example, during the Yatra's stop at a religious place, people falsely claimed that the Congress leader refused to perform aarti. The biggest lie surrounding Gandhi this year, however, was how he met a Chinese envoy  at a nightclub in Kathmandu, Nepal. The truth: the woman in the video was a friend of the bride at the wedding that Rahul Gandhi was attending in Nepal — not a Chinese diplomat. Arvind Kejriwal The Delhi chief minister and Aam Aadmi Party supremo had a great year. A massive victory in Punjab, making inroads in Gujarat, and the AAP gaining national party status — these are big achievements. However, Kejriwa l was also the subject of a lot of misinformation in 2022, especially in the run-up to the Gujarat Assembly Elections. For example, there were photos and videos of people supposedly attending AAP rallies in Gujarat while wearing Narendra Modi masks . These, however, were from the 2020 Delhi polls. During the run-up to the Punjab election, a video of Kejriwal admitting his ties to the BJP and the RSS  went viral. Of course, it was doctored. Not all such falsehoods were anti-Kejriwal though. One such featured an edited and out-of-context news clip  that claimed the AAP was faring better than the BJP and the Congress in Gujarat. Kejriwal himself shared this video (and later deleted it). Bhagwant Mann Another AAP member, the Punjab chief minister, was constantly in focus. Especially during the Assembly election in the state. There were the obvious ones with liquor stores  and liquor bottles photoshopped to Mann's images. But there were also serious ones like doctored videos  that made it look like Mann called his party's leader, Kejriwal, a dacoit! Obvious fake you may think - but still many fell for it. The worst of this misinformation was the allegation that Mann had been photographed with Goldy Brar , the gangster allegedly responsible for the murder of Siddhu Moose Wala. The photo featured a different Goldy Brar, not the alleged killer. But before it was debunked, it spread like wildfire. Nupur Sharma The now-suspended BJP spokesperson was in the eye of the storm for a big part of 2022. In May, during a TV news debate, Sharma made controversial remarks about Prophet Mohammed. This was followed by outrage, protests, communal violence, and international backlash. And of course, a lot of misinformation. There was fake news about UPA's presidential candidate Yashwant Sinha  promising to arrest Sharma if he took office. There were lies about how a group protesting against Nupur Sharma in Kolkata killed a policeman. A lie was also viral on social media that a Hindu man in Kolhapur  murdered a Muslim person over supporting Nupur Sharma. Of course, these weren't the only public figures who were surrounded by fake news. PM Modi, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and Sidhu Moose Wala, among others, were constantly encompassed by half-truths and whole lies.
